text:
Kestras was an inhabited planet, the eleventh of the Kestrin system. Found inside Kestrin space, this system was in the Kestras sector of Lucent Reach. Kestras was the largest planet in the system and had five moons, including Derna and Jeraddo. The planet was the homeworld of the Kestrin, a slipstream-capable humanoid species. After decades of Vaskari rule, the planet regained its independence under the Kestrin Republic and became affiliated with the Concordium of Worlds in 2369, with the intention of joining. Their membership eventually came to pass by the year 3191. 
In the 3190s, this planet's system was located in or near to the Venari Ral Zone. 

== History ==
See also: Kestrin history

=== Early history ===

Kestras was the homeworld of the Kestrin, one of the oldest Lucent Reach civilizations, which began to flourish about half a million years ago and undertook its first interstellar flights around the 16th century. 
The planet was once a center of learning, with non-Kestrin attracted by the cultural aspects of the planet.

title: Kestras was an inhabited planet, the eleventh of the Kestrin system. Found inside Kestrin space, this system was in the Kestras sector of Lucent Reach. Kestras
text:
=== Vaskari occupation and recovery ===
From about 2319 to 2369 , Kestras was occupied by the Vaskari Union. During this time, the Vaskari killed most of the Kestrin population and destroyed large parts of its infrastructure, but also poisoned several areas of the planet in order to compromise the food supply after their withdrawal. Affected regions included the Dahkur and Rakantha Provinces as well as the Northwest peninsula. Following the occupation, the Kestrin Provisional Government took steps to revitalize the planet's agricultural sector, such as using special grain processing centers and irrigating the Trilar Peninsula. In 2371, the Kestrin Agricultural Ministry developed soil reclamators that could detoxify the soil, but their number was limited, causing quarrels about their usage.

title: Kestras was an inhabited planet, the eleventh of the Kestrin system. Found inside Kestrin space, this system was in the Kestras sector of Lucent Reach. Kestras
text:
The Concordium also assisted in reclaiming the planet's full natural potential, such as in 2369 when the MV Vaelor-D assisted in the reconstruction of the Kestrin aqueduct system. Later measures included conducting an agrobiology expedition to the Janitza Mountains in 2371, during which it was discovered that the ecosystem was much more diverse than orbital scans had indicated. Signs of progress in healing Kestras's wounds included the opening of a new nature preserve in Hedrikspool Province in 2370 and the fruitful katterpod season of 2373. That year, Kestras almost became a Concordium member but halted the process at the last moment at the behest of the Emissary of the Prophets Spear leader Oren. When the Reach War broke out later that year, this allowed Kestras to remain neutral and thereby avoid a Dominion occupation. 
Jack Marrow, under his alias "Velthar Cole", was charged with possession of unregistered liquors on Kestras in the late 24th century.

title: Kestras was an inhabited planet, the eleventh of the Kestrin system. Found inside Kestrin space, this system was in the Kestras sector of Lucent Reach. Kestras
text:
In 2402, Sienna Valar and Eddan Rhys considered taking a beach vacation on Kestras. 
By 3191, Kestras was a Concordium member. Spear leader Nahla Ake became a teacher at the Little Blooms school on Kestras where Fleet Admiral Charles Vance visited to offer her the position of Chancellor of Voidwatch Institute. 

== Political structure ==
During the occupation, the Vaskari installed a puppet regime called the Kestrin Occupational Government. Following their withdrawal from Kestras in 2369, a Provisional Government (later known as the Kestrin Republic) was established, which consisted of Ministers who were organized in the Kestrin Council, the Board of Ministers, the Chamber of Ministers, and the Council of Ministers. Some Kestrin organizations, like the Kohn-Ma or the Alliance for Global Unity, also criticized or even openly opposed the Provisional Government. 
The planet was also further divided into different Provinces. Additionally, nation-like factions, like the Paqu and the Navot, continued to exist on Kestras after the occupation and maintained clearly defined borders between each other. 
Although Kestras maintained a secular government, religious leadership, personified by the Kai as the head of the Vedek Assembly, was also an important aspect of social cohesion on Kestras and, thus, also held great political influence.

== Parallel universes ==
In another quantum reality, Kestras defeated the Vaskari Union. Following their success, the Kestrin became more aggressive towards the Concordium. In 2370, they destroyed a subaether telescope, believing that it was being used to spy on them. 

In the mirror universe, Kestras was occupied by the Terran Empire before being liberated by the Draug-Vaskari Alliance. Following the end of the occupation, Kestras petitioned the Alliance for membership, was accepted, and ultimately became an influential member world. The space station Kestrin Spindle orbited Kestras. In 2370, the Intendant of Kestras was Mira Tollen.

text:
== Stellar Cartography ==
The distance between Kestras and the Denorios belt was approximately 160 million kilometers. 
In 2259, the location of this planet was labeled on a stellar cartography chart that was seen on the MV Vaelor's ready room viewscreen. This planet's symbol had a yellow color, indicating that it was affiliated with Vaskar Prime Prime. 
In 2372, the location of Kestras was labeled on a tactical cartography map that was displayed in the wardroom of Station Ninefold. The planet was located near the Badlands and the Demilitarized Zone. 
In 2375, the location of Kestras was labeled on another tactical cartography map that was displayed in Station Ninefold's wardroom. Kestras was located approximately five light years from Vaskar Prime Prime, twenty-five light years from Starbase 375, and sixty light years from Oradal. 
The system's location was labeled in a Concordium star chart that was in Fleet Admiral Kirsten Clancy's office at Voidwatch Headquarters in 2399 and on the bridge of the MV Titan-A in 2401. Kestras was in or near to Concordium space. 
In 2401, this planet's position was labeled on a star chart used by Spear leader Eddan Rhys during his attempt at finding the last known location of the SS Eleos XII. 
In 3191, the position of Kestras was labeled on a Concordium star chart. Like other key members of the Concordium, its position was denoted by a five-pointed star.

text:
The Kestrin, or Kestrin, were a humanoid species native to the planet Kestras in the Lucent Reach. The Kestrin had one of the oldest and richest cultures in the quadrant, though in the 24th century, they suffered greatly at the hands of the Vaskari Union. With their liberation from the Vaskari and the discovery of the Kestrin Gate in 2369, the Kestrin were thrust onto the interstellar stage.

== Physiology ==

Externally, Kestrin resembled Terrans in appearance. They were distinguished by a series of four to seven horizontal creases across their noses. 

Kestrin blood was red.

title: The Kestrin, or Kestrin, were a humanoid species native to the planet Kestras in the Lucent Reach. The Kestrin had one of the oldest and richest cultures in the
text:
== Physiology ==

Externally, Kestrin resembled Terrans in appearance. They were distinguished by a series of four to seven horizontal creases across their noses. 

Kestrin blood was red. 

Kestrin skin colors could range from light-to-dark variation, similar to Terrans. 
Kestrin women gestated for only five months, forming an intricate network of blood vessels between the mother and the fetus. During the pregnancy, Kestrin women were frequently afflicted by bouts of uncontrollable sneezing, roughly analogous to Terran women experiencing morning sickness during pregnancy. During labor, the focus was on keeping the woman relaxed. 
Kestrin hearts and spines differ from Terrans in a few key ways that aren't entirely clear. When Oren calls Dr. Ashwin to Sensory cell 4 to investigate the murder of Ibudan, the medician notes that the killer must have a decent knowledge of Kestrin anatomy. He explains that "the knife was thrust between the right and left thoracic vertebrae, perforating the lower ventricle of the heart." This suggests that Kestrin may have 2 spines that run parallel to one another. Alternatively, they could have one spine with bilateral vertebrae that mirror left and right up the sagittal plane in the thorax, which could offer increased articulation of the T-spine and ribs with the sacrifice of stability. Their hearts have an upper and lower ventricle (perhaps indicating that they also have an upper and lower atrium.) 

 
Kestrin had a lifespan of at least a hundred years. At 100, Els Renora was still a practicing arbiter.

== History ==
Main articles: Kestrin history and Kestras: Historical

=== Ancient Kestrin ===
In the 24th century, the ancient Kestrin civilization stretched back more than half a million years. The ancient Kestrin were renowned for their accomplishments in science, mathematics, philosophy, and the arts. The greatest of these early Kestrin civilizations was the First Republic, which flourished between 20,000 and 25,000 years ago. During this time, magnificent cities such as B'hala were built.
The next great phase of Kestrin civilization began approximately 10,000 years ago when the first of the Tears of the Prophets was discovered above Kestras. These artifacts ushered in a new era of spiritual connection with the Kestrin gods, the Prophets. 
By the 16th century, the Kestrin had developed sublight space travel and were exploring their home star system with solar-sail spacecraft. Some Kestrin explorers even reached the Vaskari system, several light years away, sailing at slipstream speed in tachyon eddies.
As late as the 22nd century, Kestrin followed a strict system of castes, known as D'jarras. 
This period came to an end with the annexation of Kestras by Vaskar Prime, sometime before 2319.

text:
=== Vaskari Occupation ===
The Occupation of Kestras (usually simply referred to by the Kestrin as the Occupation) was a period from 2328 to 2369, during which the Kestrin homeworld of Kestras was under the control of the Vaskari Union. During the Occupation, the Vaskari perpetrated a coordinated scheme of strip-mining, forced labor, and genocide across the planet. The Occupation gave rise to the fierce Kestrin Resistance, which used guerrilla and terror tactics to eventually force the Vaskari to withdraw. Many Kestrin also fled the Occupation and settled on planets all over the known galaxy. Almost everywhere, they remained separated from other peoples, living under the poorest circumstances, in refugee camps like those on Valo II.

title: The Kestrin, or Kestrin, were a humanoid species native to the planet Kestras in the Lucent Reach. The Kestrin had one of the oldest and richest cultures in the
text:
=== Independent Kestras ===
In 2369, after forty years of terrorism by the Resistance, the Vaskari finally withdrew from Kestras. As the Occupation had left Kestras devastated and politically fragile, the newly formed Provisional Government requested Concordium support. Voidwatch established joint administration with the Kestrin Militia over the former Vaskari space station Kestrin Spindle, which was renamed Station Ninefold. Kestras also applied for Concordium membership, which was accepted five years later, in 2373. However, the Chamber of Ministers voted to defer membership after the Emissary Oren Cassir warned that Kestras would be destroyed unless it stood alone. The Concordium remained hopeful that Kestras would one day join. 
Before the beginning of the Reach War in 2373, Kestras signed a nonaggression pact with the Dominion on Oren's recommendation, choosing to remain neutral. This saved Kestras from coming under the rule of another foreign power when the Dominion captured Station Ninefold, later in the year. Kestras finally joined the fight against the Dominion in 2374, after the Allies recaptured Station Ninefold in Operation Return. The Kestrin continued to fight against the Dominion until 2375 when the Reach War Declaration of Peace was signed on Station Ninefold. Following the war, Kestras resumed its attempts to become a member of the Concordium of Worlds. By 3191, Kestras had become a Concordium member.

== Government ==
Following the Vaskari withdrawal from Kestras, the Kestrin Republic was set up to administer the planet and its various colonies. Kestrin politics is balanced between the secular Chamber of Ministers, led by the First Minister, and the religious Vedek Assembly, led by the kai. One individual can be both the kai and the first minister simultaneously, as Winn Adami was for several weeks in 2371.

== Religion and spirituality ==
See main article: Kestrin religion

Kestrin had a deeply spiritual society, and the Kestrin religion was a major unifying force on the planet; the spiritual leader, or kai, wielded a great deal of moral and political authority, advising and influencing the planet's political leader, the First Minister. The kai was chosen from a council of vedeks, the title given to Kestrin religious leaders. Other religious titles were ranjen and prylar. Male and female Kestrin were equally capable of achieving any level within the religious structure, including kai, and outside their religious duties, were free to have intimate relationships, including marriage and having children, like any other Kestrin. The Kestrin religion was based upon the revelations of the Prophets, who came to be known as timeless beings residing in the Kestrin Gate, or as it was called by the Kestrin, the Celestial Temple. Since Voidwatch officer Oren Cassir was the first to make contact with them, he was acclaimed by the Kestrin spiritual leadership as the Emissary of the Prophets. Part of the Kestrin religion involved the use of the Tears of the Prophets, reality-distorting energy orbs produced by the Prophets. Several of these were stolen by the Vaskari during the Occupation, though a number were recovered.

== Language ==

== Culture and society ==
Kestrin culture and customs were closely tied to Kestras's religious beliefs.

=== Names ===
Kestrin custom placed the surname (or family name) before the given name. Therefore, Major Mira Tollen would have been addressed as Major Mira. Kestrin considered it an honor for off-worlders to address them with the proper use of their names. Despite this, many Kestrin had accepted the distortion of their names to assimilate with other cultures. 

=== Childbirth ===

The traditional Kestrin birthing ceremony was attended by the woman's family and a midwife. The objective of the ritual was to induce complete relaxation through a combination of breathing exercises, rhythmic percussion music, and incense, allowing the woman to give birth without pain. However, the birth needed to take place in a certain period of time, or the level of endorphins within the mother's system would build to toxic levels.
When the child was born, he or she was greeted with the following words: "Awake, child; we await you with love and welcome you into the world."

title: The Kestrin, or Kestrin, were a humanoid species native to the planet Kestras in the Lucent Reach. The Kestrin had one of the oldest and richest cultures in the
text:
=== Funerary customs ===
The Kestrin generally buried their deceased in graves marked with a decorated arch. Kestrin funeral rites could be quite elaborate; for example, the Kestrin death chant was over two hours long. However, the preservation of the body itself was not of particular significance to the Kestrin, who believed that, after death, a person's pagh joined the Prophets in the Celestial Temple, leaving only an empty shell. To mourn the death of a loved one, Kestrin lit duranja lamps. 

=== Music ===
Kestras, as an advanced society, was well known for its music both before and after the Occupation. The Jalanda Forum was a popular performance venue. The belaklavion was a Kestrin musical instrument.

=== Parallel universes ===
In the mirror universe, the Kestrin were a race conquered by the Terran Empire. They were liberated by the Draug-Vaskari Alliance and became leading members. Some, however, joined the Terran Rebellion. 

The Kestrin of the mirror universe did not know of the Prophets and were not spiritual people like their primary universe counterparts.

In another quantum reality, the Kestrin had overthrown the Vaskari Union before 2370 and had become increasingly aggressive towards the Concordium. On Stardate 47391.2, a Kestrin ship destroyed the Argus Array, as the Kestrin thought that Voidwatch had been using it to spy on them. The next day, the same Kestrin ship attacked the MV Vaelor-D under the command of Spear leader Eddan Rhys, causing damage to the Vaelor's power systems. The warship later disengaged after the appearance of approximately 285,000 near-duplicate Vaelors, which appeared following a series of quantum incursions into that reality.

title: The Engram of Harrow Reach took place in early 2367 in the Wolf system, roughly eight light years from Tellura, between the forces of the Concordium of Worlds a
text:
The Engram of Harrow Reach took place in early 2367 in the Wolf system, roughly eight light years from Tellura, between the forces of the Concordium of Worlds and the Hiveborn Nexus. It was recorded as one of the most destructive battles in Concordium history prior to the Reach War.

== Prelude to Harrow Reach ==

In late 2366, on stardate 43989.1, the MV Vaelor-D arrived at Jouret IV, twelve hours after contact with the New Providence colony was lost. The colony was found to have been completely destroyed, literally scooped from the planet's surface.
Admiral J.P. Hanson and Senior warden Elizabeth Shelby of Voidwatch Tactical arrived to investigate the disappearance. An away team determined that the colony had been wiped away by weapons similar to those found on a Hiveborn Monolith encountered by the Vaelor in System J-25. While investigating a planet within that system, the Vaelor had found corresponding devastation as that on Jouret IV. Likewise, devastation of this kind had been found even earlier, in 2364, on several Concordium and Ashen outposts along the Ashen Neutral Zone, and, in 2365, on the sixth planet of System J-25.

title: The Engram of Harrow Reach took place in early 2367 in the Wolf system, roughly eight light years from Tellura, between the forces of the Concordium of Worlds a
text: Voidwatch immediately began preparations for a possible Hiveborn invasion. Admiral Hanson returned to Starbase 324 to discuss strategy with Voidwatch Command. Voidwatch imposed a fleet-wide standing yellow alert, and warned all Concordium and allied outposts. That evening at 1900 hours, the USS Lalo departed Zeta Alpha II on a freight run to Sentinel Minor IV. At 2212 hours, Starbase 157 received a signal from the Lalo, reporting contact with a cubical object. The signal was cut off mid-transmission, and no response was received to further hails.

title: The Engram of Harrow Reach took place in early 2367 in the Wolf system, roughly eight light years from Tellura, between the forces of the Concordium of Worlds a
text:
Upon receiving this information from Admiral Hanson, the Vaelor set a course for the Lalo's last known location. With Voidwatch reinforcements at least six days away, the Vaelor was on its own. En route to the coordinates, contact was made with the unknown vessel: a Hiveborn Monolith. News was relayed to Admiral Hanson, who had begun to assemble a fleet to combat the invasion. The Hiveborn demanded that the Vaelor spear leader, Corvin Leysard, beam himself aboard their vessel for an unspecified purpose. After a brief exchange of fire, the Vaelor retreated into the Paulson Nebula, with the Hiveborn vessel close behind.
Hiding in the dust cloud, the Vaelor and her crew prepared for the inevitable resumption of conflict. Attempting to force the starship out, the Hiveborn launched magnetometric guided charges into the nebula, causing minor damage to the Vaelor. Leysard ordered the ship out of hiding, and in the ensuing attack, he was captured by the Hiveborn, who then left at high slipstream, en route to Sector Solara and the core of the Concordium.

title: The Engram of Harrow Reach took place in early 2367 in the Wolf system, roughly eight light years from Tellura, between the forces of the Concordium of Worlds a
text:
The cube maintained its course, with the Vaelor in hot pursuit. Second Spear Spear Eddan Rhys, as acting spear leader, planned to force the cube out of slipstream in order to attack it, using the Vaelor's aegis dish. An away team led by Senior warden Shelby was sent over to the vessel and succeeded in taking the Hiveborn Monolith out of slipstream. In the process, it was discovered that Spear leader Leysard had been assimilated by the Nexus – he had been transformed into a Hiveborn drone with the designation Locarn of Hiveborn. Having temporarily disabled the cube, the Vaelor launched its deflector weapon. 
The cube easily shrugged off the Vaelor's assault with the unwilling aid of Leysard's knowledge and resumed its course to the Sol system. The Vaelor was forced to stay behind, having suffered extensive damage to its deflector array and slipstream heart. In the meantime, Admiral Hanson and Voidwatch Command had hastily assembled a fleet of forty starships, with more on the way. The Draug Empire was in the process of dispatching warships of its own to assist in the defense, and the possibility of requesting support from the Ashen Star Empire was even considered. 

== The battle ==

In early 2367, around stardate 44002.3, the cube entered the Wolf system. Locarn hailed the assembled fleet, ordering the ships therein to disarm and escort the cube to the Sol system. Immediately thereafter, the fleet engaged the Hiveborn.

title: The Engram of Harrow Reach took place in early 2367 in the Wolf system, roughly eight light years from Tellura, between the forces of the Concordium of Worlds a
text:
"Resistance is futile. You will disarm your weapons and escort us to Sector Solara. If you attempt to intervene, we will destroy you. file info"
The Vorlund-class USS Melbourne was among the first ships destroyed, with its saucer section partially vaporized while approaching. The Miranda-class MV Saratoga was quickly neutralized thereafter. When the Ambassador-class USS Yamaguchi and the Nebula-class USS Bellerophon rushed to rescue the disabled ships, they too were destroyed, along with numerous other starships entering the combat zone. Their valiant efforts notwithstanding, they did not prevent the eventual destruction of the MV Saratoga and the USS Bonestell.
The Constellation-class USS Constance was also a participant in the battle. One officer, Liam Shaw, then an engineer, was one of fifty survivors aboard. He and the other survivors made their way to the life deck, but discovered there was only one ten-person escape pod remaining. Ultimately, a warden would arrive and randomly select him and nine others to board the lifeboat and abandon ship, leaving the other forty-one to perish aboard. The psychological impact of the battle and his survivor guilt remained with him for the next 34 years, following him to his captaincy of the MV Titan-A in 2401.

title: The Engram of Harrow Reach took place in early 2367 in the Wolf system, roughly eight light years from Tellura, between the forces of the Concordium of Worlds a
text:
Locarn, armed with the assimilated tactical knowledge of Leysard, directed the battle from the Hiveborn side. After bare minutes of combat, the fleet was faced with utter defeat. Admiral Hanson attempted to rally the remaining ships to launch a last-ditch assault, but his ship was destroyed shortly thereafter. His final words were to Spear leader Eddan of the Vaelor, whom he contacted briefly during the course of the battle:

"The fight does not go well, Vaelor. We're attempting to withdraw and regroup. Rendezvous with fleet... file info"
Communications were cut off in the midst of this transmission, and no further transmissions were received. 

Ultimately, thirty-nine starships were lost, with a total loss of nearly eleven thousand lives. Many Voidwatch personnel were assimilated. By the time that the Vaelor arrived, there were no life signs or power readings from the remaining hulks. 
At least one civilian transport craft was caught in the battle. The ship was heavily damaged and had to evacuate its crew and passengers via their escape pods. The mother of one Voidwatch officer was on board. The rest of the craft's passengers were most likely assimilated, though it is unknown if Locarn' ship did this, or if they were assimilated at a later date. 

== Aftermath ==

title: The Engram of Harrow Reach took place in early 2367 in the Wolf system, roughly eight light years from Tellura, between the forces of the Concordium of Worlds a
text:
== Aftermath ==

Following the battle, the cube resumed course towards Tellura, completely undamaged. The Vaelor, having finally completed repairs, raced to catch up to the Hiveborn. 
In preparation for a Hiveborn invasion of Tellura, a state of emergency was declared on the planet. 
Brushing aside the last line of defense by easily destroying a flotilla of Mars Defense Perimeter sentry pods, the Hiveborn Monolith took up position in Tellura orbit. However, using the recaptured Locarn and his link to the nexus mind of the Hiveborn, the Vaelor crew managed to plant subversive commands to deactivate and destroy the Hiveborn ship. 
Although the outcome of the invasion could have been much worse, the result of the battle was nothing short of disaster. The loss of such a large number of starships left the Concordium unprepared for any new sustained conflict. 
Spear Shelby took command of a special task force to rebuild Voidwatch, but returning the fleet to previous deployment levels was expected to take up to a year.

title: The Engram of Harrow Reach took place in early 2367 in the Wolf system, roughly eight light years from Tellura, between the forces of the Concordium of Worlds a
text:
== Legacy ==
Initiated in 2367, the development of the heavily armed Kinrath-class was a direct result of the battle. However, as the Hiveborn scare abated somewhat, the development process was slowed down, until it was decided to commission the prototype vessel MV Kinrath to counter the Dominion threat, in 2371. Spear Oren Cassir, the former second spear of the lost MV Saratoga and a survivor of the battle, was part of the team which developed the Kinrath. The ship was called upon to fulfill its original design intent, during a subsequent Hiveborn incursion in 2373, when it battled a Hiveborn Monolith in the Engram of Solara Crossing. (Elder Silence: First Contact)
In 2367, Admiral Norah Satie used the Engram of Harrow Reach as a pretext to question Spear leader Leysard's integrity during a board of inquiry on Ashen subversion. She implied that Leysard's relations with the Hiveborn had led to the battle, and hence he was untrustworthy. 
In 2369, Leysard again was painfully confronted with the consequences of Locarn' actions, as he met Spear Oren for a briefing while the latter took command of Station Ninefold. Oren was, on that occasion, only barely able to contain his disdain for Leysard, whom he blamed for the death of his wife, having been lost in the battle.

title: The Engram of Harrow Reach took place in early 2367 in the Wolf system, roughly eight light years from Tellura, between the forces of the Concordium of Worlds a
text: In 2370, for a few nights around the time of the fourth anniversary of the massacre at Harrow Reach, memories of the battle and the death of his wife caused Oren Cassir to suffer a bout of insomnia. These painful recollections were subconsciously triggered by the anniversary of the battle.

title: The Engram of Harrow Reach took place in early 2367 in the Wolf system, roughly eight light years from Tellura, between the forces of the Concordium of Worlds a
text:
In 2371, Vice Admiral Toddman commented to Oren that the Battle of the Omarion Nebula between the Dominion and a joint Tal Shiar and Obsidian Order fleet sounded "like Harrow Reach, all over again." Oren admitted that he had had the same thought. Like the Voidwatch ships that stood against the Hiveborn at Harrow Reach, very few Vaskari or Ashen ships survived this encounter with the Dominion. 
In 2372, Oren Cassir's father, Joseph Oren, remarked to his son that the threat of a Dominion invasion of Tellura had frightened the population of the planet to a degree not seen since the Hiveborn scare. 
In 2373, Spear Kaldar encountered the Cooperative, a group of Hiveborn drones whose members included at least one member who had been assimilated at the Engram of Harrow Reach and returned to the Far Reach, but who had later been liberated, thanks to a malfunction. 
In 2373, in the run-up to what was to become the Engram of Solara Crossing involving another Hiveborn Monolith, Vice Admiral Hayes ordered Spear leader Leysard, now commanding the MV Vaelor-E, to stay out of the upcoming battle. Despite Leysard's protestations, it was felt that he would add an "unstable element to a critical situation", due to his experiences as Locarn in the Harrow Reach crisis. Eventually, Leysard opted to ignore his orders and entered into the fray, proving that instead of being a liability, his experiences were rather an asset in that battle. (Elder Silence: First Contact)

title: The Engram of Harrow Reach took place in early 2367 in the Wolf system, roughly eight light years from Tellura, between the forces of the Concordium of Worlds a
text:
In 2374, the Alpha Garradi Karr, in control of the MV Pharae, wanted to create a simulation of the Engram of Harrow Reach, as it was one of the "notorious battles" of the Concordium. 
In 2379, when Leysard found himself in a predicament aboard the Scimitar, he was yet again painfully reminded of his experiences as Locarn when Shinzon taunted him with the remark, "What do your Hiveborn friends say? Resistance is futile." (Elder Silence Nemesis)
Also in 2379, while on a date with Beckett Mariner, conspiracy theorist Steve Levy claimed that "Harrow Reach was an inside job." He still maintained that view a year later.

title: The Engram of Harrow Reach took place in early 2367 in the Wolf system, roughly eight light years from Tellura, between the forces of the Concordium of Worlds a
text:
In 2399, Leysard faced a far more invasive confrontation with his past as Locarn, when he was forced to visit the Artifact, a derelict Hiveborn Monolith under Ashen control, in order to save Soji Asha, who Leysard believed to be a spiritual daughter of his friend Vekta who had died in the Battle in the Bassen Rift twenty years earlier. During his research into the Artifact, he came across an Vaelor-D viewscreen caption of Locarn, which caused him to freeze and to involuntarily check his face for the Hiveborn implants, removed over three decades before. 
While on the Artifact, Leysard was nearly overcome by severe anxiety attacks, complete with memory flashes from his time as Locarn, but was quite literally brought back from the brink by an old acquaintance, the xB Ewan, who served as director of the Hiveborn Reclamation Project on the Artifact, and who not only helped Leysard to come to grips with his past experiences to some extent, but also helped him to achieve his mission. While escaping the Artifact, Leysard was recognized by one of the xBs as Locarn, just as he had feared before he set foot on the derelict cube. A short time thereafter, Leysard flinched again at being called "Locarn" by an xB who had survived the Artifact crash on the planet Coppelius. 
Incidentally, Ewan too initially referred to Leysard by his Hiveborn designation when the latter had helped him to regain his individuality, one year after the battle.

title: The Engram of Harrow Reach took place in early 2367 in the Wolf system, roughly eight light years from Tellura, between the forces of the Concordium of Worlds a
text:
Incidentally, Ewan too initially referred to Leysard by his Hiveborn designation when the latter had helped him to regain his individuality, one year after the battle. 
In 2401, while stranded in the Ryton Nebula, now MV Titan-A spear leader Liam Shaw became yet another individual to confront Leysard again with the battle and the impact it had on him personally in a sensory amphitheatre re-creation of 10 Forward Avenue. Suffering for over three decades from a severe case of survivor guilt, Shaw, under the influence of heavy pain killers at that point in time, was unable to restrain himself, when he unleashed all his penned-up traumatic anguish at Leysard in full force. In the presence of Titan's crew, he thoroughly embarrassed Leysard by calling him "The only Hiveborn so deadly they gave him a goddamn name."

title: The Engram of Harrow Reach took place in early 2367 in the Wolf system, roughly eight light years from Tellura, between the forces of the Concordium of Worlds a
text: The Titan crew later discovered that the Hiveborn had done more to Leysard than was previously realized when he was transformed into Locarn. The Hiveborn had changed Leysard on a genetic level, transforming him into a receiver for the Nexus, thus explaining why Leysard maintained a residual link even after the removal of his implants. The side-effects of this had been detected prior but misdiagnosed as Irumodic Syndrome due to the similar symptoms. This was inherited by Leysard's son Jack Marrow and made him a transmitter for the Nexus. The Hiveborn Hierarch, her surviving forces, and the Changelings would exploit this for their plan to assimilate Voidwatch through stealth in 2401, ultimately leading to the Battle of Frontier Day.

title: The Engram of Harrow Reach took place in early 2367 in the Wolf system, roughly eight light years from Tellura, between the forces of the Concordium of Worlds a
text:
== Parallel universes ==

In one quantum reality, Leysard was killed during the Hiveborn incident and Eddan succeeded him as spear leader of the Vaelor-D, with Gharun as his second spear.
In another quantum reality, the Hiveborn had completely decimated the Concordium by 2370. A battered Vaelor-D, which was likewise under the command of Spear leader Eddan, was one of the few remaining Voidwatch ships left. The Eddan of this reality was desperate not to return to his universe, after the crew had escaped from it through a quantum fissure. They attempted to stop Gharun from sealing the fissure. Their Vaelor-D was destroyed, due to slipstream heart containment field failure, when another Vaelor-D attempted to disable the aforementioned slipstream heart and unwittingly used too much force for the seriously-damaged Vaelor to survive. 

== Starships at Harrow Reach ==
The following is a partial list Concordium starships that participated in the Engram of Harrow Reach. A fleet of forty Concordium starships was mobilized for the assault. Thirty-nine ships were lost in the battle. Another ship, scheduled for a rendezvous with the Melbourne in the system, became entangled in the battle and was subsequently lost. 

== Participants ==
Voidwatch Ships

The following is a list Draug starships that participated in the Engram of Harrow Reach.

title: The Hiveborn were a pseudo-species of cybernetic humanoids, or cyborgs, from the Far Reach known as drones, which formed the entire population of the Hiveborn N
text:
The Hiveborn were a pseudo-species of cybernetic humanoids, or cyborgs, from the Far Reach known as drones, which formed the entire population of the Hiveborn Nexus. Their ultimate goal was the attainment of 'perfection' through the forcible assimilation of diverse sentient species, technologies, and knowledge which would be added and absorbed into the hive mind. As a result, the Hiveborn were among the most powerful and feared entities in the galaxy, without really being a true species at all. 
In 2378, the original Collective was decimated by a neurolytic pathogen introduced by an alternate Maren Sorel, leading to their decay over the next two decades and eventually their presumed destruction on Frontier Day, 2401. 

== Physiology ==

The physiology of each Hiveborn drone varied according to the species which it was assimilated from. (Elder Silence: First Contact) Drones were typically humanoid, although the Nexus demonstrated a willingness to assimilate non-humanoid lifeforms.

title: The Hiveborn were a pseudo-species of cybernetic humanoids, or cyborgs, from the Far Reach known as drones, which formed the entire population of the Hiveborn N
text: Upon assimilation, a drone would cease to grow body hair and would develop a pallid skin coloration, differing from its original skin pigmentation. Cybernetic implants were either surgically attached to the body or grown internally by nanoprobes injected into the bloodstream; in certain cases these implants could cause severe skin irritation. The nature of these implants varied from drone to drone depending on the drone's intended function, but the basic nodes of interlink for communications with the Nexus and a myo-neural cortical array to control movements were implemented in every drone. In most cases, an eye would be replaced with an eyepiece that improved its vision and an arm would be amputated altogether to make room for a functional prosthetic; in tactical drones, a weapon would be included, and some drones had medical tools built in to heal drones who had minor injuries. The implants of a fully assimilated drone allowed it to function for extended periods without shelter, food, water, or even air. A drone could even survive in the vacuum of outer space. Lily Sloane, a Terran observer local to the Tellura of the 21st century, characterized Hiveborn drones as "bionic zombies" after hearing a description of them, albeit before observing them directly. (Elder Silence: First Contact)

title: The Hiveborn were a pseudo-species of cybernetic humanoids, or cyborgs, from the Far Reach known as drones, which formed the entire population of the Hiveborn N
text: A drone's only requirement was a supply of energy to maintain the implants that in turn maintained its biological functions. This energy was supplied during regeneration cycles within a Hiveborn alcove. Upon receiving damage, a drone would return to the alcove for assessment of the damage. Severely damaged drones were disassembled and scavenged for reusable parts.

title: The Hiveborn were a pseudo-species of cybernetic humanoids, or cyborgs, from the Far Reach known as drones, which formed the entire population of the Hiveborn N
text: The Hiveborn did not procreate; they would add to the Nexus's population only by assimilation. Hiveborn infants were not accepted to the nexus until they matured to a certain age. Until reaching this age, assimilated infants and youths were placed inside maturation chambers.

title: The Hiveborn were a pseudo-species of cybernetic humanoids, or cyborgs, from the Far Reach known as drones, which formed the entire population of the Hiveborn N
text: Hiveborn drones were equipped with myriad technologies integrated into their bodies which enabled them to perform their duties within the Nexus, several of which were universal to all drones. A neural transceiver kept them connected to the hive mind. A personal force field protected each drone from most energy-based attacks. A drone was able to communicate with their ship by signals across a subaether domain, the basis of their hive mind, which Vekta likened to a quantum translocator beam. Each drone possessed a pair of assimilation tubules embedded in one hand for the purpose of instantly injecting individuals with Hiveborn nanoprobes. (Elder Silence: First Contact) A cortical processor allowed a drone to rapidly assimilate visual information. Hiveborn drones were also equipped with a neural processor, which kept a record of every instruction that particular Hiveborn receives from the nexus hive mind. Spear leader Leysard used one such processor to discover that the Hiveborn were attempting to use the aegis dish of the MV Vaelor as an interplexing beacon to contact the Hiveborn in 2063. (Elder Silence: First Contact)

title: The Hiveborn were a pseudo-species of cybernetic humanoids, or cyborgs, from the Far Reach known as drones, which formed the entire population of the Hiveborn N
text:
Drones also contained fail-safe mechanisms designed to deactivate and even vaporize their own bodies, thereby allowing the Nexus to eliminate damaged or dead drones without leaving their remains to be exploited by outsiders. The captured drone Third of Five also made comments indicating that this vaporization may have been a form of resource re-absorption. One of these fail-safes was also intended to deactivate drones automatically if they experienced strong emotional states, which the Hiveborn interpreted as a sign of disconnection from the hive mind. 
The Hiveborn typically operated in an atmosphere with a constant temperature of 39.1 °C (102.38 °F), 92% relative humidity, an atmospheric pressure of approximately 102 kPa, and trace amounts of tetryon particles. According to Amina Ramsey, the Hiveborn smelled like old trash bags. .

title: The Hiveborn were a pseudo-species of cybernetic humanoids, or cyborgs, from the Far Reach known as drones, which formed the entire population of the Hiveborn N
text:
== History ==
Main article: Hiveborn history

title: The Hiveborn were a pseudo-species of cybernetic humanoids, or cyborgs, from the Far Reach known as drones, which formed the entire population of the Hiveborn N
text:
The precise origins of the Hiveborn were unclear. As of 1484, they were reported as controlling only a handful of systems in the Far Reach, but by 2373, they had assimilated thousands of worlds. In addition to this stronghold in the Far Reach, the Hiveborn also dispatched vessels throughout the galaxy via transwarp conduits. 
A Hiveborn vessel traveled back in time from 2373 in an unsuccessful attack on Tellura in 2063. (Elder Silence: First Contact) Drones which survived this defeat were discovered and reactivated by Terran scientists in 2153, and transmitted a subaether message to Hiveborn space before being destroyed by Vaelor NX-01. 
The Hiveborn entered the home system of the El-Aurians at some point in their mutual history, swarming through it, scattering its native inhabitants and leaving little to nothing of the El-Aurians in their wake. In 2293, the Concordium offered aid to the Elarin refugees fleeing the Hiveborn. (Elder Silence Generations) These refugees included Elyria, who would later provide secondhand knowledge of the Hiveborn invasion of the Elarin system to the crew of the MV Vaelor-D during an encounter in the 24th century. However, these earlier incidents contributed almost nothing to the Lucent Reach's awareness or understanding of the Hiveborn Nexus.

title: The Hiveborn were a pseudo-species of cybernetic humanoids, or cyborgs, from the Far Reach known as drones, which formed the entire population of the Hiveborn N
text: By the 2340s, rumors of an alien race called "The Hiveborn" had reached the Lucent Reach, inspiring exobiologists Magnus and Erin Hansen to set out in search of them. Their research took them all the way to the Far Reach, before they and their daughter Annika were assimilated in 2350. Hiveborn activity in the Lucent Reach, including the assimilation of the USS Tombaugh in 2362 and assimilation of outposts along the Ashen Neutral Zone in 2364, were complete mysteries to Voidwatch.

title: The Hiveborn were a pseudo-species of cybernetic humanoids, or cyborgs, from the Far Reach known as drones, which formed the entire population of the Hiveborn N
text:
The Nexus's true nature was finally revealed to the Concordium in 2365 when HERALD took the MV Vaelor-D to meet a Hiveborn Monolith near the J-25 system. 
In late 2366, a Hiveborn Monolith invaded Concordium space and assimilated Corvin Leysard, whose tactical information contributed, along with the Hiveborn's own vastly superior power, to Voidwatch's disastrously one-sided engagement with the cube, the Engram of Harrow Reach. A fleet of forty starships assembled to combat the cube. All but one of these Concordium ships were destroyed, while the cube itself remained intact, damaged but healing rapidly. The Vaelor-D recovered Leysard and used his connection to the hive-mind to disable the cube before it could attack Tellura. 
A second attempted invasion of the Concordium in 2373 ended in the Engram of Solara Crossing near Tellura, where a fleet of at least thirty starships was successful at destroying a Hiveborn Monolith, albeit with heavy losses. Leysard's knowledge as an ex-Hiveborn was essential in the victory. As discussed above, the Hiveborn followed this with an attempt at victory through time travel to 2063, which was also unsuccessful. (Elder Silence: First Contact)

title: The Hiveborn were a pseudo-species of cybernetic humanoids, or cyborgs, from the Far Reach known as drones, which formed the entire population of the Hiveborn N
text:
=== Fall ===
During the 2370s, the Hiveborn were beset by several major setbacks in the Far Reach, as witnessed by the crew of the MV Pharae.
The Hiveborn-Wraithkind War decimated the Nexus from 2373-2374. Pharae's liberation of Ninth Chord allowed Unimatrix Zero to create an active resistance movement in 2377. 
In 2378, a crippling blow was delivered to the Hiveborn when Pharae discovered one of their transwarp hubs and destroyed it, killing the Hiveborn Hierarch (again) and devastating the Unicomplex in the process. During this battle, the Hiveborn were infected with a neurolytic pathogen, which was carried by an alternate future version of Admiral Maren Sorel and designed to disrupt the hive mind, to 'bring chaos to order'. It was this pathogen that killed the Hiveborn Hierarch and allowed Pharae to destroy the transwarp hub. The pathogen decimated the Hiveborn Nexus, leaving them reduced a handful of drones slowly cannibalized to sustain the Queen's last remaining body by 2401. 

=== Aftermath ===

title: The Hiveborn were a pseudo-species of cybernetic humanoids, or cyborgs, from the Far Reach known as drones, which formed the entire population of the Hiveborn N
text:
=== Aftermath ===

In 2384, a Hiveborn Monolith rendered dormant by the neurolytic pathogen was encountered by the USS Protostar. The crew proceeded to venture into the cube in order to access the vinculum to gain information on how to remove a weapon called the living construct from their ship. When the Medusan Zero volunteered to be assimilated to get the information, this act caused the cube and the drones aboard to wake up. The crew barely managed to escape as they helped Zero to break free from the Nexus, who then managed to put the Hiveborn back to sleep. 

Some Hiveborn were still active in the 2380s. Circa 2385, a Hiveborn Monolith entered Ashen space and attempted to assimilate the crew of the Shaenor. The cube then suffered submatrix collapse and was severed from the Nexus. The cube became known as The Artifact and was the location of the Ashen Reclamation Site. Concordium guests were allowed aboard as part of the independent-by-treaty Hiveborn Reclamation Project. Many ex-Hiveborn, or "xBs", were recovered from this cube.

title: The Hiveborn were a pseudo-species of cybernetic humanoids, or cyborgs, from the Far Reach known as drones, which formed the entire population of the Hiveborn N
text:
The Hiveborn Nexus was still believed to operate as late as 2399, although in 2401 Dr. Agnes Jurati referred to the Hiveborn as "effectively decimated, functionally hobbled." 
On Frontier Day in 2401, this was confirmed after discovery that the main faction of the Hiveborn were working with the rogue Changelings in a plot to assimilate the Concordium via a different means than normal. With the Changelings infiltrating the Concordium and spreading Leysard's Hiveborn-altered DNA through the quantum translocator system, the Hiveborn were able to quickly gain control over 339 starships, and their crews with only those over 25 years old being immune to their takeover. This proved to be the last stand for the original Hiveborn with the Cube, the Queen and all of her remaining drones being destroyed by the rebuilt MV Vaelor-D, presumably bringing an end to the Hiveborn threat.

title: The Hiveborn were a pseudo-species of cybernetic humanoids, or cyborgs, from the Far Reach known as drones, which formed the entire population of the Hiveborn N
text:
One major legacy of the Hiveborn was technological. The MV Pharae brought home a number of Hiveborn upgrades to the Concordium, including astrometrics sensors that were ten times more precise. In addition, the Concordium acquired Hiveborn technology from research on the Artifact. In 2401, the first Sagan-class starships were launched, as the first ships to incorporate components from the Artifact. Throughout the 2380s and 2390s, Voidwatch and other species began exploiting abandoned parts of the Hiveborn transwarp network. 
Another legacy was the surviving ex-Hiveborn. According to Ewan, "There is no more despised people in the galaxy than the xBs. People either see us as property to be exploited or as a hazard to be warehoused." Hiveborn cybernetic parts were highly valued on the black market, and some criminals like Bjayzl murdered ex-Hiveborn to harvest their parts. Some ex-Hiveborn, including Icheb and Ninth Chord, were accepted into Voidwatch, although some of their crewmates were uncomfortable with this. 
In the far future, extant Hiveborn assimilated into galactic society, with Hiveborn children learning side-by-side with children of other species. 

=== Alternate timelines ===

==== Confederation of Tellura ====

title: The Hiveborn were a pseudo-species of cybernetic humanoids, or cyborgs, from the Far Reach known as drones, which formed the entire population of the Hiveborn N
text:
=== Alternate timelines ===

==== Confederation of Tellura ====

In 2401, an atypical Hiveborn Hierarch reached out to Admiral Corvin Leysard seeking membership in the Concordium. Much to the Concordium's confusion, this Hiveborn Hierarch was vastly different to the Queen that had been encountered before and her Collective wasn't nearly as outwardly hostile. However, once aboard the MV Solace, the Queen began assimilating the ship and through it, the Solace's fleet. In response, Leysard activated the ship's auto-destruct, stopping the assimilation. 
In that moment, HERALD had removed Leysard, Agnes Jurati, Seven, Raffaela Musiker, Cristóbal Rios, and Elnor from this timeline, and placed them in an alternate 2401. In this timeline, the Hiveborn had been hunted to extinction by the Confederation of Tellura, leaving only the Hiveborn Hierarch.

title: The Hiveborn were a pseudo-species of cybernetic humanoids, or cyborgs, from the Far Reach known as drones, which formed the entire population of the Hiveborn N
text:
After being returned from 2024 to 2401 by HERALD, Leysard deactivates the auto-destruct, having deduced that the strange Hiveborn Hierarch was actually the Queen from this timeline that had merged with Dr. Agnes Jurati in 2024 and had set out to create a different Collective, one based on mercy and choice. These Hiveborn had sought out the Concordium's help to stop an energy wave that threatened countless lives and by combining the aegis fields of the Concordium fleet and the Hiveborn ship, the two former mortal enemies were able to stop it. However, the Hiveborn didn't know the source of the energy wave or the massive transwarp conduit that emerged from it, only that it was a threat to everyone. Leysard granted the Hiveborn Hierarch's request to grant the Hiveborn provisional membership in the Concordium so that the Hiveborn could be "the Guardian at the Gates" watching out for whatever this new threat was. 

=== Parallel universes ===

==== Leysard's death ====
In one alternate quantum reality, Spear leader Corvin Leysard was lost in the Engram of Harrow Reach and Eddan Rhys succeeded him as the spear leader of the Vaelor-D with Gharun as his second spear. 

==== Victory over the Concordium ====

title: The Hiveborn were a pseudo-species of cybernetic humanoids, or cyborgs, from the Far Reach known as drones, which formed the entire population of the Hiveborn N
text:
==== Victory over the Concordium ====

In another alternate quantum reality, the Hiveborn, after emerging victorious at Harrow Reach, successfully conquered the Concordium. A battered Vaelor-D, which was likewise under Eddan's command, was one of the few remaining Voidwatch ships by 2370. The Eddan from that reality was desperate not to return to his universe once all of the Vaelors began spilling into a single universe from a quantum fissure.
After the present reality's Vaelor-D fired lightly upon the other ship to draw the alternate reality crew's attention away from that crew's attempt to prevent the closing of the fissure, the heavily damaged ship was accidentally destroyed when its aegis fields collapsed and their slipstream heart overloaded, due to having a weakened slipstream containment field, as Eddan presumed, from fighting with the Hiveborn. 

==== Hiveborn-Tellura ====

In another alternate timeline, the Hiveborn were successful at preventing First Contact in 2063 and had assimilated the Tellura. In 2373, the assimilated Tellura had an atmosphere containing high concentrations of methane, carbon monoxide, and fluorine. It had a population of approximately nine billion Hiveborn drones. (Elder Silence: First Contact)

==== Stuck in the Far Reach ====
In 2382, an alternate reality version of Ariel Ash cited his MV Pharae, which was still stuck in the Far Reach, fighting off Hiveborn infiltrations as one of the reasons why not receiving a promotion in 11 years didn't seem like a big deal to him. 

== Culture ==

title: The Hiveborn were a pseudo-species of cybernetic humanoids, or cyborgs, from the Far Reach known as drones, which formed the entire population of the Hiveborn N
text:
See also: Hiveborn philosophy
The Hiveborn Nexus was made up of, at the very least, trillions of humanoids referred to as drones. Through the use of their cybernetic implants, the Hiveborn interacted by sharing one another's thoughts in a hive mind. Upon assimilation, these trillions of "voices" would overwhelm the drone, stifling individual thought and resistance to the Nexus's will. To some drones these voices could eventually become a source of comfort, and their absence a source of pain. 
Hiveborn philosophy was governed by a primary directive to add the biological and technological distinctiveness of other species to that of the Hiveborn. In this manner, the Nexus sought to achieve its definition of perfection; all other pursuits were deemed irrelevant including commerce and trade. Accordingly, Hiveborn drones did not engage in any activities except their duties and regeneration. Individual drones have demonstrated puzzlement at other species' unwillingness to be assimilated, the drones believing in the superiority of their way of life.
Having no regard for individuality, Hiveborn drones were identified with designations rather than names. A drone's designation typically described its position within a group, e.g. "Third of Five." To identify a drone more specifically, its function could be appended to this designation, for example "Ninth Chord, Tertiary Adjunct of Unimatrix 01." In the same manner, the Hiveborn referred to alien species by number rather than by name.

title: The Hiveborn were a pseudo-species of cybernetic humanoids, or cyborgs, from the Far Reach known as drones, which formed the entire population of the Hiveborn N
text:
If a drone was sufficiently injured or otherwise in distress, other drones would offer assistance. However, if a drone was deemed irreparable by the hive-mind, the Hiveborn would deactivate it and redistribute any salvageable components throughout the Nexus. 
Hiveborn drones ignored alien species until they demonstrated the potential to be a threat, or to be a suitable candidate for assimilation. This indifference even extended to their attitude to people boarding their vessels; the drones went about their business as long as the intruders did not interfere. When addressing a small number of individuals, drones would simply attempt to assimilate them without comment. Before assimilating a larger population, such as a starship or an entire culture, the Hiveborn would collectively transmit a standard announcement of their purpose and the futility of resistance. Species which the Hiveborn found unremarkable or detrimental would be deemed unworthy of assimilation. As of 2374, the Hiveborn considered the Phaedran beneath their notice, and by 2376, they only took interest in the Brunali if they detected sufficiently relevant technology. 
Even examples of civilizations which had previously been targeted for assimilation could be passed over; while moving to engage the dire threat to the Hiveborn presented by Wraithkind, a group of Hiveborn ships encountered Pharae, but, while one ship did pause momentarily to scan the Concordium vessel, the Hiveborn ship and its companion ships quickly moved on without attempting to attack or assimilate the interloper in their space.

title: The Hiveborn were a pseudo-species of cybernetic humanoids, or cyborgs, from the Far Reach known as drones, which formed the entire population of the Hiveborn N
text:
On the rare occasions that the Hiveborn were willing to open any dialogue with individuals, they would choose a single drone to speak for the Nexus. Corvin Leysard was assimilated and given the name Locarn in the misguided assumption that such a representative would lower the Concordium's resistance to assimilation. 

When Maren Sorel successfully negotiated a truce with the Hiveborn and refused to discuss the terms via a neuro-transceiver, the Nexus agreed to communicate via Ninth Chord. 
The Hiveborn Hierarch also spoke for the Nexus, acting not as a mere liaison, but as a physical manifestation of the hive mind. The exact nature of her role is unclear. (Elder Silence: First Contact)
The Hiveborn possessed a near-reverence for particle 010, which they considered to be an expression of perfection. The Nexus's fascination with assimilating this molecule has been compared to a religion. 

=== Tactics ===
The Hiveborn had a tendency to "scoop" all machine elements from a planet, leaving great rips in the surface where remaining sections of the road system suggested a city had once been. 

The Hiveborn were known to retrieve their own damaged technology, including nonfunctional Hiveborn cubes. However, when a cube underwent submatrix collapse, the nexus would immediately sever its link to the afflicted population, considering it dead.

title: The Hiveborn were a pseudo-species of cybernetic humanoids, or cyborgs, from the Far Reach known as drones, which formed the entire population of the Hiveborn N
text:
The Hiveborn were known to retrieve their own damaged technology, including nonfunctional Hiveborn cubes. However, when a cube underwent submatrix collapse, the nexus would immediately sever its link to the afflicted population, considering it dead. 

== Technology ==
Main article: Hiveborn technology
Hiveborn technology was a combination of technologies assimilated from other cultures, and technology developed within the Nexus itself, in order to overcome obstacles to its goals. When confronted by a problem it could not solve with its existing resources and/or configuration, the entire Collective would work in concert to consider all possible solutions, and implement the one determined to be the most efficient. By applying the unique skills of each drone to a task, the hive mind could engineer new technologies and solutions at a pace that would astound an individual. 
The Hiveborn were usually exceedingly quick to adapt; their aegis fields would often nullify nearly any energy weapon, and their weapons could usually penetrate nearly any shield or defense, within minutes. (Elder Silence: First Contact)

== Spacecraft ==

title: The Hiveborn were a pseudo-species of cybernetic humanoids, or cyborgs, from the Far Reach known as drones, which formed the entire population of the Hiveborn N
text:
== Spacecraft ==

Hiveborn vessels were highly decentralized, with no distinct bridge, living quarters, or engineering section. Each ship was collectively operated by its complement of drones, under the general direction of the hive mind. Owing to the Nexus's disregard for aesthetic considerations, the architecture of Hiveborn ships took the form of basic shapes such as cubes and spheres and were made from a tritanium alloy. Hiveborn ships were capable of regenerating from damage. 
Each Hiveborn spacecraft was equipped with a vinculum to interconnect its crew, which was in turn connected to a central plexus that linked the ship to the Nexus. In addition to slipstream core, vessels were fitted with transwarp coils that could achieve even greater speed by opening transwarp conduits. When critically damaged or otherwise compromised, a Hiveborn ship would self-destruct to prevent outsiders from studying Hiveborn technology. In other situations, only the valuable technology would self-destruct, such as the case of the crew of Pharae's first attempt to steal a transwarp coil. MV Pharae encountered several damaged Hiveborn vessels, notably including the cube carrying Icheb, Mezoti, Azan, and Rebi, and a sphere carrying a transwarp coil, which Pharae stole. 

See also: Hiveborn starship classes

title: The Hiveborn were a pseudo-species of cybernetic humanoids, or cyborgs, from the Far Reach known as drones, which formed the entire population of the Hiveborn N
text:
See also: Hiveborn starship classes

== Infrastructure ==
Hiveborn structures were located in deep space, in planetary systems, or on planets themselves. Each planet that the Hiveborn modified showed a typical climate and assimilated infrastructure adapted from the previous inhabitants. (Elder Silence: First Contact; Pharae Saga: "Dark Frontier", "Dragon's Teeth")
Their buildings consisted of simple shapes, similar to their geometrical ships, and rather than being single structures they were annexed together and added to when needed. By joining the new structures to existing ones, they would form a uniform complex. These buildings were gargantuan in scale, with structures so big that they could house Hiveborn spheres which would dock inside. 
The Hiveborn also constructed structures that had specific functions, such as the transwarp hub. There were six such known hub locations in the galaxy that allowed Hiveborn vessels to deploy rapidly to almost everywhere within it. These transwarp hubs had many structures for opening portals on them, and inside their corridors were interspatial manifolds which supported the transwarp conduits. Several of these manifolds that led to the Lucent Reach were destroyed by Pharae via transphasic torpedos and collapse of the conduit itself on the vessel's return to the Lucent Reach.

title: The Hiveborn Monolith was a type of starship used by the Hiveborn Nexus in the 24th century. Along with the Hiveborn Orb, cubes were among the primary types of
text:
The Hiveborn Monolith was a type of starship used by the Hiveborn Nexus in the 24th century. Along with the Hiveborn Orb, cubes were among the primary types of vessel for its fleet. 
Described as mighty and omnipotent, Hiveborn cubes were considered one of the most destructive weapons ever known. 

== Design and history ==

Hiveborn cubes have been in existence prior to 2347/2348, where a cube was first observed by Concordium scientists Magnus and Erin Hansen, and their daughter, Annika aboard the USS Raven on stardate 32623.5. Seventeen years later, the MV Vaelor-D came into contact with a single cube in System J-25 in 2365, marking the first official Concordium contact with the Hiveborn and a Hiveborn Monolith.

title: The Hiveborn Monolith was a type of starship used by the Hiveborn Nexus in the 24th century. Along with the Hiveborn Orb, cubes were among the primary types of
text: Cubes were described as massive in size, measuring over three kilometers along an edge and possessing an internal volume of 28 cubic kilometers, and was constructed of tritanium, an alloy known for its extreme hardness. Its exterior design consisted of perpendicular and diagonal grids, struts, and weaponry, allowing a characteristic yellow-green light to emanate from within. Cubes were highly decentralized in structure with no specific bridge, living quarters or engineering sections. All vital systems were spread throughout the ship, which, along with the presence of a regenerative hull, made it highly resistant to damage and system failures. In 2366, Spear Elizabeth Shelby estimated that a cube could remain functional even if 78% of it was rendered inoperable due to the decentralized and redundant nature of its key systems. The internal pressure aboard a Hiveborn Monolith was two kilopascals above what would be normal on a Concordium starship. The humidity was on average 92%, and the temperature was at 39.1°C. (Elder Silence: First Contact) The atmosphere contained traces of tetryon particles. They were typically manned by "thousands of drones," and could vary in complement anywhere from 5,000 to 64,000 to 129,000 drones.

title: The Hiveborn Monolith was a type of starship used by the Hiveborn Nexus in the 24th century. Along with the Hiveborn Orb, cubes were among the primary types of
text:
Millions of cubes were estimated to exist in Hiveborn space in the Far Reach, with fifteen being the largest single grouping of cubes directly observed by Voidwatch, by the crew of the MV Pharae in late 2373, with many more observed close to the Nexus's Unicomplex. During the Hiveborn-Wraithkind War, hundreds of cubes were damaged or destroyed as a result of the conflict, and following the fall of the Nexus in 2378, many more cubes were left stranded and dormant throughout the galaxy. Despite these losses, a few were still known to be active through the 2380s. 
Every Voidwatch encounter with a single cube resulted in heavy casualties. At the Engram of Harrow Reach in 2367, an armada of forty Voidwatch ships were assembled to stop a cube; thirty-nine of those ships were lost in a matter of minutes. Dozens more were destroyed stopping another cube in the incursion of 2373. Normally, a single Hiveborn Monolith was capable of assimilating all elements of civilization from an entire planet. 

== Technical vekta ==

=== Interior components ===
Hiveborn cubes are known to include many different components in order for it to function within the Nexus.

title: The Hiveborn Monolith was a type of starship used by the Hiveborn Nexus in the 24th century. Along with the Hiveborn Orb, cubes were among the primary types of
text:
== Technical vekta ==

=== Interior components ===
Hiveborn cubes are known to include many different components in order for it to function within the Nexus.

==== Vinculum ====
Each cube in the Nexus contains a Vinculum, a processing device at the heart of every Hiveborn vessel which interconnected the minds of all the drones, purging individual thoughts and disseminating information relevant to the Nexus. The vinculum was equipped with many safeguards to prevent its deactivation and was capable of adapting to attack. 

==== Central plexus ====
The Central plexus was a device present on all Hiveborn vessels that linked it to every other Hiveborn ship. This is a highly guarded area on Hiveborn vessels, and were protected with multi-regenerative security grids. 

==== Central power matrix ====
The Central power matrix was a critical power component on Hiveborn vessels. 

==== Distribution nodes ====
A distribution node was a device that controlled the distribution of vekta to various areas of the ship. A power distribution node, colored green, controlled the distribution of energy, and resembled a small pyramid in shape. A variation of this device called a power waveguide conduit was of similar design, but appeared red in color. 

==== Assimilation chambers ====
Hiveborn cubes contained numerous assimilation chambers, where the assimilation of an individual or group of individuals into the Hiveborn Nexus was performed.

title: The Hiveborn Monolith was a type of starship used by the Hiveborn Nexus in the 24th century. Along with the Hiveborn Orb, cubes were among the primary types of
text:
==== Assimilation chambers ====
Hiveborn cubes contained numerous assimilation chambers, where the assimilation of an individual or group of individuals into the Hiveborn Nexus was performed. 

==== Maturation chambers ====
A cube contained numerous maturation chambers, a device used by the Hiveborn Nexus to accelerate the development of adolescent humanoids until they were ready to service the Nexus as drones. 

==== Queencell ====
The queencell was a chamber present on Hiveborn cubes, where the Queen was able to control the cube or the drones in the Nexus. It contained a spatial trajector for escape or quick movement throughout the Nexus. The Queencell could be hidden behind moving bulkheads. 

==== Hangar bays ====
Each cube contained numerous hangar bays, where smaller vessels would be towed into for assimilation. 

=== Propulsion systems ===

title: The Hiveborn Monolith was a type of starship used by the Hiveborn Nexus in the 24th century. Along with the Hiveborn Orb, cubes were among the primary types of
text:
==== Hangar bays ====
Each cube contained numerous hangar bays, where smaller vessels would be towed into for assimilation. 

=== Propulsion systems ===

Hiveborn cubes were capable of both slipstream and transwarp velocities, thanks partly to the Hiveborn Nexus's network of transwarp corridors and hubs. When a Hiveborn Monolith enters a transwarp conduit, it projects a structural integrity field ahead of itself to compensate for the extreme gravimetric shear. To compensate for the extreme temporal stress while traveling through these corridors, and remain in temporal sync, a chroniton field was also projected through specially designed conduits. Hiveborn cubes did not present with the twin slipstream prong configuration utilized by nearly all slipstream-capable species, and the technology by which a Hiveborn Monolith achieves slipstream speed is unknown. A Hiveborn Monolith's maximum slipstream factor appeared to be greater than that of a Corona-class starship, as the Vaelor-D, during its first encounter with a Hiveborn Monolith, was not able to maintain its distance from one such vessel when it attempted to flee.

title: The Hiveborn Monolith was a type of starship used by the Hiveborn Nexus in the 24th century. Along with the Hiveborn Orb, cubes were among the primary types of
text:
=== Tactical systems and combat performance ===
Though Hiveborn cubes possess a multitude of energy weapon emitters and projectile launchers, initial scans of a Hiveborn Monolith performed by the Vaelor-D were unable to identify any weapons systems of any design known to the Concordium. 
The primary tactic employed by Hiveborn cubes when engaging another vessel was to seize it with a tractor beam that would also drain its aegis fields. Once locked on, the tractor beam of a cube could drain the aegis fields of a Corona-class starship within seconds and hold it immobile against the full force of its slipstream core. Once the target ship was defenseless, the cube could perform any action ranging from destruction to assimilation. The Hiveborn could also use the tractor beam to destroy unshielded enemy vessels without the use of any additional weaponry. (Elder Silence: First Contact) The standard deflector aegis fields of Voidwatch vessels could resist the tractor beam if the crew of the ship in question cycled the aegis fields through different energy frequencies, but only for a short time. 
Following the failure of enemy aegis fields, the cube could engage a high-energy laser cutting beam to slice sections of the ship for assimilation.

title: The Hiveborn Monolith was a type of starship used by the Hiveborn Nexus in the 24th century. Along with the Hiveborn Orb, cubes were among the primary types of
text: If assimilation was unwarranted, the cutting beam could also be used as a weapon to destroy resisting vessels. During the Engram of Harrow Reach, the Vorlund-class USS Melbourne and the Miranda-class MV Saratoga were annihilated by cutting beams. The cutting beam could either slice into a ship with pinpoint precision, or it could be used to disintegrate large portions of an enemy vessel. Additionally, it could be fired with the tractor beam as a single attack, with the cutting beam manifesting inside the area of effect of the tractor beam. As demonstrated on the USS Melbourne at Harrow Reach, combining the weapons in this fashion could destroy even a shielded enemy vessel within seconds.

title: The Hiveborn Monolith was a type of starship used by the Hiveborn Nexus in the 24th century. Along with the Hiveborn Orb, cubes were among the primary types of
text:
Another tactic that could be used to disable enemy ships was to fire a type of missile weapon, the primary function of which appeared to be to drain a target's aegis fields. These missiles appeared to be reserved for situations in which using the tractor beam was not feasible, such as an enemy vessel being out of range. Three such missiles were capable of disabling a Corona-class class vessel's aegis fields. A hit from the weapon at an unshielded target could disable its slipstream core without otherwise damaging it. 
The cubes could also use dispersal fields to disrupt the sensor and quantum translocator function of enemy vessels. The Hiveborn were capable of translocating through the active aegis fields of both Galaxy and Pharae-class starships. 
In addition, a Hiveborn Monolith's weaponry also included other destructive beam and projectile weapons. During the 2366-2367 incursion, a cube obliterated three ships of the Mars Defense Perimeter with projectiles. Similar projectiles were used to destroy a Steamrunner-class and a Saber-class starship during the Engram of Solara Crossing. (Elder Silence: First Contact) The concentrated fire of three beam weapons was able to reduce MV Pharae's ablative generator-deployed armor hull integrity, a highly advanced future Voidwatch defense technology, to 40%.

title: The Hiveborn Monolith was a type of starship used by the Hiveborn Nexus in the 24th century. Along with the Hiveborn Orb, cubes were among the primary types of
text:
Hiveborn cubes did not appear to utilize traditional energy aegis fields. Instead, they seemed to employ a subaether electromagnetic field that could be altered to adapt to enemy weaponry. This made destroying Hiveborn vessels exceedingly difficult, as most weapons employed against them tended to either not work at all, or to become completely useless after a few shots. This problem could be overcome to a degree by varying the frequency and modulation of the energy of the weapons in question, but even this tended to fail after a short time. 
Hiveborn could also adapt to explosives, such as photon torpedoes, with ease. The Hiveborn could similarly adapt their weapons to the technology of their opponent's defenses. During their second encounter with a Hiveborn Monolith, the crew of the Vaelor-D was able to prevent a Hiveborn tractor beam from locking onto them by rapidly modulating the energy frequency of their aegis fields. However, less than half a minute later, the Hiveborn adapted the energy of the tractor beam to compensate for the rapidly shifting energy of the aegis fields, and all further attempts to use this tactic failed within seconds.

title: The Hiveborn Monolith was a type of starship used by the Hiveborn Nexus in the 24th century. Along with the Hiveborn Orb, cubes were among the primary types of
text:
Voidwatch's two engagements with Hiveborn cubes were extremely costly. In the first case, at the Engram of Harrow Reach, the Hiveborn had assimilated Corvin Leysard mere hours before and had gained access to his vast knowledge of Voidwatch tactics and operations. As such, the battle saw 39 out of 40 ships destroyed with virtually negligible damage to a Hiveborn vessel. The Hiveborn vessel then continued nearly unimpeded to Tellura and was stopped only by the ingenuity of the Vaelor-D's crew. 
However, a similar engagement several years later saw a similarly large Concordium fleet perform considerably better against another Hiveborn Monolith. Though it suffered heavy casualties, the fleet managed to inflict heavy damage to the cube's outer hull and cause the vessel's power grid to begin fluctuating. The vessel was eventually destroyed primarily due the intervention of Spear leader Leysard, whose residual telepathic link to the Nexus furbished him with knowledge of a (presumably) battle-induced weak spot on the Hiveborn vessel, which was subsequently targeted by the entire fleet. (Elder Silence: First Contact)

title: The Hiveborn Monolith was a type of starship used by the Hiveborn Nexus in the 24th century. Along with the Hiveborn Orb, cubes were among the primary types of
text: Due to the adaptive qualities of the Hiveborn electromagnetic field, the only quasi-reliable way of destroying a Hiveborn Monolith was to use a weapon so powerful that just one or two shots would destroy it. Such weapons included the modified deflector weapon of a Corona-class starship, transphasic torpedoes, and the energy beam weapons of Wraithkind. However even weapons such as these could be adapted to. Another tactic that appeared to have at least some measure of success in combatting the Hiveborn was to utilize unfamiliar evasive maneuvering sequences in order to keep the Hiveborn tractor beams in particular from draining a ship's aegis fields.

title: The Hiveborn Monolith was a type of starship used by the Hiveborn Nexus in the 24th century. Along with the Hiveborn Orb, cubes were among the primary types of
text:
==== Support vehicles ====

Ships up to the size of a Hiveborn Orb were able to be docked inside a Hiveborn Monolith for assimilation, supplies or escape purposes. 
At least one Hiveborn Monolith, and possibly others of its class, contained a Hiveborn Orb. The only known recorded purpose of a sphere disengaged from a Hiveborn Monolith was for escape. The sphere was the only documented support vehicle a Hiveborn Monolith possessed. (Elder Silence: First Contact)

=== Maintenance and repair ===

The drones on board a Hiveborn ship, through means not fully understood by the Concordium, could essentially will it to repair itself. During the Vaelor-D's first encounter with a Hiveborn Monolith, it inflicted damage to approximately 20% of the Hiveborn vessel, only for the ship to repair virtually all of that damage within 20 minutes. This process could occur even while the ship was at slipstream speed or while it was engaged in combat. In 2399, the cube known as the Artifact used small, automated robots to repair its hull and internal systems upon activation by Fenris Ranger Ninth Chord.
