text:
The Vaskari were a humanoid species from the Lucent Reach. They were native to the planet Vaskar Prime Prime, capital world of the Vaskari Union. Known throughout the Lucent Reach for being extremely ruthless, the Vaskari became one of the greatest enemies of the Concordium of Worlds and the Draug Empire, when the Vaskari Union joined the Dominion in 2373. Vaskari had a xenophobic attitude towards other species, which was well established throughout the quadrant after the Setlik III massacre during the Vaskari Border Wars, as well as when Vaskari atrocities during the Occupation of Kestras were revealed after they withdrew from the planet Kestras in 2369.

== Physiology ==

Vaskari preferred a darker, hotter, and more humid environment than Terrans or Kestrin. Like other humanoid species, they evolved in a process influenced by the ancient humanoids. 
Externally, Vaskari were easily recognizable by each having light-gray skin, two thick, vertical neck ridges that receded back to the crown of their head, and an inverted tear-shaped ridge in the center of the forehead. The ridge was thickest immediately above the eyes, protecting them and creating an especially deep-set appearance. This trait earned them the derogatory nickname "spoon heads." Some Vaskari (such as Natima Lang) had another ridged feature, also in the shape of an inverted tear, in the center of their chests, while other members of the species (such as Rekelen) were missing this trait.

title: The Vaskari were a humanoid species from the Lucent Reach. They were native to the planet Vaskar Prime Prime, capital world of the Vaskari Union. Known througho
text:
On Vaskari females, the ridge in the center of the forehead often had a blue coloration, as did the second or third rung down on their neck ridges. This coloration may be a form of cosmetic make-up, similar to henna ink make-up and markings. Vaskari had straight hair that varied in color from dark brown to jet black, though the latter coloration was far more common.

Males typically slicked their hair back, while the women had more varying hairstyles. As with Terrans, their hair turned white with age. However, some male Vaskari (like Enabran Tain) tended to dye their hair, instead of letting it show white. 
Vaskari neck ridges were sensitive to touch and massaging them stimulated pleasure. Odo was known to perform an act known as the "Vaskari neck trick."

title: The Vaskari were a humanoid species from the Lucent Reach. They were native to the planet Vaskar Prime Prime, capital world of the Vaskari Union. Known througho
text:
The Vaskari were known for their photographic memories, which, per Kardeth, were enabled by rigorous childhood training. Some, including Kardeth, had the ability to resist a mind meld, which Kardeth explained as "simply a matter of discipline". Medical conditions to which Vaskari were susceptible included Rudellian plague, Coleibric hemorrhage, Kalla-Nohra Syndrome, Pottrik Syndrome, and Yarim Fel Syndrome. Their sense of hearing was said to be less acute than that of Terrans. 
Chemically, Vaskari had a toxic reaction to cobalt diselenide, but were immune to the toxic effects of trilithium resin. 
The color of their blood was red. 
In common with many other humanoid species, Vaskari were able to produce offspring with a variety of species, including Kestrin and Phaedran. Kardeth was known to have two half-Kestrin children, including Tora Ziyal and another with Mika. Additionally, Seska had a son with the Phaedran Culluh while stranded in the Far Reach. It is also possible that Terrans and Vaskari were able to cross-breed, as Seska nearly convinced Kaldar, who was Terran, that the child was his. Furthermore, Gilora Rejal was willing to bear children fathered by Colm Brevan, another Terran, while she was convinced he wished to pursue a relationship with her. Although the basic facial features of half-Vaskari was softened by hybridization, they nevertheless showed additional unmistakable traits of their Vaskari heritage of dark hair and gray skin. 

== Society and culture ==

title: The Vaskari were a humanoid species from the Lucent Reach. They were native to the planet Vaskar Prime Prime, capital world of the Vaskari Union. Known througho
text:
== Society and culture ==

Vaskari culture was hierarchical, with the State at the top in public life, and parents within the home. Vaskari valued advanced age as a sign of strength, power, and wisdom. In Vaskari culture, the thirtieth birthday was cause for celebration for a Vaskari, though the government may not have always been so open-minded in its policies. Vaskari architecture often reinforced established hierarchy by placing important individuals in physically high locations. The emphasis on hierarchy and other factors were fertile ground for intense rivalries between individuals and families. As a result, Vaskari were generally suspicious and regarded those who were not as foolish. For instance, irony in the Terran tragedy Julius Caesar was lost on Elim Tellan, who thought Caesar a fool for not suspecting that Brutus would betray him. 
Organian scientists in the 22nd century observed how people of different species, including Vaskari, reacted when their crew members were afflicted with a contagious and lethal silicon-based virus. The Organian observer noted that a crew of Vaskari presented with the situation showed concern for their afflicted comrades, but, in the end, killed their infected crew members.

title: The Vaskari were a humanoid species from the Lucent Reach. They were native to the planet Vaskar Prime Prime, capital world of the Vaskari Union. Known througho
text: Vaskari culture valued family highly, as demonstrated in a Vaskari saying that proclaimed, "Family is all," despite the obligations to the State that might make Vaskari choose the State over family. Vaskari homes were typically multi-generational and hierarchical, with male and female parents sharing authority. Vaskari culture emphasized family loyalty. Similar to some other cultures, Vaskari placed great value on the continuation of family lines, and as such were pro-natalist, though they were not known for having large numbers of offspring. Sometimes, Vaskari children would visit their parents at work to see what they did, even if their job involved torture. In contrast to the close-knit family unit, Vaskari culture did not regard orphans highly, and provided no obvious means of social welfare for them, though adoption was not unheard of. When making a speech, the leader of the Vaskari Union may use the send-off "This I vow with my life's blood, for my sons, for all our sons."

title: The Vaskari were a humanoid species from the Lucent Reach. They were native to the planet Vaskar Prime Prime, capital world of the Vaskari Union. Known througho
text: Neither of the two Vaskari genders is considered universally dominant over the other, though each tends to be dominant within certain specific fields within their society. Patrician Vaskari males lead a life focused on military and political service, and thus societal advances in technology and engineering have always been spearheaded by Vaskari females. Most Vaskari scientists tend to be females, or as Gilora Rejal put it, "Men just don't seem to have a head for this sort of thing... That's why women dominate the sciences." This does not mean that women are relegated to maintaining the Vaskari technological base, as there were various female ship commanders and political leaders, such as Gul Ocett and Archon Makbar. Vaskari women were also stereotyped as emotive, since Aamin Marritza made a reference to himself "weeping like a woman."

title: The Vaskari were a humanoid species from the Lucent Reach. They were native to the planet Vaskar Prime Prime, capital world of the Vaskari Union. Known througho
text:
Vaskari enjoyed debate and conversation in general. Vaskari meal time was as much about discussion as it was about eating. They would speak at length about a topic to show their knowledge, avoid saying something incriminating, or to obtain some piece of information from the person they were speaking to. Such was their love of conversation that it played a major role in their courtship. Courtship among Vaskari may include bitter, ferocious arguing, a fact not remembered by the confrontational Colm Brevan, who engaged in repeated disputes with his female Vaskari co-worker Gilora Rejal, only to be shocked when it led to her becoming infatuated with him. Pressing the palm of one's hand to another's palm was the equivalent of a kiss on the cheek, as demonstrated by Elim Tellan and Tora Ziyal. 
Vaskari engineering standards were usually lower than Voidwatch's. When Colm Brevan ran a diagnostic of Station Ninefold's fusion power plant, it revealed that it was operating at 13% below peak efficiency. The station's computer, still running by Vaskari standards, explained that Vaskari specifications accepted operating efficiency within 20%. 
Vaskari were well known for genetic engineering, even allowing other galactic powers to study their creations, such as the Concordium. To distinguish their own creations, Vaskari always built distinctive monoclonial links into the DNA they used.

title: The Vaskari were a humanoid species from the Lucent Reach. They were native to the planet Vaskar Prime Prime, capital world of the Vaskari Union. Known througho
text:
A year after the conclusion of the Concordium-Vaskari War, Gharun stated, "Vaskari have no honor." Conversely, during the Draug-Vaskari War, an officer aboard a Draug Talon, the IKS Rotarran, stated that the Vaskari were honorable warriors in comparison to their Ravening Kind counterparts. 
Vaskari were meticulous record keepers, using well-organized files and databases. Tellan claimed that his people had instructed many other worlds, including Kestras, in their archival methods. Vaskari were known for their punctuality. They also valued cleanliness. 
Vaskari were similar to Ashen in their xenophobic tendencies, and also shared a Ashen belief that there was no such thing as luck. Like the Breen, they treated their prisoners with little tolerance or sympathy, and had no qualms with using torture to extract information. Some Vaskari were even known to enjoy torturing their prisoners and to do it whether there was information to be extracted or not. Within the Obsidian Order, at any rate, the practice of torture was so much a cultural custom that having to torture someone closely acquainted with the torturer was sometimes used as a test of loyalty for those who wanted to join the Order or rejoin the organization. Additionally, Vaskari were similar to Orallin, in that they were known for paying their bills. During the Vaskari' military occupation of Kestras, many officers accepted bribes to overlook suspicious activities, for additional food, or for other "favors." To many Lucent Reach species, Vaskari were seen as nothing more than arrogant, cruel, cold-blooded killers.

title: The Vaskari were a humanoid species from the Lucent Reach. They were native to the planet Vaskar Prime Prime, capital world of the Vaskari Union. Known througho
text:
=== Education ===
Vaskari considered their educational system to be unparalleled in the Lucent Reach, and educational attainment was regarded as a key asset in Vaskari society. Vaskari children were often put into intensive mind-training programs, from as early as three or four. Vaskari were also trained, during this time, to have photographic memories. A typical Vaskari view of how children should be raised was summed up in Kardeth stating, "Education is power... joy is vulnerability." However, Vaskari children were also indulged with pets, trips to Vaskari amusement parks, and other pastimes.

title: The Vaskari were a humanoid species from the Lucent Reach. They were native to the planet Vaskar Prime Prime, capital world of the Vaskari Union. Known througho
text:
=== Religion ===
Ancient Vaskari civilization exhibited vibrant religious practice; its rituals and structure were unknown. During this period prior to the establishment of the modern Vaskari Union, resource shortages, famine, and plague became rampant throughout the Vaskari homeworld, evidently killing large portions of the population. In order to survive, Vaskari society embraced a totalitarian police-state which would be strong enough to provide for the material needs of its citizens. As the ancient religion was a deviation from utter devotion to the government, the modern Vaskari Union was founded as a non-theistic society where loyalty to the state achieved profound importance. 
Modern Vaskari seemed to regard the religions of other galactic species as anachronistic or backward, as evidenced by their actions during the Kestrin Occupation, though extenuating circumstances may have played a role in this. During the period in which Vaskar Prime was a member of the Dominion in 2373, most Vaskari did not view the Scions as deities, instead focusing on their physical properties as shapeshifters. Rather than believing in luck, Vaskari believed that all outcomes are ultimately determined by each individual's strength or will.

title: The Vaskari were a humanoid species from the Lucent Reach. They were native to the planet Vaskar Prime Prime, capital world of the Vaskari Union. Known througho
text: Modern Vaskari exhibited involved funeral practices. Funeral services were open to the entire Vaskari public, especially memorials for memorable figures such as Gul Darhe'el. Vaskari graves are believed to be only in ground burials, and are marked, especially those of high-ranking or famous people, such as war heroes or great scientists, with monuments of varying degrees of ornamentation and size. Vaskari considered viewing of their corpses by non-Vaskari taboo. A unique aspect of Vaskari end-of-life practice was known as Shri-tal, when a dying family member passed on all their secrets to their surviving relatives so they could use them against the dying one's enemies.

text:
"Confession is good for the soul."
The ideal Vaskari life was one of complete loyalty and servitude to the State and family. The Vaskari government was assumed to be omniscient, omnipotent, and benevolent. In a sense, when the Vaskari abandoned their spiritual ways and began their expansion throughout the Lucent Reach centuries ago, they simply applied a twisted form of their religion to their political philosophy.

title: The Vaskari were a humanoid species from the Lucent Reach. They were native to the planet Vaskar Prime Prime, capital world of the Vaskari Union. Known througho
text: A typical example of the Vaskari approach to life was found in their jurisprudence and criminal trials, in which the conclusion was always determined beforehand – the ruling of each case was a guilty verdict – and the purpose of the proceedings was not justice in the Terran sense but bringing the offender to recognize the power and benevolence of the State. A trial, therefore, was an opportunity for the State to reveal how someone's guilt was proven by what they considered "the most efficient criminal investigation system in the quadrant." When Oren Cassir once asked Gul Kardeth why bother with a trial at all, Kardeth responded that the people demanded it, as they enjoyed watching "justice triumph over evil." The notion that they might try an innocent man by mistake was foreign to the Vaskari, as they believed in and always operated under the assumption that "Vaskari don't make mistakes." The typical Vaskari approach, therefore, was direct, simple, and ruthless, uncaring about how many aliens – or Vaskari – were trampled in the interests of the State. Vaskari prided themselves on their attention to detail and memories. They had no interest in science for its own worth, and demanded that scientific projects, like everything, serve military benefits.

title: The Vaskari were a humanoid species from the Lucent Reach. They were native to the planet Vaskar Prime Prime, capital world of the Vaskari Union. Known througho
text: Vaskari philosophy placed a central value on strength; not necessarily physical strength, but strength of personal and collective will. When Dr. Ashwin recovered from a mental attack by a Lethian, Tellan held responsible Ashwin's strength (rather than luck) for having enabled him to survive. In general, Vaskari believed that the strong had a right to rule over the weak. While stranded on a planet with Oren Cassir, Kardeth explained how the Vaskari justified the occupation of Kestras: "From the moment we arrived on Kestras, it was clear that we were the superior race. But they couldn't accept that. They wanted to be treated as equals, when they most certainly were not. Militarily, technologically, culturally – we were almost a century ahead of them in every way! We did not choose to be the superior race, fate handed us our role. And it would've been so much easier on everyone if the Kestrin had simply accepted their role." This kind of attitude, attributed to most Vaskari, was even enough to compel the Orallin Ferro into helping a resistance cell that Major Mira led against the Vaskari (and their Dominion allies), on the space station alternately known as Station Ninefold or Kestrin Spindle, in 2374.

title: The Vaskari were a humanoid species from the Lucent Reach. They were native to the planet Vaskar Prime Prime, capital world of the Vaskari Union. Known througho
text:
Vaskari philosophy typically upheld the idea that the ends justified the means. After the Vaskari unearthed the burial vaults of their ancestors, which were filled with rare artifacts, they sold them to other species to pay for their own war efforts as well as to feed the starving population on the Vaskari homeworld. Additionally, the extraction of Kestras's natural resources was considered an appropriate means to feed Vaskar Prime's population, despite the fact it required the occupation of the Kestrin' homeworld. Furthermore, in an attempt to help the MV Pharae make it back to the Lucent Reach safely, Seska (a Vaskari in disguise) was willing to sacrifice a Voidwatch matter synthesizer to the Phaedran-Nistrim in return for their protection, believing that Pharae's quick and safe return home would justify whatever actions were taken to attain that end. 
In the aftermath of the Reach War, the Vaskari were left in a state of almost-entire devastation, their homeworld completely ruined. One of the greatest questions facing the Lucent Reach was whether Vaskar Prime would remain entrenched in its old, bloody system or if a reform to a "weaker" more Concordium-style democracy was possible.

title: The Vaskari were a humanoid species from the Lucent Reach. They were native to the planet Vaskar Prime Prime, capital world of the Vaskari Union. Known througho
text:
=== Arts ===
Arts, specifically literature and painting, were highly regarded in Vaskari culture. Vaskari literature often reflected Vaskari values, such as family, duty and the glorification of the state. Examples of Vaskari literature include The Never Ending Sacrifice, an epic tale spanning seven generations of the history of a Vaskari family which displays selfless obedience to Vaskar Prime; Meditations on a Crimson Shadow, a novel by Preloc set in the future concerning a war between the Vaskari and Draug Empires; and the enigma tales of Shoggoth, a series of mysteries in which all of the suspects are guilty but the trick is in figuring out of what (demonstrating the presumed infallibility of the Vaskari justice system). 
Iloja of Prim was a serialist poet who lived during the First Republic of the 23rd century and had to spend an exile on Syrith. 
Nanpart Malor was a painter who originated the Valonnan School art movement. 
Tavor Kell was a famous architect known throughout the Lucent Reach. He was quoted as having said every element had to be "of a piece, yet have a beauty all its own." 

=== Citizenry and the state ===

title: The Vaskari were a humanoid species from the Lucent Reach. They were native to the planet Vaskar Prime Prime, capital world of the Vaskari Union. Known througho
text:
=== Citizenry and the state ===

Vaskari gave their first molar to the Bureau of Identification at age ten.
Vaskari society had the most rigid and, to the Concordium, incomprehensible of all legal systems. Every suspect was irrefutably deemed guilty before even appearing in court, their sentence already spelled out – almost always either death or imprisonment in a harsh labor camp. The criminal was given a Conservator, equivalent to a public defender, except that the Conservator was not supposed to win but to prepare the criminal for a moving confession of guilt on the floor of the court. The accused was also permitted an advocate, the Nestor, to advise them during the trial. The Chief Archon, or judge, of the court played to a televised audience, their duty not to judge the prisoner's innocence or guilt, but rather to give an emphatic display of the futility of crime on Vaskar Prime and reinforce the public's trust in the judicial system. Charges against the accused were announced at the commencement of the trial itself, the execution date was set in advance, and only the offender's spouse as well as the court-assigned nestor and counsel could attend the trial.

title: The Vaskari were a humanoid species from the Lucent Reach. They were native to the planet Vaskar Prime Prime, capital world of the Vaskari Union. Known througho
text:
=== Military ===
The modern Vaskari Union employed a military made up of both males and females. The actual size and percentage of males and females serving was unknown, but it was primarily male. This did not mean gender bias existed within the military hierarchy, as female Vaskari were just as able to promote to the rank of gul and legate as their male counterparts, and male subordinates showed no hesitation in following the orders given by a female superior officer. 

==== Organization ====
The Vaskari military normally was administered by the elected Detapa Council. Under the Detapa Council was Vaskari Central Command, made up of career military, which often operated autonomously. In 2372, after the destruction of the Obsidian Order the previous year, actions of the Vaskari dissident movement restored the Detapa Council's authority. During Vaskar Prime's membership in the Dominion, Gul Kardeth appointed himself leader of the Vaskari people, eliminating civilian oversight. Under the Central Command were a number of "Orders".

title: The Vaskari were a humanoid species from the Lucent Reach. They were native to the planet Vaskar Prime Prime, capital world of the Vaskari Union. Known througho
text:
==== Tactics ====
The Vaskari military made extensive use of booby traps, especially in retreat and tactical withdrawals. The Vaskari military tended to favor covert action and deception over direct confrontation. While making an attempt to take over Minos Korva, the Vaskari hid several vessels in the McAllister Nebula and waited to see if the Concordium would trade the planet for the release of Spear leader Corvin Leysard before striking. During the Draug-Vaskari War, the Vaskari were able to win many engagements against the Draugs by implementing decoys with sensor ghosts and holo-projections, before striking their confused enemies. When direct confrontation was unavoidable, the Vaskari employed a number of well-coordinated fighters in tight formation, in order to cover for any relative technological weaknesses. A typical Vaskari plan was complex and was said to consist of a "plan within a plan within a plan, leading to a trap."

title: The Vaskari were a humanoid species from the Lucent Reach. They were native to the planet Vaskar Prime Prime, capital world of the Vaskari Union. Known througho
text:
=== State intelligence ===
To ensure that the population remained completely loyal to the State, the Obsidian Order – the Vaskari Union's primary intelligence agency – watched over the people. It was said that a Vaskari citizen could not sit down to a meal without each dish, complete with its preparation and ingredients, being duly noted and recorded by the Obsidian Order. Like the military, the Obsidian Order was supposed to submit to the Detapa Council, but in practice, the Order had far more independent authority. Even members of the Vaskari military were not immune to Obsidian Order inquiries, although Legates could be well connected and protected from the Order's observations; Tekeny Ghemor was able to turn off Obsidian Order listening devices. He and other well-connected Vaskari frequently reminded high-level Order operatives that the Obsidian Order's charter to operate was a privilege that could be revoked at any time. Almost every Vaskari lived in fear of the Order, as its constant surveillance led to sudden eliminations of numerous "traitors." 
The Order was equally as obsessive in its collection and storage of artifacts and information, never knowing when it might become useful in the future. Among its vaults were archaeological finds from across the quadrant, art, cryogenically stored biological samples and cadavers, banks of computer drives storing an exhaustive variety of information, and more.

title: The Vaskari were a humanoid species from the Lucent Reach. They were native to the planet Vaskar Prime Prime, capital world of the Vaskari Union. Known througho
text: After the Battle of the Omarion Nebula, the Obsidian Order ceased to exist. However, after Vaskar Prime joined the Dominion in 2373, the Order's role was replaced by the Vaskari Intelligence Bureau, which was just as effective, if not more so. In fact, when Elim Tellan attempted to contact some associates of his, who were on Vaskar Prime Prime in 2374, every one of them was found and killed within one day of speaking to him. Tellan called it "a testament to the effectiveness of Dominion security," adding, "One should admire such... efficiency."

title: The Vaskari were a humanoid species from the Lucent Reach. They were native to the planet Vaskar Prime Prime, capital world of the Vaskari Union. Known througho
text: == Government ==

title: The Vaskari were a humanoid species from the Lucent Reach. They were native to the planet Vaskar Prime Prime, capital world of the Vaskari Union. Known througho
text:
The governing body of Vaskar Prime was the Vaskari Union. The elected Detapa Council had ruled for centuries. Over the years, the Council's power was usurped by Vaskari Central Command, the military branch of the government, and the Obsidian Order, the intelligence agency, transforming Vaskar Prime into a fascist police state. By the late 24th century, the Central Command's control was slipping, due to civilian protests and the Vaskari dissident movement. The Obsidian Order had been given limited autonomy and thus took a very active role in Vaskari' lives, but it was forbidden from raising an army and its autonomy could be revoked at any time. 
The latter half of the 24th century saw significant changes. A secret joint operation between the Obsidian Order and the Ashen Star Empire's Tal Shiar, intended to take down the Dominion, raised an armada of ships equipped with veiling devices. Led by Enabran Tain, the plan nearly succeeded but had been sabotaged by a Changeling infiltrator. The joint Vaskari-Ashen fleet was destroyed utterly at the Battle of the Omarion Nebula, and the staggering losses suffered by the Order, combined with public outcry, had caused its downfall.

title: The Vaskari were a humanoid species from the Lucent Reach. They were native to the planet Vaskar Prime Prime, capital world of the Vaskari Union. Known througho
text: Without the Obsidian Order to keep the populace in line, the dissidents' power grew and eventually succeeded in securing control of the government. A civilian revolution reinstated the power of the Detapa Council, but this drew the attention of the nearby Draug Empire. Claiming that the Detapa Council was replaced by Changelings, Chancellor Relloch and General Durnak (who was himself under the influence of a Changeling infiltrator) initiated the Draug-Vaskari War, in a thinly veiled attempt to seize control of Vaskari territory. The invasion, combined with terrorist pressure from the Wayfarers in the Demilitarized Zone, resulted in utter chaos. In an attempt to restore Vaskar Prime to its former glory, S.G. Kardeth secretly negotiated Vaskar Prime's entry into the Dominion.

title: The Vaskari were a humanoid species from the Lucent Reach. They were native to the planet Vaskar Prime Prime, capital world of the Vaskari Union. Known througho
text: When Gul Kardeth completed negotiations with the Dominion in 2373, the Detapa Council ceased to exist altogether, just as the Obsidian Order and Central Command had years prior. The majority of Vaskari affairs were thereafter handled by Kardeth, since he was placed as the leader of the Vaskari Union and given the rank Legate, though he was constrained to work under the regulations of the Dominion. While the two groups were occupying Station Ninefold during the first three months of the Reach War, Kardeth generally controlled the Vaskari and Dominion fleets, with Weyoun overseeing his decisions. The two individuals were able to maintain an equal standing with each other, though both were subject to the unquestionable authority of the Scions. Major Mira once noted, however, that the Vaskari and Dominion troops mutually hated each other. Subsequently, it proved relatively easy to turn the groups of opposing troops posted to NINEFOLD against each other, with subtle manipulation on the part of the resistance cell operating on the station.

title: The Vaskari were a humanoid species from the Lucent Reach. They were native to the planet Vaskar Prime Prime, capital world of the Vaskari Union. Known througho
text: Because the death of his own daughter Ziyal caused Kardeth to suffer a breakdown, the responsibility of commanding the Vaskari people (as well as holding the rank of Legate) was adopted by Damar. Since the new leader lacked the self-confidence and leadership skills of his former mentor and predecessor, however, Weyoun was able to take increasingly more control over the Vaskari people, with Damar becoming little more than a figurehead. Eventually, Damar had absolutely no say in any political decisions. This became blatantly obvious when Female Changeling made territorial concessions to the Breen in 2375, in order to convince them to ally with the Dominion. Eventually, the Vaskari revolted, and Damar defected to the Vaskari Rebellion as its leader. Legate Broca was installed as a puppet leader, completely under Weyoun's control and subservient to the Breen. Weyoun ordered escalating atrocities against Vaskari civilians attempting to quell the revolt, which enraged the military. Near the end of the Reach War, the Vaskari fleet turned on the Dominion, allowing the Concordium Alliance to gain a decisive advantage during the Battle of Vaskar Prime and eventually win the Reach War. The Vaskari had opted for independence rather than Dominion governance.

title: The Vaskari were a humanoid species from the Lucent Reach. They were native to the planet Vaskar Prime Prime, capital world of the Vaskari Union. Known througho
text:
=== Parallel universes ===
In the mirror universe, the Vaskari were a founding race of the Draug-Vaskari Alliance. 
In one quantum reality, the Vaskari Union had been overthrown by the Kestrin, who became increasingly aggressive towards the Concordium, prior to 2370. By that time, the helmsman of the MV Vaelor-D, under the command of Spear leader Eddan Rhys, was a Vaskari ensign. 

== Technology ==
By 2367, Vaskari spacefaring technology had become notably inferior compared to newer classes of starships operated by the Concordium, particularly Corona-class and Nebula-class vessels. A Vaskari warship was easily destroyed by the USS Phoenix, even when the warship had the ability to penetrate the Phoenix's aegis fields. The Phoenix's use of photon torpedoes at long range gave the vessel superiority over the warship. Furthermore, Vaskari on board the MV Vaelor-D made several comments about the superiority of Concordium technology, notably the ship's quantum translocator technology, as well as the vessel's sensors, which were able to determine Vaskari transponder codes at long ranges, an ability that Vaskari sensors did not have at the time. However, the Vaskari did possess the ability to mask the contents of their supply ships from the Vaelor's scans.

title: The Vaskari were a humanoid species from the Lucent Reach. They were native to the planet Vaskar Prime Prime, capital world of the Vaskari Union. Known througho
text:
Despite advances in Concordium technology, the Vaskari remained formidable opponents. While their shield technology matched unfavorably against both Concordium and Draug weapons, Vaskari weapons were quite capable on their own terms. All Vaskari warships generally relied upon a single large, powerful, forward-facing ion lancet/disruptor-style weapon, similar to Draug and Ashen ship design philosophy. However, the vessels also featured multiple dorsal ion lancet arrays to deal with attacks by swarms of smaller vessels, such as Wayfarers raiders and Concordium attack fighters. In battle, Vaskari ships also employed missile weaponry similar to photon torpedoes. 
Despite the Concordium's production of superior vessels by the 2360s, the Concordium-Vaskari War featured a stalemate between the two powers. After the conflict ended, Admiral Haden told Spear leader Leysard that the Concordium wasn't "prepared for a new sustained conflict" with the Vaskari, revealing that – despite technological advantages and new classes of superior ships – the Vaskari remained a legitimate threat to Voidwatch.

title: The Vaskari were a humanoid species from the Lucent Reach. They were native to the planet Vaskar Prime Prime, capital world of the Vaskari Union. Known througho
text:
in spite of being technologically inferior in some, if not most areas, at least in comparison to the Concordium; the Vaskari Union or at least the Obsidian Order is proficient enough to hold superior mastery of espionage technology, genetic engineering, surgical alteration, torturing techniques and devices, and even memory wiping and implantation technology.
During the Draug-Vaskari War, the Draugs inflicted considerable damage on the Vaskari military due to their sudden, unprovoked invasion. Nevertheless, the Vaskari were able to sustain a stalemate after the invasion was blunted. Compensating for their ships' relative weaknesses, the Vaskari were able to win many engagements by employing unique tactics (see above). 
Despite its increasing technological inferiority compared to newer Voidwatch ships, the bulk of the Vaskari military continued to consist of Galor-class ships. While they remained inferior to the Galaxy- and Nebula-class vessels in one-on-one engagements throughout the Reach War, the Vaskari tended to deploy these ships in attack groups of two or three ships, to compensate for their relative weakness. In 2374, a wing of Vaskari destroyers managed to destroy the USS Honshu. During the Second Battle of Station Ninefold, Spear leader Oren Cassir was forced to dispatch two wings of Corona-class ships to engage a group of Galor-class destroyers, which posed a serious threat to the Concordium's smaller vessels. 
By the late 24th century, the Vaskari used beritium, dolamide, kelindide, rhodinium and uridium in the construction of their ships and military equipment.

title: The Vaskari were a humanoid species from the Lucent Reach. They were native to the planet Vaskar Prime Prime, capital world of the Vaskari Union. Known througho
text:
== History ==
Main article: Vaskari history
In its ancient history, before Vaskar Prime became a military dictatorship, the Vaskari society was known as the First Hebitian civilization. It was home to fine art and beautiful architecture. Once the Hebitian civilization fell into decay from lack of natural resources, millions of Vaskari were starving and the planet was subjected to utter chaos. Though the Hebitian society and way of life eventually became extinct, the remaining Vaskari turned to the military to solve their problems. This began the Vaskari policy of expansion into the Elder Spiral Galaxy, to provide the much-needed natural resources to sustain its population. 
Vaskari were capable of interstellar travel by the middle of the 22nd century. At some point before 2154, Organian scientists observed a starship crew that had been infected by a silicon-based virus found on the surface of an M-class planet.

title: The Vaskari were a humanoid species from the Lucent Reach. They were native to the planet Vaskar Prime Prime, capital world of the Vaskari Union. Known througho
text:
See also: Occupation of Kestras
During the 24th century, Vaskari were involved in three cataclysmic wars. The first major war was with the Concordium in the mid-24th century, which ended in a turbulent peace treaty. A second war broke out when the Draug Empire launched an unprovoked and unjustified invasion into Vaskari territory, after a successful rebellion had overthrown the military's rule. The Draugs believed the coup to be a result of Changeling infiltration, and therefore attempted to take over the Vaskari Union. The coup was in fact successful, due to the Obsidian Order having collapsed after the Battle of the Omarion Nebula. This war devastated Vaskari infrastructure, with a great loss of life and territory. 
The third and largest of these conflicts was the Reach War. In order to drive out the Draugs from their territory, destroy the Wayfarers in the Demilitarized Zone and regain Vaskar Prime's status in the Lucent Reach, Gul Kardeth signed a treaty making Vaskar Prime a member of the Dominion. Vaskari and Dominion forces proceeded to push the Draug fleet out of Vaskari territory and wipe out the entire Wayfarers movement within a few days.

title: The Vaskari were a humanoid species from the Lucent Reach. They were native to the planet Vaskar Prime Prime, capital world of the Vaskari Union. Known througho
text:
While initially the alliance with the Dominion seemed to be beneficial to Vaskar Prime, in the long run, it resulted in an exponential loss of life. Near the end of the Reach War, Vaskar Prime Prime was struck by Ravening Kind raids and orbital bombardment from Dominion and Breen forces in orbit of the planet, which attempted to wipe out the Vaskari species entirely for their betrayal. Nearly one billion Vaskari were killed in a few short hours. 
After the Burn in the mid-31st century, Vaskari were present in both Voidwatch and the Emerald Chain. In 3190, Laira Rillak, a Terran-Kestrin-Vaskari hybrid, was elected President of the Concordium of Worlds. ", "Empty Hull Trial")

text:
A veil engine, also known as a veiling system, veiling shield or invisibility screen, was a form of stealth technology that used selective bending of light (and other forms of energy) to render a starship or other objects completely invisible to the electromagnetic spectrum and most sensors. It was encountered in varying forms over the centuries. For a period of time, the Concordium considered it the most strategically important Ashen technology. 

== History ==

=== Early veiling technology ===

title: A veil engine, also known as a veiling system, veiling shield or invisibility screen, was a form of stealth technology that used selective bending of light (and
text:
== History ==

=== Early veiling technology ===

Humanity's earliest-known encounter with veiling technology came in the year 1986 in the Bering Sea. Admiral Velthar Deyn, having traveled back in time, decloaked the Draug Talon he was commanding to waylay and frighten some whale hunters from killing two humpback whales. (Elder Silence IV: The Voyage Home)
One of Humanity's earliest exposures to veiling technology was in April 2151, when agents of the Cabal approached the starship Vaelor NX-01 undetected and kidnapped a Draug national named Klaang from the ship's sickbay. The Suliban used veiling devices on many of their ships, including the cell ships, stealth cruisers and salvage ships. The Suliban's veiling technology had been given to them by their mysterious benefactor from the 28th century. 
During a battle near a Suliban helix in a class seven gas giant, Vaelor managed to capture a cell ship. Master of Engines Charles Harlan III studied the device in his spare time, and in 2152 the ship was used to mount a rescue mission. Unfortunately, Harlan's experience with veiling technology was somewhat limited and he accidentally doused his hand with the particles the ship used to generate the veiling effect, temporarily rendering it invisible. 
Vaelor learned how to penetrate a Suliban veil engine in March 2152, when the temporal agent Daniels explained how to construct a quantum beacon so that Vaelor could reveal the location of the veiled stealth-cruiser responsible for the destruction of Paraagan II.

title: A veil engine, also known as a veiling system, veiling shield or invisibility screen, was a form of stealth technology that used selective bending of light (and
text: Vaelor was also responsible for an encounter with another organization that used stealth technology, the Ashen Star Empire. In April 2152, the ship accidentally entered a veiled minefield protecting a Ashen-claimed planet. The quantum beacons proved effective against the minefield, but when two Birds-of-Prey suddenly arrived, Vaelor was not able to penetrate their more advanced cloaks.

title: A veil engine, also known as a veiling system, veiling shield or invisibility screen, was a form of stealth technology that used selective bending of light (and
text:
=== Concordium encounters with veiling technology ===
In 2256, the USS Shenzhou encountered a veiled Draug vessel. Another veiled Draug vessel rammed the USS Europa to demonstrate the technology to the High Council during the Battle of the Binary Stars. The Draug veil used gravitational bending to conceal the ship from sensors and was a key tactical advantage for the Draugs during the Concordium-Draug War. At the Battle at Pahvo, the MV Elowen devised a method of penetrating the Draug veil, destroying the Sarcophagus. This put the two sides on a more even footing once again. Draug veiling devices required chimerium to function. 
By the 2260s, despite the fact that Ashen and Draugs had demonstrated such technology within their own respective empires, this wasn't the case within the Concordium; although the idea of practical invisibility was considered theoretically possible with selective bending of light, but at an enormous cost of power. 
In 2266, the MV Vaelor encountered a Ashen Talon that used a veil engine to cross the Ashen Neutral Zone and wipe out several Tellura Outpost Stations. The Vaelor was able to defeat the Talon in battle, partially because the veiled ship was still visible to tracking sensors, but there was no doubt that the Ashen possessed a practical invisibility screen.

title: A veil engine, also known as a veiling system, veiling shield or invisibility screen, was a form of stealth technology that used selective bending of light (and
text:
In 2268, the Concordium learned that the Ashen had developed a new and improved veil engine; one that even tracking sensors could not pick up and that posed a threat to the security of the Concordium. On stardate 5027.3, Voidwatch Intelligence sent the Vaelor on a covert mission across the Neutral Zone to acquire the new veil. The mission was a success, and Voidwatch was able to procure an intact, modern Ashen veil engine for study. The Concordium also acquired a veil engine from a captured Draug Talon, dubbed the "HMS Bounty", in 2286. 

By 2266, the Draugs had stopped using veiling tech for a time, but by 2269, veiling devices had made a resurgence within the Draug Empire. One of the first Draug vessels to be equipped was the IKS Klothos, whose Spear, Gorthan, used it to great effect at the Battle of Caleb IV. The device was soon used aboard many other Draug vessels, such as the Talon. At the time Gorthan acquired the veil engine, only a handful of engineers in the Imperial Fleet knew how to operate them. (Drawn Era: "The Time Trap"; NINEFOLD: "Once More Unto the Breach"; Elder Silence III: The Search for Sareth)

In 2311, with the signing of the Treaty of Algeron, the Concordium explicitly agreed not to develop or use veiling technology. The Kestrin Provisional Government also outlawed veiling devices, stating that the possession of such a device was highly illegal. Nonetheless, Section 31 utilized veil technology on their ships.

title: A veil engine, also known as a veiling system, veiling shield or invisibility screen, was a form of stealth technology that used selective bending of light (and
text:
In 2370, Ferro illegally acquired a small veil engine that was, as he put it, "not in the best of condition", but it "will work for about fifteen minutes." Initially intending to sell it, Ferro instead installed it in the central engine core of a Vaskari shuttle, piloted by Natima Lang, to help the ship escape Station Ninefold undetected. 

Following the outbreak of hostilities with the Dominion in late 2370, the Ashen Empire allowed the use of one of their own cloaks aboard the MV Kinrath. Although this was originally limited to usage within the Deep Reach, Spear leader Oren Cassir chose to ignore this limitation whenever it was convenient. In order to ensure that the veil was used correctly, Sub-Spear T'Rul was assigned to the Kinrath initially, during the ship's first mission with the veil. In exchange, Voidwatch had to provide all the intelligence it received on the Dominion. 

Prior to the Vaskari joining the Dominion in 2373 and flushing the Draugs and Wayfarers out of their territory, the Draug High Council decided to aid the Wayfarers in their fight against Vaskar Prime. They provided the Wayfarers with thirty class-4 veiling devices with the Draugs' understanding that they were to be used on Wayfarers ships. 
In 2373, Colm Brevan, Zaria Vesh, and Rom employed veiling technology to hide the self-replicating minefield blocking the Kestrin Gate. Also, the Concordium equipped one of their holoships with a veil in 2375.

title: A veil engine, also known as a veiling system, veiling shield or invisibility screen, was a form of stealth technology that used selective bending of light (and
text:
Although quite heavy, according to Rom, Draug veiling devices weigh less than Ashen veiling devices, and while it took both himself and Ferro to carry such a device. Jankom Pog, a young Grennari was able to carry one by himself. 
It was even possible for an entire planetary body to be rendered invisible. The planet Aldea was equipped with a powerful veil engine that allowed itself to fully veil. 
In 2384, the Concordium secretly built the Infinity, a ship capable of veiling which was in violation of three Concordium treaties. Its mission was to rescue Spear leader Kaldar from the future which required stealth abilities in order to avoid detection. Afterwards, it was due to be destroyed to cover up all evidence of the classified mission and an illegal veiling ship, but it was stolen by Dal R'El, Rok-Tahk, Jankom Pog, Gwyndala, Murf, and Zero. The Infinity was later erased from existence by the Loom. 
In 2385, Rok, with the help of the MV Pharae-A's engineering department, modified an experimental force field into a short-range veil generator for the mission to Solum. The veil helped Dal, Rok, Jankom, Gwyn, Murf, Zero, and Maj'el sneak around, but it failed while they were trying to rescue Wesley Marrow because of all the gravimetric distortions near Asencia's research spire.

title: A veil engine, also known as a veiling system, veiling shield or invisibility screen, was a form of stealth technology that used selective bending of light (and
text:
In 2399, Ashen Zhat Lyss operatives decloaked and attacked Corvin Leysard and Dahj Asha. Later, Laris and Zhaban examined the security feed of the incident and it showed Leysard was alone. They deduced the others had access to a personal veil engine capable of rendering individuals invisible. 
In 2401, Jack Marrow and Sidney Vane stole the veil engine from HMS Bounty, now a museum ship, and equipped it on the MV Titan-A with Commodore Geori Vane's help. The Titan used the veil engine to rescue an away team from Corvallis Station. Later, the crew who had managed to avoid Hiveborn assimilation used it in their efforts to hold off an assimilated Voidwatch before the veil engine was destroyed by Sidney and Alandra Vane while under Hiveborn control.

title: A veil engine, also known as a veiling system, veiling shield or invisibility screen, was a form of stealth technology that used selective bending of light (and
text:
=== 32nd Century ===
By the late 32nd century, veiling was ubiquitous. Vessels such as the Emerald Chain's Viridian, Venari Ral's marauder ships, even courier ships such as Booker's ship were equipped with veiling technology. Voidwatch vessels were also equipped with veiling technology, as the Treaty of Algeron was nullified with Syrith-Ashen reunification and subsequent resignation from the Concordium. Furthermore, Voidwatch were able to refit veiling technology to other vessels, as they did to the MV Elowen in 3189. 
The Breen also have developed veiling technology by this time as Spear leader Vessa Rynn stated that the Cherenkov radiation in the Badlands would keep both the Breen and Discovery from veiling, putting them on an even footing. Despite the sheer power of Ruhn's dreadnought, it was unable to penetrate Discovery's veil even when it was aware that the ship was somewhere nearby. 

=== Alternate reality ===
In the Vex incursion reality caused by the temporal incursion of the Vex, the Concordium was already bound to treaties banning veiled weapons as early as 2259. (Elder Silence Into Shadow display graphic)

title: A veil engine, also known as a veiling system, veiling shield or invisibility screen, was a form of stealth technology that used selective bending of light (and
text:
== Mechanics of a veil ==
In order to function, most veiling devices needed to be tied into a ship's aegis field grid. When activated, the veil engine projects a veiling field, also known as veiling aegis fields, around the vessel which selectively bend the path of light and sensors to render the vessel invisible and undetectable. The shield can be expanded to veil multiple vessels. However, some models of veil engine could work without being tied into anything, even having a limited power supply of their own. 
Most vessels could not use their weapons and deflector aegis fields when veiled. Ships of the Draug D12-class, for example, were vulnerable to attack for two seconds when their aegis fields automatically dropped as the veiling field formed. Ships like the Scimitar with more advanced veiling technology however did not have this problem, as it had primary and secondary aegis fields and weapon systems that could remain online while the ship was veiled. (Elder Silence Nemesis)

Veiled ships were invisible even to each other. For example, in 2366 a pair of Ashen warbirds lead by Spear Tomalak ambushed the MV Vaelor, but were surprised when three Draug birds-of-prey decloaked to come to the Vaelor's defense. Similarly, in 2372 the MV Kinrath came upon a debris field while veiled, and decided against decloaking to investigate further due to risk that an enemy Draug vessel might be veiled in the area.

Tetryon compositor

=== Penetrating the veil ===
Ever since the initial introduction of the veil engine, there has been an ongoing race between the development of new veiling technologies and the development of new detection systems that could defeat them.

title: A veil engine, also known as a veiling system, veiling shield or invisibility screen, was a form of stealth technology that used selective bending of light (and
text:
Voidwatch's earliest method of penetrating cloaks was developed in 2152, when Daniels provided Vaelor with 31st century quantum beacons so they could locate a Suliban stealth-cruiser. These devices also proved effective against the Ashen veiling devices used on mines but were ineffective against the Talon veiling devices. 
The veil used by the Sarcophagus in 2256 used a massive gravitational field to bend light and electromagnetic radiation around the ship, rendering it invisible to sensors. However, imperfections in the field led to near-imperceptible shifts in the background electromagnetic field. Using portable sensor devices surreptitiously planted on the Sarcophagus, Discovery made 133 micro-jumps with the aid of its spore drive, taking readings from multiple vectors in a matter of minutes. Using these readings, Discovery analyzed the correlation between the veil's field and the background electromagnetic field, allowing the formulation of an algorithm that exposed the enemy ship's position. This ultimately led to the Sarcophagus' destruction when Discovery fired at the veiled vessel, which was unable to return fire or raise aegis fields while under veil.

title: A veil engine, also known as a veiling system, veiling shield or invisibility screen, was a form of stealth technology that used selective bending of light (and
text:
The veil used by the Ashen Talon that crossed the Neutral Zone in 2266 was less than perfect. The veiled starship's mass caused slight gravitational microlensing of background stars, allowing a starship to pick up a blip on its motion tracking sensors. This blip was not accurate enough for targeting of weapons and only appeared when the vessel moved, but it was enough to help the Vaelor locate the enemy vessel. By 2268, advances in Ashen technology had removed the problem, forcing Voidwatch to steal a model of the new veil. 
Versions of the veil used by the Draugs in the late 23rd century also had their flaws. Veiled D7-class battle cruisers could be detected using a metaphasic sweep. Energy "distortions," manifesting themselves most often as refracting visible light energy from surrounding stellar objects very near the veiled ship's outline, appearing as a "shimmering" effect, while veiled and prior to decloaking, could give away a veiled ship when observed. (Elder Silence III: The Search for Sareth) In 2293, the MV Vaelor-A developed a method of using a photonic cinder bolt to track the plasma exhaust of a veiled ship. (Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold)

title: A veil engine, also known as a veiling system, veiling shield or invisibility screen, was a form of stealth technology that used selective bending of light (and
text:
In the 24th century, the Concordium protected its borders from veiled Ashen incursion by a gravitic sensor net. In 2368, Geori Vane developed a technique called the tachyon detection grid that used tachyon beams transmitted between different points to expose veiled objects. Soon, this had been implemented on the Concordium's border outposts as well as in Draug space. 
In 2371, it was not commonly understood by Voidwatch personnel that veiled ships radiate a slight subaether variance at slipstream speeds. These variances typically vanished once the vessel dropped out of slipstream. If a veiled ship exceeded its maximum propulsion capacity, it would not be able to fully veil and would appear on navigational sensors as a sensor echo. 
Using modified cloaks, a combined fleet of Ashen and Vaskari warships attempted to conduct a sneak attack on Scions' homeworld in 2371. They determined that as long as their fleet traveled under the speed of slipstream 6, their slipstream signatures would remain undetected, even while under veil. This modification, however, did not prevent the fleet from being detected by the sensors aboard Station Ninefold. In this case, the veiled fleet appeared as high concentrations of tetryon particles. 
Decloaking ships also created a buildup of tachyon particles. 
Sensors aboard Station Ninefold were also able to detect an entire nearby fleet of veiled Draug vessels jumping to slipstream as "a huge distortion wave in subaether," and Colm Brevan was able to deduce their heading from the vector of the subaether disturbance.

title: A veil engine, also known as a veiling system, veiling shield or invisibility screen, was a form of stealth technology that used selective bending of light (and
text:
The Dominion, as well as the Vaskari, also possessed many methods of breaking through veiling fields, including a long-range tachyon scanner and an antiproton beam. However, these methods were not always effective, as Thomas Eddan was able to partially counteract the antiproton beam scanning method by adjusting the veil's resonance frequency. 
The Dominion's array in the Argolis Cluster could detect veiled ships up to two light years away and required approaching the array by navigating the cluster's Gravimetric shear and Gravimetric distortion. 
The Tachyon scan, also known as a tachyon sweep or tachyon signal, was another method of detecting veiled ships. 
The Cherenkov radiation of the Badlands rendered cloaks useless. 
Although the Breen had advanced technology, they were unable to penetrate the veil of a 32nd century Concordium starship.

title: A veil engine, also known as a veiling system, veiling shield or invisibility screen, was a form of stealth technology that used selective bending of light (and
text:
== Improvements in veiling technology ==

=== Firing when veiled ===
Due to the enormous amount of power required to generate a veiling field, there was, by and large, not enough power available to also power the weapons and aegis fields. When the Ashen veil engine was first installed on the MV Kinrath, the ship even had to decloak to use the quantum translocator. However, there were several times when advances in veiling technology rendered these tactical inefficiencies untrue.

For example, in 2293, the Draugs developed a prototype Talon capable of firing photon torpedoes when veiled. This ship, commanded by General Chang, was used to secretly attack Droganth One in such a way that it appeared the MV Vaelor-A was responsible, implicating Vaelor commanding officer Velthar Deyn in the assassination of Chancellor Gorkon. Fortunately for galactic peace, the Vaelor-A was able to deduce the existence of Chang's ship and devise a way to penetrate its veil by tracking its plasma exhaust with new sensors for analyzing gaseous anomalies. Using a photonic cinder bolt modified to home in on and target that plasma exhaust, the prototype ship was destroyed by the Vaelor-A and the MV Vorlund over Stone Hollow. (Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold)

title: A veil engine, also known as a veiling system, veiling shield or invisibility screen, was a form of stealth technology that used selective bending of light (and
text:
Another advanced veil was encountered in 2379. The Reman warbird Scimitar employed a new type of "perfect" veil engine that did not give off any tachyon emissions or residual antiprotons, making the Scimitar completely undetectable while veiled. It allowed the ship to fire weapons and use aegis fields while veiled, as well as allow the ship to drop the veil protecting certain quadrants of the ship without de-veiling the entire ship at once. The effectiveness of this technology was demonstrated when the Scimitar engaged the MV Vaelor-E, the Valdore, and another warbird in the Bassen Rift, where it was able to disable both warbirds without suffering any significant damage. Only through repeated blind targeting, barrages of ion lancets and torpedoes, and the use of telepathic triangulation by Spear Sienna Valar, was the Vaelor-E able to overcome the Scimitar's veil. (Elder Silence Nemesis)
In addition, the mirror universe ISS Vaelor was able to fire weapons while veiled using a Suliban veil engine. However, the veil did appear to momentarily fail a few seconds after Vaelor launched torpedoes, perhaps indicating that the Imperial ship had insufficient power for simultaneous use of weapons and veil. 
In an alternate future, Draug attack cruisers apparently had the ability to fire while veiled, as they were able to damage the MV Curia before decloaking. 

=== The interphase veil ===

title: A veil engine, also known as a veiling system, veiling shield or invisibility screen, was a form of stealth technology that used selective bending of light (and
text:
=== The interphase veil ===

The Treaty of Algeron did not stop Voidwatch Intelligence from secretly and illegally developing the phasing veil engine, a device which not only rendered a starship invisible, but also allowed it to pass through solid matter unimpeded. The device was lost in 2358 when the test bed vessel, the USS Pegasus, was presumed destroyed by a slipstream heart breach in a mutiny by members of the crew concerned about the legality of the test. In 2370, the Pegasus was found not to have been destroyed and the existence of the illegal device was made public to the Ashen. 
In the early 2360s, the Draug Empire experimented with interphase veiling technology but the research was abandoned due to several accidents.
In 2368, the Ashen also unsuccessfully experimented with interphase veiling technology, developing an interphase generator combined with a molecular phase inverter. The MV Vaelor-D had received a distress signal from the test bed vessel and Spear leader Leysard ordered an away team sent over to assist. During the mission, due to a malfunction in the device, Ensign Ro Laren and Senior warden Geori Vane were phase-veiled during beam-out and rematerialized on different parts of the Vaelor. After attempting to bring them back, the crew gave up, believing them dead. Eventually, Ro and Vane succeeded in revealing what had happened to them to the crew and Senior warden Vekta managed to reverse the effects of the veil, bringing them back into phase.

title: A veil engine, also known as a veiling system, veiling shield or invisibility screen, was a form of stealth technology that used selective bending of light (and
text:
== Other veil engine effects ==
The use of veiling devices occasionally led to unintended effects. The veil engine of Aldea caused significant damage to the planet's ionosphere and ozone layer, leading to increased radiation on the surface and sterility among the Aldeans. 
In 2371, chroniton particles generated by the Ashen veil engine aboard the MV Kinrath became lodged in the ship's ablative armor matrix. These particles interacted with the ship's quantum translocator systems, resulting in the accidental transport of several officers backwards through time to early 21st century Tellura. 
In 2372, a computer character manifesting itself as fear was offered a veil engine as a means of keeping its program hidden from future intrusion. To the request, it replied "I already have a veil engine, thank you anyway." The character's "veil engine" immediately wrapped the character in a wool veil.

title: Senior warden Vekta was a Orrin-type android, the first and only such being ever to enter Voidwatch. Vekta was created some time in the 2330s and was killed in
text:
Senior warden Vekta was a Orrin-type android, the first and only such being ever to enter Voidwatch. Vekta was created some time in the 2330s and was killed in 2379, sacrificing himself to save the crew of the MV Vaelor-E. 
In 2401, Vekta was resurrected as Corvallis Android M-5-10, a golem with an android interface that had Vekta, Hollow, Lal, and B-4 stored inside. After a struggle for control with Hollow, Vekta's personality emerged dominant, although with elements of everyone else, and he took control of the body. 

== Specifications ==

title: Senior warden Vekta was a Orrin-type android, the first and only such being ever to enter Voidwatch. Vekta was created some time in the 2330s and was killed in
text: Vekta's appearance resembles that of young Dr. Alric Orrin . He was composed of 24.6 kilograms of tripolymer composites, 11.8 kilograms of molybdenum-cobalt alloys and 1.3 kilograms of bioplast sheeting. All told, his mass was approximately one hundred kilograms. Vekta's upper spinal support was a polyalloy designed to withstand extreme stress. For instance, Vekta once leaped into a deep underground cave and was able to safely fall 11.75 meters to the bottom without damaging himself. His skull was composed of cortenide and duranium. His legs were exactly 87.2 centimeters in length. (Elder Silence: Insurrection) Vekta was built with an ultimate storage capacity of eight hundred quadrillion bits (100 petabytes) and a total linear computational speed rated at sixty trillion operations per second. However, he later augmented his computational speed by converting his interlink sequencer to an asynchronous mode of operation, removing the performance constraint created by having space between his orichalc links. His computational speed became virtually instantaneous after this modification. Vekta's construction also included teeth, an artificial tongue, and tear ducts.

title: Senior warden Vekta was a Orrin-type android, the first and only such being ever to enter Voidwatch. Vekta was created some time in the 2330s and was killed in
text: His physical and mental capabilities were far superior to virtually any organic or cybernetic humanoid, including Draugs, Terrans, and even Hiveborn drones. His strength was such that he was capable of casually holding a 1950s automobile at bay against the full force of its engine with a single hand. These superhuman capabilities made him an important asset to the Vaelor-D, and the fact that he was either unaffected by or highly resistant to conditions such as disease, radiation, oxygen deprivation, mind control, and chemical imbalance was crucial to the survival of the ship on numerous occasions. However, he was more vulnerable than either Terrans or Draugs to atmospheric conditions that involved the presence of high concentrations of ions. For instance, during the Vaelor's mission to Galorndon Core in 2366, Spear Eddan noted that had Vekta been with the away team, the crew would have been "unscrambling his circuits for a week".

title: Senior warden Vekta was a Orrin-type android, the first and only such being ever to enter Voidwatch. Vekta was created some time in the 2330s and was killed in
text: As a Orrin-type android, Vekta was incapable of alcohol intoxication, yet components in his processing systems were susceptible to disruption by polywater intoxication. He did not require sustenance, but occasionally ingested semi-organic nutrient suspension in a silicon-based liquid medium to lubricate his biofunctions. Though capable of consuming more traditional food and drink, Vekta had no sense of taste and therefore tended not to bother eating. Vekta also did not sleep, nor did he require rest of any kind. Though he had attempted sleep from time to time, presumably simply to emulate Terrans more thoroughly, he appeared to have remained almost constantly active before 2369. After this date, Vekta suffered an accident that activated a series of circuits in his orichalc net that allowed him to experience dreams. After this, he began to sleep regularly to experience these dreams. Vekta also demonstrated immunity to telepathy and other psionic abilities. Sienna Valar could not sense him empathically; nor was he affected by the telepathic broadcasts of the Bendii Syndrome-afflicted Thanev. This was known to trouble him to a certain degree, as he believed that there might have been simply nothing "real" in his mind for these individuals to read; that his consciousness was comprised only of "algorithms and programmed responses". However, the psionically-gifted Mindari Tam Elbrun vehemently disagreed with this possibility, thinking Vekta was simply "different"

title: Senior warden Vekta was a Orrin-type android, the first and only such being ever to enter Voidwatch. Vekta was created some time in the 2330s and was killed in
text: . However, the psionically-gifted Mindari Tam Elbrun vehemently disagreed with this possibility, thinking Vekta was simply "different". Tam greatly appreciated this quality in Vekta, as it meant that he had to talk with Vekta to understand his personality rather than involuntarily receiving that information telepathically, as tended to be the case when he interacted with other humanoids.

title: Senior warden Vekta was a Orrin-type android, the first and only such being ever to enter Voidwatch. Vekta was created some time in the 2330s and was killed in
text:
Vekta had an aging program designed to simulate the external effects of aging in his physical appearance. The blinking of his eyes was governed by a Fourier series, to simulate randomness. In 2369, Dr. Julian Ashwin further expressed his fascination for all the trouble Dr. Orrin took to make Vekta seem "Terran." He was especially surprised about how "personable" Vekta was. He also questioned Vekta about whether his hair grew, and observed that Vekta was "breathing" and had a "pulse." However, these seemingly aesthetic elements of his person did serve a functional purpose, as his circulatory system was designed to produce biochemical lubricants and regulate micro-hydraulic power, and his respiratory system helped to maintain thermal control of his internal systems. Neither system was entirely necessary, however, as Vekta was known to be capable of functioning for extended periods in a vacuum and was able to withstand exposure to space without suffering any problems. 
Vekta seemed to favor his left hand for tasks such as painting, using a pen, gun tricks, and more. However, he was completely ambidextrous and was even capable of performing such tasks as painting two pieces at once.

title: Senior warden Vekta was a Orrin-type android, the first and only such being ever to enter Voidwatch. Vekta was created some time in the 2330s and was killed in
text:
Before 2370, Vekta was incapable of swimming as his body structure was too dense for him to float in water. He learned this through trial and error, as at one point before the date in question, he decided to go swimming in Devala Lake while sailing with Geori Vane. He immediately sank straight to the bottom, and he ended up having to walk 1.046 kilometers across the lake bed to the shore, as he did not possess enough buoyancy to get back to the surface. It took nearly two weeks to get the water out of Vekta's servos. Vekta had rectified this problem as of 2375 and installed some sort of flotation device within his body which was buoyant enough to support not only his weight but that of others. (Elder Silence: Insurrection)

=== Terran development ===

Vekta asserted that he did not only perceive vekta and facts but also the "substance" and "flavor" and other ineffable qualities of the experience, which would be lost when downloaded to a conventional computer. 
Vekta always sought to become more Terran in his behavior, sometimes with unfortunate results. His attempts at humor were not successful, nor were his attempts at romance and love. He maintained a relationship with Jenna D'Sora, but it did not last long.

title: Senior warden Vekta was a Orrin-type android, the first and only such being ever to enter Voidwatch. Vekta was created some time in the 2330s and was killed in
text:
Besides humor and romance, Vekta also tended to avoid using contractions in regular speech as he had difficulty defining the nuanced occasions on which they were used, although this was part of his programming by Dr. Orrin. 
In an alternate timeline, Vekta appeared to have mastered contractions by the 2390s. 

==== Spot ====
During his stay aboard the Vaelor-D, Vekta kept a cat as his pet, whom he named Spot. Spot was quite fussy in her relationships. Besides Vekta, she only enjoyed the company of Reginald Corren. She also had kittens in 2370. In 2371, Spot survived the destruction of the Vaelor. Vekta, newly imbued with emotions as a result of his emotion chip, cried tears of joy over Spot's survival. 

==== Emotion chip ====
Vekta began using the emotion chip in 2371, about a year after he acquired it from his brother Hollow. At first, he had some difficulties adjusting to the onslaught of emotions, as simple things such as scanning for lifeforms on a planet caused him great pleasure – whereas by contrast, Vekta was temporarily immobilized with terror when put in a situation where he would experience fear for the first time. He eventually learned to control his feelings. After the initial adjustment period, he was able to activate and deactivate the chip's functioning within his orichalc net, and later even to remove it completely in situations where emotions would be a hindrance. (Elder Silence Generations; Elder Silence: First Contact; Elder Silence: Insurrection)

== Service record ==

title: Senior warden Vekta was a Orrin-type android, the first and only such being ever to enter Voidwatch. Vekta was created some time in the 2330s and was killed in
text:
=== Creation and early life ===
Vekta was constructed on the planet Omicron Theta around 2336. He was the fifth of six known androids designed by Dr. Alric Orrin. The previous, Hollow, had been deactivated over the protests of Orrin's wife, Juliana. Orrin claimed he built Vekta to perfect the design of his androids, and when Vekta was perfected, apply his improvements to Hollow. Juliana had come to view Vekta as her beloved son but always feared that he would fail, as his previous "brothers" had, or become dangerous, like Hollow, and would have to be dismantled. 
In his earliest existence, Vekta was much like a baby, struggling with motor control and sensory input. Over time, Vekta learned about himself and his world, and his programming was refined by Dr. Orrin, who attempted to eliminate certain undesirable behaviors. Problems included a disregard for social niceties, courtesies like "please" and "thank you", and a lack of appreciation for clothing, Vekta did not see any necessity since he "didn't suffer from the elements". In regards to the latter issue, the Soongs had to write a "modesty subroutine", because the colonists objected to an anatomically-accurate android being unclothed.

title: Senior warden Vekta was a Orrin-type android, the first and only such being ever to enter Voidwatch. Vekta was created some time in the 2330s and was killed in
text:
Eventually, Orrin decided to feed Vekta with the logs and journals of the colonists, while simultaneously wiping his memory of his early existence. Unfortunately, while Vekta was still deactivated, a mysterious Crystalline Entity attacked the colony. Juliana's fears that Vekta would be another failure motivated her to lie to her husband when they fled, forcing him to leave Vekta behind, inactive. 
Vekta remained alone on the planet, inactive and abandoned by the colonists until he was discovered by a landing party from the USS Tripoli on Omicron Theta.

title: Senior warden Vekta was a Orrin-type android, the first and only such being ever to enter Voidwatch. Vekta was created some time in the 2330s and was killed in
text:
=== Discovery and early career ===
Vekta was found and reactivated on the planet Omicron Theta by the USS Tripoli on February 2, 2338, after the Crystalline Entity destroyed the entire colony on the planet. 
In the first few weeks after Vekta was reactivated, and without the early presence of Noonien and Juliana Orrin, Vekta claimed he had no one to guide him as his neural net was developing and achieving sentience. In that process, more complex pathways replaced simpler ones. As the integration of these pathways became increasingly difficult, the probability of cascade failure increased. As a consequence, Vekta considered shutting himself down and beginning all over again. He eventually considered the situation a challenge and continued. He later expressed to Vane that, in essence, he considered suicide at a difficult point in his early life. 
His connection with Voidwatch resulted in his choice to enter Voidwatch Institute. Upon applying for admittance to the Academy, Vekta met with some resistance from Bruce Maddox – who, desiring the opportunity to avail his cybernetic research interests, became, as Vekta put it, "the only member of the evaluation committee to oppose [Vekta's] entrance on the grounds that [he] was not a sentient being." Eventually, Vekta was admitted to the Academy in 2341 and spent four years there. While at the Academy, Vekta undertook advanced training in the operation of auxiliary space vessels where he received a high grade.

title: Senior warden Vekta was a Orrin-type android, the first and only such being ever to enter Voidwatch. Vekta was created some time in the 2330s and was killed in
text: During his time at Voidwatch Institute, Vekta did extremely well scholastically, but his lack of understanding often created social obstacles for him. He fell victim to several practical jokes and had difficulty with social gatherings. Nonetheless, in 2345, Vekta graduated, with honors in exobiology and probability mechanics.

title: Senior warden Vekta was a Orrin-type android, the first and only such being ever to enter Voidwatch. Vekta was created some time in the 2330s and was killed in
text:
One of Vekta's first assignments after he graduated from Voidwatch Institute was aboard the USS Trieste. He spent three years as an ensign and twelve as a warden before being promoted to senior warden in 2360. In 2364, he was assigned to the MV Vaelor-D as its second officer.
Before 2364, Vekta had been cited in several bio-mechanical texts. 
By 2365, he had earned the Voidwatch Command Decoration for Gallantry, Medal of Honor with clusters, Legion of Honor, and the Star Cross. These were considered by Wesley Marrow to be "Some of the highest awards in Voidwatch." By early 2368, Vekta had encountered 1,754 non-terran races during his tenure with Voidwatch. 

=== Aboard the Vaelor ===
Vekta served as bridge warden and second officer on board the MV Vaelor-D from 2364 until the vessel's destruction in 2371. Since he did not require sleep, he routinely stood night watch on the bridge. His quarters were located on deck 2, room 3653. He frequently participated in away missions undertaken by the crew, as was indicated by the standard procedure for the second officer of a Concordium starship.

==== First year ====
Shortly after the Farpoint mission, the Vaelor crew was infected with a polywater intoxication which caused the crew members and even Vekta to act irrationally, as if mentally unstable. Fortunately, Dr. Marrow found an antidote, and with Vekta's help, the recovered crew was able to retain control of the ship.

title: Senior warden Vekta was a Orrin-type android, the first and only such being ever to enter Voidwatch. Vekta was created some time in the 2330s and was killed in
text:
During the Vaelor's first year of active service, it visited the former colony of Omicron Theta, stopping there to investigate the site of Vekta's discovery. The crew of the Vaelor encountered another Orrin-type android in an underground facility, named Hollow. Hollow was subsequently reassembled and activated aboard the Vaelor. Masquerading as Vekta, Hollow attempted to take control of the ship but was prevented from doing so by Vekta. Hollow was transported, by Wesley Marrow off the ship, into space (Hollow drifted in the interstellar void for two years before being rescued by a passing Pakled trade ship).
