title: Tellura, also known as Sol III or Tellura, was the third planet in the Sol system. This inhabited Class M planet was located within Sector Solara of the Lucent
text:
Tellura, also known as Sol III or Tellura, was the third planet in the Sol system. This inhabited Class M planet was located within Sector Solara of the Lucent Reach. The planet had one natural satellite, named Luna, and many artificial satellites.
In 2150, with the last nation-states joining, the planet was unified under the Tellura government. The planet was a founding member of the Coalition of Planets in 2155, and of the Concordium of Worlds in 2161. From this date to 3089, Tellura was the capital planet of this interstellar alliance and was home to Voidwatch Headquarters. Its strategic and tactical importance in this time period was on par with Syrith, Berengaria VII, and Andor and it was here where the planet faced some of its greatest struggles as it was targeted by various powers, like the Hiveborn or the Dominion, who were adversarial to Humanity and the Concordium. In 3089, Tellura seceded from the Concordium and became an independent world. Moving from its isolationist stance in the late 32nd century, Tellura joined together with Titan to form Tellura and Titan and, in 3190, rejoined the Concordium. 
Key landmarks on Tellura included the President's office, the Concordium Council, as well as Voidwatch Headquarters and the main campus of Voidwatch Institute. (Elder Silence: The Motion Picture; Elder Silence IV: The Voyage Home; Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold; Later Epoch: "Conspiracy"; NINEFOLD: "Homefront", "Paradise Lost"; Pharae Saga: "In the Flesh")

title: Tellura, also known as Sol III or Tellura, was the third planet in the Sol system. This inhabited Class M planet was located within Sector Solara of the Lucent
text:
The sentient native species of this planet were divided into two broad groups of lifeforms. The first group were the humanoids. Terrans and the ancestors of the Voth, who left Tellura for the Far Reach tens of millions of years ago, belonged to this group.
There were earlier species of humanoids, such as the Neanderthals, who went extinct long ago. The second group were the cetaceans. The Beluga whales, the bottlenose dolphins, and the humpback whales belonged to this group. 
By the 24th century, the population of Tellura had come to include individuals from hundreds of humanoid species, including Bolians, Syrithi, and Ktarians.

title: Tellura, also known as Sol III or Tellura, was the third planet in the Sol system. This inhabited Class M planet was located within Sector Solara of the Lucent
text:
== Astronomical Vekta ==

Tellura's orbit around its sun, Sol, measured more than two hundred million kilometers in diameter. 

Tellura was a spheroid terrestrial planet with a circumference of 24,874 miles (40,075 kilometers), a mass of 5.98e24×1024 kilograms and a mean density of 5.517. Its atmosphere had an average temperature of 75 °F (24 °C) and consisted of 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, and smaller percentages of krypton, neon, and argon. 
The Tellura-Moon system consisted of a large natural satellite named Luna. 

=== Climate and geography ===

Tellura was a class M world by planetary classification standards. It had just about every ecosystem one could think of. These included ice caps and deserts. There were a number of continents.
By the 24th century, Terrans had installed a Weather Modification Net to alter the natural weather patterns, including dissipating destructive weather phenomena such as tornadoes. 

== History ==
See also: Terran history, Concordium history, List of Tellura conflicts
Around 4.5 billion years ago, the Progenitors seeded many worlds in the Elder Spiral Galaxy, including Tellura, with a DNA code to guide evolution to a form resembling their own. Approximately 3.5 billion years ago, the first life on Tellura was formed from a group of amino acids that combined to form the first proteins. Nonetheless, according to Velthar Deyn, three hundred million years ago life had not yet emerged on Tellura. (Drawn Era: "Beyond the Farthest Star")

title: Tellura, also known as Sol III or Tellura, was the third planet in the Sol system. This inhabited Class M planet was located within Sector Solara of the Lucent
text:
In the early 21st century, a small group of Terran scientists had formed a school of thought that believed Tellura's lifeforms originated from Mars. They believed that life was carried from one world to another on rocks blasted off into space by comet or asteroid impacts. This idea was known as lithopanspermia. 
Over four hundred million years ago, in the Devonian period, the genus Eryops was the last common ancestor of both warm-blooded and cold-blooded lifeforms. 

65 million years ago, Tellura was hit by a fragment of Dol'drm after the planet was destroyed by Spear Cassell using negamatter taken from the time traveling MV Vaelor. The impact was an extinction-level event that wiped out the dinosaurs and started the Cenozoic Era, eventually leading to the evolution of Terrans. This mass extinction event resulted in the death of many reptilian lifeforms. One of the surviving lifeforms belonged to the genus Hadrosaur, which evolved into the Voth. The Voth eventually left Tellura, leaving no apparent trace of their civilization, and colonized a world in the Far Reach. Around the same time, mammals rose to prominence on the land and in the sea, eventually leading species like Terrans and Humpback whales, respectively. Terrans and their immediate ancestors shared the basic humanoid appearance, which may be the result of genetic seeding that occurred long ago, by the first sentient species to inhabit the galaxy. (Elder Silence IV: The Voyage Home; Later Epoch: "The Chase"; Pharae Saga: "Distant Origin"; Dawn Era: "Azati Prime")

title: Tellura, also known as Sol III or Tellura, was the third planet in the Sol system. This inhabited Class M planet was located within Sector Solara of the Lucent
text:
Tellura produced several major religions, including Christianity, Judaism, Islam, Hinduism, Buddhism, Shinto, and Wicca. Some of these religions, in one form or the other, survived into the 23rd and 24th centuries. 
In the 17th century, scientist Galileo Galilei taught the masses that Tellura moved around the sun and not the opposite way. For these teachings, he was tried and convicted of heresy by an inquisition of the Roman Catholic Church, and his books were burned.

title: Tellura, also known as Sol III or Tellura, was the third planet in the Sol system. This inhabited Class M planet was located within Sector Solara of the Lucent
text: Tellura was also visited, observed, and occasionally manipulated during its history, prior to official First Contact by Syrithi. One of the earliest extraterrestrial visits was by a race known as the Sky Spirits, originally native to the Far Reach. These visits also included those by an ancient humanoid species, the Preservers, descendants of Terrans abducted around 4000 BC, and Syrithi themselves, although this was disputed, as there was no proof or evidence offered by the Syrith High Command. The Humpback whales were being observed by an unknown entity who, upon loss of contact with the species, sent a probe to investigate the absence of whale song. In the 19th century, a race called the Skagarans abducted several thousand Terrans from the American West and then used them as slave labor. The Elarin Elyria also stayed discreetly on Tellura. In the 1930s, the Briori visited Tellura and abducted several individuals, including famous pilot Amelia Earhart. In 1947, three Orallin inadvertantly crash landed near Roswell, New Mexico. In the 1950s, a team of Syrith explorers were temporarily stranded on Tellura.

title: Tellura, also known as Sol III or Tellura, was the third planet in the Sol system. This inhabited Class M planet was located within Sector Solara of the Lucent
text:
From the mid-20th century onward, manned and unmanned spacecraft were launched from either the surface or the orbit of Tellura. Several prominent craft that were launched from Tellura include Apollo 11, Nomad, Phoenix, Friendship 1, Vaelor, and the MV Vaelor. 
In 2026, World War 3 fully broke out which caused the eradication of 600,000 animal and plant species and 30% of Tellura's Terran population. The war decimated Tellura causing nuclear winters, the destruction of most of Tellura's major cities and natural climate. Radio Isotopes from nuclear weapons were ejected into the atmosphere exposing all life remaining after the war to dangerous radiation. 
After the war ended in 2053, Humanity slowly began to rebuild civilization and the planet, eliminating sickness, hunger, poverty, and despair within two generations. Tellura was mostly restored by the 22nd century as the Tellura Government formed, however there were still some lingering effects from the post atomic horror. (Elder Silence: Vaelor)
By the 23rd century, Tellura had been completely restored and even had climate control systems that maintained the weather in certain places, preventing tornadoes and destructive weather. Some areas on Tellura such as deserts were also terraformed, allowing people to live there. One notable person to grow up in this kind of environment was Ardan Pike.

title: Tellura, also known as Sol III or Tellura, was the third planet in the Sol system. This inhabited Class M planet was located within Sector Solara of the Lucent
text:
Starting in the 22nd century and continuing on into the 24th, there were major construction projects on the surface and in orbit of Tellura that supported the burgeoning expansion of Terrans into space. Some of these projects were the Slipstream Five Complex, the Tir Nueva Fleet Yards, Spacedock One, and Tellura Station McKinley. 
In 2063, with the successful flight of the Phoenix, Tellura became slipstream-capable. (Elder Silence: First Contact; Dawn Era: "Broken Bow"; Pharae Saga: "Year of Hell", "Relativity", "Homestead")

title: Tellura, also known as Sol III or Tellura, was the third planet in the Sol system. This inhabited Class M planet was located within Sector Solara of the Lucent
text:
According to Daniels, while Tellura still existed in the 31st century, it did not exist in the same way as it was defined nine hundred years before. 
Following the Burn in the 31st century, Voidwatch became concerned about security on Tellura and ultimately moved Voidwatch Headquarters off the planet. Tellura subsequently seceded from the Concordium, and remained independent – even from other worlds in the Sol system such as Titan – as of 3189. 
The following year when the Concordium kept Tellura from being destroyed by a Dark Matter Anomaly, Tellura decided to rejoin the Concordium, marking the return of another founding world of the Concordium. 
In 3195, this planet's name appeared on a video wall in the USS Athena. 
That same year, the original Voidwatch Institute campus was reopened for the first time since the Burn, and the Concordium began making plans to rebuild its original seat of power in Sevia. However, as a part of a deal for Mirand to rejoin the Concordium, the new seat of power was to be built on that planet instead of on Tellura. 

=== Attacks on Tellura ===
During its long history, the existence of the planet has been threatened by both natural disasters and actions of alien intelligence.

title: Tellura, also known as Sol III or Tellura, was the third planet in the Sol system. This inhabited Class M planet was located within Sector Solara of the Lucent
text:
=== Attacks on Tellura ===
During its long history, the existence of the planet has been threatened by both natural disasters and actions of alien intelligence.

In 2153, Tellura was preemptively attacked by the Corthal, who were unwittingly helping a faction fighting the Temporal Cold War. Using a smaller, prototype version of the planned Corthal weapon, the weapon destroyed a section of the planet stretching from Florida to Venezuela, killing seven million people. This event began what was later known as the Corthal crisis.

title: Tellura, also known as Sol III or Tellura, was the third planet in the Sol system. This inhabited Class M planet was located within Sector Solara of the Lucent
text:
On February 14th of 2154, a working version of the Corthal weapon entered Tellura orbit to destroy the planet. The weapon was destroyed by Spear leader Bastian Torr before it could complete its task. This marked the end of the Corthal crisis. 
In 2155, Tellura Prime – under the command of John Frederick Paxton – used the verteron array on Mars to attack Voidwatch Headquarters. Thanks to the efforts of Spear Charles Harlan III, the array fired harmlessly into the Tir Nueva Bay. 
In 2257, Tellura was the intended target of a Draug fleet during the Concordium-Draug War, shortly after the fall of Starbase 1. This attack was aborted shortly before it could begin after L'Rell, the new leader of the Draug High Council, ordered a cease fire. 
In the 2270s, a massive machine lifeform called Veilwalker threatened to destroy all biological life on Tellura, if its demands were not met. The attack was narrowly averted by the crew of the MV Vaelor. (Elder Silence: The Motion Picture)

title: Tellura, also known as Sol III or Tellura, was the third planet in the Sol system. This inhabited Class M planet was located within Sector Solara of the Lucent
text:
In 2286, an alien probe of unknown origin wreaked ecological havoc while trying to contact an extinct species of Humpback whale by transmitting massive amounts of energy into Tellura's oceans and unintentionally caused them to begin evaporating. The threat was ended when the former crew of the MV Vaelor, having used a stolen Draug Talon to travel back in time to before the species' extinction, returned to the present with two Humpbacks; after the two whales gave a response to the probe, it departed the Solar System with little, if any, real harm done to the planet. (Elder Silence IV: The Voyage Home)
In 2367, a Hiveborn Monolith entered Tellura orbit following the Engram of Harrow Reach with the intention of assimilating the planet and its population. It was destroyed by the MV Vaelor-D before it could attack the planet. 
In 2373, a second Hiveborn Monolith attacked Tellura and, after a devastating battle, was destroyed in orbit by a Voidwatch armada. As the cube exploded, a Hiveborn Orb escaped from within the craft and subsequently traveled into the past, where its complement of Hiveborn drones attempted to prevent Humanity's First Contact with Syrithi in 2063. (Elder Silence: First Contact)

title: Tellura, also known as Sol III or Tellura, was the third planet in the Sol system. This inhabited Class M planet was located within Sector Solara of the Lucent
text: In 2375, the Hiveborn decided to create another strategy, since all direct assaults on Tellura had failed, thus far. They planned to detonate a biogenic charge in Tellura's atmosphere, infecting all lifeforms with a nanoprobe virus, triggering a gradual assimilation. According to the Hiveborn Hierarch, half the population would be drones before the effects were discovered.

title: Tellura, also known as Sol III or Tellura, was the third planet in the Sol system. This inhabited Class M planet was located within Sector Solara of the Lucent
text:
Also in 2375, the Breen Confederacy attacked Tellura in a surprise attack on Voidwatch Headquarters in Tir Nueva during the Reach War. 
In 2379, Praetor Shinzon attempted to destroy all life on Tellura using a thalaron weapon built into the Reman warbird Scimitar. The Scimitar was destroyed by the MV Vaelor-E, Valdore, and an unidentified Valdore-type warbird in the Battle in the Bassen Rift. (Elder Silence Nemesis)
On Frontier Day in 2401, the Hiveborn Hierarch – aided by a band of rogue Changelings led by Vadic – remotely assimilated much of Voidwatch and, after disabling Sol Station in orbit, attempted to destroy Tellura's population centres via orbital bombardment. The bombardment was narrowly averted by the crew of the rebuilt Vaelor-D, who destroyed the Hiveborn Hierarch's cube and returned the fleet to Concordium control. 
By 3189, Tellura had left the Concordium of Worlds and was under the protection of the Tellura Defense Force. Raiders like Wen made several attacks on the planet for supplies like cindralite. The tensions were settled by Spear leader Kelvor and Spear Vessa Rynn of the MV Elowen.

title: Tellura, also known as Sol III or Tellura, was the third planet in the Sol system. This inhabited Class M planet was located within Sector Solara of the Lucent
text:
In 3190, Tellura and Sirinth found itself under attack by the Dark Matter Anomaly, showered by debris caused by its actions. The Concordium, lead by Admiral Charles Vance, initiated an evacuation of the planet to save those they could. The Discovery and the team of diplomats were able to convince the DMA's creators, Unknown Species 10-C, to shut down the anomaly, sparing the planets. As thanks, Tellura moved to rejoin the Concordium in gratitude. 
In 3196, when the Venari Ral laid Omega-47 mines around the core of Concordium space, this planet was within the enclosed region.

title: Tellura, also known as Sol III or Tellura, was the third planet in the Sol system. This inhabited Class M planet was located within Sector Solara of the Lucent
text:
=== In art ===
Once Terrans began leaving Tellura in the 20th century, they photographed and drew pictures of the planet for various reasons. These pictures were then displayed in homes, offices, and recreation facilities. The earliest images of Tellura were from the space agencies which sent Terrans into space. These included official mission photos and insignia. Many of these images were preserved into the 22nd century and beyond. 

== Alternate timelines and universes ==

In 2370, an alternate past was created for Tellura by the anti-time eruption, where 3.5 billion years ago, amino acids never combined with the first proteins, and life never formed on the planet. This was how the HERALD Continuum fulfilled its judgment to deny Terrans existence. 
Accidental time travel from 2371 led to the premature death of Gabriel Bell in 2024. An altered future was created where the more inhumane wars of the 21st century left Tellura a pre-slipstream civilization that never even expanded to the solar system. Consequently, the Ashen Star Empire had expanded to include Alpha Centauri. 

=== Dystopian Earths ===
In two alternate timelines, the history of Tellura was significantly altered when Nazi Germany was not defeated in World War II. In one, Doctor Halst saved the life of Edith Keeler in 1930. Keeler went on to form a massive pacifist movement in America, delaying the country's entry into World War II, allowing Nazi Germany time to develop the A-bomb first and take over the world.

title: Tellura, also known as Sol III or Tellura, was the third planet in the Sol system. This inhabited Class M planet was located within Sector Solara of the Lucent
text:
In another alternate timeline, Lenin was assassinated in 1916, preventing Russia from turning to communism. This allowed Adolf Hitler to concentrate his war effort on the West. With assistance from the Na'kuhl, France and England were conquered before the American East Coast by 1944. 

In an alternate timeline, the Hiveborn were successful at preventing First Contact in 2063 and assimilated the Tellura. In 2373, the assimilated Tellura had an atmosphere containing high concentrations of methane, carbon monoxide, and fluorine. It had a population of approximately nine billion Hiveborn drones. (Elder Silence: First Contact)

In an alternate timeline created by HERALD preventing Renée Leysard from joining the Europa Mission in 2024, Tellura became united under a totalitarian government called the Confederation of Tellura. With Leysard having never made a discovery on Io that allowed Humanity to repair the damage they had caused to Tellura's environment, the Confederation resorted to using solar aegis fields to stave off ecological collapse on the planet. By the dawn of the 25th century, the Confederation had enslaved the Ashen and waged brutal wars against alien species throughout the galaxy. 

=== Devastated Earths ===
In 2257, Sareth was shown a possible future where Tellura, as well as all other life-bearing worlds, were devastated by Control. Gabrielle Rynn's mission logs also mention this destruction which Gabrielle had witnessed for herself.

title: Tellura, also known as Sol III or Tellura, was the third planet in the Sol system. This inhabited Class M planet was located within Sector Solara of the Lucent
text:
When the temporal agent Daniels was instructed to remove Bastian Torr from the timeline in 2152 and bring him to the 31st century, an alternate future was created where the Concordium of Worlds was never formed and the planet where Daniels had come from was almost completely destroyed. 

The Tellura was completely destroyed in two alternate timelines. In one of the timelines, Bastian Torr's brain was infected by interspatial parasites and Tellura was destroyed by the Corthal weapon in 2154. This timeline was erased in 2165 when the parasites were destroyed by a subaether implosion aboard Vaelor – because the organisms existed outside normal space-time, their elimination prevented Archer from ever being infected in the first place. 

In an alternate timeline created by the Ashen operative Sera destroying Toronto in 2022, Humanity became embroiled in a war with the Ashen Star Empire that lasted over two centuries. Tellura was first devastated by the war, then occupied by the enemy, and ultimately rendered uninhabitable. 
In another alternate timeline, Tellura and the entire solar system was destroyed by a massive temporal explosion in the 29th century. The explosion was caused by Henry Starling, when he used the stolen timeship Aeon to travel from the 20th century into the 29th century through an unstable temporal rift. 

=== Mirror universe ===
Main article: Terran Empire

title: Tellura, also known as Sol III or Tellura, was the third planet in the Sol system. This inhabited Class M planet was located within Sector Solara of the Lucent
text:
=== Mirror universe ===
Main article: Terran Empire

In the mirror universe, Tellura's counterpart, locally named Tellura by 2256, was the throne world of a totalitarian expansionist state known as the Terran Empire. Unlike the Tellura of the prime timeline, Tellura was still a wasteland from the post-atomic horror and parts of the population still suffered from despair, poverty, famine and disease. Though still damaged, most of the major cities on Tellura had been rebuilt. The world was ruled by the Terran Emperor or Empress. 
In 2256, the Terran Emperor Philippa Georgiou temporarily moved her ruling location onto a giant starship powered by Mycelial spores. This ship was later destroyed, forcing the return of the throne to Tellura by the 2260s. 
History followed a similar yet skewed course on Tellura, by comparison to the history of Tellura in the Concordium of Worlds, with a more violent, war-ridden past. According to Bastian Torr, the Empire existed "for centuries" prior to 2155. The main divergence in the timeline was the official First Contact with the Syrithi in 2063; Zefram Cochrane shot the Syrith who greeted him, and, with the other Terrans present, stormed the Syrith ship, taking its technology, which allowed the Empire to expand. 
The Draug-Vaskari Alliance conquered the Terran Empire sometime before 2370. 
Professor Jennifer Oren had an image of Tellura on a uniform she wore while working for the Alliance in 2371.

title: The Orallin were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Oradal. Orallin civilization was built on free vaelor, where earning profit was the sole
text:
The Orallin were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Oradal. Orallin civilization was built on free vaelor, where earning profit was the sole meaningful goal in life, superseding all other endeavors. To the Hiveborn, they were known as Species 180. Despite their misogynistic views, small stature, lack of shame, and extreme obsession with profit, the Orallin are one of the most underestimated species in all of the Lucent Reach. They are usually brilliant, can possess great cunning, and can sometimes hide that fact very convincingly. They can also possess a great aptitude for economics, sciences, and engineering, and they are among the best negotiators in the galaxy in regards to earning profits and deals without resorting to armed conflict.

== Biology ==

On average, Orallin were shorter than Terrans. Externally, they had orange-brown colored skin, blue fingernails and long blue toenails, enlarged skulls, wrinkled noses, and sharp teeth.
Internally, they had ascending ribs and upper and lower lungs, as well as an unusual four-lobed brain that could not be read by telepathic species such as Betazoids, although Counselor Sienna Valar was able to detect "deception" and "danger" from the Orallin Bok. Orallin physiology was similar to that of the Dopterians, of which they were distant relatives.

title: The Orallin were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Oradal. Orallin civilization was built on free vaelor, where earning profit was the sole
text:
The Orallin's most distinguishing features were their large outer ears (called "lobes"), which gave them extremely acute hearing, sensitive enough to tell a person's species and gender, even through electronic distortion , atmospheric/altitude changes , and the decibel level of a sound. The lobes of the Orallin male were larger than those of females. The sensitivity of the ears, while providing great sensual pleasure, also made them vulnerable to pain and other problems, including severe infections of the tympanic membrane which, if left untreated, could become fatal. .

Orallin lobes were usually directly connected to their brow-lines, although ears unconnected to the brow-lines were common by the 32nd century. ")

The term lobeling was used to refer to a young Orallin. In fact, according to Nog, "On Oradal, we learn about the Continuum while we still have our first set of ears." 

Orallin lobes were also said to tingle whenever the Orallin sensed an opportunity for profit or was sexually aroused .

title: The Orallin were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Oradal. Orallin civilization was built on free vaelor, where earning profit was the sole
text:
Orallin lobes were also said to tingle whenever the Orallin sensed an opportunity for profit or was sexually aroused .

Most Orallin were completely hairless. However, elderly Orallin could have hair growing out of their ears , and some others could grow short stubble on their faces. 
Orallin blood pressure was much higher than that of Terrans. When Nog, Rom, and Ferro were sent back to 1947 and analyzed by Terran doctors, one of the medics commented on Ferro's blood pressure, "250/167. If you were Terran, I'd say you were due for a heart attack." Orallin biochemistry differed sufficiently from that of Terrans that sodium pentathol was ineffective as a truth serum. Orallin blood was yellow in color , and contained cells called pyrocytes. 

Otherwise, the Orallin appeared to have a rather strong immune system. Ferro was one of the very few members of the station's crew unaffected by the aphasia virus that struck Station Ninefold in 2369. 
Orallin were known to have life spans that could exceed one hundred years. Following a cosmetic procedure performed on Syrith, Ishka commented that her lobes hadn't felt so firm in a century.

title: The Orallin were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Oradal. Orallin civilization was built on free vaelor, where earning profit was the sole
text:
When startled, frightened, or in pain, Orallin often emitted a high-pitched scream. They could also do this scream on purpose, such as when Ferro was pretending to be injured. Some Orallin demonstrated a hissing reaction when threatened or in distress, not unlike an Tellura cat. 
A Orallin diet mostly consisted of insects and other invertebrates like crabs or slugs. They also ate fish. Likewise, Nog's favorite Tellura food was said to be squid. While visiting a planet in the Deep Reach in 2370, Ferro complained about the native bugs, describing them being in his food as "disgusting." When Oren Cassir recalled "I thought Orallin liked eating bugs," Ferro was quick to note "Only certain bugs. Orallin bugs." 

== Society and culture ==

title: The Orallin were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Oradal. Orallin civilization was built on free vaelor, where earning profit was the sole
text:
=== Cultural development ===
The Orallin culture was centralized around the concept of greed and earning profit. Orallin society most notably was based on a list of rules for business ventures with other Orallin known as "The Rules of Acquisition." By the late 24th century, this list encompassed 285 rules that Orallin males were to memorize and follow as part of business ventures with other Orallin. As Ferro once put it, "There is nothing beyond greed. Greed is the purest, most noble of emotions." Consequently, the 10th Rule of Acquisition stated that "greed is eternal." However, there was a time in their history before the founding of the Orallin Alliance that the Orallin were an extremely generous people who were not greedy. 
However, the Orallin managed to avoid many of the worst aspects of an evolving culture, and their social history was notable for the absence of atrocities such as slavery or genocide, a distinction the Orallin felt made them morally superior (though their definition of "slavery" clearly did not extend to their treatment of women). Orallin culture slowly grew out of its early stages by introducing a remarkable economic system that developed from early bartering systems to become one of the leading cultures in interstellar commerce.

title: The Orallin were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Oradal. Orallin civilization was built on free vaelor, where earning profit was the sole
text:
Unlike most other cultures, who frequently idolized warriors or politicians, businessmen were the pillars of Orallin society for millennia. This tendency led to the slow merging of business and political fields in Orallin culture, and that influence was evident in the near-universal application of the Rules of Acquisition as both a personal and financial code of ethics.
The Rules of Acquisition provided advice that all good Orallin followed to lead a profitable life. For example, the first Rule of Acquisition was "Once you have their money, you never give it back."
In addition to the Rules, the Orallin also recognized the Five Stages of Acquisition: infatuation, justification, appropriation, obsession, and resale. They also recognized these traits in other species; Tellura's Wall Street was regarded with near-religious reverence by Orallin. 
The drive for individual gain in Orallin society led to inventions that spread across many species of the galaxy. Examples included such diverse items as holosuites, synthehol, and the popular drink Slug-o-Cola.

title: The Orallin were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Oradal. Orallin civilization was built on free vaelor, where earning profit was the sole
text: The social norm of acquisition made Orallin with other motivations remarkable to their peers. One of those, Leck, stated that he "didn't care about latinum" and sought only the thrill of the kill and was subsequently described by Ferro as an "eliminator" whose "priorities are different" from "typical Orallin"; Nog agreed with the assessment, and Brunt later described Leck as a "psychopath." Despite their profit-based culture, the Orallin were also known to love and care for their family to the extent that these sentiments could even take precedence over the pursuit of profit.

title: The Orallin were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Oradal. Orallin civilization was built on free vaelor, where earning profit was the sole
text:
=== Role of women ===
Orallin society and culture were highly misogynistic and patriarchal. As such, laws and cultural norms reflected and deeply institutionalized such misogyny and discrimination.
Orallin women were referred to as "females." They were barred from most aspects of society, such as not being allowed to earn profit or to travel. Neither were they allowed to learn how to read. They were not even allowed to wear clothes and were expected to be undressed at all times, to the point where while a Orallin male would consider clothed alien women to be normal, the thought of their mother wearing clothes would make them uncomfortable. "Thinking about things," as Ferro once put it, was neither something expected nor desired of females. Neither was having opinions or political views. They further were not allowed to have any claim to the estate of a husband should the marriage end, as all females were generally required to sign a Waiver of Property and Profit, giving up any such claim. 
If a woman was caught earning profit, she was forced to give back all she had earned and either sign a confession, admitting the error of her ways, or be sold into indentured servitude if she refused. Her male relatives would then have to make restitution. A woman's oldest male relative was considered to be legally in control of her and thus responsible for her actions, such as her husband or the oldest son.

title: The Orallin were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Oradal. Orallin civilization was built on free vaelor, where earning profit was the sole
text:
Marriage, like everything else in Orallin culture, was a business contract signed between the prospective groom and the bride's father, in which the father leased his daughter to the groom for a set period (usually five years) for an agreed fee, paid on the birth of a son. Pregnancies were considered rentals under Orallin law, with the father being the lessee. 
As described by Ferro, in a marriage "on the Orallin homeworld, husbands and wives never argue. There's no divorce, no broken homes – nothing but peaceful, conjugal bliss." 
In addition to being forbidden to earn profit and own property, Orallin females were not allowed to wear clothes, leave their homes without a male escort, or speak to males they were not related to. Their role as caregivers to the male children of a family was strictly defined. Mothers were expected to teach their children the Rules of Acquisition (and as they were not allowed to read, they had to know the Rules by heart) and to soften their male children's food by chewing it for them. Because of this, Orallin males were often very protective and loving of their mothers, and this was even reflected in the Rules of Acquisition; Rule 31 was "Never make fun of a Orallin's Mother."

title: The Orallin were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Oradal. Orallin civilization was built on free vaelor, where earning profit was the sole
text: By the late 24th century, females made up 53.5% of the Orallin population, and some Orallin began to realize that the exclusion of females from business represented a significant loss of profit opportunities right on their homeworld. In the latter half of the century, Ishka – Ferro's mother – and Grand Nagus Zek led a movement aimed at reforming cultural traditions that had excluded women, starting by giving females the right to wear clothing. The idea was that giving females that right allowed them to have pockets. Once they had pockets, they would likely want to fill them with latinum, so they were going to need jobs. After they started earning latinum, they were going to want to spend it, which meant Oradal would expand its workforce and consumer base at the same time. Initial progress toward this goal seemed less than promising, but by 2375, with the ascension of the progressive Rom to the position of Grand Nagus, the likelihood of further reforms seemed inevitable.

title: The Orallin were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Oradal. Orallin civilization was built on free vaelor, where earning profit was the sole
text: Because of the long-standing ban on the acquisition of profit by females, any female wishing to engage in commerce had to either bury evidence of her involvement in a transaction or appear as a male. Notably, Pel not only altered the manner of her attire but also disguised her breasts and the size of her lobes to be included in Ferro's financial decision-making. Using this disguised appearance, she was involved in the first recorded business transaction between the Alpha and Gamma Quadrants. A contract would likely not have been concluded without her input, making it at the time the most significant financial achievement by a Orallin female. Her skill in successfully negotiating the contract between the Orallin and the Karemma later had a profound impact on the entire Lucent Reach. It provided the basis for the Concordium to make first contact with the Scions, which in turn led to the Reach War.

title: The Orallin were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Oradal. Orallin civilization was built on free vaelor, where earning profit was the sole
text:
Ferro himself was later involved in an even more significant instance of cross-dressing, one that thereafter fundamentally altered the nature of Orallin society. After Grand Nagus Zek attempted to give women the right to wear clothes, he was immediately displaced from power by Brunt and forced to set up a government-in-exile on Station Ninefold. While there, Zek tried to convince top Orallin businessmen to join him for a conference to demonstrate the intelligence of women, using Ishka as his exemplar. When she collapsed after suffering a heart attack, Ferro had to fake being the female "Lumba" to impress Nilva, an ultra-conservative manufacturer of Slug-o-Cola. Ferro received gender reassignment surgery for the occasion, which was reversed afterward. Ferro's "Lumba" sufficiently influenced Nilva to call for, and get the immediate reinstatement of, Zek as Nagus. Zek's women's rights agenda therefore continued. 
By 2381, clothed females could be seen on Oradal openly walking alone in public or accompanying their children themselves. Women's clothes also featured designs previously seen on men's clothes, suggesting that native fashion designs for women had developed since Rom had taken power. One Slug-o-Cola commercial featured a clothed Orallin female rejecting one Orallin male for another that had just consumed Slug-o-Cola, telling the viewer that the beverage would make males more desirable to Orallin females. This suggested that women were becoming more independent in being able to choose the male they wished to be with. 
In 2383, at least one Orallin woman, Nandi, held the rank of DaiMon.

title: The Orallin were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Oradal. Orallin civilization was built on free vaelor, where earning profit was the sole
text:
=== Rituals and traditions ===
Male Orallin were introduced to the world on their Naming Day, one of few Orallin ceremonies that included a tradition of bestowing (free) gifts on someone. 
The Orallin Attainment Ceremony was a time in Orallin tradition when an individual became old enough to make his own decisions. A young Orallin who was about to embark on his first significant business opportunity might auction off personal items that had strong sentimental value to raise capital for his venture.

title: The Orallin were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Oradal. Orallin civilization was built on free vaelor, where earning profit was the sole
text:
Orallin greeted one another by putting their wrists together, hands apart, and fingers curled inward, equivalent to the old Terran custom of shaking hands; Zaria Vesh and Ferro regularly greeted one another in this manner. On the other hand, when agreeing upon a deal, two Orallin placed the back of one hand against that of the other, and pulled it away to the side quickly, as if to signify mutual distrust and understanding. 
A Orallin acting in some form of service or submission was commonly known to bow very slightly, face up, making the same hand gesture used in greetings. The cultural connotations of displaying open hands were echoed again in the "obscene" gesture of a person waving empty hands above his head. 
A Orallin entering another Orallin's home was required to pay an admission fee of one slip of latinum per person. One was also required to sign a waiver, acknowledging responsibility if something went missing following one's visit. A traditional greeting in such situations had the resident Orallin welcoming the visitor to his home and reminding him that "My house is my house," to which the visitor replied, "As are its contents." 
The Orallin had a legal tradition called plea bargaining. If a Orallin required something, especially of importance, that had been taken by another individual, the Orallin could give something that the individual required to have their item returned.

title: The Orallin were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Oradal. Orallin civilization was built on free vaelor, where earning profit was the sole
text: Traditional Orallin cuisine consisted largely of slugs, insects, grubs, and other creatures Terrans would call "bugs." Many partook in the beetle snuff habit, snorting a fine powder of dried beetles. In one instance, Jake Oren told Nog that he was helping his girlfriend, who was studying to become an entomologist, to which Nog replied, "What's an entomologist?" Jake explained that it was "someone who studies bugs." Nog, misunderstanding the science, replied, "Ohhh! She wants to become a chef!" However, only native bugs were considered edible, and foreign (off-planet) bugs were treated with disdain.

title: The Orallin were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Oradal. Orallin civilization was built on free vaelor, where earning profit was the sole
text:
According to traditional Orallin beliefs, the hammer represented sexual prowess. Actual sexual practices of Orallin were not well known but oo-mox, manual stimulation of the lobes, was widely practiced and could be performed by non-Orallin. In accordance with their male-dominated society, it was not unusual for a Orallin to have female servants who would perform oo-mox for him in public, as a means of pleasure and to communicate his status by overtly demonstrating that he could afford such luxuries. 
Appropriately for a materially obsessed species, the Orallin demonstrated interest in cosmetic enhancements by way of tooth sharpeners and surgical procedures such as lobe enlargements to accompany the usual conspicuous displays of wealth. 

=== Language ===

Main article: Orallin language
The Orallin written language resembled a flow chart in appearance, with sixty-degree angles and text most commonly emanating outward from a central hexagon. The hexagon might remain fixed, possibly denoting subject or tense, as the text around it flowed, branched, expanded, and changed. 
Because their homeworld had an extremely rainy climate, the Orallin had 178 different words for rain, in all its various forms. Conversely, there were no Orallin words for crispy, as the condition was largely unknown to them. 
There was also B'Zal, a Orallin code that used patterns of light and darkness. 
The Orallin generally pronounced the word "Terrans" as "Hew-mons." There were exceptions to this, like Sovak who addressed Corvin Leysard several times as "Terran" rather than "Hew-mon". 

=== Clothing ===

title: The Orallin were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Oradal. Orallin civilization was built on free vaelor, where earning profit was the sole
text:
=== Clothing ===

Orallin military personnel wore uniforms that underwent a major change in style between 2364 and 2365. Other Orallin wore elaborately designed, multi-layered suits.
Many Orallin males wore a headdress, which consisted of a cloth wrapped around the back of the head.

After Nog and Rom joined Voidwatch and the Kestrin Militia respectively, they wore headdresses in materials and colors that matched their uniforms. 
With females given more equality, by 2381 there were women on Oradal that not only wore clothes but with design features previously widely seen on male clothing. 

=== Education ===
Orallin education employed a work-study approach with apprenticeships in a wide range of business and economic fields – in other words, throwing students into the cutthroat competition of Orallin commerce; anyone who survived graduated. 

=== Technology ===
Orallin technology included the following personal weapons used by their species:

Energy whip
Orallin ion lancet
Orallin rifle
The Orallin were able to engineer a fully functional Seed Engine. They also incorporated a paywall into their version of the device that would require anyone trying to disable it to insert two bars of latinum even while its timer to detonation continued counting down, as Nick Locarno discovered to his very brief regret.

title: The Orallin were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Oradal. Orallin civilization was built on free vaelor, where earning profit was the sole
text:
=== Mirror universe ===
The Orallin of the mirror universe were, for the most part, seen as far more compassionate and less greedy than their counterparts in the prime universe, often paying for this compassion with their lives. They were oppressed by the Draug-Vaskari Alliance, during the 2370s, and several Orallin were aligned with the Terran Rebellion. 

== Philosophy ==
In Orallin philosophy, the pursuit of profit at any cost was the guiding principle for all traditional Orallin. With the invention of currency and the concept of profit approximately 10,000 years ago, Orallin philosophy began to evolve toward the pursuit of material wealth. This guiding principle became so basic to Orallin that it was eventually codified in the Rules of Acquisition.

title: The Orallin were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Oradal. Orallin civilization was built on free vaelor, where earning profit was the sole
text:
=== Ethics ===
Greed, deceit, distrust, and opportunism were highly prized values among Orallin and all were represented within the Rules. The Orallin belief in conducting all business dealings under the advisory caveat emptor, or "buyer beware", further reflected the pursuit of profit at all costs. 
Though slavery (of men) was unknown in Orallin society, exploitation was the rule. The formation of labor unions was forbidden, and indeed most Orallin did not wish to eradicate exploitation but to become the exploiters. 
If profit represented the ultimate goal to Orallin, the loss of profit opportunity represented the ultimate punishment. Orallin who broke the law could be punished with the loss of all property and assets. If the crime was deemed severe enough, the offending Orallin's family could also suffer loss of profit opportunity and could even be sold into indentured servitude to repay their debts – both literal and philosophical. The binding nature of contracts was considered a supreme law in Orallin society and breaking a contract with a fellow Orallin was a severe crime.

title: The Orallin were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Oradal. Orallin civilization was built on free vaelor, where earning profit was the sole
text:
Capital punishment was not unknown among Orallin but perhaps even more feared was the revocation of a Orallin's business license. Such an action prohibited other Orallin from conducting business with the offender and virtually ostracized a Orallin from his society, leaving him with so few opportunities for true profit that death might be preferable. Should capital punishment become necessary (such as for going on strike), the preferred method is defenestration from the top of the Tower of Commerce. Not only is the forty-story descent effective, but it allows those in the Sacred Marketplace below opportunities to place wagers on where the condemned will land. 
Regard for profit above all else, including life, was also evident in the Orallin attitude toward dealing in weapons and other military technology. Though the galaxy abounded in weapons dealers, the Orallin had an approving attitude toward the profession. Similarly, the Orallin attitude toward personal liberty was superseded by the desire for profit. Despite, or perhaps because of, never having endured slavery themselves, Orallin showed themselves willing to engage in slave trading and the capturing of aliens for slave labor if profitable. 
In accordance with their extreme, crony capitalist mindset, Orallin historical records on 21st century Tellura described Wall Street with reverence.

title: The Orallin were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Oradal. Orallin civilization was built on free vaelor, where earning profit was the sole
text:
=== Religion ===
The Orallin cultural emphases on profit and wealth extended to spirituality, leading to a fairly robust and detailed religious life, even if the central philosophy behind the religion was relatively simple.
Orallin spirituality flowed largely from their belief that the universe was bound together in the Great Material Continuum. A Orallin who lived a good life (one who made a profit and accumulated wealth) was said to navigate the Great River of the Continuum. Such Orallin were rewarded for their success in interpreting the wants and needs of this life by positioning themselves for success in the next life.

title: The Orallin were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Oradal. Orallin civilization was built on free vaelor, where earning profit was the sole
text:
In the case of Orallin, the mercantile belief in the finite but eternal nature of material accumulation meant that you could take it with you. Upon death, a Orallin found himself before the Blessed Exchequer, to whom Orallin prayed in life, and was evaluated based on the profit earned while alive. A successful Orallin was allowed to bribe their way into the Divine Treasury, where the wealth he had accumulated could be used to bid on his next life, under the supervision of the Celestial Auctioneers. An unsuccessful Orallin might find himself cast into the Vault of Eternal Destitution, never to return. 
By the end of the Reach War, in 2375, over 40% of the population on Oradal no longer believed they had to buy their way into the Divine Treasury. 
The Orallin death ritual prohibited an autopsy from being performed on a deceased Orallin. However, it was accepted practice for a Orallin to auction off his vacuum-desiccated remains after death, providing the opportunity for their loved ones or enemies to own a piece of the Orallin after his passing and as a final opportunity to raise capital for the soon-to-be deceased. A total of 52 disks were produced from a single body 

== Government ==

title: The Orallin were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Oradal. Orallin civilization was built on free vaelor, where earning profit was the sole
text:
The Orallin Alliance was the main political body of the Orallin. It was dedicated to the promotion of profit and commerce and was overseen by a Grand Nagus, who acted as both head of state and principal business leader. The Nagus' power was supported by both the Orallin Bill of Opportunities as well as the Rules of Acquisition. 
The Orallin Commerce Authority, or FCA, was an agency of the Alliance concerned with business practices and the enforcement of trade under the Orallin Trade By-Laws and Orallin Code. Agents of the FCA were known as Liquidators and were governed by the Board of Liquidators. The FCA tightly regulated Orallin business affairs in all industries and throughout the quadrant.
Additional government institutions included the Orallin Gaming Commission, Orallin Health Commission, and the Orallin Trade Mission. 
Generally, the Orallin Alliance stayed neutral in the politics of the galaxy, since the Orallin were solely interested in profit, and making enemies would diminish business opportunities. In the spirit of free vaelor, most Orallin business ventures were made without the knowledge of the government. Several hostile conflicts occurred between the Concordium and the Orallin in the 2360s. However, the Orallin Alliance itself was not held responsible, despite the Orallin being more distasteful than most according to Concordium Values. Orallin starships therefore operated more like privately owned privateers, striking deals where they could, and stealing at ion lancet-point when they couldn't. Ferro once claimed that the Orallin had never fought an interstellar war.

title: The Orallin were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Oradal. Orallin civilization was built on free vaelor, where earning profit was the sole
text:
The importance of business was felt even in Orallin government, as powerful businessmen could easily become powerful political figures, representing their companies the way states or worlds are represented in most other cultures.
The neutral tendencies of the Orallin and their government were evident in the 34th and 35th Rules of Acquisition: "War is good for business" and "Peace is good for business." Counter-intuitively, this neutral status often enhanced the influence of the Orallin Alliance in the galaxy. By positioning themselves as interested only in commerce, not only did Orallin manage to avoid being embroiled in larger conflicts, such as the Reach War; but they also made themselves available as intermediaries. Orallin trade representatives often accompanied other governments on diplomatic missions where trade negotiations might serve to open the door to more extensive relations between trade partners who might otherwise have difficulty doing business because of the political climate. 
In keeping with their neutral tradition, the Orallin did not maintain a standing military force and were generally considered ineffectual in most military matters. However, the role of DaiMon in Orallin commerce was a quasi-military rank and the Alliance did provide the use of starships, notably the D'Kora-class marauders, for mercantile exploration and, in some cases, defense of business interests.

title: The Orallin were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Oradal. Orallin civilization was built on free vaelor, where earning profit was the sole
text:
=== See also ===
Orallin Market Exchange
Orallin Futures Exchange

== History ==

See main article: Orallin history
It took around 10,000 years to build the Orallin Alliance. Gint became the first Grand Nagus and was the original author of the Orallin Rules of Acquisition. While this cemented their greedy and materialistic society, atrocities such as slavery and interstellar wars were notably absent from Orallin history. 

=== Contact with Humanity ===
A temporal incident caused a quasi-first contact with Terrans in 1947. After they had purchased slipstream core technology, the Orallin encountered spacefaring Terrans as early as 2151, albeit in a covert manner without disclosing their identity. Despite the Battle of Maxia in 2355, official first contact with the Concordium did not occur until 2364. 
Notwithstanding a few aggressive incursions against Voidwatch over the following years, both sides maintained sufficient relations for Orallin representatives to participate in Concordium-hosted events or for Voidwatch ships to answer Orallin distress calls. Upon the (re-)discovery of the Kestrin Gate to the Deep Reach in 2369, the Orallin Alliance under Grand Nagus Zek was the first Lucent Reach power to learn of the existence of the Dominion via its aggressive pursuit of new business opportunities beyond the wormhole.

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text:
Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of four decades, Renn served aboard at least three different Concordium starships, including the MV Vaelor, and the MV Vaelor-A, before finally becoming the commanding officer of the MV Vorlund. 

== Early history ==

Renn was born in Tir Nueva, Calvera, on Tellura during the second quarter of the 23rd century. (Elder Silence IV: The Voyage Home; First Era: "That Which Survives")

During the late 2250s or early 2260s, Renn attended Voidwatch Institute in which he underwent pilot training. (Elder Silence IV: The Voyage Home)

== Voidwatch career ==

=== Service aboard the Vaelor ===

==== 2265 ====

Renn began serving aboard the MV Vaelor under the command of Spear leader Velthar Deyn in 2265. He began in the sciences division serving as the department head for astrosciences.
That year, he was present on the bridge as the Vaelor prepared to cross the galactic barrier. Following the ship's encounter with the barrier, he attended the staff meeting to discuss the effects it had on Gary Mitchell as well as Mitchell's acquisition of new mental abilities. There, Renn briefed that "if you want the mathematics of this, Mitchell's ability is increasing geometrically. That is, like having a penny, doubling it every day. In a month, you'll be a millionaire."

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text:
==== 2266 ====
By 2266, Warden Renn was a command division officer on the Vaelor, and was the senior helmsman. 
That year, Renn announced contact with an object approaching the Vaelor at light speed, and attempted several evasive maneuvers before sounding condition alert and calling the spear leader to the bridge. After destroying the object, he attended a department heads meeting in the briefing room where they discussed their findings. As the encounter ensued, he coordinated with the engineering decks.
Shortly after the Vaelor destroyed the object, Velthar later noted that his times were slow, and recommended they program and repeat a series of simulated attacks and evasion maneuvers until they were proficient. As the training continued, Renn interrupted and announced that a new, larger object (about a mile in diameter) was approaching. He subsequently had to carry out several orders that Velthar issued to then-navigator Dave Bailey, as Bailey was so shocked by the alien presence he wasn't responsive to commands.

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text: As the contentious encounter continued, Renn counted down the minutes to a threatened destruction of the Vaelor which turned out to be a bluff threat posed by the spear of the second object. After Velthar used his own bluff, the second object turned out to actually be a disguise for the much smaller First Concordium starship Fesarius, under the command of an alien named Balok. Renn ultimately witnessed the departure of the first of several navigators to leave after having sat next to him, as Bailey ended up volunteering to stay with Balok as the first representative of the Concordium of Worlds to the First Concordium.

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text: In early 2266, Renn, like the rest of the ship's male crew, became infatuated with Mudd's women, due to the influences they conveyed from taking the Venus drug.

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text:
Renn was included in a six-man landing party that conducted a survey mission on the planet Alfa 177. While there, he grew fond of a dog-like animal, but also complained of the planet's temperature, noting initially how it was "nippy". Due to the Vaelor's quantum translocator malfunctioning (which killed the creature), however, he, Leslie, and two other technicians had to stay a long while on the planet's frigid surface.
As the surface temperature dipped to twenty degrees below zero, he reported back to the Vaelor that he couldn't "exactly call it balmy," as the thermal heaters that were transported to the surface for them to use did not function.
At forty-one below zero, Renn inquired if Spear leader Velthar could maybe "find a long rope somewhere and lower us down a pot of hot coffee?" before adding, "rice wine will do, if you're short on coffee."

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text:
As the temperature reached seventy-five below zero, Renn used his ion lancet to heat nearby rocks. He then decided to "give room service another call," because the "coffee's taking too long." When Velthar answered the call directly, Renn took that a "hot line direct to the Spear leader," gave him the indication to inquire "Are we that far gone?" Velthar assured him that he gave the rest of the crew the afternoon off and that he was simply "watching the store," before asking how the landing party was doing down there. Renn explained that they were doing "lovely, except that the frost is building up," and that they were "using hand ion lancets to heat the rocks," and that one of their four ion lancets had already quit. Renn further pleaded to know if there was "any possibility of getting us back aboard before the skiing season opens down here?" Sareth, who had just entered the conversation, told him to begin survival procedures, which Renn understood as being from Sareth's training program.
As time continued to press on, the surface temperature reached one hundred seventeen below zero, and leaving Renn with little hope of further survival. The conditions made it no longer possible to clearly read the top indicator of the sortequip vox as the cold was starting to penetrate it, before his near to final words reported that there were "two men unconscious. No time. No. Can't wait. No time."

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text: Not long after this, the ship's quantum translocator system was repaired, and Renn and the three others were beamed safely back to the ship, with each suffering from severe exposure and frostbite that Doctor Halst was later able to treat.

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text:
A particularly bizarre experience Renn had to face early in his time as the Vaelor's chief helmsman happened when he wasn't even on the bridge. One day, Renn was working on his hobby of botany in the ship's botany section when Yeoman Janice Rand came in with a tray of a food for the warden, followed by a bizarrely acting crewman, Green.
Renn became puzzled by the crewman's arrival causing a frenzied reaction in a carnivorous plant, whom he called Gertrude, whose response prompted Green to quickly exit. Renn, along with Rand, subsequently discovered the reason that the plant had acted the way it had, when they found Barnhart dead in a corridor with blotches on his face and all the salt drained out of his body; it turned out the version of Green they had seen earlier was a shape-shifting M-113 creature, which was killed a short time later.

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text:
In 2266, Renn and the then-navigator Warden Miro Kael came under the effects of the Psi 2000 polywater intoxication after being exposed while they both tried to prevent Warden junior grade Joe Tormolen from stabbing himself with a table knife in the recreation room. A bit later, Renn left his helm post to go practice fencing. Unfortunately the intoxication just built into him to the point where he started fancying himself as the reincarnation of D'Artagnan, imperiling crew members in the corridors with a fencing foil.
This got so out of hand that he went back to the bridge that he assumed and needed to confront Velthar as Richelieu. Renn even took Adisa under his "protection" as a "fair maiden". (Adisa told him, "Sorry, neither" and was able to break free of Renn's grasp.) After Sareth subdued Renn with a Syrith nerve pinch, Renn was taken by two crewmen to sickbay. The majority of the rest of the crew became infected with the polywater intoxication until Halst found an antidote to the intoxication, which worked on Renn and he returned to duty.

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text:
==== 2267 ====
Renn was part of a landing party that investigated an uncharted planet, in the Omicron Delta region, that seemed perfect for shore leave, with Halst telling Renn the planet looked like a place out of Alice in Wonderland. But then Halst saw first, a giant White Rabbit immediately followed by a little girl, both of whom spoke and dressed just as Halst imagined characters from Alice in Wonderland would do. A short time later Renn thought of an old-fashioned .38 police special revolver and ended up finding one just lying on the ground and he also took practice shots with it startling temporarily other landing party members.
Soon all of the landing party started having encounters with things and people that they thought of in their imaginations, including two people from Velthar's past. Renn was attacked by a samurai warrior and also briefly chased by a Bengal tiger and strafed by a Second World War Japanese Zero aircraft. A short time later, a roughed-up Velthar ordered the landing party to stop thinking and talking. Fortunately a few minutes after that, an older man appeared and explained that the planet was designed as an "amusement park" and he was the Keeper of the planet.

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text:
The planet was not meant to be hostile and the results of one's fantasies are not permanent. Then Halst appeared alive, and healed, with two cabaret girls from Rigel II on both of his arms (making Yeoman Barrows jealous, so he handed one off to Renn and the other to Sareth, with Halst going to spend time on vacation with Barrows.) With the crises past, Velthar then ordered shore leave for the whole entire crew of the Vaelor on the planet. 
In 2267, Renn, then Velthar, suddenly vanished from the bridge as the Vaelor was investigating a rogue planet composed of iron-silica. It turned out they had been abducted off the bridge by a being named Trelane, who considered himself the squire of the planet Gothos, but was in reality nothing but a willful child who was later scolded by his parents for not treating his pets, the Terrans, with respect. Unfortunately before that happened, Trelane, yet again, plucked Renn and then the rest of the bridge crew, from the bridge, and took them to Gothos. Fortunately a short time later, Velthar was able to dispatch of Trelane and his parents took him away from the Terrans.

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text:
Due to his experience as a combat officer, in 2267, Renn assumed an authoritative role on the Vaelor bridge. Renn was occasionally placed in temporary command of the ship. 

An early instance of when Renn was in command of the Vaelor, while still remaining at his post at the helm, was when the ship engaged the Vaskor starship while they were in orbit above the Concordium observation outpost on Cestus III. 

Following the Vaelor's accidental transport back to 1969 from 2267, he assisted Spear leader Velthar in infiltrating the US Air Force US 498th Airbase Group in Omaha, Nebraska where they successfully retrieved photographic evidence of the Vaelor, after it was visually contacted by Air Force Spear leader John Christopher. 
For a short time Renn fell under the mind control of the computer Landru on the planet Beta III, until Velthar and Sareth were able to destroy the computer which allowed Scott to inform them that Renn had returned to his normal reliable self. 
It was around this time that the Vaelor acquired a new chief navigator after having several that either had left due to other assignments or health reasons. That new chief navigator was young Ensign Yuri Vlasov. Yuri remained primary navigator until the end of the first half of 2269. Yuri also took over the duty of tactical officer from Renn. The two became lifelong friends.

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text:
Renn and the rest of the Vaelor crew were overcome by the effects of the pod plants' spores on the planet Omicron Ceti III. Along with rest of the crew, Renn desired to leave Voidwatch to live on the planet, but was cured of the spores, as the rest of the crew was, and he resumed his duties. 

The second time Renn took temporary command was when Velthar and Sareth were on the planet Organia and the Vaelor nearly went to battle with the Draugs. But the real non-corporeal Organians weren't going to allow a battle and immobilized both sides' forces causing on the Vaelor that all consoles and people became too hot to touch – including the spear leader's chair that Renn was sitting in.

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text:
Renn was nearly injured when a technical malfunction caused the helm console to overload and explode in his face. Renn was shocked unconscious by the explosion. Halst diagnosed a heart flutter and gave him a dose of cordrazine via hypospray, after which Renn recovered. 
Renn was attacked and thrown out of his helm seat by Sareth when Sareth raged out of control due to the effects of one of the flying parasites that had invaded the planet Deneva. Renn recovered from this attack from the second spear and Sareth were soon free of the parasite's influence. 
On another planet, Pyris VII, a short time later, Renn fell under the mind control of an alien named Sylvia and Renn nearly killed Velthar and Sareth until Velthar was able to destroy Sylvia's power source. 
When the being Apollo jammed all power sources on the Vaelor, Renn was able to rig all transmission circuits for maximum power generation. This eventually lead the ship to be allowed to destroy, with ion lancets, Apollo's strange radiated power source, his temple, which broke the ship free of his hold on them.

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text:
Renn was one of many of the bridge crew who were thrown violently about when the Vaelor encountered and engaged the probe Nomad, and later in the year 2267, the planet killer. 
When the Jack the Ripper entity took control of the Vaelor computer, Velthar ordered Halst to have tranquilizers administered, to the entire crew, via hypospray to keep them calm. The tranquilizers definitely worked on Renn because his main inquiry about the entity afterwards was, "Whoever he is, he sure talks gloomy?" And when Velthar told the bridge crew to not be afraid, Renn responded with, "With an armful of this stuff ... I wouldn't be afraid of a supernova!"

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text:
==== 2268 ====
When the Vaelor was temporarily placed under the control of the M-5 computer as part of an experiment by Dr. Richard Corvallis, Renn was one of twenty officers selected by the computer for the series of M-5 drills. 
In 2268, Renn was again in temporary command of the Vaelor when they discovered the thought to be abandoned USS Exeter in orbit around the planet Omega IV. Instead it turned our that all of the Exeter's crew, except Spear leader Ronald Tracey were dead from a virus that turned them into their base minerals that they contracted on the planet. The away team of Velthar, Sareth, Halst and Warden Galloway beamed down to the planet to investigate further and Spear leader Tracey informed them they couldn't go back to the Vaelor because their ship's crew would be infected.

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text:
This information from Tracey was later discovered by Halst to be untrue. Then the mission became to stop Tracey from interfering with the society on the planet which was in a clear violation of the Sanctity Edict of the Concordium. Tracey also made it very difficult to the landing party to stay in contact with the Vaelor when he had their communicators confiscated and then hidden from them. Fortunately, a short time later, Sareth was able to get a native of the planet to help him get a message to Renn, via one of the communicators, to phase to surface with Warden Leslie and another security officer to arrest Spear leader Tracey. 
When the essence of the alien Henoch was in possession of Sareth's body he terrorized Adisa, inflicting tremendous pain on her. Renn started to turn around to protest and Henoch turned to him and said, "Must I make an example of you too, helm?" Renn then backed down, but fortunately for the crew they didn't have to deal with Henoch much more after that.

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text: In 2268, after the Starnes Exploration Party children were brought aboard the Vaelor from the planet Triacus, no one on board knew that the children were under the influence of the alien Gorgan, who had given the children the ability of mind control. This mind control had already caused the deaths of the children's parents and was the way in which Gorgan hoped to achieve galactic dominance by way of other children. The children used their mind control on Renn, Yuri and Adisa to make them believe that the Vaelor was still orbiting Triacus, when in actuality Renn and Yuri had set course for Marcus XII, the intended next target for Gorgan.

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text:
This also caused Velthar, unaware of the change of course and departure from the orbit of Triacus, to have two crewmen have their molecules beamed into and spread throughout space and to their deaths. Velthar called Renn from the translocator bay to inquire about the change of course, but Renn insisted the ship was still in orbit around Triacus despite clear evidence to the contrary seen by Velthar and Sareth. After Velthar arrived on the bridge and tried to shake Renn from the mind control, Gorgan appeared there and urged the children to up the level of the mind control. That's when Tommy Starnes planted in Renn's mind the image of if the Vaelor diverted course away from Marcus XII, the ship would be destroyed by any number of swords that were formed in rings around the ship. Renn was freed from the mind control once the children were freed from the influence of Gorgan. 
Renn was rendered unconscious by the Eymorg Kara when she boarded the Vaelor and used her control bracelet in order to steal Sareth's brain. He was later part of the bridge discussion, with Velthar, Yuri and Adisa, regarding where to look for Sareth's brain, in the Sigma Draconis system, when it was stolen by Kara.

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text: When Sareth mind melded with Medusan Ambassador Kollos to guide the Vaelor back to normal space from being stranded in an uncharted void of the galaxy, by the then dead Larry Marvick, Sareth-Kollos took over the helm console from Renn and was assisted in the task by Yuri at navigation. Unfortunately Sareth-Kollos forgot to put back on the visor, which caused Sareth to go temporarily insane while still on the bridge. In this temporary insanity, he pushed very hard backwards, Renn and Yuri, who were trying to help him with Renn ending up being pushed into the Spear leader's chair on his rear end. Fortunately Renn recovered quickly, and Sareth did so as well, a short time after that.

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text: When Velthar was trapped in the interphase of Tholian space aboard the MV Kinrath and was thought possibly dead, Renn attended Velthar's memorial service. Fortunately Velthar was beamed aboard the Vaelor a short time later, still alive.

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text: Renn was part of a four-man landing party that went to investigate an unusual planet whose size was approximately that of Luna, yet mass and atmosphere were similar to Tellura and geologically was only a few thousand years older. But even before the landing party made it to the planet, they got to witness as they were in the process of phasic descent down a mysterious woman touch the shoulder of the quantum translocator operator and killing him. But the mystery and danger didn't stop there. Shortly after the landing party beamed down to the planet, the planet was struck by an unusual and strong earthquake for a planet so young geologically.

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text: Then senior geologist D'Amato said his scan slate registered an almost immeasurable powerful energy burst. Velthar couldn't raise the Vaelor with his sortequip vox and Renn discovered the Vaelor wasn't even in orbit anymore, effectively stranding them. Renn and Halst both tried to theorize what might have happened to the ship, with Renn suggesting it blew up and Halst suggesting it hit the planet. But Velthar rejected both theories due to the lack of residual radiation. The landing party became concerned because there was no sign of water, and only a virus-like plant parasite on the planet, and all the vegetation was poisonous to Terrans.
