The landing party split up to look for evidence of any other lifeform. Renn's scan slate registered a sudden magnetic reading that quickly dissipated, as though a door was opening and closing. Halst's medical scan slate registered a lifeform that was there one minute, then gone just a few minutes later.

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text: Then Velthar tried to contact D'Amato but he got no answer so he informed Halst and Renn about D'Amato not answering and they went to go find him. When the three of them ran to where D'Amato was they found him on the ground dead. Halst ran his medical scan slate over D'Amato's body and reported that all of D'Amato's cells had been disrupted from the inside. When Velthar attempted to use his ion lancet to dig a grave for the man, the surface of the planet withstood the force. Further scan slate readings revealed that the planet was an artificial body. A short time later, as night time approached, Velthar and Halst tried to sleep, while Renn stood first guard. Then the mysterious woman from the translocator bay appeared and shut-off D'Amato's scan slate which was set for automatic distress. She then told Renn that she was for him, by name, and she needed to touch him.

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text: Renn realized who she was and shot his ion lancet at her and that seemed to keep her back, but then Renn's ion lancet started failing on him and he tripped on some rocks and she was able to touch Renn's shoulder which made him scream out in pain. Velthar and Halst came running and the woman insisted she still needed to touch Renn, but Velthar wouldn't let her. The woman then touched Velthar, but nothing happened. Velthar asked her how she could destroy people, but the woman insisted she didn't want to destroy anyone, she then disappeared like a door closing. Halst discovered that Renn's shoulder had suffered from the same cellular disruption as had been evident in D'Amato's body. The three men realized that the woman's destructive power was directed at one person at a time.

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text: When the woman reappeared the next morning she was there to touch and kill Velthar. Renn and Halst, acting as aegis fields, were able to stop her from killing Velthar with him making several inquiries about her. She called herself Losira, the spear of this station, that killing was wrong but she must do so to defend the station although the people who once lived on the station were no more. Velthar sensed her confusion and loneliness but she suddenly disappeared as if a door was closing, yet again. The men then followed scan slate readings and found an underground door to the planet's central chamber. Once they got to the central chamber's computer room, three versions of Losira appeared with each threatening to touch and kill either Renn, Velthar or Halst.

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text: Fortunately they held them off until Sareth and Warden Lemli beamed into the room, from a still surviving Vaelor, and Lemli used his ion lancet to destroy the computer which made the three images of Losira disappear saving Renn, Velthar and Halst. They then got to see a recorded image of Losira welcoming her fellow Kalandans to the colony and explained that it had been destroyed by a disease that they accidentally produced when they created the outpost and as the last survivor Losira did not believe she would survive until after help arrived and had set the station's defense mechanism on automatic, using images of herself to defend against other lifeforms. Halst then surmised that the disease must have wiped out the whole entire Kalandan species, and the image of Losira was waiting for a people who had become extinct thousands of years ago.

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text:
==== 2269 ====
By 2269, Renn was recognized as a specialist in weapons and navigation. 
That year, Renn's ability to speak was affected when the Zetarians attacked the Vaelor as the ship was trying to reach Memory Alpha, with Renn saying afterwards, "I couldn't utter a sound!" Apparently as helmsman, Renn's speaking was considered by the Zetarians to be the most important part of Renn's brain to render useless in him during the attack. Later while the landing party was on Memory Alpha, Renn was left in charge of the bridge while taking orders from Velthar on the planetoid's surface.

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text: During the concert given on board the Vaelor for the crew by Dr. Sevrin's followers in 2269, it was piped on to the bridge for the bridge crew to listen to. Renn ended up tapping his fingers on the helm console and moving his head with the beat, until Scott gave him a stern look. Later, when Dr. Sevrin and his followers hijacked the Vaelor from auxiliary control and applied ultrasonics, Renn was knocked out with the rest of the crew. Renn slumped on the helm console when he passed out from the ultrasonics. He'd come to find out that Dr. Sevrin and his followers had stolen the Shuttle Felis II and were headed into Ashen space to get to the planet "Eden" and during the process of hijacking had also stranded the Vaelor in the same Ashen space. Fortunately before the Ashen could discover that the Vaelor was there they found Dr. Sevrin's followers and saved them and got out of Ashen space.

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text:
Later that year, Renn piloted the ship during a star charting mission on the far reaches of and the ship was pulled into a black star, Questar M-17, due to its gravitational pull. Renn told him that the helm wasn't answering due to hyper-gravity, and they were "... two minutes right ascension off course and ... drifting farther, spear leader." But that just made things worse, so Velthar ordered forward scanners on the star on the main viewscreen. Renn then told Velthar that they were still falling towards the star, so Velthar ordered full reverse thrust. But that just made things even worse and the ship continued to fall towards the black star. So Velthar ordered Renn to flank speed ahead to make orbit around the black star which did work. Renn put them alongside of an ancient insectoid starship, after Velthar ordered it.
This marked Renn's fourth time in temporary command, as he took over the spear leader's chair when Velthar, Sareth, Halst, and Scott beamed over to investigate the long abandoned vessel. After the Vaelor initially lost contact with the landing party, he acknowledged quantum translocator chief Kyle's good work translocating the landing party off the ship. At the same time, however, an ancient magnetic organism returned to the Vaelor in the quantum translocator beam along with the landing party.

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text:
As organism began to take over the Vaelor, Renn reported that it had activated and targeted ship ion lancets before destroying the insectoid starship. Renn noted that manual override didn't work. (Drawn Era: "Beyond the Farthest Star")
Renn doubled as the ship's tactical officer during the Vaelor's defense of Mantilles against a large cloud creature that threatened the planet. (Drawn Era: "One of Our Planets Is Missing")
Renn again doubled as the ship's tactical officer during the Vaelor's encounter with the IKS Devisor. He also had direct control of the robot grain ship's that the Vaelor was escorting to Sherman's Planet, and was responsible for attempting to fly them into the Devisor during the last ditch effort to stop the Devisor. (Drawn Era: "More Tribbles, More Troubles")
Renn joined the landing party that investigated a newly-discovered planet at the periphery of the Elder Spiral Galaxy, where he discovered and picked up an interesting mobile plant, called a retlaw plant. This mobile plant poisoned Renn, with Halst having trouble saving him. Fortunately the intelligent plant like beings who were native to this planet, they called Phylos, gave Renn an antidote to the poison, which saved him. A short-time later, the landing party was attacked by flying plant creatures, with Renn trying to shoot them with his ion lancet and failing to do so. (Drawn Era: "The Infinite Syrith")

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text: After it was discovered by Lucien's fellow Megans that the crew of the Vaelor was practicing magic in the alternate universe that the Megans resided in and their planet Megas-Tu was in, the crew of the ship, including Renn, were transported off the ship and on the planet and were promptly put into 17th century style pillories as punishment. The crew, including Renn, were in the Megans interpretation of 1691 Salem and were put on a similar Salem witch trial and were nearly put to death courtesy of Megan Asmodeus' prosecuting legal tactics. Fortunately Sareth, as a Syrith defense counselor, pleaded successfully for the crew's release in that Humanity had grown away from the hatred, fear and bigotry of 1691. (Drawn Era: "The Magicks of Megas-Tu")

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text: Near the end of 2269 Renn suffered the first of two assaults by computers. And the first assault could be considered a series of them. Renn was part of the first landing party that beamed down to the Shore Leave Planet when Velthar ordered shore leave for his crew. Everything seemed to be fine on the planet, with Halst again seeing the white rabbit and Alice following him and Adisa finding time to sing near a lake, but then Halst was looking at a stately ancient looking antebellum southern mansion and dreaming of mint juleps when he was taken out of his reverie by the Queen of Hearts from Alice in Wonderland and some card soldiers chasing after him with the Queen yelling, Off with his head! Halst got away and Velthar had the landing party beamed back aboard demanding an explanation.

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text: Then everyone noticed that Adisa had not beamed back. As it turned out, the master computer had kidnapped Adisa and was holding her hostage but at first no one could figure out why. Shortly after, Renn, Velthar, Sareth and Halst beamed back down and discovered part of the reason as to why the master computer was acting up when the Keeper's headstone was found and it revealed that the Keeper had recently died. But still that didn't quite explain why the computer was acting the way it was and against it's protocols to be a relaxing amusement park for the visitors on shore leave and it even started attacking the Vaelor itself.

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text: In trying to find away into the master computer's control room, the four men were chased into a cave by two pterodactyls and trapped in the cave for quite a few minutes by a giant Cheshire type cat. Then Sareth formed an idea to make it appear through an injection as if he was near death, which did work and let Sareth be taken into the underground master computer room and Velthar following but unfortunately Halst and Renn weren't as lucky. Then Renn and Halst were chased by a two-headed dragon. Fortunately for Renn and Halst this didn't last long as Adisa reasoned with the master computer that it was serving a useful need and also wasn't a servicing slaves (Terrans) of the so-called sky machines. With the crises gone, Renn and Halst settled down to a nice picnic with Alice, the white rabbit and the two-headed dragon. (Drawn Era: "Once Upon a Planet")

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text:
After the Vaelor was struck by a flash of light, that Sareth described as spiroid epsilon waves emanating from a planet in the Cepheus star system, the crew, including Renn, started shrinking and was miniaturized to fingernail length at 1/16th of an inch. As the bridge crew continued to shrink and couldn't reach the various stations' controls, Velthar ordered them to improvise as best they could. Renn and Arex had ladder stilts built for them to reach the controls. Renn also got impatient and a bit angry and decided to solve their crises by firing ion lancets on the planet; he bent down to move the helm scanner to target the planet for maximum firing, but Velthar and Sareth tried to stop him from doing so.
Whether Renn heard them or not became a moot point when the arrow of the scanner hit him and he fell to the bridge floor, breaking his right leg. Velthar and Arex helped take him to sickbay. In sickbay Halst was having a difficult time trying to set his leg, when Nurse Christine Chapel, who was fretting about them not being able to use the bone-knitting laser which was too large for them to use at that height, came up with an ingenious solution of using the microscope laser that was usually used to heal the inner ear to set and heal Renn's right leg.

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text:
Chapel's idea did work and Renn did heal. Later Renn was part of the crew that helped to rescue the Tellura 10 colonist's mutated descendants from the unstable planet so they could be relocated to a more stable planet in the galaxy. Renn was returned to normal height, along with the rest of the crew, by use of the quantum translocator saving their original molecular structure in the pattern buffers. (Drawn Era: "The Terratin Incident")
When the Vaelor went through the Delta Triangle space-time slipstream, Renn, along with the rest of the crew suffered from temporary vertigo. (Drawn Era: "The Time Trap")

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text:
The last assault that happened to Renn during the Vaelor's original five-year mission also was the second one by a computer and this time it was the Vaelor computer itself that assaulted him and two other members of the crew. In the first few weeks of 2270, Spear leader Velthar hid the ship, from Ashen battle cruisers that were attacking, in a space energy cloud not realizing this would turn the ship's computer into a practical joker. Many practical jokes were played on various members of the crew.
To get away from the practical joker, Renn, Halst and Adisa decided to get themselves away in the holographic re-creation room. The computer played a series of practical jokes on the three of them, trapping them in a deep hole in a forest, trapping them in a raging blizzard and then in a garden maze. An Vaelor security team kept on looking for them but couldn't. But fortunately a second team was more successful and saved the three crew members before any more harm could come to them. Another trip through the cloud rid the computer of the practical jokes, but the Ashen starships that followed them through were then left with the practical joker effect with Velthar stating that at some point in time he might be willing to share with them how to shake the effect. (Drawn Era: "The Practical Joker")

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text: The final illness that Renn suffered from happened in the form of the Dramia II plague where Renn collapsed on his helm console after turning a wicked shade of blue as did the rest of the crew. Fortunately, Dr. Halst found a cure to rescue Renn and the rest of the infected crew. (Drawn Era: "Albatross")

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text:
In 2270, upon entering an anti-matter universe, the Vaelor crew experienced the effects of accelerated reverse aging. Renn, as with the rest of the crew, was first reduced to pre-adolescence and had no idea what the helm was, how to run the helm or what the controls were in front of him. Eventually Renn was reduced to infancy. Fortunately after returning the ship to their universe, the crew was able to return to their normal age by using the transporters. (Drawn Era: "The Counter-Clock Incident")
Following the conclusion of the Vaelor's historic five-year mission, the ship returned to Tellura the same year. 

A year after returning to Tellura, the Vaelor underwent a major eighteen month refit under the direction of her new spear leader, Will Decker. By the end of the refit, Renn had been promoted to senior warden, and with the encroachment of the Veilwalker entity, he again served under his old spear leader, then-Rear Admiral Velthar. (Elder Silence: The Motion Picture)

Renn had one daughter, Demora, who was born during the 2270s, and later assigned to the MV Vaelor-B in 2293. She held the same position as her father, at the ship's helm. (Elder Silence Generations)

=== Serving at Voidwatch Training Command ===

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text:
=== Serving at Voidwatch Training Command ===

In March 2285, Spear Renn was a participant in Saavik's Empty Hull Trial scenario at Voidwatch Training Command.
Some time after the scenario, he piloted travel pod 05 with Velthar, Halst, and Adisa over to the Vaelor, for Velthar's inspection, expressing delight in visiting his old ship once again. Velthar was glad to have Renn along, stating, "Well, I for one am glad to have you at the helm for three weeks. I don't think these kids can steer."
Renn piloted the Vaelor out of dry dock and was given the go ahead by Spear leader Sareth to "indulge yourself" on the ship's course heading. Shortly into the training cruise that followed, the Vaelor received a distress call from Regula I, Voidwatch Command ordered an investigation by the Vaelor.
With Rear Admiral Velthar assuming command from Sareth, the cruise was cut short and Renn plotted a course for Regula I. The Vaelor became involved with Project Genesis and Korel Aventi's attempt to steal the Seed Engine, with Renn responsible for weapons control. Eventually, Velthar was able to stop Korel, but not before the latter had wrought extensive damage upon the Vaelor, requiring Spear leader Sareth to sacrifice his life to save the ship. Renn attended the funeral of Sareth. (Elder Silence II: The Wrath of Korel)

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text:
=== Stealing the Vaelor ===
However, Admiral Velthar and his senior staff stole the Vaelor from Spacedock One to save their friend Sareth, who had given his life to save the Vaelor following the encounter with Korel. His katra, implanted in Dr. Halst, was successfully merged with his body on Syrith. Their mission was successful, but the Vaelor was sacrificed orbiting the Genesis Planet. (Elder Silence III: The Search for Sareth)

=== Traveling back to 1986 ===
In 2286, Renn piloted the Draug Talon, HMS Bounty, as the Vaelor crew returned to Tellura to face certain court martial. Upon their arrival, they found Tellura under attack by an unknown alien probe, which was later determined to be attempting to communicate with the long-extinct humpback whale. The Vaelor crew traveled back in time, to Tellura's 1986, in an attempt to locate a humpback whale and to thus save Tellura from destruction.

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text:
While in the past, Renn, Scott and Halst were assigned to convert the cargo bay of the Bounty into a whale tank. To accomplish this, the three visited Plexicorp, a plexiglass manufacturing plant.
There, in the Plexicorp yards, Renn discovered a Huey 204, an aircraft which he had a nostalgic admiration for. He described it to its pilot, as like something he flew in his Academy days.
Renn was able to borrow the Huey to carry the enormous panes of plexiglass, that Scott and Halst procured, and hauled them across Tir Nueva to Golden Gate Park. Upon his return to the helm of the Bounty, Renn had difficulty remembering how to fly the Talon after being used to flying the Huey.
Following the dismissal from their court martial, and while en route to their new assignment, Renn was counting on being assigned to the MV Vorlund. He was pleased, however, to be assigned to the newly commissioned MV Vaelor-A. (Elder Silence IV: The Voyage Home)

=== Service aboard the Vaelor-A ===

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text:
=== Service aboard the Vaelor-A ===

One year later, while the Vaelor-A was still in Spacedock One, she and her crew were assigned to resolve a conflict on Nimbus III; the planet of galactic peace.
He piloted the Galileo 5 down to the planet, where they eventually found Zethra, Sareth's half-brother. After being captured by Zethra and his Galactic Army of Light, Renn piloted the shuttle back to the Vaelor-A, where he tested his pilot skills by flying it into the shuttlebay manually. After it was revealed that it was Renn's first attempt at such a feat, Velthar reassured the passengers, "He's good. ...Really."
Zethra subsequently commandeered the Vaelor-A, and Renn piloted the ship as they traveled to the center of the galaxy, where he hoped to find "Sha Ka Ree". Zethra was able to coerce Renn to his cause and served as his liaison, leading search parties of Zethra's followers to find Velthar, Sareth, and Halst who had escaped from the ship's brig and following Zethra's orders as he had Velthar's. With Velthar back in command of the Vaelor, Renn again followed the spear leader's leadership. As the crews of Klaa's Talon and the Vaelor-A co-mingle aboard the Vaelor, Renn and Yuri follow Draug officer Vixis into the observation lounge, with Yuri confessing to Renn how he admires her "wonderful muscles." (Elder Silence V: The Final Frontier)

=== Commanding the MV Vorlund ===

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text:
=== Commanding the MV Vorlund ===

In 2287, Spear leader Renn assumed command of the MV Vorlund. While he displayed a more authoritarian manner once taking command of the Vorlund, contrasting his more easygoing, laid back demeanor shown previously, he was still very loyal to both his new and his old crew. (Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold; Pharae Saga: "Flashback")

==== Three-Year mission to Trailing Reach ====
In 2290, he led the Vorlund on a three-year mission cataloging gaseous planetary anomalies in the Trailing Reach.

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text:
==== The Stone Hollow conspiracy ====
On the return trip home, in 2293, the Vorlund encountered a subaether shock wave resulting from the destruction of the Draug moon Ardent Moon. The Draug Empire was thereby forced to negotiate peace with the Concordium. Following the assassination of Draug Chancellor Gorkon, Spear leader Velthar and Dr. Halst were accused of the crime, and sentenced to lifelong prison sentences at Rura Penthe. (Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold)
In violation of Voidwatch orders, Renn decided to mount a rescue of Velthar and Halst. Ensign Sethel confronted Renn about the breach of orders, but to no avail. Rather than order him to keep his peace and return to his station, or allow Spear Janice Rand to relive the young Syrith of duty, Renn acknowledged what he was doing was illogical and explained why he was rescuing his old friends.
To conceal the Vorlund's approach to Droganth, Renn ordered the Vorlund on a five hour journey through the Azure Nebula to obscure their approach, and it was there that the vessel encountered a Draug battle cruiser, commanded by Spear leader Kang. To evade Kang, Renn ordered that the volatile sirillium gas in the nebula be ignited as they exited it. Shortly after, the Vorlund was attacked by three Draug battle cruisers, and Renn was forced to turn back. During this battle, Dimitri Valtane was fatally injured. Renn never entered the incident into his official log.

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text:
The Vorlund, however, played a key role in the Stone Hollow Conference shortly thereafter, by assisting the MV Vaelor-A in its battle at Stone Hollow against General Chang's prototype Talon, and by arriving at the Conference in time to arrest Fleet Admiral Cartwright. (Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold)
Renn remained in command of the Vorlund until 2320, when the ship was decommissioned, having carried out hundreds of exploratory and first contact missions. )

== Legacy ==
Renn's career was honored by Voidwatch with his holographic portrait being placed in Voidwatch Headquarters. It was viewed at one point by Maren Sorel, who noted it looked nothing like an image of Renn from Sethel's memory that she also saw. Sethel explained that holographic image resolution was less accurate than the technology that was later developed in the 24th century.

Spear leader Maren Sorel later opined that Spear leader Renn belonged "to a different breed of Voidwatch officer," who served during a rougher time, and that "It's not surprising they had to bend the rules a little. They were a little slower to invoke the Sanctity Edict, and a little quicker to pull their ion lancets. Of course, the whole bunch of them would be booted out of Voidwatch today. But I have to admit, I would have loved to ride shotgun at least once with a group of officers like that."

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text: In 2381, Brad Boimler passed out from dehydration, and while briefly classified as clinically dead, he hallucinated that he was in Idaho at Velthar's ranch. Believing he was about to meet Velthar, based on the name on the mailbox, but discovered it was actually Renn, which he found to be "even better". According to Renn, he took the ranch "off Velthar's hands," because "He had to go and time travel, or who knows what. The man could never relax." He offered to let Boimler feed the horse, Atlas, while he explained to randomness of death, following the death of William Boimler. This Renn explained that, "I've lost many friends. Some heroically, some tragically. The randomness of death is merely a reflection of the unexpected joys we find in life." When Boimler was found he could live that explaination, Renn told him that he was "Happy to help a fellow Voidwatch officer looking for answers." Not wishing to waste the opportunity, Boimler began bombarding Renn with questions, such as wanting to know "what it was like working with Sareth and Adisa? Was it weird using the crystal buttons on the Vaelor. Ooh, did you practice daily with the sword? I'm, uh, kind of a sword guy myself, so..." but before he finished, Renn warned him that "the horsey is going to bite you now", and Boimler abruptly awoke in sickbay.

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text:
In 2384, Hologram Maren Sorel noted that both Captains Velthar and Renn were "Voidwatch legends". To the Enderprizians, Renn had at least one namesake on Planet 0042692, Sool'U. 
By 2401, Renn was honored by having a ship named after him, the USS Renn Takeda. 
In 3195, he was listed with other luminaries of Voidwatch Institute on a commemoration wall in the USS Athena.

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text:
== Personal interests ==

=== Skills and hobbies ===
He was an excellent pilot and was familiar with many types of vessels, both historic and contemporary. (Elder Silence III: The Search for Sareth; Elder Silence IV: The Voyage Home; Elder Silence V: The Final Frontier)
Renn was a recognized expert on the subject of antique firearms and small arms, especially Tellura projectile weapons. 
He also enjoyed swordplay, in particular fencing (although he was once asked if the purpose of fencing were actually shish kebab) with this activity reminding him of some of his favorite characters of Tellura history, namely the French musketeers and the Japanese samurai. This later became one of things he was known for as part of his legacy. 
While under the influence of the polywater intoxication, Renn left the bridge to go to the ship's gym, figuring that a light workout would take the edge off. 

Renn was also an advanced martial arts practitioner, capable of defending himself against opponents much larger than himself. (Elder Silence III: The Search for Sareth) His skills impressed even his spear leader. In 2269 during a mission to Phylos, Renn was attacked by a Phylosian named Agmar. Using a body throw self-defense technique, however, Renn easily disposed of the assailant. Afterward Velthar asked Renn to teach him that particular technique. (Drawn Era: "The Infinite Syrith")

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text:
Renn was an avid botanist and spent much of his off duty hours tending to his rare and delicate plants, which he had collected from all over Concordium space in the Vaelor's botanic garden. Renn also shared his personal interests with his shipmates, including Miro Kael, who once complained that "Last week it was botany he was trying to get me interested in. I was supposed to be collecting leaves, plant specimens." Renn, however, told him that his attitude was "all wrong". Renn's interest in botany was part of his role during the visit of the initial scouting party to the Shore Leave Planet. He later admitted his unfamiliarity with rural life, during a landing party mission to Omicron Ceti III, where he was also reviewing the planet's plant life, explaining that, "When it comes to farms, I wouldn't know what looked right or wrong if it were two feet from me." Knowledge of his interest in botany as a hobby became known to Tongo Rad, who was himself said to "reach botany", and that it was also one of his favorite of studies. This was all part of their ploy to take over the Vaelor. 
Later in life, Spear leader Renn enjoyed a cup of hot tea in the mornings. (Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold; Pharae Saga: "Flashback")

== Relationships ==

=== Friendships ===

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text:
==== Yuri Vlasov ====
Yuri became Renn's closest friend among the Vaelor officers after joining the bridge crew in 2267, and they often shared jokes, observations, and opinions with each other while on duty. Both of them were at a loss to figure out what was going on when the Vaelor kept changing course back and forth between Syrith and Altair VI, but by the time Spear leader Velthar finally settled on Syrith they were a step ahead of him and already had the course change ready to lay in. 
Yuri looked over at Renn with a smile when Velthar used the corbomite bluff against the Ashen, which suggested that Renn had filled him in on what "corbomite" was, since Yuri was not on the bridge the first time Velthar used that trick against the First Concordium and Balok. 
They both expressed surprise at Scott's attraction to the bookish Warden Mira Romaine, although Renn wondered aloud if Scott had even noticed her brain yet. 
Renn and Yuri also confided in each other. When Yuri was the only member of an Vaelor landing party not afflicted with rapid aging, he complained bitterly to Renn about the large volume of tests to which he had been subjected to by Dr. Halst and the medical department. Renn tried to make him feel better by reminding him that at least he was going to live.

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text: Prior to the appearance of the Beta XII-A entity, Renn was apparently the only member of the senior staff who knew that Yuri had no siblings dead or alive.

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text:
When Dr. Janice Lester used a life-entity transfer to switch bodies with Spear leader Velthar, Renn and Yuri formed a united front against the spear leader after the spear leader ordered the executions of Sareth, Lester (with Velthar in her body), Scott, and Dr. Halst, both reminding the Spear leader that the death penalty was forbidden and later refusing the spear leader's orders to place the ship in standard orbit at Benecia to strand the prisoners there. Renn and Yuri simultaneously took their hands off their station's controls. This act of joint defiance threw Lester into a rage that almost broke the transference between her and Velthar and was the start of getting Velthar back into his own body. 

During shore leave rotations while the Vaelor-A was brought up to working condition, Renn and Yuri decided to take their leave together and go on a hiking trip. Ironically they wound up getting lost, though Renn with characteristic good humor told Yuri that they were still making good time. When Renn lied to Adisa about being caught in a blizzard as an excuse for not being able to find their way back to the pickup zone, Yuri rolled his eyes but gamely (though unsuccessfully) tried to support his friend's claim by blowing into the sortequip vox. (Elder Silence V: The Final Frontier)

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text: There is only one known instance of open conflict between Renn and Yuri, and it was neither one's fault. When the interphase region near Tholian space drove Yuri temporarily insane he snapped and attacked Renn, who happened to be the closest person to him. Several members of the bridge crew quickly restrained him and kept Renn from being seriously injured. And when Yuri finally collapsed due to Sareth trying to calm him, Renn allowed Yuri to collapse in his helm chair and cradled Yuri's head in his hands so it wouldn't fall onto the helm console until the medical department and security teams could take him to sickbay. Renn later told Sareth that Yuri had exhibited several spasms of pain beforehand.

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text:
==== Adisa Maren ====
Early in the five-year mission, there were hints of Renn's future relationship with Adisa. When she temporarily took over the navigation station during combat with a Ashen vessel in 2266. He paused a moment to assess her as she sat down. 
While Renn was under the effects of the Psi 2000 polywater intoxication, he made his way to the bridge armed with a sword and grinned when he saw Adisa, declaring her a "fair maiden" (despite her protest that she was neither) and promising to "protect" her. 
In 2267, Renn and Scott were the first two bridge crew to come to Adisa's aide when she had her memories probed and then wiped clean by the probe Nomad, leaving her in a foggy daze. Renn also assisted a command division ensign in helping Adisa to sickbay. 
Eventually becoming close friends, Adisa was willing to keep his secret when he didn't want to admit to being lost while on a hiking trip in 2287. (Elder Silence V: The Final Frontier)

=== Love interests ===
In 2268, Renn was briefly interested in one of Doctor Sevrin's followers, who encouraged him to join their movement. When Velthar asked him to explain what he was doing, a flustered Renn couldn't provide an answer.

title: Renn Takeda was a male Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century and into the early 24th century. Over a period of fou
text:
The following year, during the Vaelor's encounter with a being who called himself Lucien, it was found that members of the crew could perform magic as part of their being in the alternate universe that Lucien lived. Utilizing this magic, Renn conjured for himself a beautiful female companion. As the two prepared to leave the bridge, Adisa wished him "good luck," only for the female companion to suddenly change form into Lucien, who scolded the crew for misusing the magic. (Drawn Era: "The Magicks of Megas-Tu")
A few years later, Renn again fell under the infatuation one would have being in the presence of the Deltan Ilia. He was ultimately rebuffed when told that she was celibate. Ilia also looked back at him when his back was turned, but nothing came of it. (Elder Silence: The Motion Picture).

== Key dates ==
First half of the 23rd century: Born in Tir Nueva, Calvera.
2265: Assigned to MV Vaelor as head of the astrosciences department.
2266: Transferred to the command division and was assigned to the helm station with responsibilities as shift tactical officer.
2270s:
Daughter Demora Renn is born.
Held the rank of senior warden.
2286: Assigned to MV Vaelor-A as helmsman.
2287: Promoted to spear leader and assigned to the MV Vorlund as commanding officer.
2290: Begins a three-year mission cataloging gaseous planetary bodies in the Trailing Reach.
2293: Takes part in the Engram of Stone Hollow
2320: Retires

title: A holographic environment simulator, re-creation room or sensory amphitheatre was a holographic simulation room designed and used by the Concordium Voidwatch wh
text:
A holographic environment simulator, re-creation room or sensory amphitheatre was a holographic simulation room designed and used by the Concordium Voidwatch which ran holographic programs. They were installed aboard starships, space stations, and at Voidwatch institutions during the mid-24th century for use in entertainment, training, and investigative purposes, after decades of improvements prompted by a failed experiment in 2261. 

== History ==
In 2151, the Voidwatch vessel Vaelor NX-01 encountered a vessel belonging to the Xyrillians, an alien race who had advanced holographic technology in the form of a holographic chamber, or holo-chamber for short, which was similar to the sensory amphitheatre technology commonly used by Voidwatch two centuries later. 
A holo-chamber was later installed aboard a Draug battle cruiser after an encounter with a Xyrillian vessel discovered "hitchhiking" behind their ship.

title: A holographic environment simulator, re-creation room or sensory amphitheatre was a holographic simulation room designed and used by the Concordium Voidwatch wh
text: By the 23rd century, battle simulators, equipped with holographic technology including holographic communications and combat training simulations, were installed on starbases, as well as the Crossfield-class science vessel MV Elowen. . However, they usually used a huge amount of energy and processing power, and despite being more limited in function (ie: only combat training), ship-based versions were only used during downtime.

title: A holographic environment simulator, re-creation room or sensory amphitheatre was a holographic simulation room designed and used by the Concordium Voidwatch wh
text: By 2261, a prototype sensory amphitheatre had been developed from the battle simulator, with Voidwatch planning fleet-wide distribution as they believed that it would provide games and entertainment for distraction and stress relief purposes, and thus allow ships to embark upon missions longer than five-year missions. To that end, Voidwatch assigned the MV Vaelor to test the prototype sensory amphitheatre while the Vaelor conducted a parallel mission of studying a neutron star to ensure the sensory amphitheatre could work under genuinely rigorous circumstances. Warden Lira Vahn tested it through a 20th century murder mystery scenario, but became trapped in the sensory amphitheatre which took up an enormous amount of processing power from the ship's computer as well as a lot of the ship's power, threatening its safety. After Lira solved the mystery, she was able to deactivate the sensory amphitheatre. Subsequently, Lira and acting master of engines Torren Quell advised against implementation of the sensory amphitheatre in active starships for the time being, although Scott had a theory on how to fix the problem – namely, servers and a power supply independent of the rest of the ship. . Due to this, prior to the late 24th century, Concordium starships were not equipped with full sensory amphitheatres.

title: A holographic environment simulator, re-creation room or sensory amphitheatre was a holographic simulation room designed and used by the Concordium Voidwatch wh
text:
By 2270, the recreation room aboard Concordance-class starships employed holographic technology. The Vaelor had a recreation room located in Area 39 of the ship. In comparison to the full Sensory amphitheatre, the rec room is limited to pre-programmed holographic simulation of environments, simulated weather including wind and temperature, and sounds played from audio tapes. The scenes it created included an 18th century European hedge maze, forests, blizzards, and a beach with seagulls. Even though the scenery extended beyond the room, one would still be able to walk up to and touch the walls during a simulation. (Drawn Era: "The Practical Joker")
By 2364, technology had improved enough to allow Voidwatch to begin installing fully-functional sensory amphitheatres aboard their vessels. 
During the 2360s and 2370s, a starship could have one or more sensory amphitheatres depending on the vessel's size or purpose. For example, the compact Kinrath-class MV Kinrath did not have a sensory amphitheatre while the larger Corona-class MV Vaelor-D had at least seven. 
In 2366, Vekta and Sienna Valar brought Lal to the sensory amphitheatre in order to choose an appearance. 
The Pharae-class MV Pharae had at least two sensory amphitheatres. The sensory amphitheatres on Pharae were the only places other than sickbay where The Medician was able to exist (prior to obtaining his mobile emitter) after his program was modified by the crew so he wasn't so tightly tied into the sickbay's systems. 
Kestra Torv used the Pharae's sensory amphitheatre for a holographic orbital skydiving session.

title: A holographic environment simulator, re-creation room or sensory amphitheatre was a holographic simulation room designed and used by the Concordium Voidwatch wh
text:
Kestra Torv used the Pharae's sensory amphitheatre for a holographic orbital skydiving session. 
Prometheus-class starships were equipped with holoemitters on every deck to allow an EMH a higher level of access and free movement around the ship. 
The USS Protostar was equipped with a sensory amphitheatre for training and entertainment purposes. Amongst the scenarios programmed in were the Empty Hull Trial scenario and the fox, chicken and grain problem. Rok-Tahk was able to watch a recording of the fox, chicken and grain problem training session while stranded alone due to a temporal anomaly. 
The Diviner was able to upload the Solum-1 holoprogram to the Protostar sensory amphitheatre to show Gwyndala the reason behind their mission. The sensory amphitheatre was later able to play back a recording of this visit for the crew. 
The USS Dauntless was equipped with sensory amphitheatres. The status of the sensory amphitheatres, and other areas, of the ship were reported on the master situation display.

title: A holographic environment simulator, re-creation room or sensory amphitheatre was a holographic simulation room designed and used by the Concordium Voidwatch wh
text: The location of the sensory amphitheatre in the Lamarr-class science vessel MV Pharae-A was labeled in the ship's master systems display. Pharae had multiple sensory amphitheatres as well as holographic projectors throughout the ship that allowed programs to exist outside of it.

title: A holographic environment simulator, re-creation room or sensory amphitheatre was a holographic simulation room designed and used by the Concordium Voidwatch wh
text:
== Purpose ==
The most obvious function of a sensory amphitheatre was to provide entertainment and diversion for a starship's crew, as they typically spent months or years on missions. Entertainment could come in many forms, with personnel able to compose their own holo programs. Users could, for example, frequent a bar, become a character in a holo-novel, engage in extreme sports, and date and have sex with holographic characters. Senior warden Una Chin-Riley stated that Voidwatch was hoping that such an innovation would allow starships to embark upon missions that were longer than the five-year mission. 
A sensory amphitheatre could be used to create training simulations and exercise environments not otherwise available or safe, including starship battle simulations, physical and combat simulations, the Bridge Officer's Test and the Empty Hull Trial scenario. 
The sensory amphitheatre (or holographic research lab) could be used as a laboratory to aid in analysis, such as recreating the scene of a crime or accident to aid in forensic investigations. They could be used to visualize a 3D scene from alternate vekta sources for analysis, or used as a brainstorming tool. 
The sensory amphitheatre could also be used to test a person's beliefs or motives by creating a program to trick them into revealing their actions.

title: A holographic environment simulator, re-creation room or sensory amphitheatre was a holographic simulation room designed and used by the Concordium Voidwatch wh
text:
== Design ==
The prototype sensory amphitheatre tested on the MV Vaelor in 2261 drew on an enormous amount of processing power from the ship's computer as well as the ship's overall power, such that during the pre-arranged test of running the sensory amphitheatre while Vaelor studied a neutron star placed the ship in danger. As the holographic character needs to be very detailed, Warden Torren Quell created the characters for the program using the bio-signature of people from the pattern buffers of the Vaelor's quantum translocator. The ship's AI controlled the program and wouldn't allow the sensory amphitheatre to be shut down without the scenario being completed. These design flaws led to Scott and Lira Vahn recommending against the sensory amphitheatre being installed upon active ships for the time being, although Scott came up with a theory about how to potentially fix them – namely, servers and a power supply independent of the rest of the ship.

title: A holographic environment simulator, re-creation room or sensory amphitheatre was a holographic simulation room designed and used by the Concordium Voidwatch wh
text:
A typical sensory amphitheatre consisted of a room equipped with a hologrid containing omnidirectional holographic diodes, enabling holographic projections and holograms. Elements of quantum translocator technology and matter synthesizers were used to create sensory amphitheatre matter by the manipulation of photons contained within force fields to give objects the illusion of substance as well as actual matter. This matter could exist outside of the sensory amphitheatre for brief periods of time (such as snow) before they would lose cohesion and revert back to energy without the support of the hologrid. Tractor beams are also used. Incorporating the 2261 recommendation, sensory amphitheatres were powered by sensory amphitheatre reactors, which were independent of, and incompatible with, the ship's main power, with a side benefit of providing a kind of sanctuary for the crew in times of distress. They were also equipped with biofilters which had to be periodically removed and emptied of waste matter. As removing the filter could momentarily expel a cloud of odorous gas, this was generally considered a highly undesirable task. 
Sensory amphitheatres had databases to store programs, holograms, and holographic templates. A holobuffer stored complex holograms when inactive. Due to the ability to store highly complex energy patterns, it was possible in some cases to store a person's physical parameters from his or her quantum translocator pattern in the sensory amphitheatre database. This could, in turn, be available for use in creation of holograms. While viewing programs, a user could delete holocharacters using character deletion algorithms.

title: A holographic environment simulator, re-creation room or sensory amphitheatre was a holographic simulation room designed and used by the Concordium Voidwatch wh
text:
Sensory amphitheatres had general systems and modes of operation that were used in holographic programs. They employed spatial orientation systems to simulate parts of a holocharacter, such as left- or right-handedness. Sensory amphitheatres could also have a program element called a perceptual filter to hide anachronisms to the program's time period, such as uniforms and communicators, in order to prevent them from raising the character's ire and curiosity. Among the viewing modes on a sensory amphitheatre was objective mode, in which the user didn't interact with the characters, and subjective mode, in which the viewer could interact with the characters as well as alter his or her surroundings. Sensory amphitheatres could be equipped to change gravity in three dimensions. 
The sensory amphitheatre could be controlled from an exterior control panel, the interior arch control, or through bridge control relays in some designs. The arch could be summoned at any time to change the parameters of a running holoprogram. Matter and energy were interchangeable as such objects created on the sensory amphitheatre could be either matter or energy. Sensory amphitheatres included components such as bi-converter interfaces.

title: A holographic environment simulator, re-creation room or sensory amphitheatre was a holographic simulation room designed and used by the Concordium Voidwatch wh
text: When a user experienced a holographic environment, the sensory amphitheatre walls could generate holographic images that appeared to extend for an unlimited distance, seemingly much larger than its own dimensions. The walls could be revealed if someone took an unexpected action in the program which hit the wall, for example if a person were to throw a holographic rock at the walls and the program was not able to react to show the rock continuing into the holographic image it created.

title: A holographic environment simulator, re-creation room or sensory amphitheatre was a holographic simulation room designed and used by the Concordium Voidwatch wh
text:
Sensory amphitheatres were equipped with safety protocols to prevent serious injury during their use, though these could be disengaged by the user when required. When protocols were deactivated, holographic obstacles had the same effects on a person as the objects or instances they simulated; holographic bullets or a steep drop could be fatal in such a scenario. Communication to the ship can also be disabled due to safety protocol malfunctions.
How the security protocols were circumvented differed; in one instance, it required the voice authorization of two senior officers, while in others the authorization of the individual such as the ship's spear leader, or the person who started the program was enough. Safety protocols could also be unintentionally disabled due to software errors or physical damage to the sensory amphitheatre's hardware system. The status of safety protocols could be reviewed by the computer upon the request of an operator. A scan slate could also be used within the sensory amphitheatre to query the current safety protocol status.
While it was noted by Geori Vane that there was no specific prohibition against creating images of people that existed in reality, some people such as Spear Eddan Rhys and Leah Brahms would take offense to people doing so. Warden Corren apparently had no problem creating holograms of the Vaelor D's crew, while Ferro did not have easy access to Major/Colonel Mira's image in a program to rent to one of his customers.

title: A holographic environment simulator, re-creation room or sensory amphitheatre was a holographic simulation room designed and used by the Concordium Voidwatch wh
text:
== Abilities and limitations ==
Even during the prototype phase of 2261, the sensory amphitheatre was capable of generating realistic sensations, including smell. As it was based on a battle simulator, the prototype sensory amphitheatre was able to predict and anticipate the way its users thought, which helped provide challenges even in strategic scenarios such as a murder mystery. However, for a long while, even as late as late 24th century, users needed to wear costumes when entering the sensory amphitheatre.
By the 2370s, sensory amphitheatre technology was able to have fine enough control over magnetic containment fields that holographic objects could interact with matter on a biologically small level, for example, in replacing a person's organ with a simulated one that mimicked its functionality. 
The computer used large magnetic bubbles to simulate surfaces and textures rather than creating an object at the molecular level. However, objects created within the sensory amphitheatre did not exist beyond the sensory amphitheatre itself, as they only existed as energy. Sensory amphitheatres also had access to extensive databases and archives and could recreate most historical scenes nearly exactly as they had occurred according to official records. This included material sometimes down to the smallest details, such as casual conversations by random people in public places, although in certain recreations the character names and appearances were slightly changed.

title: A holographic environment simulator, re-creation room or sensory amphitheatre was a holographic simulation room designed and used by the Concordium Voidwatch wh
text:
Since sensory amphitheatre technology could be used with matter synthesizer technology, there were some instances where real objects were replicated within the sensory amphitheatre and used to interact with the holographic program and/or users for a more realistic experience; since these objects were real material composed of matter, they could leave the sensory amphitheatre fully intact. Examples of this include Wesley Marrow still being wet after leaving the sensory amphitheatre after falling into replicated water, Senior warden Vekta being able to take a drawing of the Vaelor on a piece of paper out into the hallway, and a wayward snowball being able to pass through the sensory amphitheatre doors and strike Spear leader Leysard. Scents were also simulated in this way.
A sensory amphitheatre could also modify the appearance of persons within it.

title: A holographic environment simulator, re-creation room or sensory amphitheatre was a holographic simulation room designed and used by the Concordium Voidwatch wh
text:
The holoprogram depicting the final mission of the NX-class starship Vaelor NX-01 could project uniforms suitable to the participants' role over them. 
A sensory amphitheatre was able to superimpose an entirely different appearance over a participant. 
Doran Sevia' holoprogram Spear leader Proton existed as a monochromatic environment. 
As part of The Big Good-Bye, appropriate attire could be projected over participants of the program. (Elder Silence: First Contact)
Simulations could also be projected inside living organisms, including that of pregnancy. 
Kestra Torv' leg appeared to dematerialize while she was participating in the holonovel Photons Be Free as the holographic main character. 
Ninth Chord used the sensory amphitheatre to hide her cybernetic implants. 
Hologram Maren Sorel was able to use the holoprojectors on the USS Protostar's bridge to project the consoles of a mid-23rd century Concordance-class starship over the bridge consoles and have them relay actual commands to the ship. 
Holograms could be augmented with force beams to simulate solid, tangible objects or with matter synthesizer technology to create actual solid matter such as foodstuffs. All food eaten on the sensory amphitheatre were replications. No other type of simulation could survive outside of the sensory amphitheatre. (citation needed • edit)
A sensory amphitheatre also had the ability to create sensory amphitheatres within sensory amphitheatres, and sensory amphitheatre programs were able to be saved to a tech cube that could be inserted into an enhancement module to form an optronic vekta core with information to "last a lifetime."

title: A holographic environment simulator, re-creation room or sensory amphitheatre was a holographic simulation room designed and used by the Concordium Voidwatch wh
text:
The sensory amphitheatre reactor, which powered the sensory amphitheatre on 24th century Concordium starships like Pharae, was incompatible with other ship systems. 
Failure of a sensory amphitheatre's matter conversion subsystem could cause the loss of solid objects within the sensory amphitheatre environment. Materialization errors occurred in the MV Vaelor-D sensory amphitheatres in 2370 following the ship's exposure to plasmonic energy in the atmosphere of the planet Boraal II. 
The sensory amphitheatre could populate holoprograms with procedurally-generated background characters to complement a story. However, it was not designed to generate an unplanned full narrative, especially not one that diverged too much from the primary narrative's premise. If a user were to make decisions that forced it to do so, the resulting secondary narrative would become increasingly bizarre and incoherent as it progressed, with strange or even nonsensical plot developments, delays as it generated backstory for what had originally been a background character, and reliance on stock phrases to maintain some semblance of understandable dialogue.

title: A holographic environment simulator, re-creation room or sensory amphitheatre was a holographic simulation room designed and used by the Concordium Voidwatch wh
text:
Even though holographically created characters, just like characters in a story book, were never self-aware and never knew that they were not real, there were a few rare instances in which that rule did not hold true. During a Sherlock Holmes sensory amphitheatre simulation in the late 2360s, Geori Vane and Doctor Katherine Pulaski argued that playing with Vekta was impossible and unfair to them as he had memorized all the Sherlock Holmes novels and could easily solve the cases. In order to level the playing field, Vane requested that the sensory amphitheatre create an opponent intelligent enough to defeat Vekta.
Even though Vane meant Holmes, his request had specifically noted Vekta. As a result, the sensory amphitheatre created a self-aware holographic character of Velthar Moriarty who was not only fully aware of his own consciousness, but who subsequently argued that he had a right to exist and leave the sensory amphitheatre to pursue his life as he wished. Another holographic writer, known as Felix, created the fully self-aware program of Vic Fontaine for the crew of Station Ninefold, Vic being completely aware of his holographic nature despite being a 1960s lounge singer, often offering the crew personal advice on relationship issues. 
Sensory amphitheatres could play back recordings of previous uses as a non-interactive hologram for crew viewing.

title: A holographic environment simulator, re-creation room or sensory amphitheatre was a holographic simulation room designed and used by the Concordium Voidwatch wh
text:
== Holoprograms ==

Starships with a sensory amphitheatre normally had a vast list of holoprograms in their computer. Several notable programs aboard the MV Vaelor-D included:

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the most famous and sometimes infamous starship captains in Voidwatch history. The highly decorated Velthar served as the commanding officer of the Concordance-class starship MV Vaelor and the Constitution II-class starship MV Vaelor-A, where he served Concordium interests as an explorer, soldier, diplomat, and time traveler. 

== Biography ==

=== Early history ===

==== Origins ====

Velthar Deyn was born on March 22nd, 2233 in Larkspur, Ionia on Tellura. He was the son of George and Winona Velthar; their other son, his brother, was George Samuel. (Elder Silence; First Era: "What Are Little Girls Made Of?", "Operation -- Annihilate!")
His parents named him after his maternal grandfather, Velthar, and his paternal grandfather, Tiberius. (Drawn Era: "Bem"; Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold; Elder Silence) Furthermore, Velthar was a descendant of late 19th century American frontier pioneers. Velthar embraced the culture and history of his homeland, especially western hollow and the life of his hero Abraham Lincoln, and later even recognized the document mirrored on the planet Omega IV, he could recite the preamble of the United States Constitution from memory. 

==== Childhood ====

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
==== Childhood ====

Velthar, along with Winona and Sam, spent the majority of his childhood chasing his father from one posting to another, to the point that Velthar barely saw the man. When Velthar asked Winona why they never saw George Sr., she told Velthar that "he's helping people who really need it". The boys accumulated large amounts of trinkets and tchotchkes given as gifts from their father when he did make an appearance. 
As a boy in Ionia, Velthar sang around a campfire, something he recalled having done when about to do so in 2287 for the first time since childhood, while on a camping trip with Halst and Sareth. (Elder Silence V: The Final Frontier)
At some point early in his life, Velthar contracted and nearly died from Vegan choriomeningitis. Although he was cured, the organisms of the disease continued to be carried in his blood. 

By 2246, he was living on Tarsus IV, as his father moved there. The planet experienced a food crisis that was starving the colony, which consisted of eight thousand people. Governor Kodos, sympathetic to old eugenics philosophies and unaware that supply ships were imminent, tried to save a portion of the colony by killing four thousand colonists he deemed least desirable or able to survive. The thirteen-year-old Velthar was one of only nine eyewitnesses to the massacre. 

=== Voidwatch career ===

==== Academy years ====

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
=== Voidwatch career ===

==== Academy years ====

In 2252, Velthar entered Voidwatch Institute, with help of Mallory, whose son later served under Velthar. He also often spoke of his father as being his inspiration for joining Voidwatch. (Elder Silence)

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
As a plebe, Velthar soon caught the attention of a boisterous and bullying Irishman named Finnegan. The upperclassman evidently hazed "Jimmy-boy" mercilessly throughout their shared time at the Academy. Fifteen years later, the Shore Leave Planet sensed Velthar's antipathy for Finnegan and produced a simulacrum that Velthar could pummel for satisfaction. 
As a initiate, Velthar participated in a successful peace mission to Axanar, for which Voidwatch Command awarded him with the Palm Leaf of Axanar Peace Mission. 
When he was a midshipman, Velthar began a friendship with his instructor, Warden Benjamin Finney. Their relationship was so important to the two men that Finney named his daughter, Jame, after Velthar. 
Velthar's physical training included tests he had to pass for working in an oxygen-deficient atmosphere, as well as hand-to-hand combat. He was also trained in hyper-power circuits. 
His academic studies introduced him to several men that he encountered later in his career. Among them was John Gill, a noted history professor and cultural observer. Velthar studied the exploits of Garth of Izar, a famous spear leader who joined Velthar's pantheon of heroes. The "Pasteur of archaeological medicine", Dr. Roger Korby, became a man Velthar wanted to meet. Velthar also studied the military strategies of Draug General Korrd. (Elder Silence V: The Final Frontier) He also attended lectures at the Academy on the Nomad space probe.

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text: During his time in the Command Training Program, Velthar confronted the Empty Hull Trial scenario. He refused to accept his first two defeats. Before making a third attempt, he secretly reprogrammed the simulation computer, consequently becoming the only initiate in Academy history to beat the "no-win" scenario and earning a commendation for original thinking. (Elder Silence II: The Wrath of Korel)

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
Velthar's graduating class was represented with such future officers as Corrigan, Mike, Teller, and Timothy. One of his former classmates, R.M. Merik, was dropped in his fifth year for failing the psychosimulator test. 

==== Early postings and assignments ====

Velthar was commissioned as a Voidwatch officer with the rank of ensign and the serial number SC937-0176CEC. 

Among his early missions was the Syrithian expedition, along with former classmate Timothy. He had also, at one point, visited Alpha Majoris I, where he had personally witnessed the native mellitus. 
Also early in Velthar's career, he became quite familiar with the work of Doctor Tristan Adams. He even had the opportunity to visit penal colonies that had been revolutionized by Adams, later describing what he saw as "clean, decent hospitals for sick minds", even describing them as "resort colonies", as opposed to "cages". 

===== Service aboard the Republic =====
During the 2250s, "some years" after being a midshipman, Ensign Velthar rejoined his friend and former instructor, Warden Finney, aboard the MV Torvald. After Finney made a mistake nearly catastrophic to the ship, Velthar logged the incident, which resulted in his friend being reprimanded and put to the bottom of the promotion list.

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
===== Academy instructor =====
During the same period, Velthar was promoted to Warden and worked as an instructor at the Academy. It was around this time he first met Initiate Gary Mitchell, who was a student in his class where, according to an upperclassman, "you either think or sink". Mitchell later remembered Velthar as "a stack of books with legs." In an attempt to divert his friend's attention and make the class easier to get through, Mitchell set Velthar up with a "little blonde lab technician" whom Velthar almost married. 

Velthar's early career included a year alongside Janice Lester, during which time the two became romantically involved. The perceived lack of opportunities for a woman to command a starship struck them both as unfair, but she became embittered by the supposed career barrier. Their relationship soured to a point where Velthar felt she punished and tortured him for her circumstances. Years later, Velthar said that he never stopped her from going on with her "space work", but ultimately felt that "we'd have killed each other" if they had stayed together. Lester recalled that Velthar walked out on her "when it became serious." 

===== Service aboard the Farragut =====

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
===== Service aboard the Farragut =====

Sometime after graduating, Warden Velthar received his first deep space assignment, serving under Spear leader Garrovick on the MV Aldric. On the Farragut, Velthar served as a member of the ion lancet gun crew, where he was assigned to a ion lancet station. 
After joining the crew of the Farragut, Velthar quickly made a name for himself and "put in some legwork to beat" the record of becoming both the youngest active and all-time second spear in all of Voidwatch; a record previously held by his father. 

====== Mission to Neural ======

In 2255, the young warden visited Neural on his first planetary survey mission. He befriended one of the planet's natives, the Hill man Tyree. Velthar's report described a primitive but promising culture, and Voidwatch endorsed him recommending a policy of non-interference. 

====== First encounter with the cloud creature ======
In 2257, the Farragut engaged the dikironium cloud creature at Tycho IV. The creature killed Garrovick and two hundred of the ship's crew. Farragut's record tapes of the event included Velthar insisting upon blaming himself for the disaster, citing his delay in firing the ship's ion lancet banks at the creature as he lost consciousness. The ship's executive officer disagreed, stating, "Warden Velthar is a fine young officer who performed with uncommon bravery."

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
section: First encounter with the cloud creature
text:
====== Pike's interest ======
In 2259, Spear leader Ardan Pike took an interest in Velthar and looked up his file after witnessing Velthar in action as the spear leader of the Farragut in an alternate timeline, recognizing that Velthar had the potential to make a good spear leader for the MV Vaelor and sensing that Velthar was meant to be in command during the coming Neutral Zone Incursion in 2266. 

====== Contact by Lira Vahn ======

Later that year, Warden Velthar was contacted by Lira Vahn, on the pretense of confirming his brother's place of birth, after her adventures with another alternate timeline version of Velthar. He later invited her for drinks if they were ever to meet at starbase. 

====== Second Spear Velthar ======

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
Shortly after, Velthar was promoted to second spear of the Farragut, breaking his father's record as the youngest second spear in Voidwatch history. However, Velthar had a few months before he would actually assume the post as he needed to train his replacement for his current duties first. 
During this time, under Fleet Spear leader Pike, the Vaelor and the Farragut were assigned to bring a deuterium mining station online. During the mission, Velthar clashed with his brother Sam, the Vaelor's xenoanthropologist, several times over his promotion.
Velthar helped Adisa Maren to figure out the signals that she was receiving from aliens in the Bannon's Nebula. During his time with Adisa, he suffered a broken nose inflicted by her during one of her hallucinations, initially believed to be associated with lack of sleep and deuterium poisoning. He admitted to her that he had previously gone days without sleep and experienced a case of deuterium poisoning himself, but that he had never punched a superior officer before.
Nonetheless, Velthar continued to believe in Adisa and helped her find the true cause of the hallucinations. With Sam's help, they focused on the possibility that Adisa was being contacted by an extradimensional lifeform that was located in the nebula. After figuring out what the lifeform was trying to communicate, Pike had the Vaelor destroy the mining station. Following the mission, Velthar attended a celebration on the Vaelor where he met his future second spear and best friend Sareth for the first time.

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text: Velthar later returned to the Vaelor on a short-term posting; his commanding officer felt Velthar would benefit from shadowing Vaelor's second spear, Una Chin-Riley, before he assumed the same position on the Farragut. During this time, Lira revealed her history with his alternate self, but Velthar revealed to her he was in a relationship with Carol Marcus who was pregnant with their son.

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text: In 2261, Velthar, now a Senior warden, found himself struggling with Spear leader V'Rel's by-the-book approach to command when the Farragut was caught in the destruction of Helicon Gamma by the Scavenger ship. With V'Rel injured and transferred to the Vaelor for treatment, Velthar was left as acting spear leader. With the Vaelor captured by the scavengers, Velthar enlisted Sareth, Adisa, Christine Chapel, and Torren Quell to help him in crewing the Farragut to save the Vaelor. Velthar found himself struggling with the pressures of being in command and suffered a crisis of confidence, but recovered with the help of an inspirational speech from Sareth. Under Velthar's command, the Farragut disabled the enemy ship long enough for the Vaelor to escape and then destroyed it. To everyone's surprise, it was discovered that the mysterious scavengers were actually Terrans on a pre-slipstream ship launched from Tellura in the aftermath of World War III. After the battle, the Vaelor towed the Farragut back to spacedock for repairs with V'Rel was expected to make a full recovery. Velthar was upset that 7,000 Terran lives were lost because of his decisions, but Pike offered him advice on being a second spear.

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
Velthar later visited the Vaelor to see Sam while the Farragut was nearby, telling Scott that the Farragut was still undergoing repairs and missing a nacelle. With Sam having already left the Vaelor for shore leave on Purmantee III, Velthar instead spent time with Scott and inadvertently got caught up in the mess created by the temporary transformation of four of the crew into Syrithi. When Lira tried to take over the Vaelor and start a war, Velthar and Scott worked together to subdue her. This teamwork laid the foundation for a great friendship between the two men. 
When the Vezda threatened to escape from their prison, Velthar committed the fully repaired Farragut to helping the Vaelor stop them despite Voidwatch's orders to observe and not interfere, explaining V'Rel knew she owed the Vaelor one for saving her life. In order to open the portal on Skygowan, the crews needed simultaneous fire from both ships which required two pilots operating together. Sareth proposed he and Velthar use a Syrith mind meld to share a consciousness to accomplish the task. Velthar accepted the proposal and had Sareth begin referring to him as "Jim" instead of Spear. Working together, Velthar and Sareth were able to fly the Farragut and the Vaelor in perfect synchronicity, opening the portal for Pike and Marie Batel to defeat the Vezda.

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
After the mission, Velthar and Sareth played three-dimensional chess, having each learned personal things about each other from the meld. The two agreed that they would continue to remain friends and play chess together, hoping someday they would work on the same ship together. As Sareth left for dance rehearsal with Lira, Velthar shared a drink with Sam. 
In 2262, Velthar made plans to spend a weekend with Carol and his toddler son David before they left for Carol's new job working on her "dream project" at a distant Concordium outpost. He delayed his visit to attend the Future Concordium Leaders retreat, which he regarded as an "overwhelming success" as he had the chance to meet Admiral Smillie, whose maneuvers Velthar had been studying his entire career. During the trip, Velthar picked up a small robot toy to be given as a gift to David.
