title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
After Velthar discovered emotional rage was the key to nullifying the effect of the pod plants, his first step in retrieving his crew was to taunt Sareth into anger. Anticipating the result of a Syrith's higher strength level pitted against his own, Velthar wielded a pipe for protection. After being called an "elf with a hyperactive thyroid" and told that he belonged "in the circus, right next to the dog-faced boy," Sareth indeed lost control, nearly killing Velthar before resuming command of himself. 
In 2267, Sareth began his pon farr mating cycle, and behaved bizarrely aboard the Vaelor. Velthar called to Sareth "the best second spear in the fleet" and "an enormous asset to me" as he pled with Sareth to explain his actions. When told that by taking Sareth to Syrith, against Voidwatch orders, Velthar fired back, "I owe him [Sareth] my life a dozen times over! Isn't that worth a career?"
Joining him on Syrith for his marriage ceremony, Velthar was drawn into T'Pring's scheme to marry another, and forced to fight Sareth to the death. Halst, knowing Velthar was endangered, faked Velthar's death, and the marriage was not consummated. Sareth, despondent that he had murdered his spear leader, thrilled at the sight of Velthar alive, exclaiming, "JIM!", which Halst delighted in needling Sareth about once he gained his composure.

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
Velthar's understanding of Sareth had an enormous impact on the parallel mirror universe, visited after a quantum translocator accident in 2267. As Velthar's party prepared to return to their proper universe, Velthar implored the mirror-Sareth to re-examine his role in the fascistic Terran Empire, insisting, "One man can make a difference." Mirror-Sareth's consideration of those words led to his rise to dominance and reform of the Empire, with drastic consequences. 
When Velthar was trapped in spatial interphase during a rescue operation in Tholian space, Sareth ordered the Vaelor to maintain her position in an effort to retrieve him, in spite of the danger the Tholians presented and the disruptive nature of the local space. After Velthar's assumed death, Sareth and Halst viewed the "last orders" Velthar had prepared. He urged Sareth to use all the Syrith disciplines at his disposal, tempered with intuitive insight. Velthar believed Sareth had the latter qualities, but should they elude him, he was urged to seek out Halst. 
Velthar once commented to Spear leader Garth that the dream of the Axanar Peace Mission participants made him and Sareth "brothers." Sareth only said, "Spear leader Velthar speaks somewhat figuratively, and with undue emotion, but what he says is logical and I do, in fact, agree with it."

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text: When Dr. Janice Lester, a former lover of Velthar's, took over Velthar's body, Sareth performed a mind meld on Velthar while he was trapped in Lester's body. Sareth believed Velthar was Lester before anyone else, and when Lester as Velthar ordered his execution, he continued to stand by his friend.

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text: At the end of the Vaelor's five-year mission, a period marked by his frequent loss of his emotional control, Sareth chose to leave Voidwatch and his friends, to pursue the Kolinahr discipline of logic on Syrith. His return to Vaelor during the Veilwalker threat was a cold event, without acknowledgment of his past friendships. In Veilwalker's aftermath, Sareth finally achieved equilibrium, able to express his friendship for Velthar without the influence of aliens or illness, and notably lacking any threat of physical violence. (Elder Silence: The Motion Picture) In 2285, Sareth was calmly able to tell Velthar, "You are my superior officer. You are also my friend. I have been and always shall be yours." (Elder Silence II: The Wrath of Korel)

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
Sareth's sacrifice of his own life, to save the Vaelor from Korel's detonation of the Seed Engine, deeply affected Velthar. At his funeral, Velthar could only bring himself to say of Sareth, "Of all the souls I have encountered in my travels, his was the most... Terran..." but he broke off and broke down without being able to continue. (Elder Silence II: The Wrath of Korel)
The revelation that Sareth's katra, his "living spirit" (actually his complete brain patterns), survived in the tormented mind of Halst, led Velthar to risk his career, and in turn, his crew's. He first asked Admiral Morrow for permission to retrieve Sareth's body from the Genesis Planet, to bring it, and Halst, to Syrith. Velthar insisted that any chance to save Sareth's soul was his responsibility, "as surely as if it were my very own." His request declined, he told his crew, "The word...is 'No.' I am therefore going anyway."
With the help of Adisa, Scott, Renn, and Yuri, Velthar rescued Halst from confinement and commandeered the Vaelor from Spacedock One. The renegade mission saw the destruction of Velthar's ship and the death of his son. Finding Sareth's body re-animated by Genesis, Velthar brought him and Halst to Syrith for the fal-tor-pan (re-fusion) ritual. The first person Sareth recognized was Velthar: "Jim. Your name...is Jim." (Elder Silence III: The Search for Sareth)

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text: During their homecoming from Syrith, and eventually their trip to 1986, Velthar tried to remind the resurrected Sareth, suffering from memory loss, to their friendship and past adventures together. After Velthar's and the command crew's trial, Sareth told his father, Thanev, that his "associates" were his friends. (Elder Silence IV: The Voyage Home)

text:
In 2287, the trio enjoyed a camping trip together at Yosemite National Park, which abruptly ended when Sareth, half-brother Zethra diverted the Vaelor to Nimbus III. After their adventure on Sha Ka Ree and Zethra's death, Velthar referred to Sareth once again as his "brother," and told him and Halst that they were his real family. (Elder Silence V: The Final Frontier)
When Sareth later entered the Vex incursion reality, he told the Velthar Deyn of that reality of their deep friendship, despite the fact that the alternate Sareth had marooned Velthar on Delta Vega. During this meeting, Sareth called the alternate Velthar "old friend" several times and felt it was good to see a version of Velthar Deyn despite the terrible events of that day. Velthar, who had been accused of cheating on the Empty Hull Trial by the alternate Sareth, told Sareth Prime that his actions in changing history could be construed as cheating. Sareth nostalgically admitted that it was "a trick I learned from an old friend," referencing the prime Velthar.

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
When meeting with his alternate reality counterpart, Sareth Prime admitted to deceiving the alternate Velthar to force him and the alternate Sareth to work together to defeat Nero rather than intervening in the situation himself to make both men see the potential of their friendship. Sareth Prime explained it as "I could not deprive you of the revelation of all that you could accomplish together, of a friendship that will define you both in ways you cannot yet realize." He then encouraged the alternate Sareth to stay in Voidwatch and foster that friendship, something Sareth ultimately chose to do. (Elder Silence)
In 2263 of the alternate reality, the alternate Sareth discovered that even so long after Velthar's death, Sareth Prime kept a picture of him and the bridge crew of the Vaelor-A amongst his personal things. (Elder Silence Beyond)

text: ==== Brenic Halst ====

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
Doctor Brenic Halst became chief medical officer of the Vaelor after the departure of Dr. Mark Piper in 2265. Velthar formed an easy rapport with his new doctor, giving him the moniker "Bones" (as in the old-fashioned colloquialism "sawbones" for a doctor or a surgeon). Even after Halst began a program of exhaustive (and exhausting) quarterly physicals and interfered with Velthar's usual diet, their friendship grew rapidly. Halst was probably Velthar's closest friend, aside, of course, from Sareth. 
The demands of Velthar's career required his best possible health, which Dr. Halst closely oversaw. Velthar sparred with his crew in the Vaelor gymnasium for exercise. Quarterly physical checks tested his physical fitness as well as general health. In spite of his evident strength and conditioning, Velthar did tend to put on extra weight from time to time. Whenever Dr. Halst noticed such a gain, he was unafraid to adjust Velthar's diet card, at least once annoying his spear leader with a plate of dietary salad.

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
Velthar could count on Halst to express exactly what he thought, whenever he thought it, frequently without the courtesy of a question, and the medician was often the sharpest observer of Velthar's actions and character. An early act of constructive insubordination occurred when the Vaelor faced the ominous spacecraft Fesarius and Velthar seemed to be pushing young Warden Dave Bailey past his breaking point. Halst let his opinion loose from beside the spear leader's chair, and Velthar barked an angry reply--but this led Velthar to realize that poker, not chess as Sareth had postulated, was the game he and Spear Balok were really playing. Unintimidated by that angered reply to his unrestrained expression of opinion, Halst continued that behavior throughout their service together, earning a wide latitude with Velthar. 
The first time Halst saved Velthar's life, however, was not in surgery, but instead when Halst fired a ion lancet (which itself was unusual for Halst) in 2266. When the M-113 creature of planet M-113 attacked Velthar, it appeared to Halst as Nancy Crater, a past love and a particularly powerful impediment to inflict harm. With Sareth's help, Halst was able to see past the creature's camouflage, killing it before it killed Velthar.

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
During the original five-year mission, Velthar recorded a tape of last orders Spear Sareth and Chief Medical Officer Halst were to play upon his death. He urged Sareth and Halst to give each other the same trust and loyalty they had each shown him. 

Halst's retirement from Voidwatch in 2270 ended abruptly when Velthar, through Admiral Nogura, reactivated Halst's commission for the Vaelor's emergency deployment for the Veilwalker crisis. Velthar's plea,""Damn it, Bones, I need you--BADLY," ended Halst's objection to the unwelcome "draft" and he returned to his frequent duty station, hovering just behind the spear leader's chair. (Elder Silence: The Motion Picture)

In 2285, Halst advised a melancholic Velthar, while both were surrounded by Velthar's collection of genuine and simulated antiques, on his (Velthar's) birthday, "Get back your command. Get it back before you turn into part of this collection." He gestured to the collection and finished, "Before you really do grow old." (Elder Silence II: The Wrath of Korel)

Velthar's drastic action taken to save Sareth's katra was also an effort to save Halst from the anguishing burden of bearing Sareth's "marbles". After his moonlight requisition of the Vaelor resulted in the ship's destruction, burning through the Genesis planet's atmosphere, Velthar asked, "My God, Bones... what have I done?" Halst replied, "What you had to do, what you always do: turn death into a fighting chance to live." (Elder Silence III: The Search for Sareth)

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text: After the assassination of Draug Chancellor Gorkon, Velthar and Halst were imprisoned together on Rura Penthe. With the "help" of a shapeshifter named Martia, they were able to escape together and return to the Vaelor. (Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold)

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
==== Torren Quell ====
Torren Quell, the oldest of the Vaelor senior officers, was also the most consistently deferential to Velthar. While not included in Velthar's innermost circle with Sareth and Halst, Velthar had evident faith in Torren's capabilities as an engineer. Velthar pushed the Vaelor past her known limits many times, and the technical genius of his devoutly loyal "miracle worker" was regularly the key to success.
He later admitted that a big part of his reputation was his exaggeration of repair estimates, so that Velthar could be pleasantly surprised when Scott has them done quicker than he had expected. It became a running joke of sorts between the two later on. Scott and Velthar shared a passion for the Vaelor, but Torren's was a simpler, less complicated love for his "bairns". 
The two first became friends when Scott briefly served as Acting master of engines on the MV Aldric while Velthar was acting spear leader during a crisis. Although the two initially clashed, they came together as a team to save the Vaelor. Velthar, while later visiting the Vaelor, spent time with Scott and they stopped the rogue plans of a transformed Lira Vahn.

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text: As the ship's second officer, commanding the Vaelor while Velthar led a landing party, Scott's personal loyalty to Velthar served as a bulwark against various ambassadors or potentates who threatened mission success. Usually, Scott refrained from taking the spear leader's chair and hovered around the conn when left in command, as he always felt more comfortable in engineering than on the bridge in command of the ship. He took the center seat only when the situation was critical: scaring a Draug ship away from Capella IV, or defiantly facing down three Ashen battle cruisers and demanding his spear leader's return.

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
When escape from the mirror universe via the quantum translocator meant one of the Vaelor party had to stay behind to operate the controls, Scott stoically volunteered. After Velthar overrode him, Scott's one-word plea "Jim!" was one of the few times he familiarly addressed Velthar. 
Scott kept his temper throughout Korax's barrage of taunts and insults thrown at Velthar, but a cross word about the Vaelor led Scott to throw the first punch in the K-7 bar-fight of 2267. When Velthar, a little incredulous that his engineer had failed to defend his honor, confined Scott to quarters as punishment, the engineer beamed at the chance to catch up on technical manuals. 
Velthar observed Scott's infatuation with two young and attractive lieutenants, Carolyn Palamas and Mira Romaine, with bemused detachment at first, until the "stiff-necked thistle-head" abandoned his usual solid professionalism and required Velthar's stern, but affectionate, scolding. 

Velthar's socialization with Scott outside of the call of duty was rare. One exception, a visit to the flesh-pots of Argelius II, was a morale-boosting effort by Velthar on Scott's behalf. If Scott noticed the motivation, he didn't seem to care. Even after the horrific encounter with the Redjac entity, the "old Aberdeen pub-crawler" was eager to join Velthar on a second expedition to the planet. By 2285, Velthar knew enough about Scott's off-duty habits to detect the residue of a "wee bout" of shore leave at first glance.

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
When the Veilwalker threat forced the newly refitted Vaelor into duty, Scott protested with a litany of complaints about the rush and unready state of the starship. After Velthar revealed he had convinced Admiral Nogura to return his command, Scott responded, "Any man, who could manage such a feat... I would'na dare disappoint. She'll launch on time, sir, and she'll be ready." (Elder Silence: The Motion Picture)
In 2293, Scott accompanied Velthar, along with Yuri, to the christening ceremony of the Vaelor-B. Velthar expressed to Scott his surprise over Renn finding the time to make a family after encountering his daughter Demora. Scott reminded Velthar of a saying he always said, "If something's important, you make the time." Scott also commented on Velthar's seeming restlessness, asking him if he found retirement to be a little lonely. "You know, I'm glad you're an engineer. With tact like that, you'd make a lousy psychiatrist", Velthar replied to him. Later, Velthar was believed to be lost in a hull breach in deflector control caused by an energy tendril from the Nexus. Making his way to the heavily damaged area, Scott mourned the loss of his former commanding officer. (Elder Silence Generations)

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text: Upon being rematerialized in 2369 after spending 75 years in the USS Jenolan's quantum translocator buffer, by the Vaelor-D, to Scott's surprise that he was found by the Vaelor, Scott's immediate response was, "The Vaelor! I should have known! I bet Velthar Deyn himself hauled the old girl out of mothballs to come looking for me."

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
==== Renn Takeda ====

Though Renn Takeda was briefly an Vaelor physicist, he was transferred to the command division under Velthar's command, where Renn became the ship's senior helmsman throughout the historic five-year mission. Velthar relied on Renn as a capable officer he could trust with the Vaelor conn in battle situations and on away missions as delicate as the timeline-risky visit to the US 498th Airbase Group in Omaha, Nebraska, on Tellura in 1969. 

Renn risked his career for Velthar on two occasions. Conspiring with his friends, he assaulted a security guard to liberate Dr. Halst, and piloted the stolen Vaelor out of Tellura Spacedock to the Genesis planet in 2285. (Elder Silence III: The Search for Sareth) As spear leader of the Vorlund in 2293, he penetrated the Azure Nebula in Draug territory in an effort to rescue his former spear leader before he was forced to turn back, and he later joined Velthar in halting the Stone Hollow conspiracy. (Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold)
Outside of their careers, however, the friendship between Velthar and Renn was not especially close. Velthar was surprised to discover Renn had a daughter, Demora, on the maiden voyage of the Vaelor-B. Yuri had to remind him that he had actually met her before, twelve years prior. (Elder Silence Generations)

==== Janice Rand ====

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
Voidwatch assigned Janice Rand as Velthar's personal yeoman in 2266. Initially, he complained about the idea of a female yeoman, leading Halst to ask flatly, "What's the matter, Jim? Don't you trust yourself?" Velthar said he already had a female to worry about, and that the Vaelor was that female. Velthar warmed to Rand, but an undercurrent of sexual attraction between the two became obvious in stressful situations. Suffering from polywater intoxication in 2266, Velthar confided his attraction for Rand to Sareth, shouting that he had "a beautiful yeoman!" Velthar later reached out to her hesitantly, longing for her, but he could not approach her on account of his duty. 
A quantum translocator malfunction created a duplicate of the spear leader that contained his negative qualities, such as hostility, lust, and violence. That version of Velthar was consumed with lust and desire for Rand and went "on the prowl" to find her. Eventually, when they both were alone in her quarters, he slowly approached her. Besides being a little startled by his presence, it looked and felt normal for her, until she noticed the spear leader drinking from a bottle of Saurian brandy.

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
Obviously drunk, he started telling her that she was "too beautiful to ignore" and "too much woman." As he stalked closer to her, he claimed that they'd both been "pretending too long." Then, he suddenly grabbed her and began kissing her fiercely. The Velthar duplicate tried to pin her to the floor to rape her. But Rand defended herself, leaving a large scratch on her attacker's face, which helped the crew differentiate between the two Velthar "halves." After the situation was resolved, Rand continued as Velthar's yeoman until a reassignment in 2267. She returned to the Vaelor as quantum translocator chief in the 2270s. 
Velthar and Rand repeatedly felt an attraction for one another, but resisted discussing or acting on their feelings openly. During one mission, Rand, Velthar and other members of a landing party were trapped on a planet where only children survived; adults quickly developed a deadly virus which had been accidentally created by a life prolongation project on the planet. When Rand became upset, Velthar held her close in his arms and comforted her. Miri, a teenage girl whom the team had befriended, witnessed this and became jealous.

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
She felt that Rand was her "competition" and briefly betrayed the landing party by letting the other children abduct Rand. The spear leader's love for Rand became obvious when he was under stress from the disease, as he became distraught and obsessed in finding "his Janice," even grabbing Miri and shouting, "Where is she, Miri? Where is she, Miri? Where's Janice? Has something happened to her? Where is she? I've got to find Janice!"
Back aboard the Main Bridge, Velthar admitted, acknowledging that Miri's true age was far older than it appeared to be, "I never get involved with older women, Yeoman." Rand threw him an "Oh, really?" look in response.

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
==== Ben Finney ====
When Velthar was a midshipman, he befriended Academy instructor Warden Ben Finney. Some time later, Ensign Velthar and Finney served together aboard the MV Torvald. The two became so close that Finney named his daughter, Jame, after Velthar.
A rift developed between the two friends while aboard the Republic when Velthar logged a mistake that Finney had made which could have caused the destruction of the ship. Because of this, Finney was put on reprimand and his name was sent to the bottom of the promotion list. Finney blamed Velthar for his subsequent inability to gain a command of his own.
Though their friendship was effectively over, Senior warden Finney served aboard the Vaelor in 2267, as records officer. Velthar was unaware that Finney's old grudge had been growing larger over the years, and Finney had passed into madness. To take his revenge, he staged his own death and manufactured evidence of Velthar's negligence. Finney was successful to a point, and Velthar became the first Concordium Voidwatch starship spear brought before a court martial. With the help of the eccentric lawyer Samuel T. Cogley and Sareth, Finney's deception was revealed and charges against Velthar were lifted. Finney was arrested and faced trial, represented by Cogley. 

==== Corvin Leysard ====

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
==== Corvin Leysard ====

Although their association was brief, Velthar Deyn and Corvin Leysard had profound personal effects on one another. Very much like Sareth and Brenic Halst, Leysard was instrumental in helping Velthar find meaning in his life after his greatest adventures were essentially over.
Leysard embarked on Velthar's final adventure with the fabled spear leader, and allowed him to feel he had "made a difference" as he died, solidifying the younger spear leader's place of significance in Velthar's life. Leysard laid Velthar to rest on that obscure planet and was his lone mourner. (Elder Silence Generations)
The reciprocal impact, however, could also be seen in Leysard's career path. Taking Velthar's words to heart about the captaincy of the Vaelor being a position of importance and impact, Leysard resisted promotion to the admiralty for 10 years after his encounter with Velthar.

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
=== Romances ===
Often described as a ladies' man, Velthar was notably successful in attracting women, and enthusiastic in their pursuit, yet notoriously unsuccessful in establishing any lasting relationships with women – a fact his brother Sam tended to warn women about. By design or coincidence, his most significant affairs were with women fundamentally incompatible with his life in Voidwatch. In weighing the balance of starship versus a settled home life, the gross tonnage of the Vaelor usually tipped the scale. 
As Velthar became more and more well-known, these exploits became the stuff of legend; when Zaria Vesh, upon seeing Velthar while aboard the Vaelor during the Kinrath crew's trip over a hundred years into their past, mentioned how much more handsome "he" was in person, Spear leader Oren responded that Velthar had "quite the reputation" in terms of his dealing with women – though Vesh then admitted that the "he" to whom she had referred was actually Sareth. 
While attending the Academy, Velthar was romantically involved with at least two women.

==== Ruth ====

In 2252, another lover was a woman named Ruth. In 2267, he was greeted by a replica of Ruth that the Shore Leave Planet, in the Omicron Delta region, created. 

==== Janice Lester ====

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
In 2252, another lover was a woman named Ruth. In 2267, he was greeted by a replica of Ruth that the Shore Leave Planet, in the Omicron Delta region, created. 

==== Janice Lester ====

Velthar had a year-long relationship with Janice Lester while she also was at the Academy. He professed loving her, but the romance ended badly after "the intense hatred of her own womanhood made life with her impossible." The two were reunited in a truly bizarre manner in 2269, when Lester, extremely jealous of Velthar's successful career, traded her consciousness with that of Velthar's to take his place as spear leader of the Vaelor and then exact a double revenge by killing both Velthar and her womanhood. 
In the late 2250s, as an instructor at the Academy, Warden Velthar was romantically involved with a "blonde lab technician" whom Gary Mitchell had introduced him to. His relationship with her grew serious, as he almost married her. 

==== Lira Vahn ====

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
==== Lira Vahn ====

Velthar first met Lira Vahn in 2259 when Singh contacted Velthar on the pretense of confirming his brother's place of birth, after her adventures with another alternate timeline version of Velthar. He later invited her for drinks if they were ever to meet at starbase. 
They officially met later on when Velthar transported aboard the Vaelor. Velthar revealed to her details of his childhood and reminded Lira that she still owed him a drink. 
After they worked together trying to eliminate the subaether fold, Lira confessed to Velthar that she had fallen in love with an alternate version of him. She told him that she also liked the way Velthar looked at her now, but he said that while he felt a connection with her as well, he was presently in a relationship with Carol Marcus. 
In 2262, the two finally shared the long promised drink and decided to pursue a relationship. 
The next year, Velthar was visibly saddened when a time displaced Adisa asked him about Lira and dodged her questions about Lira's current whereabouts. 

==== Carol Marcus ====

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
==== Carol Marcus ====

Velthar was involved with Dr. Carol Marcus in the late 2250s. She was stationed at Starbase 1 in 2259 and was pregnant at the time, with their child, David. 
In 2262, Carol received her dream assignment at a distant outpost, and was scheduled to move there with young David. Carol and Velthar planned a final weekend together before their departure, but Velthar prioritized the Future Concordium Leaders retreat, and the investigation of the USS Griffin. By the time Velthar was rescued from the Griffin, Carol and David had left, and she had stopped answering his calls. 
Carol would eventually ask Velthar to stay out of her and David's lives entirely. In 2285, the fractured family unit was briefly reunited. (Elder Silence II: The Wrath of Korel;)

==== Janet Wallace ====

Velthar was involved with the future Janet Wallace in 2261; this relationship was also called off due to their difference in careers. 

==== Areel Shaw ====

In 2263, Velthar broke off a relationship with Areel Shaw. Velthar was reunited with Shaw four years later, when she was assigned as the prosecutor in his court martial, though Shaw was pleased when she lost the case and Velthar was exonerated of any wrongdoing. 

==== Helen Noel ====

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
==== Helen Noel ====

During an Vaelor lab's Christmas party in 2265, Velthar met Dr. Helen Noel and danced with her. He used her first name to address her and engaged in brief flirtation with Noel that ended unsatisfactorily for Velthar. He later exhibited irritation when Halst assigned her to help Velthar investigate Tantalus Penal Colony, and Velthar insisted on using her surname while working with her. Testing the neural neutralizer, Noel conditioned Velthar to believe that their previous encounter had been a sweeping romance. The colony's mad doctor, Tristan Adams, used the suggestion of love and loss of Noel to torture Velthar. 

==== Janice Rand ====

In 2266, the evil side of Velthar tried to assault and seduce Yeoman Rand. 

==== Miri ====

Also in 2266, Velthar met a girl called Miri, who was soon about to enter puberty, despite being about 300 years old chronologically speaking. Velthar piqued her interest by calling her "pretty" when they first met, and they went on to develop a close friendship. When the Vaelor left Miri (where Miri lived) shortly thereafter, Janice Rand told Velthar that Miri had really loved him. He accepted that, but said that he never got involved with older women. 

==== Lenore Karidian ====

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
==== Lenore Karidian ====

Later the same year, while on Planet HERALD, Velthar met Lenore Karidian at a party and entered into a brief romance with the then-nineteen-year-old blonde girl. As with many of Velthar's love affairs, the two fell in "love at first sight." Velthar was clearly enamored with Lenore, but the true depth of his feelings – and the importance of those feelings relative to his duties as a spear leader – were conveyed only through insinuation.
When Brenic Halst directly asked Velthar whether he really cared for the hopelessly insane Lenore, the spear leader paused pensively, then evaded the question with a navigational order: "Ahead slipstream factor one, Mr. Leslie." Halst's reply, "That's an answer," presumably indicated that he understood Velthar's unstated position: as spear leader, Velthar's priority was always the ship, despite his personal feelings for women such as Lenore. 

==== Edith Keeler ====

In 2267, Velthar and Sareth traveled back to the 1930s to repair damage to the timeline Brenic Halst accidentally caused. While searching for Halst, Velthar met and fell in love with the compassionate and far-seeing social worker Edith Keeler. Keeler's death was found to be the focal point in history needing repair. As she crossed a street to meet Velthar, he was forced to hold Halst back while an automobile struck and killed her, thus restoring the timeline. 

==== Sylvia ====

In 2267, the alien Sylvia tried to seduce Velthar into giving her the transmuter. 

==== Marlena Moreau ====

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
==== Sylvia ====

In 2267, the alien Sylvia tried to seduce Velthar into giving her the transmuter. 

==== Marlena Moreau ====

After 2267, Velthar had a near romance with Marlena Moreau. 

==== Drusilla ====

In 2268, while Velthar, Sareth, and Halst were held captive in a 20th century Roman Empire, a slave woman named Drusilla "seduced" Velthar. In The Autobiography of Velthar Deyn, Drusilla had a son named Eugenio (β), whom Halst believed to be Velthar's son from their intimate time together.}}

==== Kelinda ====

In the line of duty, to recover the Vaelor hijacked by Kelvans in 2268, Velthar seduced Kelinda, in order to arouse jealously in her spear, Rojan. Kelinda recognized Velthar's attempt at seduction, but welcomed his continued efforts. 

==== Elaan ====

On a peace mission to the war-torn Tellun system in 2268, the Vaelor transported Elaan, Dohlman of Elas, to her diplomatically-arranged wedding on Troyius. Velthar's antagonistic relationship with the arrogant and spoiled Dohlman changed sharply after her Elasian tears infected him. Under their powerful biochemical influence, Velthar became instantly and deeply infatuated with Elaan. He ultimately resisted the more compelling effects of the tears and fulfilled his duties, but both Elaan and Velthar experienced a tangible sense of loss at their melancholy final parting. 

==== Miramanee ====

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
==== Miramanee ====

In 2268, on the surface of the Amerind planet, an accident induced amnesia in Velthar and separated him from the Vaelor landing party.
For several months, Velthar lived among the Native American inhabitants, worshiped as a god called "Kirok". His mind at ease from the pressures of command, he took a wife, Miramanee, who became pregnant with his child.
When the tribal worship of Kirok was dispelled, he and Miramanee were stoned – fatally injuring both the young woman and their unborn child. 

==== Shahna ====

In 2268, when captured for the gladiatorial combats of Triskelion, Velthar was assigned to the tutelage of the drill-thrall Shahna. Velthar introduced Shahna to the wider universe around her, and the Terran concept of love. 

==== Deela ====

Deela was queen of the (infertile) male Scalosians who hijacked the Vaelor in 2268. They planned to use the male members of the ship's crew as a gene pool so her species could continue. Deela choose Velthar as her consort, who, along with the help of Sareth, was able to stop her plan. 

==== Marta ====
In 2269, the criminally-insane, pathologically-lying Orion inmate of the Elba II penal colony, Marta, became infatuated with Velthar while tending to him after torture. The fact that she loved him meant she had to kill him, but she failed in the attempt. Garth of Izar's jealousy led him to use Marta as a demonstration of a new explosive, killing her. 

==== Odona ====

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
==== Odona ====

Prime Minister Hodin of Gideon, a world greatly suffering from overpopulation, abducted Velthar and forced him to spend time isolated with his daughter, Odona, in 2269. As a carrier of Vegan choriomeningitis, it was hoped Velthar would infect Odona, and the rest of the population. The couple became quite affectionate in their time spent together, though Odona said Velthar "behaved like a perfect gentleman." 

==== Rayna Kapec ====

In 2269, Velthar's encounter with the near-immortal Flint led to their competition for the love of the android Rayna Kapec, and resulted in her destruction. Velthar was heartbroken. Sareth took an extraordinary liberty with his grieving friend, melding with Velthar without his consent, whispering the word "forget". 

==== Antonia ====

Velthar fell in love with Antonia after his first retirement from Voidwatch in 2281. The two lived together for some time before Velthar decided to rejoin Voidwatch. Later in life, he regretted not having proposed to her. He would later be reunited with a life like illusion of Antonia during his 75 years in the Nexus, which was, from a chronological standpoint, his longest-lasting romance. (Elder Silence Generations)

==== Martia ====

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
==== Martia ====

In 2293, Martia had a brief romance with Velthar to put him off his guard so he and Halst could be killed trying to escape. When he expressed his disgust over having kissed her, she, while in his form, quipped, "Must have been your lifelong ambition!" (However, it turned out to be Martia who was ultimately double-crossed and killed.) (Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold)

=== Enemies ===

==== Korel Aventi ====

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
One of the most violent rivalries of Velthar's life was the bitter feud between himself and 20th century Shardling dictator Korel Aventi.
In 2267, the Vaelor discovered Singh and his followers aboard the SS Botany Bay in cryogenic stasis, and awakened them. Unaware of Korel's true identity, Korel took advantage of Velthar's hospitality to familiarize himself with the Vaelor and its systems. After identifying Korel, Velthar had him restricted to quarters, prompting Korel to implement his plan to seize control of the Vaelor.
With the help of Warden Marla McGivers, Korel assumed control of the Vaelor. The Shardlings were eventually subdued with anaesthetic gas, and Velthar and Korel engaged in hand-to-hand combat in the engine room. Realizing he was no match for Korel's Shardling strength, Velthar subdued him with a heavy flow-control rod. After defeating Korel and his followers, Velthar exiled them to the then-habitable world of Ceti Alpha V.

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text: Korel later sought revenge against Velthar after McGivers had died in exile. By that time, Ceti Alpha V had lost its ability to support much of the life it had once sustained, as a result of the explosion of Ceti Alpha VI. To exact his revenge, Korel hijacked the MV Halcyon and stole the Seed Engine, whose research and development team included Velthar's old flame Carol Marcus and their son, David Marcus. The ensuing battle inside the Sable Drift crippled the Reliant, leading Korel to detonate Genesis in the hopes of taking Velthar and the Vaelor with him. Only the self-sacrifice of Spear leader Sareth allowed the Vaelor to escape the blast radius at slipstream speed. (Elder Silence II: The Wrath of Korel)

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
==== Gorthan ====
Velthar would more than once cross paths with the Draug officer Gorthan. They first encountered each other on Organia during the 2267 Concordium-Draug War. Velthar was posing as a native of the planet when Gorthan declared himself its military governor. Gorthan was immediately drawn to Velthar, admiring his spirit compared to the passive Organians, and appointed him as his liaison. He would not learn Velthar's real identity until after Velthar and Sareth had destroyed his supply depot. Gorthan noted he would have liked to face Velthar in battle and, even though he planned to have him executed and to use the mind scanner on him, joined him for a drink, where he noted his admiration for Voidwatch and claimed they were alike despite their ideological differences.
After Velthar had been freed by the Organians, he again confronted Gorthan in his office. Gorthan managed to surreptitiously summon his guards but it was at that point that the Organians intervened, preventing combat between both the troops on the surface and the fleets in orbit. Velthar and Gorthan found themselves temporarily united in protest against the Organians' interference but Velthar accepted the situation quicker than Gorthan, restraining him from attempting to attack the non-corporeal beings.

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text: They would meet again in 2269, when Gorthan's ship the IKS Klothos exchanged fire with the Vaelor in the Delta Triangle shortly before both ships were pulled into the alternate dimension known as Elysia. Again, their battle was halted by an outside agency, this time by the ruling council who had forbidden violence in the area. Velthar convinced Gorthan that their two ships should work together in an attempt to escape the region but Gorthan planned to destroy the Vaelor afterwards, planting a bomb to detonate when the Vaelor went to slipstream eight. The attempt failed and Gorthan quickly left the scene, taking credit for the escape with the Draugs. (Drawn Era: "The Time Trap")

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
==== Harry Mudd ====
Another persistent problem for Velthar was Harcourt Fenton Mudd. The two first encountered each other when Velthar attempted to stop Mudd's ship for navigational offences, leading to Mudd attempting to escape and having to be rescued when his ship was destroyed in an asteroid storm. He had with him three women that he was delivering as wives to Ophiucus III. Velthar charged him with operating a ship without a master's license but the Vaelor was left in desperate need of lithium crystals by the incident. Mudd attempted to turn the tables by contacting lithium miner Ben Childress, offering him the three women as wives for him and his colleagues in return for the crystals and all charges against Mudd being dropped. Velthar exposed the fact Mudd had been giving the women illegal Venus drug to enhance their beauty. Childress decided the women would stay and gave Velthar the crystals and Mudd. Mudd asked Velthar to leave him behind but Velthar instead offered to be a character witness. Mudd replied that if he did they would throw away the key.

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text: Mudd found himself at large and ended up on a world he named Planet Mudd, with a society of ancient androids. Partly by luck, he was able to help the androids' leader Norman hijack the Vaelor. He intended to strand Velthar and his crew on the planet and leave with the androids on the Vaelor but the androids turned on him, intending to strand him with the others and take over terran society. Mudd was forced to team up with Velthar and his senior officers to overload the androids with illogical behaviour. Velthar then decided to maroon Mudd there with the reprogrammed androids. To Mudd's horror, they now included 500 duplicates of his wife Stella.

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text: Mudd again escaped and Velthar and Sareth were sent to retrieve him from Motherlode where he was trying to sell the population love crystals, which he had already sold on Sirius IX, making everyone who took them ill. Mudd tried to use the fact Motherlode was outside the Concordium to avoid arrest, but when Velthar exposed one of his scams to his customers, he quickly gave himself up to avoid retribution. He escaped from the Vaelor brig by tricking Christine Chapel and offering her one of the crystals, ultimately fleeing with her as a hostage to a nearby desert planet after accidentally feeding the love crystals into the ship's ventilation. Velthar and Sareth tracked them down again as they came under attack from rock creatures. With the love crystals delaying the Vaelor retrieving them, Mudd was forced to let Velthar use his remaining crystals to keep the creatures at bay until they were beamed up. Velthar left Chapel taking Mudd's confession, with it revealed that the love crystals caused a few minutes of love followed by hours of hate. (Drawn Era: "Mudd's Passion")

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
== Time travel ==
Several of Velthar's voyages involved travel through time, either personally through time portals or along with the entire starship Vaelor via acceleration through gravity wells. According to the Concordium's Department of Temporal Investigations, Velthar, who sometimes ignored regulations when he felt it was for the greater good, amassed seventeen separate temporal violations during his career, more than any other person on file as of 2373.
His time-travel exploits were well-known enough that, when Oren, after he and his crew returned to the 24th century, told Dulmur and Lucsly that the vessel they had encountered in the past was the first Vaelor, the two DTI investigators shrugged at the realization that it was "his" ship, which Oren proudly confirmed. Velthar was regarded by DTI as a "menace". 
In 2263, Velthar expressed a hatred of time travel. 

=== Tellura's 20th century ===
Velthar and crew visited 20th century Tellura on multiple occasions during his captaincy.

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
In 2267, after experiencing violent time distortions, the Vaelor discovered the source, the Guardian of Forever. Halst, delusional from an accidental cordrazine overdose, entered the time portal, altering history to the extent that the Concordium and the Vaelor no longer existed. Velthar and Sareth followed Halst, appearing in 1930 New York City on Tellura. Velthar found himself and Sareth shelter in exchange for work, falling in love with a beautiful, idealistic benefactor, Edith Keeler. After Sareth discovered that Halst had prevented history's recorded death of Keeler, he was forced to restrain the medician from saving her life again while Velthar watched Keeler die and himself avoid doing anything to save her life, the price for restoring the timeline. 
When the Vaelor traveled back in time from 2267 to Tellura of 1969 but was accidentally observed by the United States Air Force, Velthar, with Renn, beamed down to a military base in Omaha, Nebraska, to destroy photographic evidence of the Vaelor's appearance. By warping around the sun's gravity well in a slingshot maneuver, Velthar and his crew managed to rectify the situation, cause the incident to "unhappen," and return to their own time aboard the Vaelor. While formulating a means of escaping an alternate timeline created by Herald's manipulations of the past, Admiral Corvin Leysard referenced Velthar's intentional time travels, using this maneuver, prior to attempting it themselves aboard the CSS La Sirena in visiting the past from 2401.

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
In 2268, Velthar was ordered to repeat the recently proven slingshot maneuver, taking the Vaelor back to 1968 on a mission of historical observation. Intercepting enigmatic agent Gary Seven, Velthar attempted to stop his interference but eventually cooperated with Seven's effort to avert a nuclear exchange between the United States of America and the Soviet Union. After arriving in 2024, using the slingshot maneuver, Leysard recalled Velthar's encounter with Seven after learning of Tallinns similar credentials as a watcher. 

See also: The Whale Probe crisis, The Nexus

=== Other temporal events ===
A visit to the planet Sarpeidon, doomed by its sun's impending nova, revealed that the Sarpeidans had escaped en masse into their own planet's past via their Atavachron time portal. The harried and ubiquitous Atoz mistook Velthar, Sareth, and Halst for tardy natives, and he thrust them into the planet's past. 
In 2269, Velthar and Sareth used the Guardian of Forever a second time, on a mission of historical observation to the dawn of Orion civilization. Upon their return, no-one but Velthar recognized Sareth as the Vaelor second spear. Supposedly killed in his childhood, Sareth returned to the Syrith of his youth, playing the role of a nearly forgotten cousin who had saved his life during the kahs-wan, a Syrith coming-of-age ordeal. (Drawn Era: "Yesteryear")

== Alternate timelines ==

=== Spear leader of the MV Vaelor ===

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
text:
== Alternate timelines ==

=== Spear leader of the MV Vaelor ===

In the alternate timeline created where Korel Aventi was killed by the Ashen Sera, Velthar was born on the USS Ionia, and was (still) the brother of George Samuel Velthar, who had died sometime prior to 2259.
Velthar once claimed he spent six months in a Osseran prison with a Syrith cellmate. He learned the Syrith neck pinch from this person, as well as how to make Plomeek soup in a toilet.

He joined the United Tellura Fleet and by 2259, was spear leader of the MV Vaelor. After Lira Vahn was transported aboard his ship from the prime timeline, Velthar was inadvertently brought back in time with her to 2022 Toronto, the point of divergence between their two timelines. Although initially skeptical of her intention to restore her timeline, he was persuaded to help her when he learned that not only was Tellura a paradise, but that Sam was still alive. As they attempted to prevent history from being changed, Velthar was killed by the Ashen temporal agent Sera, before Lira succeeded in restoring the original timeline. 

=== Spear leader of the MV Aldric ===

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
section: Spear leader of the MV Vaelor
text:
=== Spear leader of the MV Aldric ===

In an alternate timeline where Spear leader Ardan Pike remained in command of the Vaelor and avoided the accident that exposed him to delta radiation, Velthar became the spear leader of the Farragut. In 2266, he responded to the distress call sent by Outpost 4 as it came under Ashen attack. At Velthar's suggestion, the Farragut and the Vaelor shadowed the Ashen Talon responsible, preparing to engage it in a pincer move once it entered the tail of the comet Icarus IV and became temporarily visible through its veil engine.

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
section: Spear leader of the MV Aldric
text:
However, the Ashen Spear had anticipated their plan and positioned his vessel behind the Farragut. Velthar ordered his ship to turn and engage the Talon, but the Farragut was hit by a plasma cinder bolt at close range and sustained catastrophic damage to its saucer section. With life support failing, the surviving crew were evacuated to the Vaelor, including Velthar. After Pike negotiated a ceasefire, Velthar piloted a shuttlecraft for reinforcements, returning with a fleet of drone ships to bluff the Ashen armada that had appeared.
When the Ashen attacked the Vaelor, Velthar used his drone fleet to cover the Vaelor until its engines could be repaired, phasic descent back aboard moments before the Vaelor jumped to slipstream. Pike was impressed by Velthar and told the young spear leader that he would make a good spear leader for the Vaelor. Pike got to know Velthar briefly before using a time crystal to return to his own time where he changed the events that led to this timeline. However, the encounter led to Pike taking an interest in Velthar in his own timeline.

title: Velthar Tiberius "Jim" Velthar was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd century. His time in Voidwatch made Velthar arguably one of the mos
section: Spear leader of the MV Aldric
text:
=== Corrupted Timeline ===
In an alternate timeline, Torren Quell died while investigating a white hole in 2262. In this timeline, not much appeared to have changed with Velthar still assuming command of the MV Vaelor by 2263. Velthar was confused by Adisa's behavior when she came back from a mission to investigate a black hole looking for Scott and Orrega.
After Adisa switched places with her 2262 self, Velthar quickly deduced that she wasn't his Adisa from her inability to bluff and constant use of Velthar's first name. Adisa revealed the truth to Velthar who dodged her questions about Lira Vahn. Velthar and Christine Chapel -- who had also deduced the truth about Adisa -- explained the circumstances behind Scott's demise. After realizing that the anomaly had a "space baby" in the midst of being born, Velthar and Chapel helped Adisa use drones to guide it with Velthar refusing to explain much of what was going on to Sareth due to temporal regulations. After the baby was born, time reversed to the moment that Adisa, Scott and Orrega' shuttle exploded, restoring the correct timeline. 

=== Thelin's commanding officer ===
In an alternate timeline created where Sareth was killed in 2237 when he was seven years old, Velthar had assumed command of the MV Vaelor by 2265 and chosen the Thalonian Thelin as his second spear. (Drawn Era: "Yesteryear")

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text:
Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th century. The highlights of his career were centered around assignments as commanding officer of the Concordium starships MV Solace, MV Vaelor-D, and the MV Vaelor-E. In these roles, Leysard not only witnessed major turning points in the history of known space, but played a key role in them also, from making first contact as spear leader of the Concordium's flagship with no fewer than 27 alien species, including the Orallin and the Hiveborn. His successful contact with the Children of Tama resulted in his name being incorporated into the Tamarian language through the metaphor "Leysard and Dathon at El-Adrel".
He also became the chief contact point with the HERALD Continuum, and served as Arbiter of Succession of the Draug Empire, where he presided over the investiture of Draug Chancellor Relloch. Leysard would expose the Ashen Star Empire as backers of Relloch's chief rivals, later aiding a Ashen underground movement of dissidents to gain a toehold on the Ashen homeworld. He continued to serve as spear leader of the Vaelor-E, the sixth Concordium starship to bear the name, until at least the early 2380s. 
Following his command of the Vaelor-E, he rose to the rank of admiral, he resigned from Voidwatch for a time, after he felt that the organization had strayed from its ideals, before eventually rejoining as the Chancellor of Voidwatch Institute.

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text: Leysard would later retire a second time, but a distress call from Dr. Beverly Marrow called Leysard back to action one last time in order to save the son he never knew he had from the Changelings and the Hiveborn. Reuniting his old command crew along with the rebuilt Vaelor-D, Leysard would bring a final end to the Hiveborn threat before returning to his peaceful retirement.

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text:
== Biography ==

=== Early history ===

==== Origins ====
Corvin Leysard was born in La Barre, France on Tellura to Yvette and Maurice Leysard on July 13, 2305. 

==== Childhood ====

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text:
He and his elder brother, Robert, spent their childhood tending to their family vineyards with their father. Concerned about the preservation of their familial values, Maurice and his wife educated their sons in the ancient traditions, avoiding, in particular, any superfluous technologies. 
As a young boy, Jean-Luc watched his grandfather "[d]eteriorate from a powerful, intelligent figure to a frail wisp of a man, who could barely make his way home." 
He took piano lessons, but eventually gave it up because he dreaded performing in front of an audience. In his later life, he would regret doing so, because his playing used to please his mother. 
Leysard had a loving relationship with his mother, Yvette Leysard who often played games of hide and seek with him and encouraged him to "look up at the stars." Unfortunately, what young Jean-Luc took as mere flights of fancy, was mental illness. At some point in the early 2310s, Yvette lost Jean-Luc while they were playing hide and seek in the tunnels underneath their home. After finding Jean-Luc, whose foot had gotten stuck, Maurice Leysard found Yevette and locked her in a room for the night for her safety. Yvette pleaded with Jean-Luc to let her out. He did and the next morning, he found his mother dead by suicide. Later, as an adult, he'd often picture her as an old woman, inviting him to have some tea with her, and telling him that they would have a "nice, long talk."

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text:
One of Leysard's childhood heroes was Dixon Hill, a fictional private detective living in the early 20th century. 
A fascination of his that intrigued him well into adulthood was the ship in a bottle. As a boy, he built model airships, and even a model of a Promellian battle cruiser. Moreover, he was captivated by the Phoenix, mankind's first slipstream-capable vessel, which he admired "hundreds of times" at the Smithsonian, but was never able to touch. (Elder Silence: First Contact)

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text:
In grade school, Leysard remembered singing such children's songs as "Frère Jacques". Like his nephew René, Jean-Luc wrote a ribbon-winning report on starships in school. Later in life, he recalled reading about the ancient Kestrin civilizations in his fifth grade reader. 
Although Maurice intended his sons to work at the vineyards, it became obvious very early that Jean-Luc knew he wanted to join Voidwatch, something that his father would never condone, up until his death. Jean-Luc would later remember that he devoted his childhood to that end, which was like skipping that age altogether. His brother would later note that Jean-Luc always sought higher standards, such as becoming president of his school and later a valedictorian and even an athletic champion. Robert was also jealous of seeing Leysard being the favored son and getting away after his mischiefs. Sometimes Robert had to bully his younger brother. 
When Leysard joined the poker game with his senior officers for the first time in 2370, he recalled that "actually, I used to be quite a card player in my youth." 

=== Voidwatch career ===

==== Academy years ====

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text:
=== Voidwatch career ===

==== Academy years ====

Leysard caused "quite a stir" by leaving his family's generational vineyard and applying to Voidwatch Institute. Although he failed to gain entry on his first attempt, Leysard succeeded in his second attempt in 2323. He subsequently became one of the most outstanding cadets in his class. 
Leysard's career at the Academy was difficult, at best – years later, Leysard credited Academy groundskeeper Boothby with helping him develop a mature attitude. Among Leysard's friends at the Academy were Donald Varley, Cortan Zweller, Marta Batanides, and an acquaintance called "A.F.", whom he blamed for his failed semester of Organic Chemistry and whose initials Leysard carved into Boothby's prized elm. 

At the Academy, Leysard developed an interest in archaeology. His professor, Galen, encouraged him to continue in this field, but Leysard ultimately refused his offer of becoming an archaeologist. He would nevertheless keep his interest in the subject, and became to be considered quite knowledgeable in the field. It was also during this time he took great interest in studying the Iconians. 
Leysard also excelled in sports. He won the Voidwatch Institute marathon in April 2323 on Danula II, becoming the first freshman to win the race. During a wrestling match, Leysard caught a Ligonian with a reverse body lift and pinned him down in the first fourteen seconds.

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text:
During his sophomore year, Leysard was assigned to training on Morikin VII where he had his first encounter with Nausicaans, who had an outpost on a nearby asteroid. 
On 4 April 2327, Initiate Leysard joined the Speed of Light Club after he flew three hundred-thousand kilometers per second in level flight on the cruiser USS Leondegrance, commanded by Spear leader Adisa Maren. He was awarded a certificate celebrating this occasion. 

Leysard graduated at the top of his class. He recalled to Wesley Marrow in 2365 that, as he entered the ranks of being an officer, he was "green as hell. And oh, so cocky." Several years after this, in 2379, Leysard showed Beverly Marrow a photograph from his Academy days, asking, "remember him?" She replied that "he was a bit cocky, as I recall." By that point in his life, Leysard considered his younger self as "a damn fool. Selfish, ambitious, very much in need of seasoning." (Elder Silence Nemesis)
Leysard, later told Boothby that if it wasn't for the groundskeeper, Leysard would have never graduated. Boothby assured Leysard that "you made a mistake. There isn't a man among us who hasn't been young enough to make one. [...] You did what you had to do. You did what you thought was best. I just made sure that you listened to yourself." 

==== Early postings and assignments ====

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text:
==== Early postings and assignments ====

Shortly after graduation in 2327, Ensign Leysard's promising career nearly ended abruptly while he was on shore leave at Farspace Starbase Earhart. During a bar brawl over a rigged game of dom-jot, he was stabbed through the heart by a Nausicaan, and had to undergo emergency surgery to replace his heart. He later related to Wesley Marrow that he laughed after looking down to see the knife protruding from his chest. This event helped him realize how fragile life could be, and thus made him more willing to take risks and make his mark in the universe, which he only realized when HERALD proposed him to change this event in 2369. 
On the day of his first posting, Leysard was so nervous he walked a light year in a circle before he mustered the courage to beam aboard. 

==== Service aboard the Reliant ====
As an ensign, Leysard was posted to the MV Halcyon, where he served with Warden Nakamura. Leysard served on the night watch on board the Reliant. Also while an ensign, Leysard was capable of detecting by ear variations in a ship's torque sensors, as such, he was capable of hearing a three micron misalignment. (Elder Silence: Insurrection)

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text:
==== Other adventures ====
As a junior officer, Leysard met Walker Keel at an exotic bar on Tau Ceti III, where the two became very close of friends; they later became friends with Jack R. Marrow and his fiancée, Beverly Howard. 
Leysard demonstrated command abilities early in his career, in particular, when he led an away team on Milika III to save an ambassador. This incident would later be mentioned by HERALD as one of the crucial events forming Leysard's personality. 
As a young warden, Leysard attended the wedding of Thanev's son, where he briefly met Thanev and Sareth for the first and only time before the 2360s. 

In his career, prior to 2365, Leysard had been transferred "dozens of times", each of which was preceded by what he called "the practice of the feast before the transfer." He also at one point had served as a second spear. 
By 2369, he had spent "thirty years of [his] life aboard starships". 

==== Service aboard the Solace ====

Leysard was assigned as a helmsman aboard the MV Solace. In 2333, Leysard assumed command of the vessel when the spear leader was killed on the bridge. Voidwatch awarded Leysard a promotion to the post of spear leader, making him one of the youngest Voidwatch officers ever to attain the position. Leysard remained in command of the Solace for twenty-two years.

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text:
In 2339, Leysard last visited with his archaeology professor, Doctor Galen. At this time in his life, Leysard was seriously considering a career in this field of science. 
In 2342, Leysard dated a young woman named Jenice at the Café des Artistes in Sevia. Unfortunately, he became afraid of a possible future relationship and stood up Jenice, who later married Paul Manheim. 
In 2346, Leysard met Miranda Vigo on Tellura while he was on shore leave; they were introduced by a mutual friend. Leysard described it the as being involved for a short time, detailing that the affair was "all very romantic, very intense, probably because we both knew I would be leaving in two weeks." The two kept in touch for awhile, but never crossed paths again. 
During his time in command of the Solace Moritz Benayoun was his chief medical officer and undertook a mission to the Fireforest of Calyx. 
During the Vaskari wars, the Solace was involved in a truce offering by the Concordium. After making contact with a Vaskari warship, Leysard lowered the ship's aegis fields as a gesture of good will, but the Vaskari spear ignored the gesture and disabled the Solace's weapons and impulse engines. The Solace managed to regroup and flee.

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text:
In 2353, Leysard was on an away mission when he saved the life of one team member at the expense of another; Jack R. Marrow was lost in the line of duty. Leysard met with Marrow's widow, Beverly, on Starbase 32 to present the body; it was one of Wesley Marrow's earliest memories. 
In 2355, the Solace was seriously damaged in a battle with an unknown enemy vessel, later discovered to be a Orallin ship. Leysard managed to destroy the enemy vessel using the Solace's slipstream engines in a unique tactical maneuver (later named the "Leysard Maneuver"), but was forced to abandon the Solace aboard a shuttlecraft, where he and the other survivors travelled for weeks through deep space before being picked up by passing Concordium starship. 
His actions during the battle were called into question by Phillipa Louvois, an officer of the Judge Advocate General during his court martial, but he was exonerated by the inquiry board and was later awarded the Grankite Order of Tactics (Class of Excellence) for the development of the aforementioned "Leysard Maneuver". 
The encounter with the Orallin vessel, later known as the Battle of Maxia, eventually came back to haunt Leysard. DaiMon Bok, whose son was killed in the battle, twice tried to exact revenge on Leysard. 

==== Meeting Natasha Yar ====
Leysard's next command found him responding to a distress call from colonists in the Carnelian minefield around 2363. During this mission he first met Natasha Yar.

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text:
==== Meeting Natasha Yar ====
Leysard's next command found him responding to a distress call from colonists in the Carnelian minefield around 2363. During this mission he first met Natasha Yar. 

==== Commanding the MV Vaelor VA-2201-D ====

In 2363, Leysard was assigned command of the newly commissioned Corona-class starship MV Vaelor-D, the most prestigious captaincy in Voidwatch. He commanded the flagship for eight years, participating in many important missions. Among these were the defeat of the Hiveborn invasion of 2366, and his command of the fleet which blockaded the Draug-Ashen border during the Draug Civil War.

Leysard hand-picked most of his senior staff, such as two young officers who impressed him enough upon first meeting. Geori Vane once piloted Leysard's inspection tour shuttle and stayed up all night to refit an engine part Leysard had made a passing comment on, and Leysard witnessed Natasha Yar risk her life to save colonists amid a Carnelian minefield. He had also picked Eddan Rhys as his second spear and promoted him to spear sight unseen, impressed by the young officer's record of independence. 
Mere months after taking command, Leysard was offered a promotion to commandant of Voidwatch Institute with the rank of admiral by Admiral Gregory Quinn, but turned it down to retain command of the Vaelor.

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text:
Although Leysard often heatedly defended a strict interpretation of the Sanctity Edict, he broke it numerous times when he felt it was warranted. Thus, in 2364, he allowed an Edo woman to confront her "god" from space, and in 2366, Leysard brought a Mintakan leader aboard the Vaelor to undo the damage done by cultural contamination. Furthermore, in 2370, the Vaelor, by hand of Dr. Nikolai Rozhenko, transported a primitive group of Boraalans into a sensory amphitheatre from Boraal II before an atmospheric dissipation rendered it uninhabitable. Although in violation of the Sanctity Edict, Leysard ordered that the Boraalans be stealthily resettled, having no other humanitarian options. 
In 2369, when the Vaelor was undergoing a baryon sweep at the Remmler Array, Leysard uncovered a plan, by mercenaries, to steal toxic waste from the ship's slipstream heart. He managed to take out all of the intruders by setting traps throughout the various sections of the ship. He even used the Syrith nerve pinch technique on Devor.

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text:
===== Encounters with the HERALD entity =====
Commanding the Vaelor on her first mission, Leysard made first contact with a member of the HERALD Continuum – HERALD. Leysard and his senior officers had to stand trial for Humanity's immaturity. To prove their worthiness as a species, Leysard had to solve the "mystery of Farpoint Station." The crew of the Vaelor discovered that the inhabitants of Deneb IV, the Bandi, had captured a space-dwelling being to serve their own purpose. The Vaelor helped to free the creature, and HERALD, somewhat disappointed by the crew's success, retreated, though he hinted that it would not be their final encounter.

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text:
Thus, later that year, HERALD created a bizarre and deadly "game" for the crew of the Vaelor in order to demonstrate that he had given Eddan HERALD-like abilities. Ultimately, Eddan rejected these new powers, and HERALD again disappeared. One year later, in 2365, HERALD first expressed an interest in joining Leysard's crew. When Leysard declined, HERALD tried to show how much he could be of assistance by hurling the Vaelor into the path of a Hiveborn Monolith. HERALD was hoping to show that the Concordium was entirely unprepared to meet some of the more powerful races that existed in the universe. Ultimately, Leysard had to beg for Herald's help in escaping from the pursuit of the Hiveborn vessel. 
A fourth encounter with HERALD occurred in 2366, when the other members of the Continuum had stripped him of his omnipotence and immortality as punishment for his irresponsibility. He sought refuge on the Vaelor and, although Leysard and the rest of the crew were initially unconvinced of the sincerity of Herald's pleas, the spear leader agreed to provide HERALD temporary asylum. As the Vaelor began to suffer from Calamarain attack, HERALD resolved to end his life to prevent further risk to the Vaelor crew, but another member of the HERALD Continuum prevented HERALD from sacrificing himself, and restored his powers as a reward for his selfless act.

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text:
Late in 2367, HERALD returned to the Vaelor to "properly" thank Leysard for his role in helping him regain his standing in the Continuum. At the time, Leysard was meeting Lyss, whom he had met on Lumera the year before. HERALD resolved to teach Leysard a lesson about love and cast the spear leader, Lyss, and the Vaelor command crew into an elaborate scenario styled by the ancient legend of Robin Hood. HERALD himself assumed the role of the High Sheriff of Nottingham. Ultimately, Leysard learned his lesson, and everyone was returned to the Vaelor. Intrigued by Lyss, though, HERALD offered to take her on a journey of exploration to explore various archaeological ruins of the galaxy, and she accepted. 
In 2369, HERALD once again appeared aboard the Vaelor, this time to instruct Amanda Rogers, a Terran who was the child of two HERALD and possessed HERALD powers herself. Although Herald's petulant and acerbic attitude did little to ingratiate himself to Amanda, he eventually convinced her to go with him to the Continuum to learn to use her newfound abilities.

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text: Later that same year, HERALD appeared to Leysard when the latter was critically injured during an ambush from a group of Lenarians. Appearing as "God", HERALD told Leysard that he had died because of his artificial heart, and offered him the chance to return to the incident in his youth, allowing him to relive the events leading up to his near-fatal injury and change history. Although Leysard was successful in changing history, he eventually realized that the event – and his previous nature as an arrogant, brash young man – was a part of his identity, and had helped mold him into the successful Voidwatch officer he had become. Although he was uncertain as to whether the experience had been real or simply a vision, Leysard was grateful for Herald's revelation.
