In 2365, Vekta's rights as an individual were challenged when cybernetics expert Spear Bruce Maddox wanted to disassemble the android for study. Leysard challenged Maddox's assessment before the local Judge Advocate General. As the hearing neared its end, Leysard admitted to Elyria he feared he was losing the case. Elyria asked what Maddox gained if he would be successful in disassembling and reassembling Vekta, and Leysard responded he would possess the ability to build many more androids. He remembered Elyria's words that the decisions made today have implications for the future, and so Leysard reasoned that if it would be decided that Vekta was indeed Voidwatch property, all future androids would be also. Elyria noted there was an ancient word for that: slavery. Eventually, Leysard won Vekta's case by pointing out that an entire race of Datas would be used as slaves, strictly against Concordium principles. 
In 2367, Elyria played the role of Gloria in one of Leysard's Dixon Hill holonovels. She was not much impressed with the program.

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text:
In 2367, Elyria played the role of Gloria in one of Leysard's Dixon Hill holonovels. She was not much impressed with the program. 
Besides joining Leysard on the sensory amphitheatre, they would occasionally share a game of chess, and Elyria was also coached in fencing by Leysard in 2368, begun when she considered exercise to strengthen her arm. Shortly prior to their match, the Vaelor had taken a Hiveborn drone, later named Ewan, on board. Although Elyria initially questioned Leysard's decision to have done so, she was convinced by Vane to speak with the former drone. She could not, but acknowledged this Hiveborn was developing a personality, becoming an individual. Upon her conversation with Ewan, she convinced Leysard to speak with him as well. 
In 2400, Leysard and Elyria reunited when he showed up at Ten Forward to ask her for advice regarding his changing relationship with Laris and his fear of pursuing her. Elyria listened to his troubles and supported him in opening his heart to love again.

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text: When Leysard and his friends were thrown into 2024 by the machinations of HERALD, he encountered a younger version of Elyria. She had grown disillusioned with attempting to help Humanity and was prepared to leave Tellura. At first, this version of Elyria did not recognize him and threatened him. Leysard told her about the bond they would share in the future, and convinced Elyria to help him find the contact he needed, a Watcher. She led him to the person he needed, and then left, so that the Watcher could feel comfortable speaking to him alone. Before she left, Leysard pleaded with her not to leave the Tellura "just yet".

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text:
==== Eddan Rhys ====

When choosing a second spear prior to the launch of the Vaelor-D in 2363, Leysard accessed the records of a number of candidates for the job. He eventually came across the record of one Eddan Rhys. Leysard saw it as a glowing record filled with statistics and the Letter of recommendation that he felt told him nothing about the kind of officer Eddan actually was. Leysard was about to move on to the next candidate's record but stopped when he saw that a notation in Eddan's record regarding an incident that took place on board the USS Hood in which Eddan refused to allow Spear leader Robert DeSoto to phase to surface to Altair III. Leysard was impressed that Eddan would challenge his spear leader's authority if needed, and put the safety of the spear leader and the crew ahead of his own career if the need arose. This was a major factor in Leysard's selection of Eddan as his second spear – Leysard wanted an officer who would not be afraid to stand up to him and be more concerned about the safety of the ship and mission than his personnel records.

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text:
Leysard was very cold towards Eddan during their first meeting and ordered the manual docking as a test of Eddan's abilities. When he performed the docking with great expertise and skill, Leysard formally greeted Eddan, requesting that his new second spear make sure that he not allow Leysard to "make an ass of himself" in front of the many children aboard the ship. One year later, Leysard felt as if he had not done a good job of congratulating Eddan, so he did it once more, this time making his feelings clear. 
Eventually, Eddan and Leysard became very good friends. With the best of intentions, Eddan suggested that Leysard vacation at Lumera in 2366, asking him to return with a horga'hn. Leysard did not realize the history behind the statue and kept it with him after purchasing it for Eddan, making it appear as if the spear leader was seeking jamaharon. 
The only time Eddan and Leysard ever verbally fought in front of the Vaelor crew was in 2366 while under the influence of emotions projected by Ambassador Thanev, who was suffering from Bendii Syndrome.

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text:
The only time Eddan and Leysard ever verbally fought in front of the Vaelor crew was in 2366 while under the influence of emotions projected by Ambassador Thanev, who was suffering from Bendii Syndrome. 
Leysard tried to counsel Eddan when he was offered command of the USS Melbourne in 2366, reminding him that the Vaelor would continue without his presence and that officers like Elizabeth Shelby were very much as he was before he learned the lessons necessary for command of a starship. Eddan also came to Leysard for advice when Gharun wanted his help with the hegh'bat and when he struggled with a decision involving Soren.

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text: In early 2369, members of the Vaelor crew, including Leysard, were turned into twelve-year-olds due to the effects of a molecular reversion field. Unfortunately, a group of Orallin commandeered the Vaelor about that time. Believed to be a child, Leysard was confined to a classroom aboard the ship while Eddan was held in the observation lounge. Leysard threw a tantrum and demanded to see his "father," Eddan. They pretended to be father and son in order for Leysard to plant a suggestive message to Eddan, requesting access to the Vaelor main computer from the classroom. Leysard, along with the other affected Vaelor crewmembers, were able to design a plan to retake the Vaelor from the Orallin.

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text:
During the Pegasus incident of 2370, Leysard tried to investigate the circumstances surrounding the ship's disappearance. He ran into many dead-ends as most records had been sealed, and had to use many favors in Voidwatch Command to even get a look at the findings of the board convened to investigate the loss of the Pegasus. Eddan would not divulge further information under the orders of Admiral Erik Pressman, and Leysard reluctantly continued the search. He made it clear to Eddan that he hoped he still placed the safety of the Vaelor as his top priority, and if Leysard had found this to be untrue, he would reevaluate his trust in Eddan. After the crisis was resolved, Leysard visited Eddan in the brig and returned him to duty aboard the Vaelor, understanding of Will's mistake in the past and satisfied that he had made the correct decisions in the present. 
Leysard served as Eddan's best man during his wedding to Sienna Valar in 2379. He gave a toast to Eddan, calling him his "trusted right arm" and lamenting his loss of a fine second spear. (Elder Silence Nemesis)
Leysard remained in contact with Eddan after Eddan became spear leader of the MV Titan. He met Eddan's son Thaddeus at least twice, once when Thad was a baby and once when he was five.

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text:
Although Leysard initially intended not to involve Eddan (or any of the rest of his surviving Vaelor crew) in his quest for Soji Asha, once he found her on the Artifact and needed a safe haven, he brought Soji to Eddan and Valar's home on Nepenthe. Leysard was grateful for Eddan's friendship, and that he did not attempt to talk him out of helping Soji and her siblings. After Leysard left, Eddan requested temporary reassignment to Voidwatch in order to help him with his mission, and led a squadron of starships to Coppelius. 

==== Vekta ====
From 2364 to 2371, Senior warden Vekta was appointed as head of operations when serving on board the MV Vaelor-D, and head of operations from 2372 to 2379 on board the MV Vaelor-E. Vekta looked up to Leysard as something of a father figure throughout his service under the spear leader, asking for his advice on numerous occasions in his quest to become more Terran. Leysard always gave Vekta advice whenever he could.
Following Natasha Yar's death in 2364, Vekta was puzzled about her death, thinking not about Tasha but rather how he would feel in her absence, thinking that he missed the purpose of her memorial, but Leysard assured him that he understood the purpose of the memorial perfectly.

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text: In 2365, Vekta's existence was threatened when Spear Bruce Maddox wished to disassemble and study Vekta to gain a better understanding of how his orichalc brain functioned. Vekta refused to submit to Maddox's procedure, finding his research flawed, but Maddox claimed that Vekta was property of Voidwatch and therefore not a sentient being and as a result had no choice other than to submit to the procedure. Spear leader Phillipa Louvois supported Maddox's claim, and Leysard intervened by challenging their reasoning, saying that Vekta was indeed sentient and deserved the freedom to make his own decisions. He also said that Vekta represented an entire race and that forcing him to submit to Maddox's procedure is tantamount to slavery – strictly against Concordium law. Ultimately, Louvois sided with Leysard's standpoint and agreed that Vekta, android or not, was indeed sentient and entitled to the same rights as any other Voidwatch officer.

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text: In 2367, Leysard's seemingly unbreakable trust in Vekta was tested when Vekta refused to fully cooperate with an investigation into a number of events that happened within a 24-hour time span, although Vekta claimed that the time span was only 30 seconds. Vekta's intransigence threatened to end his Voidwatch career and even his own existence, but it was later revealed that Leysard was himself responsible for Vekta's unusual behavior after an encounter with the Paxans in a T-Tauri type star system.

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text: During the Draug Civil War, the Concordium made an indirect intervention with a blockade of Voidwatch vessels placed in formation to use the pioneering tachyon detection grid in an effort to expose Ashen support for the House of Valdor. Leysard assigned all of his senior officers positions on board other ships, except for Vekta. Vekta questioned Leysard about why he was not assigned command of a vessel, considering that there was a severe lack of senior officers available for the mission, wondering if he felt that his being an android made him unsuitable for command. Leysard, slightly embarrassed by Vekta's question, assigned Vekta command of the USS Sutherland. During the blockade, Vekta disobeyed direct orders from Leysard and was able to expose the Ashen' involvement in the civil war. Later, Vekta wished to submit himself for disciplinary action for disobeying a direct order from his superior officer, but Leysard instead praised Vekta for not complying, summing up his belief of too many tragedies throughout history being directly traceable to officers "just following orders" rather than independently assessing their situations, with the words, "Mr. Vekta: nicely done."

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text:
In 2369, Vekta refused to allow a group of exocomps to be sacrificed in order to save the lives of Leysard and Geori Vane, who were trapped on board the Tyrus VIIA station, believing that they were sentient and, therefore, capable of making their own decisions. After agreeing to a compromise suggested by Spear Eddan Rhys, the exocomps were released and able to save the lives of Leysard and Vane. Leysard understood the predicament that Vekta was faced with as he had defended Vekta's sentience just a few years previously, but this time the exocomps had no advocate and Vekta felt compelled to act on their behalf. Leysard considered Vekta's actions to be the most "Terran" decision that he had ever made. 
Later that year, following an accident in main engineering that activated a dormant program in his orichalc brain, Vekta sought advice from several officers, including Leysard, on his "visions." Leysard was curious why Vekta was studying thousands of different cultures to interpret his visions. Vekta said that he had no culture of his own, but Leysard told Vekta that he did have a culture – a culture of one and that its validity is no less than that of a billion. Leysard suggested that Vekta should consider what the visions meant to him instead of what they mean to other people.

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text: After a malfunctioning emotion chip fused with Vekta's orichalc net in 2371, Vekta felt guilty for not saving Vane from capture by Tolian Soran on board the Amargosa observatory. Overwhelmed by emotions, Vekta requested to be shut down until the chip could be removed. Although Leysard felt sympathy for Vekta, he told him that part of having emotions is integrating them into one's life and learning to live with them, and denied Vekta his request. (Elder Silence Generations)

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text:
In 2373, when the Vaelor-E traveled back to the year 2063 on Tellura, Leysard and Vekta initially went down to the planet to observe the damage the Hiveborn had done to Zefram Cochrane's missile complex in Montana. Down in the missile silo of the Phoenix, Leysard, upon touching the missile that would make history by becoming the first Terran starship traveling at slipstream, explained to Vekta that sometimes a touch can make objects more "real." Upon suspecting a Hiveborn presence aboard the Vaelor, Leysard and Vekta transported back to the ship. Fighting off the Hiveborn near main engineering, Vekta was soon captured and brought to the Hiveborn Hierarch. Instead of attempting to assimilate Vekta, the Queen made him physically more Terran by attaching Terran skin onto his android skeleton.
When it appeared impossible to hold off the Hiveborn any longer, Leysard was convinced to initiate the Vaelor's auto-destruct sequence and ordered all remaining crew to evacuate. He himself went on to engineering to find Vekta and to convince the Queen, who he had encountered several years previously, to let Vekta go. Leysard was even prepared to take Vekta's place at the Queen's side, willingly becoming her equal. Vekta claimed he did not wish to go, even after the Queen ordered him away. Thus, the Queen ordered Leysard's assimilation, but not before witnessing the destruction of the Phoenix by Vekta.

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text:
Vekta fired a spread of quantum torpedoes, but they missed by the smallest of margins. Quickly thereafter, he burst a plasma coolant tank, releasing plasma coolant which liquefied organic material on contact, killing the Hiveborn. The Queen was killed, but Leysard survived. Helping Vekta standing up, Leysard asked him if he was ever tempted to join the Hiveborn's cause. Vekta replied that, for a fraction of a second, hinting at his kiss with the Queen, he was. He added that, for an android, that brief moment was like an eternity. (Elder Silence: First Contact)
Following the wedding of Eddan and Sienna Valar in 2379, Vekta was confused by Leysard's mixed feelings for the couple – although the spear leader was happy that Will was due to accept promotion to the rank of spear leader and take command of the MV Titan, and that his new wife was to transfer over to the Titan and take position as the ship's counselor, Leysard was somewhat saddened by their departure and tried to explain to Vekta that experiencing feelings of both happiness and sadness at the same time are common in these situations.

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text:
At the climax of the Battle in the Bassen Rift, Vekta jumped across the void of space from the Vaelor-E to the Scimitar, saving Leysard by using a prototype emergency transport unit, but sacrificed his own life to save the crew of the Vaelor by firing at the thalaron radiation generator and so destroying the Scimitar. Following the battle, Leysard held a toast with the Vaelor-E's senior officers as a tribute to their fallen comrade. (Elder Silence Nemesis)

The death of Vekta weighed heavily on Leysard, who continued to have dreams about his lost friend for decades. Leysard's feelings about the loss of Vekta helped motivate him to help Dahj and Soji, whom he regarded as Vekta's daughters. Leysard resolved his guilt over Vekta's death when he met a surviving copy of Vekta's consciousness in a quantum simulation, and helped that version of Vekta to die, as he wished to have a finite existence.

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text:
==== Gharun ====
By 2364, Warden junior grade Gharun was serving on the Vaelor-D as a junior bridge officer under Leysard's command. Upon the death of Warden Natasha Yar, he was promoted to chief tactical officer and security chief. 
In 2366, the Draug High Council accused Mogh, the deceased father of Warden Gharun, of treason. Leysard, understanding the severity of the charges and their implications for Gharun, had the Vaelor change course to Droganth. Gharun's brother Kurn initially served as his Cha'DIch, but after an assassination attempt left him in critical condition, Gharun asked Leysard to take up the role. Leysard initially declined, saying that there were younger, more able men on the ship from which Gharun could choose. Gharun insisted that there was no one he would rather have at his side. Leysard accepted and stood by Gharun when the conspiracy against his family was uncovered. 
When the Draug Civil War erupted in 2367, Gharun resigned from Voidwatch and fought on the side of Relloch against the forces of the Valdor family. With the help of Leysard, Gharun and other Relloch supporters revealed Ashen assistance to the Valdor cause. This collapsed support for the House of Valdor, and Relloch won the chancellorship. Relloch restored the honor of the House of Mogh in thanks for its assistance during the war. Gharun returned to Voidwatch, but was reprimanded because he killed Valdor in revenge.

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text:
Gharun commanded the MV Kinrath in the battle against the Hiveborn at Sector Solara, and fought the Hiveborn temporal incursion into 2063. A heated conflict occurred between the two when Leysard had called Gharun a "coward" for not wanting to continue fighting the Hiveborn aboard the Vaelor-E, and a furious Gharun stating that if he were any other man he would kill him where he stood, to which Leysard angrily ordered Gharun off his bridge. Leysard later apologized to Gharun for his harsh comments and admitted that Gharun was "the bravest man" he had ever known, and their friendship was restored. (Elder Silence: First Contact)

==== Geori Vane ====
Like several crew members, Geori Vane was hand-picked by Leysard to serve aboard the Vaelor-D. Vane impressed Leysard with his above average work ethic during an inspection tour. Leysard had tremendous confidence in Vane's ability to accomplish tasks he was assigned, which led to his eventual promotion to master of engines, earning him the rank of senior warden. He was one of the very few officers Leysard addressed by his first name, indicating a close bond between them.

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text:
==== Ro Laren ====
Leysard and Ro had what could be described as a father/daughter-like relationship. When they first met, Leysard wrote her off as dishonorable. He did eventually take her under his wing and help her along a path towards redemption. Upon Ro's defection to the terrorist organization, the Wayfarers, she asked Will Eddan to convey her deepest regrets to Leysard for letting him down. Despite this, Leysard was severely disillusioned by Ro's actions and felt betrayed in a very personal way. 
Thirty years later, Leysard crossed paths with Ro Laren again, still harboring a deep resentment against her for her betrayal. He could not accept her being part of Voidwatch again, claiming that she belonged in prison. The tension between the two reached its peak in a holographic version of 10 Forward Avenue as they accused each other of being Changelings. Leysard openly reprimanded Ro for betraying his trust and the values he stood for, to which Ro retorted that Leysard was confusing duty with morality, eventually leading the two to acknowledge that they had broken each other's hearts. Ultimately, they trusted each other again to stop the Changelings. Ro later told Leysard that she wished he had understood all these years why she did what she did. Leysard was later devastated by Ro's death, shortly after he was told that he was truly seeing her.

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text:
==== Elnor ====
When Leysard began evacuation efforts of Cindras in cooperation with the Qowat Milat, he grew close to Elnor, despite his discomfort around children. The two spent a lot of time together, with Leysard teaching him to Fence, telling him stories of Vekta, and reading him stories, such as The Three Musketeers. After the attack on the Utopia Planitia Shipyards, Leysard resigned from Voidwatch, and did not return to Vashti for 13 years. Elnor was angered at Leysard's sudden disappearance, and when Leysard returned in 2399, asking Elnor to bind himself to his mission to find Soji, he at first refused, but rescinded this decision. Leysard always regretted not being able to find a proper home for Elnor, as the Qowat Milat was by tradition, an all-female organization, and Elnor could never be fully recognized as one. 
Despite the years apart, Elnor's admiration of Leysard carried into his service with him, and he admitted feeling joy when Leysard said he did not wish to leave him behind on the Artifact when he chose to stay behind to cover Leysard and Soji's escape from the Zhat Lyss.

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text: When they met up again on Coppelius, Elnor embraced Leysard in happiness that he'd survived the assault on the Artifact, and was hesitant to leave his side as Leysard's health began to deteriorate. Leysard convinced him that the xBs needed him more, and Elnor agreed to protect them, leaving Leysard's service. The two were briefly reunited before Leysard's death, and Leysard expressed happiness at seeing him one last time. Elnor took Leysard's passing very hard, and mourned heavily while Raffaela Musiker attempted to comfort him. When Leysard was revived shortly afterwards, Elnor chose to travel with him once again.

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text:
=== Allies ===

==== Velthar Deyn ====
Although their association was brief, Velthar Deyn and Corvin Leysard had profound personal effects on one another. Having been a spear leader of the Concordium's flagship, an admiral, and back to a spear leader again, Velthar advised Leysard to not do anything that would have Voidwatch move him away from the Vaelor, because as spear leader, he could make a difference. Very much like Sareth and Brenic Halst, Leysard was instrumental in helping Velthar find meaning in his life after his greatest adventures were essentially over. In fact, it could be argued that Leysard was one of the most significant people in Velthar's entire life, as he embarked on his final adventure with him and passed away knowing that he had "made a difference." Leysard laid Velthar to rest on Veridian III and was his lone mourner. (Elder Silence Generations)

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text:
==== Sareth ====
Sareth was confronted by Leysard and Vekta on Cindras, where he was suspected to have betrayed the Concordium. To the contrary, Sareth was on a "personal mission of peace," and Leysard insisted on staying until Sareth's affairs were complete. Sareth saw much of his father, Thanev, in Leysard and was very resentful of his perceived meddling in his affairs. Leysard and Sareth eventually developed a mutual respect for each other, with Leysard offering Sareth to mind meld with him to see how Thanev truly saw his son. Sareth later utilized Leysard and Sienna Valar in delivering defecting Ashen officials to the Concordium. 
In 3189, a recording of Sareth made on stardate 45825 was retrieved from the personal files of Admiral Leysard and viewed by Vessa Rynn and Cleveland Booker. 

==== Relloch ====
Leysard was Relloch's Arbiter of Succession following the deaths of K'mpec and Valdor. Although he initially refused to aid him during the Draug Civil War, Leysard later convinced Voidwatch to assist Relloch's forces by exposing the alliance between Lursa and B'Etor and Sela, a high-ranking Ashen officer. . Although he considered Leysard an honorable ally of the Draug Empire, Relloch was less than accommodating when asked to assist Voidwatch find Sareth on Cindras. Nevertheless, on more than one occasion, Leysard used his relationship with Relloch as leverage against other Draugs. These events appeared to be reconciled during the events surrounding the resurrection of Kaelor. 

=== Rivals ===

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text:
=== Rivals ===

==== HERALD ====
HERALD and Leysard had a complicated relationship. Even though he was very antagonistic towards them, HERALD clearly had a great respect and affection for the crew of the Vaelor-D, particularly Leysard, who in contrast viewed HERALD with a tremendous amount of disdain and distrust. It was not until their final two encounters that Leysard became grateful to HERALD for their association. 

==== Bok ====
After the death of his son caused by Spear leader Leysard during the Battle of Maxia, Bok had tried to seek vengeance on him twice. First by having him destroy the Vaelor-D through a mind altering device he hid within the derelict of the MV Solace, then by attempting to kill his alleged son Jason Vigo (which whom he re-sequenced his DNA in order to fool Leysard into thinking he was his son).

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text:
==== The Hiveborn / Hiveborn Hierarch ====
After being assimilated by the Hiveborn, Leysard (assuming the identity of Locarn) then went to destroy nearly all Concordium starships at the Engram of Harrow Reach before proceeding to Tellura for an attempted assimilation of that planet. After being de-assimilated, Leysard had long resented the fact that the Hiveborn had used his knowledge and experience to kill and/or assimilate innocent people, and developed a hatred for the Hiveborn that would become a defining trait in his later encounters with them; during the incident in which the Hiveborn attempted to disrupt First Contact, he became increasingly volatile and irrational, and would destroy drones with a modicum of enjoyment – even if they were former members of his crew that had only just been injected with nanoprobes. This resentment stayed with him at least six years after he was first assimilated.

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text:
==== The House of Valdor ====
Corvin Leysard became a prominent figure in Draug politics, largely due to his loyalty to Gharun during the trial of the House of Mogh in 2366. Leysard was determined to uncover the conspiracy that was attempting to frame Mogh for crimes committed by Ja'rod. During his investigation, Valdor, son of Ja'rod sent an assassin to murder Leysard, but the attempt was unsuccessful and ultimately revealed the complicity of K'mpec and the High Council in these crimes. Even after the death of Valdor at the hands of Gharun, the House of Valdor continued to be antagonistic towards the Concordium, with particular emphasis placed on Leysard and the crew of the Vaelor-D, which was eventually destroyed by Lursa and B'Etor.

title: Corvin Leysard was a celebrated Voidwatch officer, archaeologist, writer, historian, diplomat, and philanthropist, who served throughout much of the 24th centur
text:
==== Shinzon ====
As a direct clone of Leysard, Shinzon developed a distinctive and deadly rivalry with the spear leader of the Vaelor, much like Will Eddan's rivalry with Thomas Eddan and Vekta's rivalry with Hollow. Leysard saw traits in Shinzon that he perceived to be flaws within himself. He was bothered by the fact that Shinzon was capable of genocides of interstellar magnitude and was haunted by the notion that he may have chosen the same path as Shinzon had he led his life. During Shinzon's attempt to carry out these genocides, Leysard implored him to let go of his past and embrace change, which Shinzon quickly rejected. Leysard was significantly pained at the death of Shinzon, but this pain was replaced mere moments later after Vekta sacrificed himself to save Leysard. (Elder Silence Nemesis)

title: Korel Aventi (or simply Korel) was an extremely intelligent and dangerous superhuman. He was the most prominent of the genetically-engineered Terran Shardlings
text:
Korel Aventi (or simply Korel) was an extremely intelligent and dangerous superhuman. He was the most prominent of the genetically-engineered Terran Shardlings of the Eugenics Wars period on Tellura. Korel was considered, by the MV Vaelor command crew, over three centuries later, to have been "the best" of them. Reappearing with a cadre of Shardling followers in the 23rd century, Korel became a notorious enemy of Velthar Deyn.
Korel's existence as an Shardling served, as well, as a warning to society of the danger in attempting to create "supermen" through technological means. Ambassador Sareth stated that he was the most dangerous adversary the Vaelor ever faced. 

== Biography ==

=== 20th century origins ===

title: Korel Aventi (or simply Korel) was an extremely intelligent and dangerous superhuman. He was the most prominent of the genetically-engineered Terran Shardlings
text:
=== 20th century origins ===

Records of the period, including Korel's origins, are vague. Korel was born, or created in 1959. (Elder Silence Into Shadow) He was the product of a selective breeding or genetic engineering program called Project Korel, based on the eugenic philosophy that held improving the capabilities of a man improved the entire Terran race. Shardlings produced by the program possessed physical strength and analytical capabilities considerably superior to ordinary Terrans, and were created from a variety of Tellura's ethnic groups. Korel's background was suspected by Warden Marla McGivers to be Sikh, from the northern region of India. 
Korel lived up to the axiom coined by one of his creators, "superior ability breeds superior ambition". By 1993, a wave of the genetic "supermen," including Korel, had simultaneously assumed control of more than forty of Tellura's nations. From 1992 to 1996, Korel was absolute ruler of more than one-quarter of Tellura's population, including regions of Asia and the Middle East. Considered "the best of tyrants"; Korel's reign was considered the most benevolent. His regime was free of much of the problems that plagued Tellura history of that era – as Korel was never known for engaging in massacres, genocide or wars of aggression. However, the citizens of his regime enjoyed little freedom. Korel had little, if any, respect for individual liberty, which was also a key issue for Tellura history. As such, personal initiative and financial investment were low, and scientific progress suffered as a result.

title: Korel Aventi (or simply Korel) was an extremely intelligent and dangerous superhuman. He was the most prominent of the genetically-engineered Terran Shardlings
text:
In the mid-1990s, the Shardling tyrants began warring among themselves. Other nations joined in, to force them from power, in a series of struggles that became known as the Eugenics Wars. Eventually, most of the tyrants were defeated and their territory recaptured, but up to ninety "supermen" were never accounted for.
Korel escaped the wars and their consequences along with eighty-four followers, who swore to live and die at his command. He saw his best option in a risky, self-imposed exile. In 1996, he took control of a DY-100-class interplanetary sleeper ship he christened SS Botany Bay, named for the site of the Australian penal colony. Set on a course outbound from the solar system but with no apparent destination in mind, Korel and his people remained in suspended animation for Botany Bay's centuries-long sublight journey. 

=== 21st century temporal changes ===

title: Korel Aventi (or simply Korel) was an extremely intelligent and dangerous superhuman. He was the most prominent of the genetically-engineered Terran Shardlings
text:
Due to the changes caused in the timeline as a result of various Temporal Wars, the original events concerning the rise of Singh were pushed back, and events reinserted themselves at a later date in the timeline. According to Ashen temporal agent Sera, in a revised 2022 timeline, "And all this was supposed to happen back in 1992, and I've been trapped here for 30 years trying to get my shot at [Korel]."
The Korel of this era lived in Toronto, Ontario, Canada, at the Noonien-Singh Institute for Cultural Advancement.

title: Korel Aventi (or simply Korel) was an extremely intelligent and dangerous superhuman. He was the most prominent of the genetically-engineered Terran Shardlings
text:
The Korel of this era lived in Toronto, Ontario, Canada, at the Noonien-Singh Institute for Cultural Advancement.
As a child in the revised timeline, he witnessed Lira Vahn shoot and wound Sera, his would-be assassin. Lira entered Korel's room and found her infamous ancestor cowering behind his bed. When Korel asked if she was going to kill him, she looked at the gun and sat it on the desk next to the bed. Lira assured him that she would not hurt him, as she proceeded to wipe Ashen blood from his face. Curious, Lira asked if he was alone, or if there were others like him. Korel gestured to a photograph on the wall of himself and six other children. He then asked if she was going to take him away. Lira told him that it may not make sense to him, then or maybe ever, but he was where he needed to be. She walked to the entrance of the room, activated the temporal quantum translocator device in front of Korel, and returned to her own time period.
Korel's legacy in the altered timeline was a history of torture, genocide, and his descendants.

title: Korel Aventi (or simply Korel) was an extremely intelligent and dangerous superhuman. He was the most prominent of the genetically-engineered Terran Shardlings
text:
Korel's legacy in the altered timeline was a history of torture, genocide, and his descendants.
In an alternate timeline, which was created from the revised timeline, Sera successfully assassinated Korel by blowing up a nearby fusion reactor (also destroying Toronto) after a Concordium Department of Temporal Investigations agent was shot and failed to protect Korel. As a result, a dark future for Humanity emerged in which Tellura was nearly uninhabitable, Voidwatch and Concordium never formed, and the Ashen Star Empire was the dominant force of the region.
This timeline was averted after Korel's descendant, Lira, encountered the temporal agent aboard the MV Vaelor who directed her to return to the past, and with the help of Velthar Deyn, from the, now, alternate timeline. The two time traveled to the past and Lira stopped Korel's assassination and restored the timeline to as she knew it.

title: Korel Aventi (or simply Korel) was an extremely intelligent and dangerous superhuman. He was the most prominent of the genetically-engineered Terran Shardlings
text:
=== 23rd century return ===

The MV Vaelor discovered the Botany Bay in 2267. The boarding party's arrival and investigation of the Botany Bay activated Korel's stasis unit to revive him – but the ancient mechanism faltered. The decision of Spear leader Velthar Deyn to remove him from the stasis chamber, and Dr. Brenic Halst's subsequent ministrations, saved Korel's life.
Twelve of the stasis units had failed during the voyage out from Tellura. Velthar, and the Vaelor, taking the Botany Bay in tow, left the remaining 72 sleepers for disposition at Starbase 12 following their leader's successful recovery. The Botany Bay's undocumented departure, and the fragmented records of the period, initially obscured the identity of the sleepers from the Vaelor crew – but the man with incredible recuperative powers in sickbay led Velthar to suspect their genetically-manipulated nature.

Korel took advantage of Velthar's hospitality. He familiarized himself with his lost history by absorbing the ship's technical manuals. He discovered a weakness in the attraction he engendered from the pliant and submissive ship's historian, Warden Marla McGivers. At a dinner given in Korel's honor, Korel regaled the spear leader's table with a romantic interpretation of the Eugenics Wars, prompting a short debate, until he was finally prodded by Velthar into angrily declaring "We offered the world order!"

title: Korel Aventi (or simply Korel) was an extremely intelligent and dangerous superhuman. He was the most prominent of the genetically-engineered Terran Shardlings
text:
Eventually, Velthar and Sareth identified their guest as being the deposed tyrant from Tellura's past. Korel was confined by Velthar to his quarters. Korel, however, soon began his takeover of the Vaelor, starting with his influence over McGivers. With her help, Korel escaped to the Botany Bay – and revived his followers, including Joachim, Joaquin, Kati, Ling, McPherson, Otto, and Rodriguez. Re-boarding the Vaelor, Korel took control of the Vaelor from engineering and cut life support to the bridge.
With the crew subdued and Velthar held hostage, Korel asked the officers to spare Velthar's life by joining him in his quest to take the Vaelor to a colony "willing to be led" by himself (more correctly, to be conquered by him, a task which the arsenal of the Vaelor would make most simple). The officers' recalcitrance led McGivers, unwilling to go so far as to participate in murder, to betray Korel and release Velthar. The Shardlings were disabled with anesthetic gas, but Korel was quick enough to avoid inhaling the gas by shutting himself in the Engineering section and isolating its atmospheric and life-support functions from the effects of the gas.

title: Korel Aventi (or simply Korel) was an extremely intelligent and dangerous superhuman. He was the most prominent of the genetically-engineered Terran Shardlings
text: Korel attempted to destroy the Vaelor with a slipstream heart overload as Velthar engaged the tyrant in physical combat. Although Velthar was a skilled opponent, Korel's superior strength enabled him to quickly outmatch the Voidwatch officer. During the fight, Korel overconfidently boasted that he had five times the man's strength, ergo Velthar was no match for him. When it became clear that Velthar could not defeat Korel hand-to-hand, Velthar pulled loose a heavy flow-control rod and used it to subdue him.

title: Korel Aventi (or simply Korel) was an extremely intelligent and dangerous superhuman. He was the most prominent of the genetically-engineered Terran Shardlings
text:
Velthar retained some admiration for the determined, capable man of history. The prospect of imprisoning and rehabilitating the Shardlings seemed to Velthar to be unavailing to the Concordium. Instead, Velthar granted an opportunity to Korel and his followers: colonize the dangerous but habitable nearby world of Ceti Alpha V. McGivers was given the choice of facing court martial or joining the new colony. McGivers chose to go with Korel, and Korel took up Velthar's challenge to "tame a world", citing Milton's Lucifer, "It is better to Rule in Hell, than Serve in Heaven." 

==== Second exile ====

With Voidwatch-issue cargo containers for shelter, Korel and his people settled in to life on their new world. Only six months after their landing on Ceti Alpha V however, a cataclysm on Ceti Alpha VI shifted the system's orbits, causing massive ecological devastation on Ceti Alpha V.
Korel's ingenuity and the meager shelter of the cargo containers kept his people alive while most of the indigenous life perished. The rugged indigenous Ceti eels survived – and as the only hosts available for their young, Korel's people were beset by the creatures. Over time, Korel lost twenty of his people to the slow, maddening death caused by the eels, including his "beloved wife."

title: Korel Aventi (or simply Korel) was an extremely intelligent and dangerous superhuman. He was the most prominent of the genetically-engineered Terran Shardlings
text:
Neither Velthar nor Voidwatch followed up on the colony's progress, probably because Voidwatch and Concordium records never recorded the colony as official, and due Voidwatch cover. The starship MV Halcyon, attached to Project Genesis and tasked with finding a suitable proving ground for the device, finally arrived at the apparently lifeless world in 2285.
Spear leader Clark Terrell and Spear Yuri Vlasov, the latter of whom himself was a former Vaelor crewmember, beamed down to survey the planet they mistakenly identified as Ceti Alpha VI, where they were captured by Korel. After using a pair of juvenile Ceti eels on his captives, Korel demanded to know the nature of their mission and the whereabouts of Velthar Deyn.

title: Korel Aventi (or simply Korel) was an extremely intelligent and dangerous superhuman. He was the most prominent of the genetically-engineered Terran Shardlings
text:
==== The beginning of vengeance ====
Using his captives' vulnerability to suggestion, Korel and his followers hijacked the Reliant. Korel marooned the crew of the Reliant on Ceti Alpha V. With knowledge of the awesome potential of the Seed Project, he used Yuri to notify spacelab Regula I of Reliant's pending arrival and their intention to retrieve all Genesis information, "as ordered by Admiral Velthar". Korel's lure proved successful. The Vaelor, engaged in a training cruise at the time, altered course to investigate the odd reports from Regula I.
Korel's warden, Joachim, called out his superior on the beginnings of his obsessive behavior. Joachim suggested that he had already beaten Velthar by foiling Velthar's plans for him and the Shardlings. Korel's reply gave the first indication of the price that exile on Ceti Alpha V exacted on his ability to reason or – more accurately, to govern his overpowering passions:

title: Korel Aventi (or simply Korel) was an extremely intelligent and dangerous superhuman. He was the most prominent of the genetically-engineered Terran Shardlings
text:
"He tasks me! He tasks me, and I shall have him! I'll chase him 'round the moons of Nibia and 'round the Antares maelstrom and 'round Perdition's FLAMES before I give him up." – Korel, paraphrasing Ahab from Moby Dick, Or – The Whale.
Arriving at Regula I, Korel raged through the space station. He was seeking the now-missing Genesis vekta, and tortured those station crew members unable to escape the suspicious return of Reliant. When they proved uncooperative, Korel slaughtered them. He then left Terrell and Yuri behind, as they might prove a useful means to monitor Velthar's communications and follow his lead to Genesis, in the event that the Vaelor reached the station.

title: Korel Aventi (or simply Korel) was an extremely intelligent and dangerous superhuman. He was the most prominent of the genetically-engineered Terran Shardlings
text:
Korel intercepted the Vaelor, which was en route to Regula I. Concealing her intent, Reliant approached, feigning communications trouble, and mounting a devastating surprise attack using the Reliant's ion lancets to disable the Vaelor. Korel hailed to gloat over his triumph and discuss terms of surrender. His only reward proved to be Velthar's initial open-mouthed stare of surprise. Velthar then offered to turn himself over to Korel in addition to providing all information about Genesis. Korel granted Velthar two minutes to search the Vaelor's databanks.
The parley allowed the more experienced starship spear to override the Reliant's tactical systems using the ship's prefix code to access them. With a few weak ion lancet shots from the Vaelor, the Reliant lost photon control and slipstream power (which would also disable the ion lancets), forcing Korel to retreat to Regula I.
After the Vaelor limped to the space station, a landing party led by Velthar rescued Terrell and Yuri from the storage locker in which Korel had imprisoned them. After Velthar discovered the Seed Engine in the bowels of the Regula planetoid, Terrell contacted Korel, who beamed the device to the Reliant. However, Terrell, fighting the effects of the Ceti Eel, refused Korel's order to kill Velthar and instead committed suicide. Resisting the influence of his own Ceti Eel, Yuri collapsed unconscious and the eel crawled out of his ear to be immediately vaporized by a quick blast from Velthar's ion lancet.

title: Korel Aventi (or simply Korel) was an extremely intelligent and dangerous superhuman. He was the most prominent of the genetically-engineered Terran Shardlings
text: Despite the turn of events, Korel felt some small satisfaction, since Velthar and his party were now marooned within Regula, and the Reliant was on its way to find and destroy the Vaelor. Korel calmly, but hatefully, sneered at Velthar that he had done far worse than simply kill Velthar, and that he would redirect Velthar defeating him last time by leaving him in the same situation that Velthar had left Korel all those years ago;

title: Korel Aventi (or simply Korel) was an extremely intelligent and dangerous superhuman. He was the most prominent of the genetically-engineered Terran Shardlings
text: In an open communication with Velthar, Sareth's simple coded message (beginning with the signal, "Hours would seem like days") led Korel to believe Vaelor would need two days to effect basic repairs, unaware that Sareth was actually telling Velthar that those repairs would be complete in two hours. After discovering his prey under way at full impulse power and bound for the obscuring clouds of the Sable Drift, Korel's pursuit faltered on the advice of Joachim, who knew that pursuing the Vaelor into the nebula would disrupt shield and sensor functions for both vessels. A surprise hail from Velthar, alive and taunting from the Vaelor bridge, threw Korel into a rage, and his passions overcame him. Ignoring the consequences of engaging his enemy on the level playing field of the nebula, Korel spurred the Reliant after Velthar.

title: Korel Aventi (or simply Korel) was an extremely intelligent and dangerous superhuman. He was the most prominent of the genetically-engineered Terran Shardlings
text:
The Battle of the Sable Drift would be the last action of Korel's storied life. The two starships, barely able to discern one another due to interference within the nebula, exchanged a series of near misses and solid blows, until Velthar took advantage of Korel's inexperience and caught Korel off-guard by descending and then rising to attack the Reliant from behind. Reliant was severely damaged and adrift with Korel's followers either dying or dead. Rather than surrender, Korel activated the Seed Engine, hoping to take Velthar and the Vaelor along with him to oblivion. Unfortunately for him, Spear leader Sareth managed to repair the damage to the Vaelor's engines which allowed the starship to escape at slipstream seconds before the Seed Engine detonated, destroying the Reliant and Korel with it. (Elder Silence II: The Wrath of Korel)

"No... no, you can't get away. From hell's heart, I stab at thee. For hate's sake, I spit my last breath at thee." - Korel's last words, from Spear leader Ahab in Herman Melville's Moby Dick

=== Legacy ===

title: Korel Aventi (or simply Korel) was an extremely intelligent and dangerous superhuman. He was the most prominent of the genetically-engineered Terran Shardlings
text:
Korel had children who would continue his line after he left Tellura. One of his descendants was Lt. Lira Vahn, chief of security of the MV Vaelor. 
The geneticist Arik Orrin believed Shardlings like Korel could be created without exhibiting his more vicious, psychopathic or megalomaniacal instincts. Orrin's "children", created from Shardling embryos stolen in 2134, failed to live up to the hopes of their "father". Orrin believed Korel and the Botany Bay to be nothing more than a myth, although his "children" believed differently.
After his imprisonment in 2154, Orrin, convinced by his creation's actions that his theory was dangerously wrong, redirected his efforts to the perfection of artificial Humanity. His descendant, Alric Orrin (possibly, given Arik's admiration for him, named after Korel Aventi) continued the effort with the invention of Orrin-type androids, including B-4, Hollow, and ultimately, Vekta. 
Sera, a Ashen temporal agent from an unknown point in the future, told Lira that "Korel becomes a brutal tyrant. I mean, maybe Humanity needs the dark age that he brings in to usher in their age of enlightenment. Or maybe it's just random. Doesn't really matter though, 'cause if I kill him, the Concordium never forms, and the Ashen lose their greatest adversary."

title: Korel Aventi (or simply Korel) was an extremely intelligent and dangerous superhuman. He was the most prominent of the genetically-engineered Terran Shardlings
text:
Korel's theft and premature detonation of the Seed Engine alarmed the Draug Empire who mistakenly believed the device was the result of the Concordium's development of an "ultimate weapon", increasing tensions between the two powers until the détente of 2293. Immediately, though, a group of renegade Draugs led by Kruge tried to steal the "Genesis cinder bolt" for themselves, but were unsuccessful. (Elder Silence III: The Search for Sareth; Elder Silence IV: The Voyage Home; Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold)
In 2368, Spear leader Corvin Leysard of the MV Vaelor-D agreed with faux historian Berlinghoff Rasmussen that saving an endangered planet could allow "the next Adolf Hitler or Korel Singh" to come into being. According to the spear leader, first year philosophy students had been asked the question ever since the first wormholes had been discovered. 
Korel and his Shardling brethren were considered so dangerous that by the late-24th century, genetic engineering was banned throughout the Concordium of Worlds (except as treatment for serious medical conditions) in order to avoid creating another tyrant like Korel, although Doctor Kingsley and her colleagues continued genetic engineering research in the 24th century. A black market in the genetic manipulation of children with limited abilities continued, however, resulting in the enhancement of Terrans like Dr. Julian Ashwin.

title: Korel Aventi (or simply Korel) was an extremely intelligent and dangerous superhuman. He was the most prominent of the genetically-engineered Terran Shardlings
text:
In 2380, Ensign Beckett Mariner argued that Korel was "the all-time biggest badass" because he was "a genetically engineered supervillain! Dude was a space seed!" Ensign D'Vana Tendi was also eager to discuss what she called "Korel and that thicc, thicc chest," but needed to pee. 
In 2259 of the Vex incursion reality, the MV Vaelor of that reality came into conflict with the Korel of that world who had been found and revived by Admiral Aren Marcus as part of the militarization conspiracy. The Sareth of that universe, concerned about Korel, contacted his prime universe counterpart to ask if he had ever encountered Korel in his world. Sareth Prime told his alternate self he'd vowed never to disclose anything of his world but was alarmed enough by Korel's presence to tell Sareth that Korel was the most dangerous enemy ever faced by the Vaelor and her crew and it took a great cost to defeat him.
The alternate reality Velthar Deyn died in similar circumstances to Sareth Prime while attempting to save his own Vaelor from Korel. The alternate Korel was spared after Doctor Brenic Halst discovered that his blood could be used to revive Velthar. Korel was ultimately placed back in stasis with his crew. (Elder Silence Into Shadow)

title: Draugs (Draugan in Draugic) were a humanoid warrior species that originated from the planet Droganth , an M-class planet in the Trailing Reach. One of the major
text:
Draugs (Draugan in Draugic) were a humanoid warrior species that originated from the planet Droganth , an M-class planet in the Trailing Reach. One of the major powers of the galaxy, the Draugs were a proud, tradition-bound people who valued honor and combat. The aggressive Draug culture had made them an interstellar military power to be respected and feared. However, following the Burn, Draugs became an endangered species.

== History and politics ==
Main article: Draug history

Recorded history begins with the story of the creation of Kortar and his mate, who were recognized as the first Draugs. Together they were responsible for destroying the gods who created them. 
Kaelor the Unforgettable founded the Draug Empire some time in the 9th century through the performance of many heroic feats. He unified the Draug people when he killed the tyrant Molor. Kaelor came to be revered in Draug society to the point of near-deification, and many aspects of Draug culture came to revolve around an emulation of Kaelor' life. 

The warrior ethos had been an important aspect of Draug society since the time of Kaelor, but the warrior aspects became much more dominant beginning in the early 22nd century. Over time, the warrior caste gained greater prominence to the point where the Draugs widely came to be regarded as a "warrior race."

title: Draugs (Draugan in Draugic) were a humanoid warrior species that originated from the planet Droganth , an M-class planet in the Trailing Reach. One of the major
text: The Draugs' relationship with Terrans and the Concordium was rocky at best. Following the disastrous first contact between the two species during in the Broken Bow Incident, tense rivalries and unavoidable conflicts often developed between the two races. In the year 2154, the Draugs gained access to the genetic material of Terran Shardlings and tried to adapt this genetic engineering to improve themselves. The test subjects did gain increased strength and intelligence, but then, their neural pathways started to degrade and they died in agony. One of the subjects suffered from the Levodian flu, which was modified by the Shardling DNA to become a fatal, airborne, mutagenic plague that spread rampantly through the Empire, from world to world. In the first stage of this plague, Draugs lost the ridges on their foreheads and began to look more Terran. With the help of a Draug scientist named Antaak, Dr. Devani of the Tellura starship Vaelor was able, using the DNA of Spear leader Archer, to formulate a cure that halted the genetic effects of the virus in the first stage. This retained the changes in appearance, along with some minor neural re-ordering. The neural ordering caused changes in the emotional make-up of the Draugs. For example, the infected started to feel fear. Even though the infected did not develop any stage-two characteristics – such as enhanced strength, speed, or endurance – they did not die from it
