text: . For example, the infected started to feel fear. Even though the infected did not develop any stage-two characteristics – such as enhanced strength, speed, or endurance – they did not die from it. This left millions of Draugs changed. These alterations were even passed on to their children.

title: Draugs (Draugan in Draugic) were a humanoid warrior species that originated from the planet Droganth , an M-class planet in the Trailing Reach. One of the major
text: In the 2250s and 2260s, groups of Draugs with and without ridges had been encountered by the Concordium. By the 2270s it had become more commonplace to encounter Draugs with forehead ridges than not. (Elder Silence: The Motion Picture, et al.) Draugs did not discuss the circumstances of this mutation with outsiders and, by the 24th century, the reason for smooth-forehead Draugs was not widely known outside the Empire.

title: Draugs (Draugan in Draugic) were a humanoid warrior species that originated from the planet Droganth , an M-class planet in the Trailing Reach. One of the major
text:
By 2223, relations between the Concordium and the Draug Empire degenerated to a point of relentless hostility, which lasted for several decades. (Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold; Later Epoch: "First Contact")

The lingering tensions between Draugs and Terrans continued to rise, eventually leading to the Battle of Donatu V, near Sherman's Planet in 2245 and the Battle of the Binary Stars in 2256, which was provoked by T'Varreth in order to unite the squabbling Great Houses against the Concordium. This resulted in the first Concordium-Draug War, where the Draug Empire successfully invaded and occupied nearly twenty percent of Concordium space. 
Later, another conflict erupted into the Concordium-Draug War of 2267. The Organians quickly intervened and ended the war after only four days of fighting. Over the next several decades an uneasy peace developed, broken only by brief but fierce skirmishes and conflicts. (Elder Silence III: The Search for Sareth; Elder Silence V: The Final Frontier) A true and lasting peace finally came in 2293, with the signing of the Stone Hollow Accords, thanks to the efforts of Chancellor Gorkon and the Terran Voidwatch officer Velthar Deyn. (Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold; Later Epoch: "Unification II"; Pharae Saga: "Flashback"; NINEFOLD: "You Are Cordially Invited") Since then, despite several periods of rocky relations (see Concordium-Draug War (2372-73)), the Concordium and the Draug Empire have been steadfast allies, especially in the face of Dominion aggression in the 2370s.

title: Draugs (Draugan in Draugic) were a humanoid warrior species that originated from the planet Droganth , an M-class planet in the Trailing Reach. One of the major
text:
The Draug relationship with the Ashen people was extremely erratic. The Draugs typically regarded the Ashen Star Empire as a "blood enemy" since at least the 23rd century. Sporadic Ashen attacks against Draug colonies, such as the Stone Hollow Massacre, and interference in Draug affairs, including the Draug Civil War, continued to sour relations between the two peoples. 
The Draugs were driven to near-extinction by the Burn, losing Droganth and several other worlds. During the following Draug diaspora, they rejected help from the Concordium and became a race of refugees. In 3195, Voidwatch was able to locate a new homeworld for the Draugs, Faan Alpha, and helped the Draugs achieve the conquest they needed to settle there. The Draugs subsequently renamed the planet New Droganth. 

=== Parallel universes ===
In the mirror universe, the Draugs were one of the races subjugated by the Terran Empire. By the 24th century Draugs and Vaskari founded the Draug-Vaskari Alliance and eventually defeated their Terran occupiers. 
In the Vex incursion reality, in 2233, the crew of the USS Kelvin briefly considered whether a particular lightning storm effect, observed by the Kelvin near the edge of Draug space, might be Draug in origin. Voidwatch discarded this possibility. The phenomenon preceded the arrival of the Ashen mining vessel Vex from the prime universe. The Vex attacked and obliterated an armada of 47 Draug warbirds in 2258. (Elder Silence)

title: Draugs (Draugan in Draugic) were a humanoid warrior species that originated from the planet Droganth , an M-class planet in the Trailing Reach. One of the major
text:
By 2259 in the alternate reality, after Voidwatch's first contact with the Empire, the Draugs had conquered and occupied two planets known to the Concordium and fired on Voidwatch ships half a dozen times. Tensions between the two powers were high and an all-out war was considered inevitable. During that year, before surrendering to the Concordium, Korel Aventi destroyed three D4-class patrol ships on the Draug homeworld, killing the crews of the vessels. (Elder Silence Into Shadow)
According to Daniels, the Draugs joined the Concordium by the 26th century in one possible timeline. 

== Evolution ==

=== Origins ===

Like their Terran, Vaskari, Syrith, and Ashen counterparts, Draugs and many of the Elder Spiral's species all shared a common ancestry back to the ancient humanoids and the DNA code they produced and seeded across the galaxy. Though each evolved under separate conditions from each other, their shared DNA allowed these species to remain roughly compatible and viable with each other. 
Possessing extreme strength and speed, early Draugs - or Proto-Draugs - were quite large, weighing up to 200 kilograms. They were armored with an exoskeleton, with spines and bony plates protruding from their sides, upper arms, and back, arms that ended in clawed pincers. On their face were venom sacs, filled with a bio-acidic compound and spitting glands inside their mouth that were used for defense and marking their territory. Along with these sacs, these early Draugs had two mandibles protruding from their lower jaw.

title: Draugs (Draugan in Draugic) were a humanoid warrior species that originated from the planet Droganth , an M-class planet in the Trailing Reach. One of the major
text:
These prehistoric males used vocalizations to frighten other predators, mark their territory, and commence their mating process. These early Draugs mating rituals involving biting its intended mate, to induce pheromone production in the sebaceous glands. Once the mate was ready, the pheromones drew the male Draug back to its location. They are described as "mindless" and "filled with rage", who will attack one another. 

=== The Modern Warrior ===
Modern Draugs developed a varied line of physical attributes, ranging from well pronounced cranial ridges to what was best described with the dysphemism "pointy-headed", as coined by Harry Mudd.

title: Draugs (Draugan in Draugic) were a humanoid warrior species that originated from the planet Droganth , an M-class planet in the Trailing Reach. One of the major
text:
=== The Modern Warrior ===
Modern Draugs developed a varied line of physical attributes, ranging from well pronounced cranial ridges to what was best described with the dysphemism "pointy-headed", as coined by Harry Mudd.

==== Anatomy ====
Like most humanoids, the essence of the Draug anatomical form consisted of a head, neck, torso, and four limbs.
Internally, the Draug anatomy was markedly different from that of other humanoids. There was a great deal more multiple redundancies in their organs, a principle they called brak'lul. This allowed Draugs to survive severe injuries in battle. They had twenty-three ribs (making up a honeycomb lattice), two livers, an eight-chambered heart, three lungs, two urinary tracts, four testicles, and even redundant neural function as well as multiple stomachs. Some geneticists believed that the extra organs, notably the third lung, evolved to give Draugs greater stamina on the battlefield. Draugs had relatively little knowledge of their own biology and their medicine was very poorly developed. This was largely due to their warrior traditions – a Draug who was wounded was expected to be left to either survive through his own strength, die, or undergo the hegh'bat, a form of ritual suicide. Conversely, their society having dueled and killed each other for generations taught them what is immediately lethal for their species.

title: Draugs (Draugan in Draugic) were a humanoid warrior species that originated from the planet Droganth , an M-class planet in the Trailing Reach. One of the major
text:
The most distinctive feature of Draugs were their cranial ridges. While typically covering the forehead and the front part of the scalp, these ridges could be as small as taking up only a portion of the forehead and scalp, to as large as wrapping around the entire skull. Typically, the further back the ridges reached, the longer the skull became, resulting in some Draugs having noticeably longer skulls than others. (Elder Silence: The Motion Picture, et al.) 
Some Draugs' ridges produced spikes, a feature not usually associated with Draugs. 

Draug forehead ridges varied significantly individual-to-individual, and were essentially unique, making them an identifying feature. Young Draugs were know to craft keepsakes of their cranial ridges for their parents. 
Draug cranial ridges could be pierced, allowing jewelry to be worn through them. (Elder Silence Into Shadow)
The cranium, itself, was encased in an exoskeleton, which possessed a feature known as the tricipital lobe. 

Draug noses were typically ridged, though like their cranial ridges, these ridges varied greatly by individual. Some combination of horizontal ridges, vertical ridges, and ridges around the nostril was typical. Draug nose ridges could connect to their cranial ridges, or be separate. Some Draugs had reduced or negligible nose ridges.

title: Draugs (Draugan in Draugic) were a humanoid warrior species that originated from the planet Droganth , an M-class planet in the Trailing Reach. One of the major
text:
Eyebrows tended to grow in a more diagonal direction than other humanoids, but also had noticeably diagonal suborbital ridges where eyebrows otherwise existed.
Draugs ear structures varied in shape, from essentially terran-looking, to ridged structures outlining the ear canal, and several stages in between. Other variations have also been observed. Draugs had a more limited range of hearing in the higher frequencies than many other humanoid species.

title: Draugs (Draugan in Draugic) were a humanoid warrior species that originated from the planet Droganth , an M-class planet in the Trailing Reach. One of the major
text:
Draug eyes had round pupils, varying colors of iris, and white sclera. Draugs were known to flash more of the whites of their eyes, which they use to intimidate a rival or enemy. While Sareth claimed that Draugs lacked tear ducts, Draugs such as Kurn could be seen shedding tears, and Draug mythology stated that Kaelor once filled the ocean with his tears. (Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold, Later Epoch: "Birthright, Part II"; NINEFOLD: "Sons of Mogh")
Draug teeth typically consisted of two sharp incisors, with generally (but not always) crooked or sharpened teeth. Draugs were sometimes known sharpen their teeth, especially before going into battle. 
Draugs of both sexes usually grew hair on their heads, though it usually left the bulk of the cranial ridges exposed. Male Draugs were known to be able to grown facial hair as well. Hair was typically worn long, and was typically wavy or curly, and could be described as thick and luxuriant. Draug hair was almost always dark in color, though it did turn gray with age.

title: Draugs (Draugan in Draugic) were a humanoid warrior species that originated from the planet Droganth , an M-class planet in the Trailing Reach. One of the major
text:
Accelerated hair growth was often experienced by Draugs during puberty, or jak'tahla, along with severe mood swings and unusual aggressive tendencies. (Elder Silence: Insurrection) Draug traditions saw them shaving their hair away during wartime, though this tradition became less common into the 24th century and beyond. Draugs could be bald without the prerequiasite of wartime, however. (Elder Silence: The Motion Picture; Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold; Elder Silence Into Shadow; Dawn Era: "Divergence"; First Era: "The Trouble with Tribbles", "Day of the Dove"; NINEFOLD: "Trials and Tribble-ations") 
Many Draugs possessed vertical ridges on their necks, which could extend as far up as their chins, and sometimes could extend down onto their chests. The back of the Draug torso had strong ridging around the spinal column. For some cases, this could extend onto the shoulder blades and up onto the back of the head. Some Draugs also possessed ridges on the sides of their abdomens. The buttocks region could even be ridged. 
After birth, some Draug infants experienced a pronounced curvature to the spine, a form of scoliosis, which was correctable by surgery. This "defect" tended to run in Draug families, especially among females. Concordium medicine, fortunately, advanced beyond that, allowing an additional choice of treatment involving genetic modification of the fetus.

title: Draugs (Draugan in Draugic) were a humanoid warrior species that originated from the planet Droganth , an M-class planet in the Trailing Reach. One of the major
text:
While most Draug hands were very similar to terran hands, some Draugs seemed to have thick, sharp talon-like claws that encompassed the end of their digits, though it was unclear if these claws were biological or ornamentation. Draug feet also possessed ridged structures. 

Skin colors ranged from pale tan, to olive, brown, light gray, dark gray, and black. Some Draugs had a slightly pearlescent or metallic sheen on their skin. Albino Draugs were rare, and often considered outcasts in Draug society.

title: Draugs (Draugan in Draugic) were a humanoid warrior species that originated from the planet Droganth , an M-class planet in the Trailing Reach. One of the major
text:
==== Physiology ====
False labor was common among pregnant female Draugs, and when labor did begin, it could sometimes last several days. Like other mammalian species, Draug females were capable of lactating to breast-feed infants. 
Draug children matured far more quickly than Terran children. At the age of only one Tellura year, a Draug child had the appearance a Terran child had at about four. By the age of eight Tellura years, a Draug attained the maturity a Terran did not reach until about age sixteen. When Draug children began growing into adults, they went through jak'tahla, a Draug form of puberty. 
Rop'ngor was a common childhood disease among Draugs. 
Draugs tended to live for over 150 years. Even into advanced old age, Draugs were usually still strong enough for combat, but were still susceptible to various mental conditions associated with old age. 
Draugs were notably stronger than most humanoids, at least as strong as Syrithi. They might have even been stronger, as the half-Draug Kestra Torv was able to wrestle with the Syrith Vorik on equal grounds and eventually defeat him, despite the fact that he was larger than her. However, despite their endurance and general robustness, Draugs had a considerably lower tolerance to the cold than Terrans. 
The Draug sense of smell was notably acute; in fact, it was powerful enough to be used effectively to track down prey during a hunt. Their sense of smell was also suggested to play an integral role in their mating practices.

title: Draugs (Draugan in Draugic) were a humanoid warrior species that originated from the planet Droganth , an M-class planet in the Trailing Reach. One of the major
text: Doctor Julian Ashwin once sarcastically noted that the natural odor produced by Draugs was comparable to an "earthy, peaty aroma with a touch of lilac." To Terrans and Syrithi alike, Draug ships smelled bad. (Elder Silence IV: The Voyage Home; Dawn Era: "Sleeping Dogs") For example, Brenic Halst once referred to the environment of a Draug Talon, operated until recently by Draugs, as having a "stench." (Elder Silence IV: The Voyage Home)

title: Draugs (Draugan in Draugic) were a humanoid warrior species that originated from the planet Droganth , an M-class planet in the Trailing Reach. One of the major
text:
Draugs such as Kurn had the instinctive ability to sense the decision to kill by looking into the eyes of their opponents. Gharun despite being raised by Terrans on Tellura, retained this ability when he sensed Durnak's warrior spirit returning enough to win their duel without killing Gharun. 

Draug blood could contain ribosomes that were compatible for transfusion with a Ashen. Draug blood varied in color from dark red to more of a lightish pink. (Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold, Elowen: "Point of Light")

Draug nutritional requirements were typical of most humanoids, whereas, Dr. Pulaski once noted that, while their food was considered by most to be unpalatable, usually, "what kills us, kills them." One exception of this observation was the tea used in the Draug tea ceremony, which was toxic to the point of being deadly to Terrans, and capable of seriously sickening Draugs, as it did. 
Some sounds were inaudible to Draugs. 

=== Shardling virus ===

title: Draugs (Draugan in Draugic) were a humanoid warrior species that originated from the planet Droganth , an M-class planet in the Trailing Reach. One of the major
text:
=== Shardling virus ===

Draugs afflicted with the shardling virus, propagated by a mutation of the Levodian flu, was inadvertently created by Draug researchers who were attempting to bio-engineer enhanced warriors using DNA from genetically-modified Terran embryos left over from Tellura's Eugenics Wars. These Draugs lost their cranial ridge features, and were in essence, remarkably similar in appearance to modern Terrans. 
Though the cure for the virus had been distributed throughout the Empire, the afflicted Draugs' DNA had been altered by the virus, and condition was passed onto the descendants of the infected. Initially there were millions of Draugs who had to live with the disfigurement for well over a century. 

Though Terran in appearance and distinguishable primarily by scan slate readings alone, tribbles were still able to single out and identify these Draugs. 

=== Hybridization ===
Draug pregnancies normally ran thirty weeks, but with mixed species, gestation times were shorter. As early as seven weeks (at which point a Terran fetus doesn't even have legs) a fetus with a single Draug grandparent was already able to kick the uterine wall hard enough to be felt externally. Draugs were said to have a different setup to their internal and external sex organs, including quadritesticles and two urinary tracts in males, which made male Terrans and female Draugs sexually incompatible - or at least, more difficult. However, basic anatomy does actually appear to align between Terrans and Draugs. Whenever Draugs interbred with other species they showed characteristics of both species.

title: Draugs (Draugan in Draugic) were a humanoid warrior species that originated from the planet Droganth , an M-class planet in the Trailing Reach. One of the major
text:
The odds against Draug-Terran conceptions were rather high. However, when successful, Draug and Terran metabolisms sometimes clashed, causing biochemical fluctuations in the mother, which may lead to fainting. Draug traits remained dominant for several generations, even with a single ancestor; therefore, a child even ¼ Draug still possessed forehead ridges. It is possible to see the eventual phenotype of a hybrid while the fetus is still gestating using a holographic program and projection. If early enough in development, genetic manipulation can be taken to remove Draug DNA from the developing fetus. 
Hybridization revealed that Draug DNA tended to be more dominantly expressive in the physical appearance of their offspring.

This was found to be especially true in the case of hair color and appearance of cranial ridges, especially with Terrans. In the case of Ashen-Draug hybridization, the ears were the only visible telltale indication of their non-Draug heritage. 

== Society ==

title: Draugs (Draugan in Draugic) were a humanoid warrior species that originated from the planet Droganth , an M-class planet in the Trailing Reach. One of the major
text:
Draug society was extremely complex. Before its decline in the mid-22nd century and again in the late 23rd century, Draug society was based on a feudal system organized around traditional Great Houses of noble lineage, to which various parts of the population owed fealty. The Great Houses are traditionally represented in the Draug High Council, which was led by a Chancellor, replacing the heredity leader of Emperor.
The decline of Draug culture was demonstrated in the acts of the Draugs themselves. They stopped caring about their weapons to the point that they let them rust and even stopped caring for true honor. Sometime after the shardling virus took hold of the Draug Empire, a new regime took control, turning the Empire into an authoritarian state that kept tabs on all who served. The old ways returned in the latter 23rd and early 24th centuries respectively.

title: Draugs (Draugan in Draugic) were a humanoid warrior species that originated from the planet Droganth , an M-class planet in the Trailing Reach. One of the major
text:
Males traditionally dominated public life in the Empire, assuming the leading roles in politics and the military with only rare exceptions. There were three notable exceptions to the prohibition of women serving on the High Council. In 2257 L'Rell rose to High Chancellor and Dennas served on the High Council. The third instance occurred in 2293 when Azetbur became Chancellor of the High Council after her father, Gorkon, was assassinated (Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold). Women traditionally dominated the household and the management of the family's affairs. Draug women were treated as equals, except in politics and matters of inheritance. Law prohibited them from serving in the High Council and they could not take control of their Houses unless they had the money and no male successors of the lineage. Otherwise, Draug women were expected to exhibit the same physical prowess and lust for blood and honor as the men.
Draug society functioned through a system of family reputation and honor. Tradition was an integral part of their lives and breaking from observances was considered a grievous insult to society, an insult not forgotten easily. An offense usually brought shame to the offender's name for several generations. The highest shame was discommendation, an action by the High Council to officially strip a Draug of his personal or family honor. Bloodlines and relations were also taken very seriously by any "true" Draug. Lines comprised more than mere family members.

title: Draugs (Draugan in Draugic) were a humanoid warrior species that originated from the planet Droganth , an M-class planet in the Trailing Reach. One of the major
text:
The military was integral to Draug society, as it provides opportunities for warriors to die in battle. For the same purpose, the Empire often seeks to expand through conquest. Discipline was strictly enforced, by one's superiors and subordinates both; the latter may assassinate his superior and take his place. This gives Terrans the false impression that there are no rules, but in fact, this can be done only under certain conditions, dereliction of duty and cowardice among them, and the challenge can be made only to a direct superior. 
An integral part of tradition was the various rituals that marked milestones in a Draug's life or the history of the Empire. Most notable of the rites was the Rite of Succession, which a future leader of the Empire had to complete with a valid Arbiter of Succession (Spear leader Corvin Leysard, in the case of Relloch) overseeing the proceedings. Before the Rite could begin, there was another elaborate ceremony needed to confirm the death of the previous leader. This was known as the Sonchi ceremony.

title: Draugs (Draugan in Draugic) were a humanoid warrior species that originated from the planet Droganth , an M-class planet in the Trailing Reach. One of the major
text:
If the house that an individual Draug belonged to was dissolved or fell into dishonor, he could be adopted into another house through the R'uustai or alternative ceremonies that symbolically marked the joining of kinship and allegiance. . The Right of Vengeance, allowed Draugs to seek redress for the deaths of their family members by engaging the one responsible in single combat. The right was so important, that even the discommended could claim it against important political figures, as the discommended Gharun was able to challenge Valdor (a candidate for the title of Chancellor. 
Draugs were extremely territorial. According to the first known Draug linguist, there was no such thing as an "insignificant corner of Draug space".

title: Draugs (Draugan in Draugic) were a humanoid warrior species that originated from the planet Droganth , an M-class planet in the Trailing Reach. One of the major
text:
== Religion and tradition ==
See also: Draug religion

title: Draugs (Draugan in Draugic) were a humanoid warrior species that originated from the planet Droganth , an M-class planet in the Trailing Reach. One of the major
text:
Being a warrior and ritual were two very important elements in Draug society. Before the Burn, individual Draug warriors were expected to go through the Rite of Ascension to be recognized as a full adult. After The Burn, a young Draug can be induct into being a warrior by hunting and killing a prey 
Draugs did not believe in fate; however, they did appear to believe in some form of luck. 
A Draug who was unable to fight, and hence unable to live as a warrior anymore, had the traditional obligation of committing the hegh'bat, which was the Draug ritual suicide. Tradition dictated that the eldest son or a close personal friend must assist. That person's role was to hand the dying Draug a knife so that he could plunge it into his heart, remove it, and then wipe the blood on his own sleeve. 
Draug rituals included the R'uustai, a bonding ceremony which joined two people together in a relationship similar to brotherhood. Draug tradition held that "the son of a Draug is a man the day he can first hold a blade." 
If a Draug warrior struck another Draug with the back of his hand, it was interpreted as a challenge to the death. Draug warriors spoke proudly to each other; they did not whisper or keep their distance. Standing far away or whispering were considered insults in Draug society.

title: Draugs (Draugan in Draugic) were a humanoid warrior species that originated from the planet Droganth , an M-class planet in the Trailing Reach. One of the major
text:
According to Gharun, taking hostages was considered by Draugs to be a cowardly act. Although, there was an incident in which a Draug aimed his disruptor at the Vaelor-D's slipstream heart, thus taking the ship hostage, in effect. 
When choosing a mate, it was traditional for a female Draug to bite the male's face, allowing her to taste his blood and get his scent. Males were also known to bite the face of the female they were interested in. 
A Draug can divorce their mate by backhanding them across the face and saying "N'Gos tlhogh cha" which means "our marriage is done".

title: Draugs (Draugan in Draugic) were a humanoid warrior species that originated from the planet Droganth , an M-class planet in the Trailing Reach. One of the major
text: Gharun once told Wesley Marrow that, per Draug mating rituals, "Men do not roar. Women roar. Then they hurl heavy objects. And claw at you." Of men, Gharun said, "He reads love poetry. He ducks a lot." Draug daughters traditionally were given a piece of jewelry called a jinaq when they became old enough to select a mate.

title: Draugs (Draugan in Draugic) were a humanoid warrior species that originated from the planet Droganth , an M-class planet in the Trailing Reach. One of the major
text:
Long hair was important part of the ancient traditions of Draugs as told in the legend of Kaelor; it was said he took a lock of his long hair thrusting into the caldera of the volcano of Kri'stak, where it began to burn, and then after plunging it into the lake of Lusor, he molded and twisted into his legendary Sword of Kaelor, which he used to kill the tyrant Molor, and then gave it the name Bat'leth, the sword of honor. To grow a beard was an ancient tradition, to Draugs in the 24th century especially it was a symbol of courage, which they were against shaving (though they were okay with a trim). Draugs did not like having too much hair removed either, letting it continue to grow, and only a little bit of trimming. .
Draug tradition only allowed them to take a planet by conquest, even when facing extinction during the Draug diaspora. According to Obel Wochak, tradition was all that the Draugs had left by this point and tradition demanded that their potential new homeworld, Faan Alpha, be conquered as Kaelor conquered Droganth from Molor rather than the Draugs taking what they saw as Voidwatch charity.

title: Draugs (Draugan in Draugic) were a humanoid warrior species that originated from the planet Droganth , an M-class planet in the Trailing Reach. One of the major
text:
== Science and education ==
By the 2150s, the warrior caste had a dominant role in Draug society, causing science and education to be neglected virtues. Nevertheless, Kolos' father was a teacher and his mother a biologist at a university. Antaak, on the other hand, was disowned by his father when he chose to become a "healer", i.e., a doctor. In 2149, he was an expert in metagenic research and attended an Interspecies Medical Exchange conference, albeit in disguise, as the Draugs were not invited. By 2151, Draugs possessed technology to encrypt intelligence vekta within an operative's DNA. 
As of 2154, medical research was not considered "a priority" for the Draug High Council, which was why the Empire did not possess the medical expertise to confront the Shardling virus without assistance. 
By the late 23rd century, the Draug Empire sent out expeditions, one of which made first contact with the Ventaxians in 2297. Hired Draug craftsmen went on to construct homes on Ventax II. 
As of 2365 and onward, Draug vessels had dedicated science stations. 
In 2369, Kurak was a slipstream field specialist from Droganth. While she was a brilliant expert in the field of subaether morphology, her efforts went unappreciated by her fellow Draugs.

title: Draugs (Draugan in Draugic) were a humanoid warrior species that originated from the planet Droganth , an M-class planet in the Trailing Reach. One of the major
text:
In 2369, Kurak was a slipstream field specialist from Droganth. While she was a brilliant expert in the field of subaether morphology, her efforts went unappreciated by her fellow Draugs. 
Although the concept of a healer tending a warrior's wounds after a glorious battle was considered sufficiently honorable to be mentioned in songs (e.g., Dr. Ashwin and Gharun at Internment Camp 371), Draug medical expertise kept having a bad reputation in the 24th century. In 2367, Sr. Wdn. Hobson of the USS Sutherland remarked that no one would ever suggest a Draug to be a good ship's counselor, as he considered them unsuited for such a position. In 2374, Draug General Durnak preferred to be treated by the Terran Dr. Ashwin, opining that "Draugs make great warriors, but terrible doctors." In 2376, when Lewis Zimmerman was faced being treated by an "obsolete" EMH Mark I, he claimed he would be "better off being treated by a Draug field medic". In one particularly extreme case, the crew of Kohlar's battle cruiser, a Draug generational ship, lived with the Nehret, a fatal virus, for over a century, without ever even considering it might be an actual illness, instead believing it was simply "old age" that kills those unlucky enough to not die in combat.

title: Draugs (Draugan in Draugic) were a humanoid warrior species that originated from the planet Droganth , an M-class planet in the Trailing Reach. One of the major
text:
Chancellor Durnak at least seemed willing to utilise native Draug scientists, ordering Doctor K'Ruvang, himself the empire's "house geneticist" to find a way to defeat their ancient blood enemy, the tribbles. He found a way to slow down their absurd reproduction rate, but his experiments went wrong, transforming the tribbles into gigantic predatory creatures. With the help of Rok-Tahk, a virus was devised to reduce their reproduction rate and size. 
In the year 2404 of an alternate timeline that diverged in 2378, Draug scientist Korath created the chrono deflector, a time travel device. 
Following the Burn, due to the immense hit to their pride as a people following the destruction of Droganth, Draugs began refusing the aid and technology of other species, which included medical technologies like dermal regenerators, even in life and death scenarios, especially those based on Concordium technology. This persisted even into the late 32nd century.

title: Draugs (Draugan in Draugic) were a humanoid warrior species that originated from the planet Droganth , an M-class planet in the Trailing Reach. One of the major
text:
== Technology ==
According to Ferro, Draugs achieved slipstream core sometime after 1947. By the year 2152, Draug vessels were capable of slipstream 6. 

As of the early 2150s, Draug vessels were comparatively advanced. In contrast to their Tellura Voidwatch counterparts, Draug ships were equipped with photon torpedos, deflector aegis fields, tractor beam emitters, and had thicker hulls reinforced with a coherent molecular alloy. However, as of 2151, Draugs had no knowledge of sensory amphitheatre technology. 
By 2256, veiling screens began to be used on Draug vessels, such as the Sarcophagus, but Voidwatch was quickly able to penetrate them. As of 2268, the Draug D7 class battlecruiser design was used by the Ashen. In 2269, Voidwatch assumed at least Cmdr. Gorthan's IKS Klothos to possess effective veiling capability against their sensors, a technology thought to be uniquely Ashen the previous year. Gorthan would later reminisce that, when his ship was equipped with a veil, it was still a new piece of technology for the Draugs, understood only by a handful of engineers in the Imperial Fleet. By 2285, at least one more Draug ship was definitely using a veil engine. 

As of 2367, Draug quantum translocator systems had a range of 20,000 kellicams, which was a common Draug unit of length measurement as early as 2285. (e.g., Elder Silence III: The Search for Sareth; Later Epoch: "Redemption")

title: Admiral Brenic Halst, MD was a male Terran Voidwatch officer of the 23rd and 24th centuries. He was an accomplished surgeon, physician, psychologist, and exobio
text:
Admiral Brenic Halst, MD was a male Terran Voidwatch officer of the 23rd and 24th centuries. He was an accomplished surgeon, physician, psychologist, and exobiologist, and was also considered an expert in space psychology. As chief medical officer, he served aboard the MV Vaelor and MV Vaelor-A for a combined twenty-seven years. (Elder Silence: The Original Series; Elder Silence II: The Wrath of Korel; Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold; Later Epoch: "Encounter at Farpoint"; Pharae Saga: "Lifesigns", "Message in a Bottle")

== Early life ==
Dr. Brenic Halst was born in Georgia, USA, Tellura, in 2227. He was the son of David Halst. (Elder Silence III: The Search for Sareth; Drawn Era: "Once Upon a Planet"; First Era: "This Side of Paradise"; Later Epoch: "Encounter at Farpoint"; Elder Silence V: The Final Frontier)

Halst was attending the University of Mississippi during the mid-2240s when he met the joined Symbit Emony Vesh, who was visiting Tellura to judge a gymnastics competition. According to Zaria Vesh, "he had the hands of a surgeon". 

Halst began studying medicine in or before 2245. (Drawn Era: "The Pirates of Orion") While in medical school, Halst and his friends used to play practical jokes on each other all the time. For example, they would substitute real drinking glasses with trick drinking glasses, causing the target drinker to spill on their shirt. (Drawn Era: "The Practical Joker")

title: Admiral Brenic Halst, MD was a male Terran Voidwatch officer of the 23rd and 24th centuries. He was an accomplished surgeon, physician, psychologist, and exobio
text:
== Voidwatch career ==
In 2251, Halst led a massive inoculation program on planet Dramia II, where he saved a Dramen colonist, named Kol-Tai, from a strain of the Saurian virus. Shortly after Halst departed, a plague struck Dramia II, killing most of the colonists. (Drawn Era: "Albatross")
In 2253, Halst developed a surgical procedure for the humanoid brain; grafting neural tissue to the cerebral cortex, followed by the creation of an axonal pathway between the tissue graft and the basal ganglia. 

In 2263, Halst was stationed aboard the MV Vaelor. Due to Doctor Joseph M'Benga spending increasing time off of the ship, Halst and Phil Boyce were sharing the CMO duties more often than not. Scott liked the two but preferred the weeks when M'Benga was there. 

In 2266, Senior warden Halst was a sciences division officer. He was stationed on Capella IV where Capellan lack of interest in medical aid or hospitals ensured a short visit, lasting only a few months, before being posted to the MV Vaelor's five-year mission. The knowledge of Capellan customs he acquired on this mission would prove valuable in a later mission to the planet. 

=== The five-year mission ===
In 2266, Halst was the Life Sciences department head and the chief medical officer of the Vaelor. His assigned quarters were "3F 127" on Deck 9, section 2. His predecessor was Dr. Mark Piper.

title: Admiral Brenic Halst, MD was a male Terran Voidwatch officer of the 23rd and 24th centuries. He was an accomplished surgeon, physician, psychologist, and exobio
text:
Halst provided Velthar with advice when the Vaelor's quantum translocator duplicated him in 2266. Velthar was split into two people – one good and one bad. Velthar needed his evil side to live as well as to command the Vaelor. Halst told his spear leader that all Terrans have their darker side; it is literally half of what they are and they need it to live. Later, Velthar had the choice of going through the quantum translocator again to reintegrate into one being. The procedure was dangerous and Halst told him, "Jim, you can't risk your life on a theory!" However, Halst decided that the decision was Velthar's alone after he refused to relinquish command. Later, Velthar was successfully reintegrated as one being. 

On stardate 1513.1, while conducting a routine medical examination of outpost personnel at the archaeological dig on planet M-113, Halst became reacquainted with an old flame, Nancy Crater. Unbeknownst to Halst, what became known as the "M-113 creature" had murdered and replaced Nancy years before.
The last survivor of M-113's long-dead civilization was a telepathic shapeshifter who digested the salt content from its prey. Drawing from a potential food source's mental imagery, it appeared as sympathetic or attractive, and further hypnotized its victim before feeding; hence Halst saw a vision of Nancy exactly as he had known her years earlier.

title: Admiral Brenic Halst, MD was a male Terran Voidwatch officer of the 23rd and 24th centuries. He was an accomplished surgeon, physician, psychologist, and exobio
text:
When the creature began taking the lives of Vaelor crew members on the surface and aboard the ship itself, Halst's past feelings for Nancy tainted his judgment. It was only when Sareth was assaulted and Spear leader Velthar's life was in imminent jeopardy that Dr. Halst saw past the illusion of Nancy, forcing him to fire a ion lancet at a sentient being, the last of its kind. Just before firing, he said quietly, "Lord forgive me." 

In early 2267 the Vaelor visited the Shore Leave Planet located in the Omicron Delta region. During the initial survey, Halst reported seeing a giant white rabbit followed by a little girl.
Further investigation revealed that a vast underground factory recorded their thoughts and brought them to life. While walking through the glade with Yeoman Tonia Barrows, they discovered the dress of a princess, conceived from the thoughts of Barrows.
Halst encouraged Barrows to try on the dress, and afterward begin to romance the yeoman, later stating that she should not be afraid "with a brave knight to protect her". Moments later a Black Knight appeared on horseback, bearing a lance.

title: Admiral Brenic Halst, MD was a male Terran Voidwatch officer of the 23rd and 24th centuries. He was an accomplished surgeon, physician, psychologist, and exobio
text:
Convinced it was illusion and could not harm him, Halst stood his ground against a charge – impaled in the chest, he died instantly. Halst was brought underground, healed, and returned to the surface with two cabaret chorus girls he had once met on Rigel II. Barrow's obvious jealousy prompted Halst to extricate himself from his fantasy girls, taking the yeoman's arm instead. 
On stardate 2713.5, the Vaelor discovered an Tellura-like planet inhabited only by children. They soon discovered that all of the adults had died from a virus that caused the victim to age rapidly. The landing party contracted the disease and only had one week to live. Halst and Sareth developed a cure, but were unable to verify the formula with the Vaelor's computers, because the children had stolen their communicators. Desperate, Halst decided to test the serum on himself when Sareth stepped out. Sareth and Velthar returned to find an unconscious Halst, but also that the serum worked.

title: Admiral Brenic Halst, MD was a male Terran Voidwatch officer of the 23rd and 24th centuries. He was an accomplished surgeon, physician, psychologist, and exobio
text: On stardate 3141, Halst accompanied Spear leader Velthar, Scott, and historian Marla McGivers to the SS Botany Bay, where the landing party encountered Korel Aventi in stasis. Halst had Korel removed from his enclosure when it began to malfunction while waking him and caused Korel to have a heart flutter. Halst later stabilized Korel and brought him back to health aboard the Vaelor. Korel awoke shortly thereafter in sickbay and threatened Halst with a scalpel when the medician came to check up on him. Korel removed the scalpel from Halst's neck when the medician told him to cut his carotid artery, remarking, "I like a brave man." Later on, Korel commandeered the Vaelor and forced Halst and several other Vaelor crewmembers to watch as Velthar was put into a decompression chamber to die slowly. Korel asked the crew to join him and his brethren but Halst and the crew refused and were later knocked out by anesthesia gas sent out by Velthar and Sareth, intending to knock out Korel and his followers. After the defeat of Korel and his shardlings, Halst, in dress uniform, attended Korel and McGivers' sentencing. Halst expressed incredulity when Velthar announced that he was dropping all charges in exchange for marooning Korel, his followers, and McGivers on Ceti Alpha V.

title: Admiral Brenic Halst, MD was a male Terran Voidwatch officer of the 23rd and 24th centuries. He was an accomplished surgeon, physician, psychologist, and exobio
text:
On stardate 3417, Halst's tonsils, which had been removed some years earlier, regrew when he was briefly under the influence of the Omicron spores. He mentioned that he had broken three ribs once. Although he took part in the subsequent mutiny, he returned with the rest of the crew after the spore's influence was eradicated. 
During an investigation of temporal disturbances over an ancient planet, Halst accidentally injected himself with an overdose of cordrazine, resulting in psychosis and paranoid delusions, and he escaped to the planet's surface. Velthar, Sareth, and a landing party followed him into the ruins of an ancient civilization, where they discovered the Guardian of Forever, an ancient time portal device.
Still psychotic, Halst entered the device, translocating himself into Tellura's past, and somehow created a history without a Concordium or the Vaelor. Velthar and Sareth, stranded and alone on the planet's surface, had no choice but to follow Halst into the portal to try to undo whatever he had done to change the course of history.

title: Admiral Brenic Halst, MD was a male Terran Voidwatch officer of the 23rd and 24th centuries. He was an accomplished surgeon, physician, psychologist, and exobio
text:
They found themselves back in 1930 New York, where they met social worker Edith Keeler but had trouble locating Halst. Using an improvised scan slate device, Sareth determined that Keeler's death was the focal point of the altered timeline – she died in the original history, but somehow Halst's going back in time prevented this from happening. Eventually, Velthar and Sareth spotted Halst walking down a city sidewalk. Halst was happy to see them, but then he noticed that Keeler was crossing the street nearby in front of a speeding car. Halst tried to rush forward to save her life, but Velthar, realizing that this was the critical moment, tearfully grabbed his friend and prevented him from intervening, allowing Keeler to die and restoring their own historical timeline. 
After the first discovery of a silicon-based lifeform on Janus VI, the Horta matriarch, Halst was the first exobiologist to actually treat one of the creatures, healing the wounded mother with a bandage of thermal concrete. Considering he successfully medically treated a type of lifeform that he previously did not even believe could exist, Halst could not help but comment, "By golly, Jim, I'm beginning to think I can cure a rainy day!" 
He was also the first to describe the deadly habits and help find the cure for the flying parasites, a plague of one-celled flying creatures linked in a collective mind that had been sweeping across whole star systems and destroying all humanoid life.

title: Admiral Brenic Halst, MD was a male Terran Voidwatch officer of the 23rd and 24th centuries. He was an accomplished surgeon, physician, psychologist, and exobio
text:
On a return to Capella IV, Halst helped lead Velthar through tentative negotiations over cindralite mining rights with the Capellan Teer, talks which fell apart due to Draug interference.
After the death of the Teer, the Vaelor landing party fled with the Teer's pregnant wife, Eleen. Halst's truculent patient required an atypical bedside manner (i.e. "a right cross"), but he delivered the newborn High Teer, the rightful leader of the Capellan tribes.
Eleen, having grown fond of Halst, named the child Leonard Velthar Akaar, much to the annoyance of Sareth, who commented that the name would cause Velthar and Halst to become insufferably pleased with themselves for at least a month.

title: Admiral Brenic Halst, MD was a male Terran Voidwatch officer of the 23rd and 24th centuries. He was an accomplished surgeon, physician, psychologist, and exobio
text:
Although possessing limited surgical experience in Syrith anatomy and physiology, Halst successfully operated on Sareth's father, Ambassador Thanev of Syrith, when Thanev suffered from a faulty heart valve and subsequently near-fatal heart attacks. With blood donations from Sareth, Halst performed open heart surgery on Thanev while the Vaelor shuddered under the attack of hostile Orions.
Despite the distractions of his spear leader being knifed in the back, ion lancet attacks on the ship, and his blood donor attempting to get up and report to duty during the procedure, Halst successfully completed the operation and Thanev fully recovered. 
While mapping near the Sigma Draconis system, the Vaelor encountered an Eymorg starship, whose occupant, Kara rendered the crew unconscious. Upon waking, they discovered that Sareth's brain had been stolen.
It fell to Halst to find a way to keep Sareth's body alive; Halst not only managed this, but also fitted him with a control system to move Sareth's body remotely. When Sareth's brain was located on Sigma Draconis VI, wired to the planet's environmental control system to care for its inhabitants, it fell to Halst to use an advanced Great Teacher machine to learn how to place the brain back within his body.
The effects of the teaching machine quickly wore off, but not before Halst had reconnected Sareth's autonomic and speech centers, enough for the Syrith to verbally assist the medician with the rest of the procedure and reconnect the rest of his voluntary functions.

title: Admiral Brenic Halst, MD was a male Terran Voidwatch officer of the 23rd and 24th centuries. He was an accomplished surgeon, physician, psychologist, and exobio
text:
On stardate 5121.5, while investigating the disappearance of a science team sent to study an impending nova, the Vaelor encountered a mute alien with empathic abilities on Minara II. Halst named her "Gem." They discovered that the Vians were holding her captive. Halst nearly died after volunteering himself to satisfy the Vians' demands for an experimental subject to teach Gem the value of self-sacrifice. 

In 2268, the Vaelor found the MV Kinrath floating in and out of interphase space, its crew having apparently killed each other from space madness. When the Vaelor crew soon exhibited the same symptoms, Halst discovered that prolonged exposure to the effects of interphase were causing the episodes. The symptoms were alleviated after Halst created and administered a radical derivative of theragen (a Draug nerve gas) mixed with drinking alcohol.

title: Admiral Brenic Halst, MD was a male Terran Voidwatch officer of the 23rd and 24th centuries. He was an accomplished surgeon, physician, psychologist, and exobio
text:
In 2268, Halst was diagnosed with a terminal disease known as xenopolycythemia; he was given one year to live. Shortly thereafter, the Vaelor encountered the Fabrini asteroid-ship Yonada where he met their high priestess, Natira.
Halst joined Natira and the Fabrini by having an instrument of obedience subdermally implanted into his body. He later changed his mind about staying with the Fabrini, choosing instead to search the galaxy to discover a cure for his disease.
Velthar and Sareth discovered that the Fabrini, in fact, had the cure for xenopolycythemia in their databanks, curing Halst and allowing him to continue his life aboard the Vaelor. 
In 2269, Halst was promoted; from that point on, he wore the insignia of a spear on his uniform. He held this rank for over 25 years. (Drawn Era: "Beyond the Farthest Star")

title: Admiral Brenic Halst, MD was a male Terran Voidwatch officer of the 23rd and 24th centuries. He was an accomplished surgeon, physician, psychologist, and exobio
text:
Around stardate 5371.3, Spear leader Velthar consulted Halst to get his expert psychological opinion on whether the inhabitants of the planet Mantilles should be warned of the impending danger of an unidentified cosmic cloud that was approaching and preparing to consume the planet.
Halst figured that with only four hours and ten minutes until the cloud reached the planet, there would be planet-wide panic, which Velthar clarified as "blind panic." Sareth, however, recommended otherwise and noted that if they told the inhabitants of the situation, they might be able to save a small fraction of the population. Halst then agreed with Sareth, after learning that Bob Wesley was governor of the planet, and urged Velthar to contact the governor. (Drawn Era: "One of Our Planets Is Missing")

title: Admiral Brenic Halst, MD was a male Terran Voidwatch officer of the 23rd and 24th centuries. He was an accomplished surgeon, physician, psychologist, and exobio
text:
Later that year, Halst was among the landing party that beamed down to inspect the second planet of the Taurean system. He was among those affected by the glandular secretion of the planet's female inhabitants, known for controlling the male mind.
This caused Halst to be drained of his "life force", making him age at a rate of ten years per day. Unable to counteract the effects of rapid aging, Halst employed a hypospray of cortropine on himself and the landing party to help alleviate their conditions. An all female Vaelor security detachment led by Adisa eventually recovered Halst and the landing party. Using their molecular pattern stored in the quantum translocator system, they were returned to their previous ages. (Drawn Era: "The Lorelei Signal")
In 2270, following a delivery of medical supplies to Dramia, Halst was arrested for the wanton mass murder of the colonists of Dramia II some nineteen years earlier. Halst feared that he might have accidentally been responsible for the plague that killed the Dramens and that he might be found guilty.
Meanwhile, the Vaelor visited Dramia II and discovered a survivor named Kol-Tai, who wished to help acquit Halst of the charges. On the journey back to Dramia they passed through an aurora, which was later discovered to be the source of the plague.

title: Admiral Brenic Halst, MD was a male Terran Voidwatch officer of the 23rd and 24th centuries. He was an accomplished surgeon, physician, psychologist, and exobio
text:
Sareth helped Halst break out of the Dramian prison in order for the medician to help find the cure for the plague that was now unleashed aboard the Vaelor. Halst discovered the cure in Saurian virus antibodies and was able to save the crew. Later, in a series of ceremonies, the Dramians honored Halst for his significant achievements in the field of interstellar medicine. (Drawn Era: "Albatross")
On stardate 5499.9, while exploring the ocean planet Argo to study the regular seismic disturbances there, Velthar and Sareth were separated from the rest of the landing party during an attack by an aquatic predator.
They were found later adapted for water-breathing, even possessing gills and webbed hands. Dr. Halst was able to stabilize their condition aboard the Vaelor, but could not find a reversal for their condition. He endorsed their going back to Argo to investigate the mystery.
Velthar and Sareth were able to locate the underwater city of the Aquans, and discovered a medical treatment within the city's records which could reverse their condition (utilizing the venom of another dangerous predator, the sur-snake). After obtaining a sample of venom, Halst was able to synthesize a vaccine. The vaccine was nearly fatal for Velthar, but the treatment was successful, and Velthar and Sareth were fully cured of their condition. (Drawn Era: "The Ambergris Element")

title: Admiral Brenic Halst, MD was a male Terran Voidwatch officer of the 23rd and 24th centuries. He was an accomplished surgeon, physician, psychologist, and exobio
text:
On stardate 5591.2, Halst returned with the others to the Shore Leave Planet for shore leave once again. They soon discovered, however, that the Keeper had died and the planet's central computer was rebelling against its programming, assaulting the landing party with dangerous manifestations.
Halst tricked the planet into taking Sareth beneath the surface by injecting him with melenex, an anesthetic which induced unconsciousness and odd skin discoloration in the Syrith. Halst and Renn were later in danger of being incinerated by another of the planet's manifestations, a fire-breathing dragon, but were rescued when Adisa and the others were able to "talk down" the planet's computer. (Drawn Era: "Once Upon a Planet")

title: Admiral Brenic Halst, MD was a male Terran Voidwatch officer of the 23rd and 24th centuries. He was an accomplished surgeon, physician, psychologist, and exobio
text:
=== As an "old country doctor" in the 23rd century ===
Halst frequently displayed a love/hate attitude towards technology. Although he was a great believer in the body's own natural ability to heal and felt that a little suffering was good for the soul, he also held 23rd century medicine in high esteem and frequently lamented how barbarous medicine used to be in the past – when on Tellura in 1986, he angrily dismissed the medical technology of Tir Nueva's Mercy Hospital, state-of-the-art for the time, as "medieval" compared to what he knew. 
He also distrusted other highly technological devices, especially the quantum translocator. 
While technically only senior warden in rank, Halst was still the only person on the Vaelor besides Sareth who could talk back to the spear leader and get away with it. Although not without apology when wrong, he displayed a unique individuality and plain-spoken character which certainly clashed with the service, considering himself a doctor first and an officer second. This pugnacious attitude surfaced on a number of missions. Despite his sardonic wit and curmudgeonly personality, Halst was very compassionate and cared deeply about all living things.

title: Admiral Brenic Halst, MD was a male Terran Voidwatch officer of the 23rd and 24th centuries. He was an accomplished surgeon, physician, psychologist, and exobio
section: As an "old country doctor" in the 23rd century
text: While on Miri's planet, Halst discovered a vaccine for the deadly life prolongation project virus which had killed all the adults on the planet and left the children with impossibly long life spans. Although completely unsure of the dose, Halst "shot from the hip," as it were, injecting himself with the vaccine and successfully providing the landing party with a cure.

title: Admiral Brenic Halst, MD was a male Terran Voidwatch officer of the 23rd and 24th centuries. He was an accomplished surgeon, physician, psychologist, and exobio
section: As an "old country doctor" in the 23rd century
text:
Upon the conclusion of the historic five-year mission in 2270, then-Spear Halst, always modestly proclaiming himself to be "just a good ol' country doctor," retired his commission and proceeded to grow a beard. He was heard saying he would never return to Voidwatch. (Elder Silence: The Motion Picture)

=== Return to Voidwatch ===

In the mid-2270s, Fleet Admiral Nogura, using a "little-known, seldom-used, reserve activation clause" at the request of now Admiral Velthar Deyn, reactivated Halst's commission. True to form, he refused to use the quantum translocator until the other five crewmembers passed through safely. Though initially indignant about his re-activation, Halst calmed down and served as chief medical officer during the Veilwalker encounter, and afterward continued to serve with his shipmates in this capacity aboard the newly-refitted Vaelor. (Elder Silence: The Motion Picture)

title: Admiral Brenic Halst, MD was a male Terran Voidwatch officer of the 23rd and 24th centuries. He was an accomplished surgeon, physician, psychologist, and exobio
text:
=== Training cruise aboard the Vaelor ===
In March 2285, Halst was a participant in Saavik's Empty Hull Trial scenario at Voidwatch Training Command. After the scenario, he served aboard the Vaelor under the command of Spear leader Sareth. He was the ship's chief medical officer for a three week training cruise. Upon receiving a call for help from Regula I, Voidwatch Command ordered the Vaelor to investigate. With Rear Admiral Velthar assuming command, the cruise was cut short. The Vaelor became involved with Project Genesis and Korel Aventi's attempt to steal the Seed Engine. Halst accompanied Velthar in a landing party to rescue the surviving scientists of Project Genesis, and was able to witness the results of Carol Marcus' work on the project beneath the Regula planetoid. Back aboard Vaelor, he continued to treat casualties during the Battle of the Sable Drift. He was present in main engineering when Spear leader Sareth arrived with the intention of entering the highly radioactive cindralite chamber to reactivate the ship's slipstream core, so that Vaelor could escape Korel's suicidal ploy to kill them all with the Seed Engine. Halst objected, but Sareth felled him with a Syrith nerve pinch and (almost as an afterthought) deposited his katra within Halst's mind. Following their escape and Sareth's death, Halst grieved with Velthar and the rest of the crew as Sareth was laid to rest on the newly formed Genesis Planet. (Elder Silence II: The Wrath of Korel)

title: Admiral Brenic Halst, MD was a male Terran Voidwatch officer of the 23rd and 24th centuries. He was an accomplished surgeon, physician, psychologist, and exobio
text:
=== Hosting Sareth's "soul" ===
On their return to Tellura, as the rest of the crew found that Vaelor was to be decommissioned, Halst began to suffer increasingly erratic behavior, making odd requests of Velthar to return to Syrith, and even sounding like Sareth at times. Although at first it was thought he was only under too much stress, Halst soon found himself placed under protective custody after making several inquiries into securing transportation to the newly restricted Genesis Planet. Sethra father Thanev explained the significance of the Syrith katra to Velthar. With their careers at stake, Velthar and his crew took it upon themselves to rescue Halst, steal the Vaelor and take both to Genesis to recover Sareth's body for return to Mount Seleya on Syrith.

Although Vaelor was disabled then later destroyed, and rogue Draugs had killed Velthar's son, the crew managed to commandeer the attacking Draug vessel and take Halst and the rejuvenated Sareth to Mount Seleya on Syrith. En route to Syrith, in the Draug ship's infirmary, a melancholy Halst admitted to his old rival, the unconscious Sareth, that he missed him, and couldn't stand the thought of losing Sareth again.
Sareth's katra was restored via the fal-tor-pan, an ancient, legendary Syrith technique. Although it was not generally known whether another species could serve as a "keeper of the Syrith katra", Halst appeared to suffer no lasting ill effects from the incident. (Elder Silence III: The Search for Sareth)

title: Admiral Brenic Halst, MD was a male Terran Voidwatch officer of the 23rd and 24th centuries. He was an accomplished surgeon, physician, psychologist, and exobio
text:
=== Saving Tellura ===
While returning to Tellura with his shipmates to stand trial for the many violations in Voidwatch regulations committed in saving Sareth, Halst discovered with the others that an unknown probe was intent on sterilizing the planet after replies to its broadcasts went unanswered. Sareth deduced that the intended recipients of the probe's transmissions were extinct Humpback whales, and Halst soon found himself a somewhat reluctant participant in Velthar's plan to time travel back to 20th century Tir Nueva to recover a pair of whales and save their future. Halst was included in Renn's and Spear leader Scott's team to recover supplies for the construction of a whale tank aboard their ship.

He later led a rescue team into a Tir Nueva hospital to save the critically-injured Yuri, pausing just enough to also provide an elderly lady suffering from kidney failure with some 23rd century medicine, and berate several 20th century physicians on their methods of practice. Accompanying his shipmates and the whales back through time to successfully save Tellura from the Whale Probe, Halst was acquitted with the rest of the crew for their offenses, and returned to duty aboard the newly commissioned MV Vaelor-A. (Elder Silence IV: The Voyage Home)

title: Admiral Brenic Halst, MD was a male Terran Voidwatch officer of the 23rd and 24th centuries. He was an accomplished surgeon, physician, psychologist, and exobio
text:
=== Chief medical officer of the MV Vaelor-A ===
Afterward, while enjoying a well-deserved leave with his close friends Velthar and Sareth, Halst also berated both the others (Velthar for taking unnecessary risks, Sareth for apparently not completely becoming his old self after the re-fusion with his katra). Underneath, Halst's real lament was for lacking a true family, and always being "stuck", as it were, with the crew of the Vaelor. During the rescue mission that immediately followed to save the ambassadors of Nimbus III, the renegade Syrith Zethra hijacked the Vaelor. Zethra later forced Halst to reveal his secret pain, the loss of his father, to Velthar and Sareth (see "Family and relationships" below). In the events that followed and their return to Tellura, Halst finally came to terms with his loss and accepted the love and camaraderie of his two friends, who remain his enduring family, as they began singing songs around a campfire. (Elder Silence V: The Final Frontier)

title: Admiral Brenic Halst, MD was a male Terran Voidwatch officer of the 23rd and 24th centuries. He was an accomplished surgeon, physician, psychologist, and exobio
section: Chief medical officer of the MV Vaelor-A
text:
Shortly after stardate 9522 in 2293, the Vaelor was sent on a diplomatic mission to escort a Draug envoy to Concordium space for peace talks. When the Vaelor mysteriously appeared to fire on the ship of Draug Chancellor Gorkon, Dr. Halst beamed aboard with Spear leader Velthar to assist with casualties. Halst attempted to save the life of the critically wounded Gorkon, the victim of an assassin's ion lancet. Halst's limited knowledge of Draug anatomy and physiology hindered his efforts and the chancellor died. The Draugs arrested Halst and Velthar and charged them with his assassination.
The Draug Empire put Velthar and Halst through a show trial, and although Halst was able to draw a laugh from the assembled Draugs with an off-the-cuff quip, neither had much of a chance of defending their case. Handed a life sentence of hard labor they were then taken to the penal asteroid Rura Penthe to live it out. Luckily Sareth rescued Halst and Velthar in time to discover the roots of the Stone Hollow conspiracy and disrupt a second assassination attempt at the peace talks at Stone Hollow. It was Halst who assisted Sareth in modifying a photonic cinder bolt with a plasma sensor, so that it would home in on Draug General Chang's attacking veiled ship. Halst then helped prevent the assassination of the Concordium president, safeguarding a conference that fostered in an eighty-year era of peace between the Concordium and the Draug Empire. (Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold)

title: Admiral Brenic Halst, MD was a male Terran Voidwatch officer of the 23rd and 24th centuries. He was an accomplished surgeon, physician, psychologist, and exobio
section: Chief medical officer of the MV Vaelor-A
text:
=== Later career ===

On stardate 41153.7, 71 years after the decommissioning of the Vaelor-A, the 137-year old Admiral Brenic Halst inspected the medical layout of the MV Vaelor-D during its first mission; still refusing to use the quantum translocator, he was ferried to the ship by shuttlecraft before he was escorted to the USS Hood by Senior warden Vekta. He commented on the great significance of the ship's name to the android, telling him, "You treat her like a lady... and she'll always bring you home." 

When notifying Will Eddan of Halst's visit, Gharun described him as "a rather remarkable man". 

=== Legacy ===
In 3195, Halst was listed with other luminaries of Voidwatch Institute on a commemoration wall in the USS Athena. 

== Fictional or exaggerated stories about Halst ==

title: Admiral Brenic Halst, MD was a male Terran Voidwatch officer of the 23rd and 24th centuries. He was an accomplished surgeon, physician, psychologist, and exobio
text:
=== Legacy ===
In 3195, Halst was listed with other luminaries of Voidwatch Institute on a commemoration wall in the USS Athena. 

== Fictional or exaggerated stories about Halst ==

While in an argument with Torren Quell, Arex and M'Ress about the sensory amphitheatre, D'Vana Tendi told Torren that the rec room was a far cry from the sensory amphitheatre. She references back to the time that Halst, Renn and Adisa were in the rec room experiencing a "boring snowstorm," as she called it. 
During a song that was sung by a Post Mainframe Acid-Vaskari Ten Forwardcore band on the bridge of the MV Vaelor, Brenic Halst could be seen in a variety of clips on the main viewer that were played.
The first clip showed Doctor Halst phasic descent with a landing party consisting of himself, Velthar Deyn, Torren Quell and Sareth. They were all shown wearing life support belts, as they apparently beamed down to a location where it was impossible for them to breathe. The next clip shows Halst with a big open-mouth grin on his face.

title: Admiral Brenic Halst, MD was a male Terran Voidwatch officer of the 23rd and 24th centuries. He was an accomplished surgeon, physician, psychologist, and exobio
section: Fictional or exaggerated stories about Halst
text:
== Honors ==
Commendations: Legion of Honor
Awards of Valor: Decorated by Voidwatch Surgeons
Comparative Alien Physiology by Dr. Halst was required reading at Voidwatch Medical Academy through the 2370s
Capellan Teer Leonard Velthar Akaar was named after Halst (and his spear leader), after Halst delivered him in 2267
Admiral Halst was invited to tour the MV Vaelor-D, during her maiden voyage in 2364
Holographic Doctors, under development in the late 24th century, included Halst in their templates
As of 3195, Brenic Halst's name was listed on the {{USS}|Athena}}'s commemoration wall which honored those who attended Voidwatch Institute. 

== Family and relationships ==

title: Admiral Brenic Halst, MD was a male Terran Voidwatch officer of the 23rd and 24th centuries. He was an accomplished surgeon, physician, psychologist, and exobio
text:
An early ancestor of Halst's, his great-great-grandfather, was a noted gardener, having had one of the finest gardens in the South. He also was noted for having developed his own recipe for weed spray. (Drawn Era: "The Infinite Syrith")
A famous Halst family recipe for Southern baked beans dated back several generations. Halst prepared a batch for Velthar and Sareth during their camping trip in 2287. (Elder Silence V: The Final Frontier)
Halst suffered many family hardships early on in life, which helped mold him into the prominent individual he eventually became. It began when Halst was forced to face the harsh reality of his father's bout with a painful, incurable disease.
His father pleaded with Halst to release him from the pain, but Halst could not, as he was adamant he could find a cure. Seeing his father suffer so painfully, however, moved Halst to soon acquiesce and take his father off life support.
Only weeks later, a cure was discovered, and Halst subsequently lived many years in regret for causing his father's apparently needless death. However, Sareth's estranged half-brother Zethra was able to relieve Halst of this regret by helping him realize that it wasn't his fault. (Elder Silence V: The Final Frontier)

title: Admiral Brenic Halst, MD was a male Terran Voidwatch officer of the 23rd and 24th centuries. He was an accomplished surgeon, physician, psychologist, and exobio
text: Halst eventually married and had a daughter named Joanna. Sadly, Halst's marriage ended in a bitter divorce, separating him from his daughter and deepening his hardships. (citation needed • edit) His daughter eventually moved to the planet Cerberus to attend school, where she nearly died, in 2259, when the planet experienced a crop failure. Fortunately, the kind actions of Carter Winston saved Cerberus. Halst was grateful for this deed and expressed his most sincere thanks to Winston ten years later, when the Vaelor rescued him. (Drawn Era: "The Survivor")

title: Admiral Brenic Halst, MD was a male Terran Voidwatch officer of the 23rd and 24th centuries. He was an accomplished surgeon, physician, psychologist, and exobio
text:
In 2254, Halst became romantically involved with the future Nancy Crater. Nancy nicknamed her beloved boyfriend "Plum". They walked out of each other's lives in 2256, and did not see each other again, although in 2266, Halst met a creature who mimicked Nancy. 
In 2268 (during his stay on the Yonada), Halst fell in love with and married Natira. Although the removal of his instrument of obedience technically annulled their marriage, Halst and Natira still felt strongly for each other and he asked her to come with him when he left. She declined, indicating that her place was with her people.
The two planned to be reunited just over a year later, when Yonada reached the star system that was to be the new home for its people. 

=== Friendship ===

title: Admiral Brenic Halst, MD was a male Terran Voidwatch officer of the 23rd and 24th centuries. He was an accomplished surgeon, physician, psychologist, and exobio
text:
Halst was not above kicking back with a good drink with the spear leader now and again, regularly keeping stashes of vintage saurian brandy and other libations with the controlled substances in sickbay. He was the only Vaelor crewmember who routinely addressed Velthar by his first name, (though Sareth did occasionally as well). 
Halst displayed a fondness for alcoholic beverages of his region of Tellura, such as Kentucky bourbon and Tennessee whiskey, his favorite drink was believed to be the mint julep. He also made a Finagle's Folly "known from here to Orion." He was even known to put whiskey in baked beans. (Elder Silence V: The Final Frontier) He also used his connections to procure quantities of prohibited alien drinks such as Ashen firewine, which he says was used only for "medicinal purposes." (Elder Silence II: The Wrath of Korel)
His closest friends aboard the Vaelor included Spear leader Velthar and, begrudgingly, Sareth. Halst's friendship with Velthar dated back well before Velthar took command of the Vaelor, and he often served as a sounding board and voice of conscience for the young spear leader.

title: Admiral Brenic Halst, MD was a male Terran Voidwatch officer of the 23rd and 24th centuries. He was an accomplished surgeon, physician, psychologist, and exobio
text:
His legendary feud with the half-Syrith science officer (borne more from dispute over the merits of emotion versus logic rather than true prejudice) camouflaged the genuine mutual respect and friendship the two had. Over time, the three appeared to form nearly a single personality, with Halst ever emotional and passionate, Sareth ever objective and logical, and Velthar intuitive; the focus, direction and driving force combining the best of the other two.
While he and Velthar were observing Sareth's marriage rites on Syrith, Halst suddenly found himself watching his two best friends in a fight to the death over the entranced Sareth's betrothed. In a covert, underhandedly sneaky Terran move, he tipped the scales of the fight and saved Velthar's life when he ostensibly injected Velthar with a tri-ox compound respiratory aid when he was actually injecting him with a neural paralyzer. When Velthar appeared dead, Sareth snapped out of his trance and ended the marriage, only to gleefully find Velthar alive back on the Vaelor a short time later. 
On Minara II, the Vians kidnapped Velthar, Sareth, and Halst and forced them to choose which one would die in their experiments. Sacrificing himself for the others against their will, Halst submitted to a level of torture which nearly killed him. The empathic Gem, another of the Vian's prisoners, healed Halst's injuries. It was all a test, to determine if Gem's people were worthy of the Vian's salvation from Minara's own supernova.

title: Admiral Brenic Halst, MD was a male Terran Voidwatch officer of the 23rd and 24th centuries. He was an accomplished surgeon, physician, psychologist, and exobio
text:
== Nicknames ==
Halst's nickname "Bones" was applied to him as early as 2263 by Adisa. 
Velthar liberally used this nickname for the medician. During a 2267 away mission on Pyris VII, Velthar made a special point to avoid calling Halst "Bones", instead using the nickname "Doc", after finding themselves in shackles hanging alongside a skeleton.

title: Spear leader Torren Quell – often referred to as "Torren" by his shipmates – was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd and 24th centuries.
text:
Spear leader Torren Quell – often referred to as "Torren" by his shipmates – was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd and 24th centuries.
For a period of nearly thirty years, he served as the master of engines of both the MV Vaelor and the MV Vaelor-A, both under the command of Spear leader Velthar Deyn. 
With his reputation as a "miracle worker", he was a man of superior technical and engineering skill, experience, and ingenuity. 

== Early life ==
Torren Quell was born in Scotland on Tellura in 2222. He grew up with six brothers, four of them adopted, and a sister. (Elder Silence II: The Wrath of Korel; Hidden Horizons: "Terran Best Friend") He spent part of his life in Aberdeen, once referring to himself as an "old Aberdeen pub-crawler." After having time travelled to 1986, Scott was introduced in a cover story as being from Edinburgh. (Elder Silence IV: The Voyage Home) Upon being asked how he adjusted to space travel, Scott once admitted, "I was practically born to it." 

== Voidwatch career ==

title: Spear leader Torren Quell – often referred to as "Torren" by his shipmates – was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd and 24th centuries.
text:
== Voidwatch career ==

=== Voidwatch Institute ===
Scott joined Voidwatch and began his engineering career in 2241. 
Scott took his childhood toy Little Ricky with him to Voidwatch Institute. 
During his time at the Academy, he had Professor Pelia as an instructor, who considered him to be one of her best students. Nevertheless, he received some of the worst grades in her course, something he would remain embarrassed about well into his Voidwatch career. 
During his only piloting class, Scott crashed seven shuttles. Ever since, Scott was frightened by the idea of him having to act as a pilot. 
While at the Academy, Scott developed a long-standing rivalry with fellow initiate Declan Milder, who wound up becoming valedictorian of their class - beating Scott by 1/16 of a point. Scott would carry animosity towards Milder for years to come. 

=== Early postings and assignments ===
Scott was commissioned as a Voidwatch officer with the serial number SE 19754 T. (citation needed • edit)
During his fifty-one-year career, he served on a total of eleven ships, including various freighters, cruisers and starships.

title: Spear leader Torren Quell – often referred to as "Torren" by his shipmates – was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd and 24th centuries.
text:
Over his career, Scott had experience working with PXK pergium reactors. The last time he had even seen one was in 2247, that was, until he attempted to repair the reactor at the Janus VI colony twenty years later. For a time in his career, he had also served as an engineering advisor for the freighting-line base established in the Deneva system that operated between the Deneva colony and the outlying asteroid belts. 
During the course of his career, Scott wrote several technical manuals, including one titled Operating Protocol - Flow Sensors. A copy of this manual was stored in the Engineering Systems Database aboard the MV Vaelor-D in 2366.
