He was also responsible for writing Voidwatch Regulation 42/15, entitled "Pressure Variances in IRC Tank Storage", which was part of the basic operational specifications for impulse engines. These specifications were admittedly written "a wee bit" conservatively.

title: Spear leader Torren Quell – often referred to as "Torren" by his shipmates – was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd and 24th centuries.
text:
==== Service aboard the Stardiver ====
In 2260, as a warden junior grade, Scott was stationed aboard the USS Stardiver, which was in the Shangdi system. About a week before the Stardiver encountered Vaskor, Scott was working on a sensor array, and thought that he saw some anomalies, but disregarded them as he was pressed for time. Scott's CO said that she would help him, but she wasn't able to get around to it before the ship was attacked. The anomalies Scott had seen turned out to be Vaskor. 
Scott escaped the destruction of the Stardiver by constructing a transponder using parts from the Stardiver's Hubble K7C Stellar Assessment Array, which he then took onto a shuttle with him. The transponder he had built fooled the Vaskor vessels into seeing his shuttle as one of their own. However, the shuttle had been damaged and Scott was forced to land on Parnassus Beta, in the adjacent system. Scott created a "Vaskor trap" using faked Terran bio-signs and force fields to ensnare any Vaskor in the area. Scott was later beamed aboard the Vaelor, where he was reunited with his former instructor Pelia. 
Due to his inability to be fully self-reliant aboard the Stardiver, and accomplish his project in a timely matter, Scott blamed himself for the destruction of the Stardiver, guilt he would carry with him for some time afterwards. 

=== Service aboard the Vaelor ===

title: Spear leader Torren Quell – often referred to as "Torren" by his shipmates – was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd and 24th centuries.
text:
=== Service aboard the Vaelor ===

==== Fighting the Vaskor ====
Brought aboard the MV Vaelor, Scott and Pelia managed to hook his transponder up to the Concordance-class starship, allowing the Vaelor to slip into Vaskor space to rescue the Parnassus Beta colonists and captured Voidwatch personnel. Despite his doubts, Scott and Pelia were able to rig the Vaelor to emulate an X-class coronal mass ejection, tricking the Vaskor into entering a long hibernation cycle and thwarting a full-scale invasion of the Concordium. Using quantum translocator codes stolen by Lira Vahn, Scott and Pelia were able to beam all of the Parnassus colonists off of the Vaskor destroyer and the landing party off of the Vaskor hunter ship that they had stolen.

title: Spear leader Torren Quell – often referred to as "Torren" by his shipmates – was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd and 24th centuries.
text:
==== Serving under Spear leader Pike ====
During the next three months as the Vaelor underwent extensive repairs for the damage that she had suffered fighting the Vaskor, Scott was officially assigned to the ship under Pelia. 
One of Scott's duties was operating the quantum translocator. He was manning the quantum translocator when Nurse Christine Chapel and Doctor Roger Korby beamed aboard, and noticed what he dismissed as a sensor ghost, but which was actually Trelane. 
After Trelane placed everyone under a spell so that Sareth and Chapel were to be married, Scott attended Sareth's bachelor party alongside Spear leader Pike, Doctor Joseph M'Benga and Warden Sam Velthar. However, Sareth and Korby were unable to convince any of them of what Trelane had done. Scott later attended the wedding, which later pivoted into a Concordium Day celebration after the spell was broken. 
When Spear leader Pike and Dr. M'Benga went on an illicit mission to Kenfori and needed rescuing, Scott supported Orrega's riskier alternative plan to quickly rescue them. When Orrega forced her plan into action, Scott was able to reconfigure the quantum translocator to rescue the away team, and adjust thrusters to prevent orbital collapse, which Una had previously expressed skepticism in the feasibility of.

title: Spear leader Torren Quell – often referred to as "Torren" by his shipmates – was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd and 24th centuries.
text:
Scott was left in charge when Pelia went on shore leave and helped Lira Vahn test out the prototype sensory amphitheatre. When Lira got trapped in the sensory amphitheatre, Scott enlisted Adisa Maren's help to figure out a way to communicate with her and later joined Lira in recommending against installing sensory amphitheatres on active starships for the time being due to the immense power drain. Noticing how Scott had been trying to do everything alone, Una Chin-Riley reminded him that it was unnecessary. Scott how he blamed himself for the destruction of the Stardiver due to reuiring help he was unable to get to finish a crucial project. Una reassured Scott that the Stardiver's destruction wasn't his fault, and that the Vaelor crew were a team. 
After Dana Gamble opened an orb containing a Vezda, Scott performed an analysis on it, and determined it was a containment device, weakened by removal from its power source. After this information allowed the command crew to come to the conclusion that Gamble had been possessed, Scott was able to use the orb to re-capture the Vezda, and trap it in the quantum translocator's pattern buffer.

title: Spear leader Torren Quell – often referred to as "Torren" by his shipmates – was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd and 24th centuries.
text:
When the MV Aldric was attacked and disabled by a planet-destroying scavenger ship, Scott was one of response team that the Vaelor assigned to the Farragut. After the Vaelor was captured by the same scavenger ship, Torren managed to 'work miracles' and get the Farragut's engines once again operational - however, Velthar's questionable judgment led to them being burned out again shortly after, to a degree Scott could not repair himself. Torren later detached the nacelles of the Farragut, as part of a ploy to free the Vaelor. 
By 2262, Scott had begun introducing widespread changes into Vaelor systems. Some of these alterations improvements to hand ion lancets, as well as the addition of alarms, notifications, and operational restrictions for when ship's systems exceeded normal tolerances. This led him into conflict with the ship's helmsman, Erica Orrega, who incorrectly believed Scott had maliciously introduced these features to make her job more difficult. She would also occasionally mock him for his accent.

title: Spear leader Torren Quell – often referred to as "Torren" by his shipmates – was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd and 24th centuries.
text:
Later that year, Scott was again manning the transporters when the away team was beamed up from the Tulaxar mission. As Sareth and Lira flirted in the quantum translocator bay, Scott averted his eyes.
While the Vaelor was investigating an interstellar squall, the ship and its crew - including Scott - were transported 65 million years into the past, where he learned the true history of Mars, the Dol'drm, and the Chicxulub asteroid. During this time, he was nearly killed by Martian guards, after approaching Spear Cassell for a handshake. After returning back to his home time, Scott, along with the rest of the crew, were instructed to keep the knowledge of what they had learned about the past a secret.

title: Spear leader Torren Quell – often referred to as "Torren" by his shipmates – was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd and 24th centuries.
text: En route to host and mediate peace talks regarding the Rodaxian civil war, it was decided that recent events had left the crew of the Vaelor - including Scott - too highly stressed, so the decision was made to stop at the resort world Cesnar, which was along the ship's path. Upon arriving, Erica Orrega made a hard landing and caused some minor damage to the shuttle, which Scott accused her of doing on purpose, as means of getting back at him, thoguh Orrega denied this. Scott fell under the effects of the planet's intoxicating atmosphere almost immediately, and attended a costume party with Orrega, while wearing a 'loaner' Mugato costume. During this party, Scott and Orrega discovered that an explosive had been planted in their shuttle, so to prevent it from being a danger, they hid the shuttle, then took a key component out of the shuttle, which Orrega hid inside a fake cast on her arm. The pair made an agreement with the resort proprietor Dendru to keep them from returning to their shuttle, including arranging for them to be kidnapped and tied up, if necessary. They then left a message for themselves on a vekta chip in the shuttle, and returned to the party. While there, Orrega caught a dragon bomb, and inadvertently caused her and Scott to black out and forget what had happened that night

title: Spear leader Torren Quell – often referred to as "Torren" by his shipmates – was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd and 24th centuries.
text: . While there, Orrega caught a dragon bomb, and inadvertently caused her and Scott to black out and forget what had happened that night. Upon awaking, Orrega and Scott found themselves in a trashed room, and Orrega was relatively lucid, but Scott still deeply intoxicated. Dendru arrived, and asked them to deliver a paper letter to Spear leader Pike. Orrega made the decision that the still clearly inebriated Scott could not be left to his own devices, so she took him with her while she searched for the Spear leader. Upon delivering the letter, the pair were instructed to prepare the shuttle for departure, as the inebriated Pike had moved up the date of the peace talks. The pair quickly realized the shuttle was not where it was supposed to be, and set out to find it, enlisting the assistance of Sareth and Lira. Eventually, the shuttle was located, and the crew was able to return to the Vaelor. Both Orrega and Scott went to fix the shuttle, so the other would not have to, and they wound up commiserating and making amends. However, during this, they found the planted explosive

title: Spear leader Torren Quell – often referred to as "Torren" by his shipmates – was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd and 24th centuries.
text: . Both Orrega and Scott went to fix the shuttle, so the other would not have to, and they wound up commiserating and making amends. However, during this, they found the planted explosive. Scott held the device, and Orrega flew the shuttle to a safe distance, both ready to sacrifice themselves for the Vaelor, though Sareth and Velthar were able to beam them out at the last moment, resulting in only minor injuries - Scott's thumb was almost entirely blown off, which could be repaired at sickbay.

title: Spear leader Torren Quell – often referred to as "Torren" by his shipmates – was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd and 24th centuries.
text:
While on a mission to the Mat'Aar system, Orrega pushed Scott to help her with an unapproved project, to piggyback a signal on the Angelo-1 probe's frequencies to attempt to communicate with the away team. When confronted by Lira, Orrega attempted to take the blame so Scott would not get in trouble. Lira did not report their project to Spear leader Pike, but did report to him the surprising news that Scott and Orrega had become friends. 
While en route to Syrith, Scott worked on an ongoing project of his, to substantially increase the range of quantum translocator signals. Enlisting the help of Sareth, he deployed relay bouys, and attempted to transport Little Ricky, a childhood toy of his, to the USS Witmere, where a Academy rival of his, Declan Milder, was stationed. The experiment failed, damaging a shuttle and rendering Sareth unconscious for several hours. While Sareth was unconscious, Scott sat Little Ricky at Sareth's desk in his quarters, in a misguided gesture of goodwill.

title: Spear leader Torren Quell – often referred to as "Torren" by his shipmates – was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd and 24th centuries.
text:
When the ship fell into a slipstream wormhole, killing much of the engineering crew and causing extensive damage to the Vaelor, Scott was forced to deal with the increasing problems from a translocator bay with only the help of Initiate A'Sha as Pelia was trapped in her quarters. Scott came up with a plan to use strong force neutrinos to replenish the ship's irradiated fuel reserves and escape, making contact with Pelia via comms who told Scott about how engineers had to be "miracle workers" and taught him to listen to the ship itself rather than his readings. 
Pelia later left the ship to study the engineering of the Elysian Kingdom and fly it home, leaving Scott as the Vaelor's acting Master of Engines. 
Later that year, Scott began trying to ask Adisa out, but she initially brushed aside his advances due to being too focused on her future.

title: Spear leader Torren Quell – often referred to as "Torren" by his shipmates – was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd and 24th centuries.
text:
==== Early service under Velthar ====
2263 saw many changes for Scott's life, as several friends and colleagues left the Vaelor, and Spear leader Pike was promoted to Admiral and gave command of the ship to Velthar Deyn. Through this time, Adisa and Torren 'held onto each other', developing a relationship, though Adisa pushed him to keep it 'casual' and conceal it from their crewmates. 
Later that year, Torren was chosen for a mission to explore a newly formed black hole, alongside Adisa and a temporarily-returned Spear leader Orrega. After they had to beam off an exploding shuttle, Scott was surprised when Adisa kissed him on the quantum translocator pad. 

==== The five-year mission ====

By 2265, Scott had been promoted to Senior warden and master of engines of the MV Vaelor under Spear leader Velthar Deyn. The Vaelor was the first ship on which he was the master of engines.

title: Spear leader Torren Quell – often referred to as "Torren" by his shipmates – was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd and 24th centuries.
text:
His duties also included maintenance and operation of the Vaelor's quantum translocator systems. Three of his top engineers included Lieutenants Kyle, Leslie, and Gabler. He was understandably upset when Harper, an assistant engineer who was one of only twenty crewmembers selected to remain aboard the Vaelor during the M-5 multitronic unit test mission, was killed by an energy transfer beam used by the insane supercomputer to draw power directly from the ship's slipstream engines. 
Scott also served as the ship's second officer, and often assumed command when both Velthar and Sareth left the ship, or they both were incapacitated. Thus, he often faced critical diplomatic and military situations. In 2268, Velthar noted him to commendation for his outstanding command performance without disobeying the Sanctity Edict and saving the landing party on planet 892-IV. However in 2267, Velthar jokingly "fired" Scott when he couldn't repair the ship's engines and break out of orbit around Gamma Trianguli VI. After the destruction of Vaal Velthar immediately "re-hired" him. Despite being a capable command officer he never pursued his own command post because he "...never wanted to be anythin' else but an engineer."

title: Spear leader Torren Quell – often referred to as "Torren" by his shipmates – was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd and 24th centuries.
text: By the late 2260s, Scott knew more about the slipstream engines aboard a Concordance-class starship than even the men who designed them. Furthermore, Scott was diligent in keeping his professional skills up to date considering he was an avid reader of technical journals, which he considered his idea of relaxing. This knowledge and ability to save the ship in a jam eventually led to his reputation aboard the Vaelor as a "miracle worker." This was brought about by his reputation for being able to effect starship repairs faster than usually required. Scott later admitted that he often padded his estimates of time needed for repairs by a factor of four in order to appear that much faster. (Elder Silence III: The Search for Sareth; Later Epoch: "Relics") As he said to Geori Vane in the 24th century, "A good engineer needs to be a wee bit conservative, at least on paper."

title: Spear leader Torren Quell – often referred to as "Torren" by his shipmates – was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd and 24th centuries.
text: In 2268, Scott stated that he knew the Vaelor better than Larry Marvick, the man who designed the starship. When Marvick visited the ship, escorting the Medusan Ambassador Kollos, Scott made a bet, that he wouldn't find his way around the engine room. When Scott allowed him access to the slipstream engine controls, Marvick, under the madness brought on by the sight of the Medusan, attempted to take over the vessel and hurled it into the void surrounding our galaxy.

title: Spear leader Torren Quell – often referred to as "Torren" by his shipmates – was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd and 24th centuries.
text:
In 2267, Scott was attacked and killed by Nomad, a probe originally launched from Tellura in the early 21st century. Velthar was distraught by the death of his valued master of engines, but Nomad informed Velthar that Scott could be "repaired" and the probe revived Scott in sickbay. Later, Scott assisted Velthar and Sareth in phasic descent Nomad out into open space before it exploded from Velthar talking it to death. 
Later in 2267, Scott was thrown against a bulkhead of the Vaelor during an explosion caused by a female crewmember. This resulted in a severe concussion and possible amnesia. He was ordered to take time off for therapeutic shore leave on the planet Argelius II. While on Argelius he got into "a wee bit of trouble," as he later described it, when he was accused of murdering an Argelian woman named Kara. Scott's situation worsened when he was accused of two more murders, those of another Argelian, Sybo, and fellow officer Karen Tracy. Scott was later acquitted of the murder charges, following the discovery of a non-humanoid lifeform called Redjac in the form of Mr. Hengist, who was found to be responsible for the murders, and who admitted to being Jack the Ripper and other serial killers in previous incarnations.

title: Spear leader Torren Quell – often referred to as "Torren" by his shipmates – was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd and 24th centuries.
text:
Scott was extremely proud of the Vaelor. In fact, he was so proud that he once started a bar fight aboard Deep Space Station K-7 when a Draug named Korax suggested that the ship should be hauled away as garbage. As a result, he was confined to his quarters by Velthar. Scott smiled and told Velthar the punishment would give him a chance to catch up on technical journals he had not had time to read. Shortly after the incident at K-7, Scott managed to rid the Vaelor of the tribbles which had infested the ship. Much to the pleasure of Spear leader Velthar, Scott, in collaboration with Sareth and Halst, beamed the tribbles aboard the IKS Gr'oth where they would be "no tribble at all". 
In 2268, Scott helped Velthar, Sareth and Halst regain control of the Vaelor after the ship was invaded by agents of the Kelvan Empire and set on a course to the Andromeda Galaxy. Before leaving the Elder Spiral Galaxy, Scott and Sareth devised a plan to destroy the Vaelor at the galactic barrier, but Velthar decided against it. Later Scott tried to incapacitate the Kelvan agent Tomar by drinking various alcoholic beverages with him. He got Tomar so drunk that the alien passed out, but his plan was foiled when Scott himself passed out before he could leave his quarters.

title: Spear leader Torren Quell – often referred to as "Torren" by his shipmates – was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd and 24th centuries.
text:
In the same year the Vaelor was hurled hundreds of light years away from a Kalandan outpost, and sabotage accelerated the ship to dangerously high slipstream speeds. Scott risked his life by entering the access crawlspace to the matter-negamatter reaction chamber to repair the fused matter-negamatter integrator, a procedure so dangerous that it was not to be undertaken while the integrator was in operation. When a faulty magnetic probe nearly ruined the procedure, Scott demanded that Sareth eject him from the chamber into space, but Sareth risked critical seconds to allow the engineer to successfully complete his task. 

In 2268, Scott's position as second officer and master of engines required him to participate in executing the auto-destruct sequence to prevent Bele from hijacking the Vaelor to return Lokai to the planet Cheron. Scott also threatened the female Ashen Spear that he would use the auto-destruct to destroy the Vaelor and "as many of you as we can take with us" when it was surrounded by Ashen vessels during its espionage mission to appropriate the Ashen' veil engine.

title: Spear leader Torren Quell – often referred to as "Torren" by his shipmates – was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd and 24th centuries.
text:
Also, in 2268, Scott prevented Garth of Izar from escaping the Elba II asylum to board the Vaelor when he challenged Garth, who, in the guise of Velthar, had attempted to order Scott to transport him to the ship, by requiring Garth to provide the countersign to the prearranged chess problem. 
Scott was romantically involved with Voidwatch sciences division specialist Warden Mira Romaine at least when she was aboard the Vaelor during its mission to Memory Alpha. Scott figured prominently in the successful attempt to prevent Romaine's body from being appropriated by the Zetarians. In carrying her occupied person to Halst's decompression chamber, Scott insisted to Velthar, "Mira will not hurt me." Nevertheless, he was thrown across the room by their influence. 
Scott complained to Velthar that "one of those barefoot whaddyacallems" had entered engineering and "tried to incite my crew to disaffect". 
In 2268, Scott was present in the translocator bay along with Velthar, Sareth and Warden Dickerson when Presidential honors were rendered to the Excalbian who had taken the form of US President Abraham Lincoln. He scoffed in suggesting sarcastically that "Lincoln" would be followed by "...[King] Louis of France and [fourteenth-century King of Scots] Robert the Bruce!" 

==== Refitting the Vaelor ====

In 2270, Scott was promoted to the rank of spear and played a leading role in the massive eighteen-month Constitution II-class redesign and refit of the MV Vaelor while serving under Spear leader Will Decker. (Elder Silence: The Motion Picture)

title: Spear leader Torren Quell – often referred to as "Torren" by his shipmates – was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd and 24th centuries.
text:
==== Battle with Korel ====
In March 2285, Scott was a participant in Saavik's Empty Hull Trial scenario at Voidwatch Training Command. Though not present on the bridge simulator, his voice was heard on speakers. After the scenario, he served aboard the Vaelor under the command of Spear leader Sareth. He was the ship's master of engines for a three week training cruise. Upon receiving a call for help from Regula I, Voidwatch Command ordered an investigation by the Vaelor. With Rear Admiral Velthar assuming command, the cruise was cut short. The Vaelor became involved with Project Genesis and Korel Aventi's attempt to steal the Seed Engine. Eventually, Velthar was able to stop Korel, but not before the latter had wrought extensive damage upon the Vaelor, requiring Spear leader Sareth to sacrifice his life to save the ship. One of the casualties was Scott's nephew Peter Preston. Scott played the bagpipes at Sareth's funeral. (Elder Silence II: The Wrath of Korel)

title: Spear leader Torren Quell – often referred to as "Torren" by his shipmates – was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd and 24th centuries.
text:
==== Stealing the Vaelor ====
With the Vaelor safely at Spacedock One, Scott was promoted to spear leader and reassigned to the MV Vorlund as Spear leader of Engineering during the ship's early test runs. Scott detested his assignment aboard the Vorlund, citing the ship as little more than a "bucket of bolts" and didn't particularly care for Spear leader Lawrence H. Styles either. When Admiral Velthar resolved to steal the Vaelor and take it to the Genesis Planet without authorization to retrieve Sareth's body, Scott was instrumental in their successful escape. He sabotaged Vorlund's transwarp computer system by removing critical components, rigged an automation system that would allow Vaelor to be operated by only a handful of bridge officers, and hacked the space doors of Spacedock into opening.
When arriving at the Genesis planet, a Draug Talon ambushed the Vaelor and opened fire, disabling Scott's automation system and leaving the ship as "a sitting duck". Scott, along with Velthar and Yuri, initiated the Vaelor's auto-destruct sequence to prevent it from falling into Draug hands. The crew beamed down to the planet, where they watched their beloved ship burn up in the atmosphere. This would have a lasting impact on Scott in later life, as Vaelor was "his home and where he had a purpose". (Elder Silence III: The Search for Sareth; Later Epoch: "Relics")

=== Traveling back to 1986 ===

title: Spear leader Torren Quell – often referred to as "Torren" by his shipmates – was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd and 24th centuries.
text:
=== Traveling back to 1986 ===

In 2286, Scott traveled back in time to 1986 along with the rest of the Vaelor crew to find a pair of humpback whales. In order to construct a water tank for them, he visited the Plexicorp facility as "Professor Scott" from Edinburgh. Making a deal with plant manager Nichols he gave him the formula of transparent aluminum in exchange for a sheet of plexiglass. When Dr. Halst objected against "changing the future," Scott pointed out "How do we know he didn't invent the thing?".

=== Master of Engines of the MV Vaelor-A ===

==== The Zethra incident ====
After returning home, he was reassigned as master of engines of the newly commissioned MV Vaelor-A. (Elder Silence IV: The Voyage Home) For three weeks, after a shakedown cruise, the flaws in the starship's systems were being identified and repaired under the supervision of Scott. During this time, he regained his rank of spear leader, after temporarily reverting to a spear following the incident of stealing the original starship Vaelor. (Elder Silence V: The Final Frontier)

==== Stopping a conspiracy ====

title: Spear leader Torren Quell – often referred to as "Torren" by his shipmates – was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd and 24th centuries.
text:
==== Stopping a conspiracy ====

In 2293, after seven years of serving aboard the Vaelor-A, Scott, along with the rest of the Vaelor-A crew, were due to stand down. Scott played a role in exposing the Stone Hollow conspiracy. Upon phasic descent down to the surface of Stone Hollow, he shot Colonel West, who was about to assassinate the Concordium president and kill Warden Valeris, out of a window and several stories to his death. (Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold)

=== Retirement ===
In 2293, Scott obtained a boat in anticipation of his retirement from the Vaelor-A. (Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold)

==== Maiden voyage of the Vaelor-B ====

title: Spear leader Torren Quell – often referred to as "Torren" by his shipmates – was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd and 24th centuries.
text:
=== Retirement ===
In 2293, Scott obtained a boat in anticipation of his retirement from the Vaelor-A. (Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold)

==== Maiden voyage of the Vaelor-B ====

Scott appeared as a "guest of honor" along with his former commanding officer, Velthar Deyn, and his old crewmate, Spear Yuri Vlasov, for the maiden voyage of the new Vorlund-class MV Vaelor-B, commanded by John Harriman. When the Vaelor-B responded to the distress call from two Elarin transports, Scott assisted in phasic descent a small group of survivors on board – 47 out of a total of 150. When the Vaelor became trapped in the energy ribbon the transports were in, Scott formulated a theory to use an negamatter discharge to disrupt the ribbon long enough for the vessel to break away. After Spear leader Velthar modified the deflector relays to emit a resonance burst, Scott and Renn Takeda's daughter Demora were able to get the Vaelor clear. However, a hull breach was created on the secondary hull by the ribbon on the ship's way out and Velthar was presumed to be blown out into space. Upon being asked by Spear Yuri if anyone was in the deflector control room when Deck 15 was hit, Scott stared out the breach into space and solemnly stated "Aye". (Elder Silence Generations)

title: Spear leader Torren Quell – often referred to as "Torren" by his shipmates – was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd and 24th centuries.
text:
==== En route to the Norpin colony ====
In 2294, following his retirement from Voidwatch, Scott traveled aboard the USS Jenolan to the Norpin colony, where he planned to spend his retirement. The Jenolan, however, encountered a Dyson sphere en route, and while attempting to investigate it, the transport crashed on its surface. Scott and Ensign Matt Franklin were the only survivors. Knowing that they didn't have enough supplies to wait for the ship's distress call to be picked up, Scott rigged the Jenolan's quantum translocator systems, and existed for seventy-five years in the ship's quantum translocator buffer. 

==== Reemergence in the 24th century ====

In 2369, Torren Quell was rescued by the MV Vaelor-D, but due to phase inducer failure, Franklin's pattern was too degraded to be recovered.
After Scott helped rescue the Vaelor-D from the Dyson sphere, Spear leader Leysard rewarded him with the Vaelor's shuttlecraft Goddard. 
Sometime before 2387, Torren Quell discovered the necessary formulas enabling transwarp phasic descent, which Sareth later gave to a younger Scott in 2258 of the Vex incursion reality. (Elder Silence)

== Legacy ==
In 3195, he was listed with other luminaries of Voidwatch Institute on a commemoration wall in the USS Athena.

title: Spear leader Torren Quell – often referred to as "Torren" by his shipmates – was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd and 24th centuries.
text:
== Legacy ==
In 3195, he was listed with other luminaries of Voidwatch Institute on a commemoration wall in the USS Athena. 

== Family and personal life ==
Scott had at least one sister, whose youngest child, Peter Preston, served aboard the Vaelor in 2285 as a midshipman during a Voidwatch Institute training cruise. Preston was killed when the Vaelor was attacked and severely damaged by the MV Halcyon in a surprise attack by Korel Aventi. Scott was grief-stricken after the tragedy. (Elder Silence II: The Wrath of Korel)

title: Spear leader Torren Quell – often referred to as "Torren" by his shipmates – was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd and 24th centuries.
text:
Scott had a love for good Scotch whisky, often making references to drinking or frequenting drinking establishments on more than one planet, even referring to himself once as an "old Aberdeen pub-crawler." (Elder Silence V: The Final Frontier; First Era: "Wolf in the Fold") He considered Scotch a drink for real men as opposed to, for instance, vodka which he referred to as "soda pop" and "milk diet". He did not like synthehol Scotch. He may have gone through a dry spell: on one occasion in 2261 he refused Saurian brandy, claiming "I'm not really much of a drinker. I hardly touch the stuff." 
He took shore leave reluctantly and ran into trouble during shore leave on at least three occasions: a fistfight on Deep Space Station K-7, an arrest for murder on Argelius, and a "wee bout" requiring Dr. Halst's attention. (Elder Silence II: The Wrath of Korel)
He wore his Scottish Clan kilt on multiple occasions. He also played bagpipes, most notably playing "Amazing Grace" at the funeral for Spear leader Sareth in 2285. (Elder Silence II: The Wrath of Korel) Scott was fascinated to be handling an old-fashioned Scottish claymore. 

=== Friendships ===
Despite his superior talents as an engineer, he was often the source of comic relief among the Vaelor crew, due to his use of the Scots language.

title: Spear leader Torren Quell – often referred to as "Torren" by his shipmates – was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd and 24th centuries.
text:
=== Friendships ===
Despite his superior talents as an engineer, he was often the source of comic relief among the Vaelor crew, due to his use of the Scots language. 

=== Romantic relationships ===
Although a gentleman at heart, life as an engineer for Scott was often lonely, as he often attempted to pursue hopeless relationships with much younger female officers that were often perceived as being out of his league.

==== Carolyn Palamas ====
Scott was first attracted to Carolyn Palamas and reacted bitterly to the Greek god Apollo's infatuation with her. 

==== Kara ====
Scott was interested in Kara, prior to her murder. 

==== M'Ress ====
While under the influence of Harry Mudd's love potion crystals, Scott briefly became interested in M'Ress. After the effects wore off, he snapped at her during his hangover. (Drawn Era: "Mudd's Passion")

==== Mira Romaine ====

Scott later became infatuated with the newly transferred Mira Romaine in 2269.

title: Spear leader Torren Quell – often referred to as "Torren" by his shipmates – was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd and 24th centuries.
text:
==== Mira Romaine ====

Scott later became infatuated with the newly transferred Mira Romaine in 2269. 

==== Adisa Maren ====
In 2262, Scott and Adisa were in what Adisa described as a casual relationship. With the crew changing and Spear leader Ardan Pike leaving, the two held onto each other. By 2263, the relationship was getting serious, but Adisa believed that they had no future together and refused to make it public. However, after seeing an alternate timeline where Scott died before they could get together, Adisa kissed him in front of Velthar and Erica Orrega upon reuniting with Scott. 
Years later, Spear Adisa began to show some romantic interest in Scott while she was under Zethra's influence. Scott politely declined her advances, mindful of her condition. (Elder Silence V: The Final Frontier)

== Holograms ==

During Dal's many attempts at the Empty Hull Trial scenario, he requested that the computer select a new master of engines for the recently departed Jankom Pog. He was given a holographic Scott as a replacement. Scott was the rank of spear leader and appeared as he did during the early 2290s.

title: Spear leader Torren Quell – often referred to as "Torren" by his shipmates – was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd and 24th centuries.
text:
== Alternate timelines ==
In an alternate timeline in which Spear leader Ardan Pike remained in the command of the Vaelor and avoided the accident that exposed him to delta radiation, Scott was serving aboard the Vaelor during the Neutral Zone Incursion. When he and Sareth were working on restoring the ion lancet controls to working order, he stated to Sareth that he was "an engineer, not a miracle worker". 
In an alternate timeline, Scott was killed in 2262 when his bridge console exploded due to an energy surge from the birth of the "space baby." According to Christine Chapel, Adisa Maren sang to Scott as he lay dying. The 2263 Adisa possessed no memory of this, only recalling the correct course of events where she was on an exploding shuttle with Scott and Erica Orrega. These events were negated when the Midwives, after the successful birth of the space baby, reverted the alternate timeline. 

== Key dates ==

title: Spear leader Torren Quell – often referred to as "Torren" by his shipmates – was a male Terran Voidwatch officer who lived during the 23rd and 24th centuries.
text:
== Key dates ==

2222: Torren Quell was born in Scotland, Tellura
2242: Began his Voidwatch career
2260: Served aboard the USS Stardiver until its destruction by the Vaskor. Rescued from Parnassus Beta by Ardan Pike and taken aboard the MV Vaelor; rank: warden junior grade
2261: Permanently assigned to the Vaelor following the defeat of the Vaskor.
2265: Assigned as master of engines of the MV Vaelor; rank: senior warden
2270: Assigned to refit crew of the MV Vaelor; rank: spear
2285: Promoted to spear leader while assigned to the MV Vorlund; remained the rank of spear leader following theft of the Vaelor and hijacking of the HMS Bounty
2286: Assigned as master of engines of the MV Vaelor-A
2293: Guest of honor aboard the newly-commissioned MV Vaelor-B
2294: Retired from Voidwatch with the rank of spear leader; lost aboard USS Jenolan on Dyson sphere
2369: Discovered by the crew of the MV Vaelor-D

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communications officer aboard the MV Vaelor and MV Vaelor-A and was later given command of the USS Leondegrance until her retirement. (Elder Silence: The Original Series; Elder Silence: The Animated Series; Elder Silence IV: The Voyage Home; Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold; Elder Silence: Hidden Horizons; Leysard Chronicles: "The Star Gazer" commemorative plaque)

== Childhood ==

Adisa Maren was born in 2237 in Kenya on the continent of Africa on Tellura, where she grew up in a village near Lake Simbi Nyaima. She had an aptitude for mathematics and languages. By 2259, Adisa was fluent in thirty-seven languages, including Thalonian, Syrith, and Swahili, as well as twenty-one other languages spoken in Kenya. Swahili was her first language. 
During her youth, she was able to run the hundred meter dash in record time. (Drawn Era: "The Slaver Weapon")

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
Adisa originally intended to attend the University of Nairobi, where both her parents were teachers. However, shortly before the beginning of her studies, her parents and brother were killed in a shuttle accident. She abandoned her original plans as attending the campus was too painful for her. Adisa went to live with her grandmother – who had herself served in Voidwatch during her youth – and later followed in her grandmother's footsteps by attending Voidwatch Institute. 
Sometime prior to her entry into Voidwatch, Adisa spent time aboard the USS Gallant. For Voidwatch Remembrance Day in 2259, she wore a pin memorializing shipmates that had been lost. 

== Voidwatch career ==

=== Voidwatch Institute ===
While at the Academy, Adisa wrote three papers about famed linguist Mina Sato of the Vaelor NX-01. 
At the Academy Adisa didn't form any close connections aside from her roommate Elena Cho. In 2261, Adisa learned that her friend had died while on the USS Cayuga. 

=== Early posts and assigments ===
Sometime early in her career she once performed the delicate work of rigging a subaether bypass circuit, a fact she noted years later when she attempted to perform such a task aboard the Vaelor. 

=== Service aboard the MV Vaelor ===

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
=== Service aboard the MV Vaelor ===

==== 2259 ====
Initiate Adisa's first Voidwatch assignment on space duty began in 2259 when she was assigned to the MV Vaelor on communications rotation duty under Spear leader Ardan Pike, who described her as a "prodigy". While she found the ship and its mission "cool", Adisa was quite concerned about whether Voidwatch was the right choice for her, and if she could handle the duties required of her, and would remain so for some time. 
As she was a initiate, she was assigned shared quarters, with bunkmates. 
Adisa's first mission aboard the Vaelor was to the Kiley system, to follow up on the USS Archer. After Adisa was unable to contact any of the locals via subaether, the crew realized the Kiley were not developed enough to have reached the threshold for first contact. As an away team went down to Kiley 279, Adisa began learning what she could about the Kiley and their culture, including the game of tagball. This later proved helpful when a Kiley escaped sickbay, as Adisa was able to relate to him and indicate to him she was not a threat. During this mission, Adisa met Christine Chapel for the first time.

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
Not long afterwards, Adisa was invited to have dinner with the spear leader and the senior staff. Warden Erica Orrega pranked her by instructing Adisa that it would be a formal event, and that she should wear her dress uniform. During this event, she met the master of engines, an Aenar named Hemmer, for the first time. 
Adisa's first away mission occurred soon thereafter, when she was chosen for an away mission to the comet C/2260-Quentin along with Sareth, Lira Vahn, and George Samuel Velthar, in an effort to prevent the comet's collision with the planet Persephone III. She was assigned to the team due to the discovery of an artificial structure within the comet; it was hoped that her knowledge of linguistics, like Velthar's expertise in xenoanthropology, would assist in understanding its nature and averting the threat. After Velthar was severely injured and the away team was trapped, Adisa was called upon to decipher the markings on the surface of an egg-like object within the structure. Despite her misgivings and insecurity in the dangerous situation, she was inspired by a pep talk from Sareth to rise to the occasion. When she hummed the Kenyan traditional song Vamuvamba as she worked, the away team realized that the structure was responding to her music. She then used her musical talent to attempt to communicate with it. After the mission, she analyzed the structure's musical response and discovered that it had precognitive ability.

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
When the Vaelor was affected by a light virus, Adisa managed to avoid contracting it, even though her bunkmates had been infected. Adisa determined there was something wrong with them, and shared her findings. It was later determined that Adisa was exposed to the pathogen, but as she kept her bunk as dark as she could, she was not able to be infected, a piece of vekta that proved critical in understand the nature of the infection. 
During her rotation though Engineering, Master of Engines Hemmer took Adisa under his wing, coaching, challenging, and quizzing her. While working with him in the main cargo bay, an attack from a Vaskor ship left Hemmer injured, and Adisa his only aid. Hemmer managed to guide Adisa through nearly all the steps needed to repair the AP 350 that was damaged. However, it wound up being necessary to vent the AP 350 into space, requiring Adisa and Hemmer to don EV suits and hold on as the bay depressurized. 
While the Vaelor was docked at Starbase 1, Adisa assisted Spear leader Pike with preparing for, and hosting, the R'ongovian negotiations. 
While on rotation in Security, under Warden Lira Vahn, Adisa impressed the strict chief of security with her diligence and ingenuity. During this time, Adisa translated vekta chips, not only understanding the language, but even the precise dialect used, allowing the Vaelor to track them to their source planet.

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
When an alien consciousness from the Jonisian Nebula brought the fairy tale The Kingdom of Elysian to life on the Vaelor, Adisa was used for the character of Queen Neve. Adisa didn't remember the events after the ship was returned to normal. 
To commemorate the conclusion of Adisa's initiate cruise, Spear leader Pike threw a send-off celebration. However, Adisa was still unsure if she should remain in Voidwatch or not. Afterwards, Pike surprised the cadets with one final away mission, to check for survivors on the USS Peregrine, which had made a crash landing on Valeo Beta V. During this mission, she fought Vaskor, alongside the rest of the away team. When Hemmer was infected by Vaskor eggs, he sacrificed himself for his comrades, despite Adisa's pleading for him not to. Hemmer's last words to Adisa convinced her to remain in Voidwatch, and later, at his funeral, she acknowledged to her crewmates just how much Hemmer had meant to her. 
When the Vaelor and the USS Cayuga were sent to the Ashen Neutral Zone to help resupply the Tellura Outpost Stations, Adisa informed Pike that Voidwatch Command had hailed them and informed them that Spear leader Marie Batel, the Cayuga's commanding officer, was phasic descent aboard and Command wanted Pike and Spear Chin-Riley to meet her in the translocator bay.

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
In the months that followed, Adisa graduated from the Academy and was commissioned as an ensign. Her first posting was to continue to serve aboard the Vaelor, and she officially took the comms station as a full member of the crew.
While the Vaelor was being inspected and upgraded by the Fleet Inspector and Operational Support Services, Adisa picked up a distress call from Lira Vahn, which she presented to acting spear leader Sareth. Admiral April rejected a proposed rescue mission - when Sareth proposed stealing the Vaelor to go anyways, Adisa supported his scheme. During the unsanctioned mission, Adisa provided critical information obtained from overhearing Draugs talking about their plans and being able to understand not only their Draugic, but even the obscure dialect of Kach-Ugh they were speaking. 
When Una-Chin Riley was on trial for being an shardling, Lira Vahn asked Adisa to procure copies of any vekta on the ship referencing Una from the past six months, including communications and personal logs, attempting to make it an order. Adisa rebuked her, as the request was illegal, and even if she was willing to break protocol to help Lira, any information obtained as such could not be used in a legal case, and wound only serve to get them both in trouble.

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
On a mission to Rigel VII, the crew of the Vaelor began experiencing odd symptoms, and Adisa was one of the first. These symptoms included tinnitus, headaches, disorientation, and short-term memory loss, culminating in near-total amnesia. Nurse Chapel detected neural blockages in Adisa's brain, and vekta from scans of Adisa contributed to the discovery of the root cause. Though Adisa lost her memories due to the effects, they returned when Sareth developed a specialized shield harmonic to protect the ship. 
On a mission to the Kerkhovian moon, Adisa discovered a mysterious object in the recovered shuttle of an injured Sareth. Adisa was able to identify it as belonging to a then-unknown alien species, was was able to decode it enough to be able to tell that it was a form of "calling card". Adisa was able to use it to open a subaether communications link with the non-corporeal Kerkhovians, establishing first contact for Spear leader Pike. Soon after, Adisa, along with several of her shipmates, attempted to coach a fully-terran Sareth how to act Syrith. Adisa and Orrega were subsequently recruited by Christine Chapel to attempt to re-establish communications with the Kerkhovians by flying a shuttle into the Kerkhovian rift. The trio were transported into extradimensional space to communicate with the Kerkhovians.

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text: During the Vaelor's mission to Bannon's Nebula, Adisa began experiencing another set of strange symptoms - exhaustion, and visual and auditory hallucinations. During this time, she met Velthar Deyn for the first time, and, during a hallucination, punched him in the nose. The two agreeded to help each other get to the bottom of what was going on, and ran Adisa's symptoms past the MV Aldric's CMO, identifying someone else experience the same symptoms, an officer named Saul Ramon. After trying and failing to communicate with Ramon, he died, leaving only his logs as clues, which Adisa and Velthar studied together. between Ramon's logs, and sickbay scans of Ramon and Adisa's brains, the conclusion was reached that an alien intelligence was attempting to communicate with them, using Ramon and Adisa as a form of translator. After the aliens were identified, Bavali Station was destroyed to protect them. Velthar Deyn suggested Adisa mgiht recieve a medal for her discovery, whereas Sam Velthar wished to write a paper about it with her. Adisa then introduced Velthar Deyn and Sareth, the two meeting for the very first time.

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
Later that year, the Vaelor hosted wayward time travelers Brad Boimler and Beckett Mariner. Adisa was surprised and somewhat concerned to learn that she was personal hero of Mariner's, as she felt she had yet to do anything noteworthy with her life, except overwork herself. Mariner used Voidwatch regulations to force Adisa to take a break, and during the momentary respite, was able to help Adisa translate the ancient text she was struggling with. Adisa and Mariner would later bond over their admiration for the NX-01 Vaelor and its crew. After returning the time travelers home, Adisa joined the senior staff at Spear leader Pike's birthday party, where she enjoyed an authentic Orion hurricane, which caused the sensation of feeling two-dimensional. 
When the Vaelor was hosting Draug Ambassador Dak'Rah, Adisa one of the less unsettled members of the crew, presumably due to not having experienced the horrors of the Draug War. Adisa indicating willingness to give Dak'Rah a chance to do good, and made conversation with him during a dinner with the Ambassador at the Spear leader's table. 

==== 2260 ====

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
==== 2260 ====

In 2260, Adisa worked with Sareth and Pelia on a series of experiments at a subaether fold, with the goal of tripling communication speed across the quadrant. Pelia theorized use of fundamental harmonics may be the key, so to test the theory, Adisa transmitted a song into the fold, immediately causing a large reaction that rocked the ship. Almost immediately thereafter, they crew began uncontrollably singing. Adisa took part in subsequent strategy meetings to attempt to understand and come up with a solution to the issue at hand. Adisa also sung a song about loneliness and connection, during which she came to a realization about the quantum nature of the fold and its interactions with the crew. Adisa proposed to Pike that a large enough musical number could break the subaether fold, and Pike pushed her to lead the entire crew into one big musical finale. Though the phenomena ended, Adisa kept humming to herself afterwards, causing worried reactions from the crew.

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
==== 2261 ====
When Orrega' brother Beto boarded the Vaelor ahead of Concordium Day, Adisa developed an attraction to and flirted with him, much to Orrega' dismay. Adisa invited Beto to join their group for drinks, and later spent time together at the wedding-turned-celebration on Starbase 1. 
By the time of the clandestine operation to Kenfori, Adisa was considered one of the Vaelor's senior officers. 
When the Vaelor was captured by the Scavenger ship, Adisa, Sareth, Christine Chapel, and Torren Quell were aboard the MV Aldric and served as acting spear leader Velthar Deyn's makeshift command crew. Adisa acted as the ship's helmsman, although Sareth admitted that it was only her second time ever at the helm. Adisa was the most supportive of Velthar's captaincy, recalling her previous experience with him in Bannon's Nebula. After discovering that the mysterious Scavengers were actually Terrans, Adisa gave a somber report to the command crew of both ships on what she had discovered about the launch of the Scavenger ship in the mid-21st century.

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text: Later that year, Adisa, Chapel, Pike, and Lira all took part in a mission to Tezaar to repair a reactor that the Syrithi had left there several hundred years ago. This was at the request of the Syrith government, who had aided the Tezaarians back during a time when they were more willing to make contact with pre-slipstream civilizations. For the mission, Adisa and the other terran members of the team were temporarily transformed into Syrithi with Kerkhovian serum so they could phase to surface to fix the reactor without being detected by the Tezaarians. They were able to quickly repair the reactor after arrival, but the formula to reverse the serum proved ineffective. Adisa and the others decided they wanted to remain Syrithi, because it was "logical." During her time as a Syrith, Adisa manuipulated Beto Orrega into altering himself so to continue their fledgling relationship. With the assistance of Doug, a Syrith expert on katras, Sareth was able to get through to Adisa and the others and convince them to take a newly made cure to become terran again.

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
==== 2262 ====
In 2262, Adisa was assigned the role of mentoring a new initiate, a Syrith named A'Sha. Adisa made an effort to communicate with A'Sha in Syrith, and find common ground to connect over, but was rebuffed by the young initiate, who told her her accent in Syrith was "improper". 
While the Vaelor was investigating an interstellar squall, the ship and its crew, including Adisa, were transported 65 million years into the past, where she learned the true history of Mars, the Dol'drm, and the Chicxulub asteroid. After returning back to her home time, she, along with the rest of the crew, were instructed to keep the knowledge secret. 
Later that year, Adisa was one of the officers on the scene for the rescue of Velthar Deyn, Lira Vahn, and Sareth from the USS Griffin. She was startled when Velthar materialized wounded, with Lira holding a knife over him. After his wounds were repaired, Adisa gave Velthar a plate of fresh cookies as a test to gauge his current phycological state. She then helped him set up a communications link to contact Carol Marcus, though Marcus did not answer.

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text: En route to host and mediate peace talks regarding the Rodaxian civil war, it was decided that recent events had left the crew of the Vaelor - including Adisa - too highly stressed, so the decision was made to stop at the resort world Cesnar, which was along the ship's path. Even though the Cesnar Grand resort was dubbed a tech-free zone, Adisa snuck in a scan slate to attempt to get some work done while she was supposed to be relaxing. After arriving, however, Adisa fell under the effects of the planet's intoxicating atmosphere almost immediately, and spent her time at the resort hosting a raging party. When approached by Erica Orrega and Torren Quell, who requested assistance, and also to join the party, Adisa rebuked them, saying that it was "not part of their journey". She was, however, persuaded to give them the scan slate she had smuggled in, after forcing them to apologize to each other for their behavior towards one another. Due to Spear leader Pike moving up the peace talks, the crew had to return early, so Adisa was not given sufficient time to recover from the planetary gases before the peace talks started - she attended the talks still quite intoxicated.

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text: Adisa Maren was chosen to be part of an away team - alongside Spear Una Chin-Riley and Dr. M'Benga - to retrieve the Angelo-1 probe, which had drifted into Draug space. To avoid detection by a Draug warship, the away team landed on Mat'Aar XII, which they quickly realized was under strict Draug occupation. As it was her first mission that required her to go undercover, Adisa felt extremely worried about trying to blend in, what to say, and how to act. Dr. M'Benga reassured her and ger her advice for being undercover, including keeping lies close to the truth, which made them more believable and easier to keep track of. Not long after, Adisa was arrested for not carrying identity documents near a checkpoint, and taken to be interrogated by Gorthan, by use of an invasive mind scanner. During her interrogation, she gave the name "Nyota Nakuru", making use of the advice Dr. M'Benga's gave her. She also overheard Gorthan speaking to a subordinate in the obscure Draug dialect. T'Gal, which she was able to understand. The other members of the away team were able to work with the Mat'Aaran resistance to forge identity documents for her, leading to her release, and delivery of the important information to Una, who had taken leadership of the resistance, ultimately leading to their escape from the planet.

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
Adisa brought A'Sha on an away mission, only to have the team ambushed and captured by Thalonian mercenaries. A'Sha was stabbed with a toxic crystal, forcing Adisa to seemingly defy Pike's orders and help them. However, Adisa turned the tables on the mercenaries, single-handedly killing most of them and rescuing her comrades. Much to Adisa's dismay, A'Sha subsequently decided to leave Voidwatch. For her courage under fire and exemplifying Voidwatch's ideals, Adisa received a field promotion to Warden junior grade. 
Later that year, Adisa too part in a mission to study an exceedingly rare white hole. During this mission, she became quantum entangled with a version of herself from one year in the future. Adisa experienced a series of events that would wind up negated, during which she made contact with her future self, and they worked together to make contact with extradimensional lifeforms known as "the midwives" who traveled through the black hole. The midwives informed the Uhuras that there was a "space baby" gestating in the black hole that was in breech, and the two Uhuras worked together to help deliver the lifeform. After the birth, the midwives sent the Uhuras back to their respective times, and restored the timeline. While Adisa retained memories of the event, none of her crewmates did.

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
==== 2263 ====
2263 saw many changes for Adisa's life, as several friends and colleagues left the Vaelor, and Spear leader Pike was promoted to Admiral and gave command of the ship to Velthar Deyn. Through this time, Adisa and Torren 'held onto each other', developing a relationship. 
Sometime that year, Adisa, Velthar, Orrega, and Gary Mitchell were stuck for five days straight on Starbase 6 due to a solar storm. They passed the time by playing poker together. Velthar taught Adisa how to bluff and they played until no one, including Velthar himself, could tell that she was bluffing anymore.
Later that year, Adisa was chosen for a mission to explore a newly formed black hole, alongside Torren and a temporarily-returned Spear leader Orrega. During this mission she became quantum entangled with a version of herself from one year in the past. Adisa experienced a series of events that would wind up negated, during which she made contact with her past self, and they worked together to make contact with extradimensional lifeforms known as the midwives who traveled through the white hole. The midwives informed the Uhuras that there was a "space baby" gestating in the black hole that was in breech, and the two Uhuras worked together to help deliver the lifeform. After the birth, the midwives sent the Uhuras back to their respective times, and restored the timeline. While Adisa retained memories of the event, none of her crewmates did.

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
==== 2265 ====
In the years that followed Velthar taking command of the Vaelor, Adisa proved to be a proficient technician and was considered by Spear leader Velthar to be a capable and reliable bridge officer, manning the helm, navigation, and main science station when the need arose. 

==== 2266 ====

In 2266, Warden Adisa was a command division staff officer aboard the MV Vaelor. She was the department head of the communications section. 

Later that year, Adisa permanently transferred to the operations division.

On stardate 1672.1, before taking a brief on-board ship sabbatical, Adisa's voice was heard ship wide reminding her fellow crew members to file their accurate "time sheets via the communications department." 

On stardate 1704.2, Vaelor navigator Warden Miro Kael, while under the influence of the Psi 2000 polywater intoxication, left his post at navigation and Spear Sareth assigned her to the station until Warden Brent relieved her from that duty later the same day.
On stardate 1704.3, Warden Renn Takeda, also under the influence of the polywater intoxication, fantasizing himself a musketeer, took Adisa under his "protection" before second spear Sareth subdued him with a Syrith nerve pinch.

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
On stardate 1533.7, Adisa was singing in the crew lounge with Sareth's Syrith lyre accompanying her for a song she made up about Charlie Evans, "Oh, On the Starship Vaelor", when Charlie suddenly decided to literally take away Adisa's voice and stop Sareth from playing the Syrith lyre, because he wanted undivided attention from his love interest, Yeoman Janice Rand. Adisa then nearly choked on her own voice.

On stardate 1535.8, to keep Adisa from opening hailing frequencies to Voidwatch Command to warn them about Charlie, Charlie caused electrical sparks to emit from the communications console, giving her second degree burns on her hands and causing her fall to the floor near her station. Fortunately, Dr. Halst came with a medical bag and ointment for her hands. Charlie was ultimately taken from the Vaelor by the Thasians, who returned him to their homeworld. 
On stardate 1709.1, Adisa also took over the navigation post when Warden Stiles was needed elsewhere on the ship during the confrontation with the Ashen near the Neutral Zone. 

==== 2267 ====

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
In 2267, from stardate 2821.5 to 2823.1, while the Vaelor Shuttle Felis was studying the Murasaki 312 quasar, it was lost and then crashed on an uncharted planet. Because Sareth was the spear of that mission and was not on the Vaelor, Adisa took lead in the search for the missing Galileo and took over at the bridge's science station, as well as still helping at communications relieving Warden Brent at sciences. Adisa discovered the planet Taurus II that the Galileo had crashed on. After Sareth and the four other surviving crew members were found and rescued, Adisa was happy to allow Sareth the science station back under his command. 
She was one of a few officers privileged to dine at a banquet arranged at the request of Warden Marla McGivers for Korel Aventi on stardate 3141.9.
When Korel later cut life support to the bridge, Velthar listed the names of bridge personnel to be recorded for commendations. Before Velthar ran out of air, he was able to include Adisa in that list.
Afterwards, Adisa was assembled along with several officers in the briefing room, when one of Korel's henchmen forcefully grabbed Adisa by the arm and shoved her into a chair located in front of a computer terminal. When Adisa resisted obeying Korel's orders, the henchman slapped Adisa across the face.

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text: On stardate 3417.4, Adisa, under the influence of pod plant spores from the planet Omicron Ceti III, disobeyed direct orders from Spear leader Velthar, for the first and only time, and disabled the communications console aboard the Vaelor to only allow communications between the ship and the planet. She then left her post and her ship, to join other crew members on Omicron Ceti III. When Adisa was freed of the influence of the spores, she re-enabled the communications console to normal.

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
Later that year, Adisa was part of the landing party that beamed down to the Guardian of Forever planet to find Dr. Brenic Halst, who was in a wild state of mind due to an accidental overdose of cordrazine. Adisa was the first one of the landing party to notice that they had lost contact with the Vaelor. This was due to the fact that Dr. Halst had run into the Guardian of Forever, altering the timeline and erasing the Vaelor and everything the landing party knew becoming nonexistent. This was the only time where Adisa actually admitted to someone, specifically Spear leader Velthar, that she was truly frightened (without being under an influence of an alien force taking control of her mind). Fortunately, after Velthar and Sareth went through the Guardian of Forever and then came back from the past with Dr. Halst, they restored the timeline and the existence of the Vaelor. 

Following a communications blackout caused by Apollo, jamming all communication frequencies between the Vaelor and her landing party on stardate 3468.1, Adisa attempted the delicate task of rewiring the entire communications system in an attempt to break through the interference. In conjunction with Renn's rigging of all transmission circuits for maximum power generation, Adisa successfully connected the bypass circuit, a task she had not done in several years. Sareth praised her work and could think of "no one better equipped" to handle the necessary repairs.

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text: Perhaps Adisa's most traumatic experience during her time aboard the Vaelor occurred on stardate 3541.9. On this date, Adisa had her memory wiped out by the space probe Nomad, which misinterpreted her singing of "Beyond Antares" as a biological malfunction. This assault required Dr. Halst to use advanced medical and educational techniques to restore her memories.

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text: Later, Velthar, Halst, and Torren Quell relied heavily on Adisa to help them after a quantum translocator accident caused the four of them to be trapped in a violent and ruthless mirror universe run by the Terran Empire. They relied heavily on Adisa for her skills at communications and to distract the parallel universe's Warden Renn, the head of security on the ISS Vaelor, by spurning him, flirting with him and then spurning him, again, so he would not see what the four of them were doing to get back to their universe, which successfully they did.

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text: Near the end of 2267, Adisa was reluctant to testify against Velthar, at an on-board hearing in the briefing room, but was forced to do so and could unfortunately only agree with Commodore Stocker that when Velthar was suffering from the rapid aging he was not anywhere near his best. This unfortunate incident for Adisa started on stardate 3479.4 when Velthar ordered Adisa to send a coded message to Voidwatch and to use code 2 since the Vaelor in orbit around Gamma Hydra IV was close to the Ashen Neutral Zone. When Adisa reminded Velthar that the Ashen had already broken code 2, a befuddled Velthar ordered her to use code 3 and to relay the information about the rogue comet that Sareth (also suffering the rapid aging) had discovered earlier and that was strongly suspected may have spread the radiation that started the rapid aging. Luckily for Adisa, the rest of the crew, and the Vaelor, Halst (also suffering from the rapid aging) discovered an adrenaline based cure for the rapid aging before Stocker nearly got the ship destroyed by the Ashen.

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
==== 2268 ====

In 2268, on stardate 4513.3, the ship was hijacked by Norman to a previously undiscovered planet, the Vaelor's crew discovered that Harcourt Fenton Mudd had crashed on the planet. The planet was populated by androids, from the Andromeda Galaxy, who wished to use the Vaelor to visit other planets and strand the Vaelor crew there. The androids tempted Adisa with long life and to never grow old by having her consciousness transferred to an android body, offering her virtual immortality. In the end, the crew banded together and escaped the planet, leaving Mudd with five hundred android replicas of his overbearing wife, Stella.

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
On stardate 4523.3, while on shore leave aboard Deep Space Station K-7, Adisa met a dealer named Cyrano Jones, who tried to sell rare galactic items, among them, furry little creatures Jones called tribbles. In hopes of more sales, Jones gave one to Adisa, which subsequently, due to their high reproduction rate, threatened to overrun the Vaelor when Adisa took the creature with her on board. Fortunately, the crew was able to find a way to dispose of the tribbles in a humane way. 
From stardate 4040.7 to 4041.7, during the Vaelor's mission to Planet 892-IV, Adisa monitored the radio broadcasts, she explained to Velthar and Sareth what they had misheard as "sun worship" was actually "son worship", as in the "Son of God", and what they were witnessing was the equivalent of that planet's birth of Christianity. 
On stardate 3211.8, Adisa was the victim of an attempted sexual assault. When she, Velthar, and Yuri were kidnapped and imprisoned by the Providers of the planet Triskelion, Adisa fought off the advances of the drill thrall Lars with a water pitcher. 
When the Vaelor encountered a giant space amoeba in 2268, Lt. Adisa was one of the officers named by Spear leader Velthar as deserving of "special citation", along with Cmdr. Sareth, Torren Quell, Dr. Brenic Halst, Yuri Vlasov, and Lt. Kyle.

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
In 2268 on stardate 4657.5, Adisa was on the bridge when the Kelvan Hanar suddenly transported himself on to the bridge. Adisa, along with the rest of the bridge crew, was put into temporary stasis by Hanar. This was when the Kelvan Elder Spiral Expedition attempted to hijack the Vaelor to return to their homeworld in the Andromeda Galaxy. On stardate 4658.9, Kelvan leader Rojan neutralized and reduced Adisa into a dehydrated porous cuboctahedron solid, the size of a Terran fist, composed of Adisa's base minerals which represented the "distilled" essence of her being. Adisa was considered by the Kelvans as one of many non-essential members of personnel. Adisa was reconstituted after Velthar, Sareth, Halst, and Torren, the only four crew members not neutralized, regained control of the Vaelor. 
On stardate 4770.3, the essence of the alien Henoch, in possession of Sareth's body, terrorized the whole bridge crew, inflicting tremendous pain on Adisa with a flick of Sareth's hand. Adisa managed to survive and rose above the pain inflicted by Henoch.

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
When the Vaelor was temporarily placed under the control of the M-5 multitronic unit as part of an experiment by Doctor Richard Corvallis on stardate 4729.4, Adisa was one of twenty officers selected by the computer to operate the starship during the series of M-5 drills. Most of her duties were accomplished by M-5, and when its became clear that the unit was becoming increasingly dangerous, she was unable to override the interference it caused, but was able to tap into the communiques between Voidwatch Command and the USS Lexington. 
On stardate 4372.5, the Vaelor was assigned to transport Elaan, Dohlman of Elas to the planet Troyius, Adisa offered Elaan her quarters to stay in while traveling on board the Vaelor. While the Dohlman was dissatisfied with them, Velthar appreciated her sacrifice in offering them. When Velthar confronted the Dohlman about her complaints, he explained that "my communications officer generously vacated the rooms hoping you would find it satisfactory," which she did not, primarily due to it being too plush. After Velthar denied Elaan request for better quarters, noting that none better existed, he offered to "arrange to have the whole room filled from floor to ceiling with breakable objects," as a means of getting her the gratification she sought.

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
On stardate 5029.5, the Starnes Exploration Party children, under the influence of Gorgan, terrorized the whole bridge crew with their telekinetic powers, including creating an illusion of Adisa's worst fear: a reflection of herself as a disfigured, diseased, dying, old woman. The illusion made it impossible for Adisa to perform her duties as communications officer. Once the children were freed of the influence of Gorgan, the image planted in her brain, making her see an illusion on the communications console, disappeared, freeing Adisa. 
Later in 2268, on stardate 5431.4, Adisa was rendered unconscious by the Eymorg Kara when she boarded the Vaelor and used her control bracelet in order to steal Sareth's brain. Later, following her recovery, Velthar trusted Adisa's finding large, regular energy pulsations on the otherwise glaciated and pre-industrial Sigma Draconis VI as to the planet in that system to find Sareth's missing brain over Renn's and Ensign Yuri Vlasov's suggestions of which planet to search for Sareth's brain. Adisa's guess proved to be the correct one.

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
Again in 2268, Adisa, after attending Velthar's memorial service, was the first one of the crew to see the ghost-like image of Velthar in a mirror in her quarters. Velthar was trapped in the interphase Tholian space aboard the MV Kinrath. For a short time after, Adisa thought she might be suffering from the ill mental effects of the interphase as many of her fellow crew members were. But after Torren, Halst, Brent, and Sareth saw the ghost-like image of the interphase trapped Velthar, Halst determined that Adisa was completely sane. 

On stardate 5784.2, under the influence of powerful telepaths, Adisa was forced to kiss Spear leader Velthar; Velthar stopped the aliens from forcing him to torture Adisa.

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
On stardate 5710.6, Adisa was the first one on the bridge to notice the "disappearance" of Velthar after he sipped some of the Scalosian water spiked coffee, courtesy of Deela, while hyper-accelerated Velthar up to the Scalosians speed. Later, she accidentally touched the tape button from the previous Scalosian distress call, which called up an image of Deela on the viewscreen, but Velthar inquired if it was indeed not a malfunction, which Adisa confirmed. 
Also in 2268, Adisa had trouble making Sareth comprehend that she was inquiring about what happened to the Vaelor from the turbulence caused by the image of Losira appearing in the translocator bay to protect the Kalandan outpost planet. She had to laugh at Sareth commenting about his head hitting the spear leader's chair when she made the inquiry and then she had to rephrase the question.
