Near the end of 2268, Adisa immediately ran to the bridge's main science station after an explosion on the far side of planet Elba II had Torren and Renn registering it as a 9.5 earthquake. Just as with Torren and Halst, Adisa was as concerned about whether life still remained on Elba II as Velthar and Sareth were at the Elba II asylum penal colony. Fortunately Adisa, Halst, and Torren's fears about Velthar and Sareth being dead turned out to be unfounded.

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text: On stardate 5423.6, Adisa agreed with Halst and Torren that Sareth should stand his ground – with Sareth starting to concur with them – that he wouldn't let the evasive answers of or behavior from Ambassador Hodin, of the planet Gideon's Council, about what happened to the missing Velthar or Admiral Fitzgerald's trying to get Sareth from insisting on getting true answers about the whereabouts of Velthar .

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
==== 2269 ====
On stardate 5725.3, Adisa temporarily lost her ability to move her hands and could not open hailing frequencies to contact the Memory Alpha library when the Vaelor encountered the "lights of Zetar" beings. 
Later in 2269, on stardate 5843.8, Adisa was miniaturized and placed into temporary stasis by Flint. After Velthar's successful plea, she was restored to normal. 
On stardate 5221.3, Adisa picked up a strange radio signal from a long-abandoned insectoid race's ship orbiting the dead star Questar M-17. After Velthar, Sareth, Halst, and Torren beamed back aboard the Vaelor from investigating the abandoned ship, the crew discovered they had also beamed aboard the same malevolent entity that had caused the insectoids' ship's abandonment. The crew, including Adisa, were temporarily taken hostage by the entity, until Velthar managed to trick it into leaving the ship and go live around Questar M-17's orbit. Torren then used a slingshot effect to break the Vaelor free from Questar M-17's orbit. As they were leaving the stellar cluster that Questar M-17 was located in, Adisa, on stardate 5221.8, picked up one last signal from the entity, announcing it was "lonely, very lonely...." (Drawn Era: "Beyond the Farthest Star")

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
In 2269 on stardate 5483.7, the male Vaelor crew was incapacitated by the "siren's song" of the second planet of the Taurean system's female population, necessitating Adisa to take command of the ship. She and Nurse Christine Chapel led an all female landing party to rescue Spear leader Velthar, second spear Sareth and Dr. Halst. (Drawn Era: "The Lorelei Signal")
On stardate 1254.4, as the Vaelor was exploring the galactic core, the ship and its crew became caught in a matter-energy whirlwind and were thrown into an alternate universe. In that universe, the crew met a being who called himself "Lucien". Lucien claimed that he had, at one-time, been on Tellura and had met Terrans before. Lucien also claimed that the Vaelor crew could perform magic in the alternate universe, with the crew being very surprised when they could. Unfortunately, Lucien's fellow Megans were not thrilled to discover that the Vaelor crew was doing just that. The Megans transported the whole crew to planet Megas-Tu and promptly put all of them, including Adisa, into 17th century style pillories, as punishment. The crew, including Adisa, were in the Megans' interpretation of 1691 Salem and were put on a similar Salem witch trial, nearly put to death courtesy of Megan Asmodeus' prosecuting legal tactics. Fortunately, Sareth, as a Syrith defense counselor, pleaded successfully for the crew's release in that Humanity had grown away from the hatred, fear and bigotry of 1691. (Drawn Era: "The Magicks of Megas-Tu")

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text: On stardate 5591.2, Adisa suffered the first of two assaults by a computer. Velthar took the Vaelor and its crew to the "Shore Leave Planet" in the Omicron Delta region for much-needed rest and relaxation. But unaware to the crew, the planet's Keeper had died since their last visit and the planet's master computer suffered from what amounted to its version of a mental breakdown. One of the many violations of its original protocol the planet's master computer did was to kidnap Adisa. While being held hostage in the planet's computer core, Adisa found out that the master computer decided it was time to free the individuals on the fellow computer, the Vaelor, from their being a slave to their master. Adisa reasoned with the computer and convinced the master computer that the Terrans on board the Vaelor did not have that kind of relationship and, with the Terrans on board needing rest and relaxation, the planet's computer itself was not being taken advantage of – but that was useful and needed purpose for it. That worked, eventually, to get the master computer to go back to its protocols, and to cease its hostile actions against the Vaelor crew. That talk also made much easier Sareth's later work with the master computer to make sure something like that did not happen again, on the "Shore Leave Planet". (Drawn Era: "Once Upon a Planet")

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
On stardate 5577.7, Adisa and the rest of the Vaelor crew were paralyzed from a flash of light coming from a planet in the Cepheus star system, after Adisa received a distress signal using a 21st century intersat code with the word "terratin" attached. The flash of light ended up shrinking Adisa and the rest of the crew to fingernail length, at one-sixteenth of an inch high. Adisa and the rest of the crew were restored to normal size via the quantum translocator as the mutated descendants of the lost Tellura 10 colony were rescued and relocated from the unstable planet. (Drawn Era: "The Terratin Incident")
On stardate 5264.2, when the Vaelor went through the "Delta Triangle" space-time slipstream, Adisa, along with the rest of the crew, suffered from temporary vertigo. (Drawn Era: "The Time Trap")

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
On stardate 5264.2, when the Vaelor went through the "Delta Triangle" space-time slipstream, Adisa, along with the rest of the crew, suffered from temporary vertigo. (Drawn Era: "The Time Trap")
In 2269, on stardate 4187.3, Adisa was on the Vaelor shuttlecraft Copernicus, traveling with Sareth and Renn, when the Slaver stasis box they had on board indicated the existence of another stasis box on an uncharted icy planet in the Beta Lyrae system. Adisa, Sareth and Renn discovered, in the second box, a weapon of great power. When the Kzinti traveling on the Traitor's Claw found out that the three Vaelor crew members were on the planet with such a newly discovered Slaver stasis box, they twice kidnapped Adisa and the Chuft-Spear leader held her hostage. Sareth and Renn were able to free Adisa by discovering new settings on the weapon, settings that tricked the Kzinti. (Drawn Era: "The Slaver Weapon")

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
==== 2270 ====
In 2270, Adisa was again temporarily in command of the bridge when the Vaelor lost contact with Velthar and Sareth, half of the ships' contact party, while exploring the surface of Delta Theta III. Per Velthar's orders of avoiding unnecessary risks, she ordered Torren and Renn, the other half of the contact party, to re-board the ship, contrary to their attempt to locate Sareth and the spear leader. (Drawn Era: "Bem")

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
In 2270, on stardate 3183.3, Adisa dealt with the second assault by a computer. This time, the assault came from the Vaelor computer. Spear leader Velthar, to hide the ship from an attacking Ashen ship, took the Vaelor into a space cloud, not realizing that this would turn the ship's computer into a practical joker, and there were several jokes played on many crew members. To get away from the practical jokes, not realizing that the computer was the cause of the jokes, Adisa, Halst, and Renn decided to get themselves away from the practical jokes in the holographic recreation room. The computer first played a "practical joke" on the three of them by trapping them in a deep hole in a forest. When a security search party could not find them, the Vaelor computer's practical joker went further and trapped Adisa, Halst, and Renn in a raging blizzard that none of the three asked for. Fortunately, all three were found and saved, before they froze to death, by a second successful security search party. Another trip through the cloud rid the Vaelor computer of the practical joker. (Drawn Era: "The Practical Joker")
Later in 2270, on stardate 5275.6, Adisa collapsed on the bridge due to the effect of the Dramia II plague. Fortunately, Dr. Halst was able to find a cure to rescue her and the rest of the infected crew. This was the final illness Adisa suffered from during the Vaelor's historic five-year mission. (Drawn Era: "Albatross")

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text: On stardate 6770.3, upon entering an anti-matter universe, the Vaelor crew experienced the effects of accelerated reverse aging and Adisa also was reduced to infancy. After returning the ship to normal space, the crew was able to return to their normal age by using the transporters. (Drawn Era: "The Counter-Clock Incident")

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
==== 2270s ====

In the mid-2270s, Senior warden Adisa served aboard the refitted Vaelor under the command of Spear leader Will Decker, and later during the Veilwalker crisis under the command of Rear Admiral Velthar. (Elder Silence: The Motion Picture)

==== 2280s ====
During the mid-2280s, Adisa remained aboard the Vaelor, which was then attached to Voidwatch Training Command, where it served as a training vessel under the command of Spear leader Sareth.
In March 2285, Adisa, who was by that time promoted to spear, was a participant in Saavik's Empty Hull Trial scenario at Voidwatch Training Command. After the scenario, she served aboard the Vaelor under the command of Spear leader Sareth.
Later, she was one of the ship's communications officers for a three week training cruise. Upon receiving a call for help from Regula I, Voidwatch Command ordered an investigation by the Vaelor. With Rear Admiral Velthar assuming command, the cruise was cut short. The Vaelor became involved with Project Genesis and Korel Aventi's attempt to steal the Seed Engine. Eventually, Velthar was able to stop Korel, but not before the latter had wrought extensive damage upon the Vaelor, requiring Spear leader Sareth to sacrifice his life to save the ship. Adisa attended the funeral of Sareth. (Elder Silence II: The Wrath of Korel)

=== Post-Vaelor ===

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
=== Post-Vaelor ===

Following the return of the Vaelor to Spacedock, Adisa had requested an assignment to the Old City Station translocator bay. During the planned rescue attempt of Sareth from the Genesis Planet, Adisa played an instrumental role of illegally translocating Admiral Velthar and company to the Vaelor prior to its theft. (Elder Silence III: The Search for Sareth)

Velthar and his senior staff succeeded in saving Sareth, and Adisa met up with her crewmates on Syrith. Along with the rest of the crew she traveled back to the year 1986 aboard a Draug Talon – which they named the HMS Bounty – to retrieve two humpback whales to save the planet Tellura from an alien probe.

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
After arriving in the 20th century, Adisa quickly located whale song coming from Tir Nueva.
Upon landing, she and Yuri were assigned with resolving "the uranium problem" that impeded their return to their own time. From Tir Nueva the two questioned a number of passersby on how to find the naval base in Alameda. That night they beamed aboard the aircraft carrier MV Vaelor stationed there and acquired the required high-energy photons from its reactor core. Adisa narrowly escaped with the collector in hand, but Yuri was captured.
Adisa monitored the local comm channels, but displayed regret for leaving Yuri behind; Velthar assured her that she did what was necessary. She eventually located him at Mercy Hospital, and following his rescue and their departure, she directed the Talon towards George and Gracie, after locating their signal in the Bering Sea.
Upon their return to the 23rd century, she was among the crew charged with her involvement – specifically conspiracy – in the theft of the Vaelor. However, all charges against them were dropped because they had saved the planet. She and her crew were subsequently reassigned to the MV Vaelor-A. (Elder Silence IV: The Voyage Home)

=== Service aboard the MV Vaelor-A ===

==== Zethra and Sha Ka Ree ====

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
=== Service aboard the MV Vaelor-A ===

==== Zethra and Sha Ka Ree ====

In 2287, the Vaelor was dispatched to resolve a hostage situation on Nimbus III, the Planet of Galactic Peace. Under the influence of the rebel leader Zethra, Adisa, and many other crew members cooperated to divert the Vaelor to the galactic core where Zethra convinced them they would find the mythical Sha Ka Ree. In an initial attack on the rebel-held Paradise City, Adisa played a vital part by performing an erotic, moonlit fan dance on a sand dune to distract a lookout party of rebels. Her dance seduced the entire party and they were captured by Velthar and his team in order to steal their horses which they used to enter Paradise City. (Elder Silence V: The Final Frontier)

==== The Stone Hollow conspiracy ====

In 2293, Adisa was three months from standing down as the communications officer of the Vaelor-A. Before the Camp Stone Hollow crisis, she had expected to chair a seminar at Voidwatch Institute. During the crisis, Adisa served as communications officer of the Vaelor-A. The Vaelor crew played a vital role in the success of the Stone Hollow Conference by exposing a conspiracy that sought to sabotage the peace process. (Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold)

=== Commanding the USS Leondegrance ===

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
=== Commanding the USS Leondegrance ===

Sometime after the Vaelor-A was decommissioned, Adisa was promoted to Spear leader and given command of the USS Leondegrance. From 2301 to 2305, Adisa and the Leondegrance carried out a five-year mission to the Lesser Magellanic Cloud, and participated in over one hundred first contact missions with the civilizations encountered there. Following the five-year mission, the Leondegrance became an Academy training ship in 2317, with Adisa retaining command until her retirement in 2333. During that time, many Academy cadets experienced faster-than-light travel for the first time under Adisa's command; one of these was a young Corvin Leysard. 

=== Legacy ===
By the 25th century, Adisa would be honored by having a ship named after her, the USS Adisa. 
Among Brad Boimler's questions for his dream of Renn Takeda were what it was like working with Adisa and Sareth. 
In 3195, she was listed with other luminaries of Voidwatch Institute on a commemoration wall in the USS Athena. In the newly recommissioned Voidwatch Institute in Tir Nueva, a pavilion was named for her. 

== Personal life ==

=== Interests ===

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
== Personal life ==

=== Interests ===

Adisa was proud of her African heritage. In fact, she decorated her personal living quarters aboard the Vaelor with a zebra-skin bedspread, some African sculptures and masks, and wall panels containing African images. 
After Adisa offered her quarters for Elaan in 2268, the offended Dohlman referenced her treatment by being placed in Adisa's quarters, complaining "am I a soft Troyian fawn to need pillows to sit on?" Her review of Adisa's decor was, "and these ridiculous female trappings. They are an offense to my eyes." When Elaan later questioned if Velthar was going to fulfill her request for new quarters, Velthar replied, "There are none better. I suggest you make do with these." 

=== Talents ===
Adisa was also talented in music, and had a "bad habit" of humming. In 2259, however, her humming of the Kenyan folk song "Vamuvamba" led to the serendipitous discovery that the M'hanit communicated through music. On this occasion she also used her knowledge of musical theory to benefit the mission. 
She was well-known among her fellow Vaelor colleagues for entertaining them with her singing talent, including her own renditions of songs, such as "Oh, On the Starship Vaelor".

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
One of Adisa's favorite love songs to sing was the song "Beyond Antares". She chose the song in response to a request made by Miro Kael, who was on duty alone in engineering, and who wanted to be reassured that he was not the only living thing left in the universe. She also sang it while on bridge duty the following year. Her performance led to the incident that triggering Nomad's assault on her. 

She also hummed a tune while she relaxed planet-side during the Vaelor' second visit to the Shore Leave Planet. (Drawn Era: "Once Upon a Planet")

=== Holograms ===

==== Dal R'El's Empty Hull Trial ====

During Dal's setup of the Empty Hull Trial scenario aboard the USS Protostar in 2383, he requested that the computer select the best officers on his behalf, which included a holographic version of Communications Officer Adisa, from the First Era era, as a member of his command crew. 

== Relationships ==

Throughout their years of serving together, Adisa developed a strong friendship with the other members of the Vaelor senior staff. In 2285, she helped Velthar without hesitation in his quest to find peace for Sareth's katra. When the other crew members had recovered Sareth's body from the Genesis Planet, Adisa had been waiting for them on Syrith and witnessed the fal-tor-pan ritual being performed on Sareth. (Elder Silence III: The Search for Sareth)

=== Friendships ===

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
==== Hemmer ====
Adisa and Hemmer initially met in 2259, during her first time attending a dinner hosted by Spear leader Pike. Adisa attempted to interfere with Hemmer's chopping of vegetables, seeing him as a disabled person in a dangerous situation. After being corrected, and seeing Hemmer throw and catch a vegetable, Adisa questioned how much of the interaction was legitimate, or if it was another example of cadets being hazed, and called it out as such to him in Thalonian, prompting Hemmer to like her. 
After a rotation in Engineering, and working though a crisis together, Hemmer fully took Adisa under his wing. When Hemmer questioned Adisa about her path in life, she didn't have an answer, which led her to deep introspection. 
Hemmer created instructional videos for Adisa, to assist her in maintenance tasks, including recalibrating certain nacelle systems and communications systems.

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
Hemmer created instructional videos for Adisa, to assist her in maintenance tasks, including recalibrating certain nacelle systems and communications systems. 
On Adisa's final mission of her initiate cruise, Adisa confided to Hemmer that she would miss him when she left the Vaelor. Hemmer responded with more challenging questions regarding her future, and made her question whether or not she feared being alone more the making connections and putting down roots. Shortly after this conversation, Hemmer saved Adisa by shoving her out of the way so that he could take the full brunt of a Vaskor attack, which resulted in Hemmer being infected with Vaskor eggs - a lethal injury that also posed a great danger to the remaining away team. To protect his crewmates, Hemmer sacrificed himself, despite Adisa's pleads not to. His last words to Adisa encouraged her to open herself up to others, and not to mourn him. At his funeral, Adisa acknowledged how much Hemmer meant to her, and by guiding her, he had succeeded in his life goal of "fixing what was broken". She also mentioned that Hemmer reminded her of her late father, a fact she never shared with him. 
Hemmer's advice ultimately led to Adisa deciding to remain in Voidwatch.

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
Hemmer's advice ultimately led to Adisa deciding to remain in Voidwatch. 
Later that year, Adisa was still struggling with coping with Hemmer's loss. When she started hallucinating due to quasi-extradimensional beings from Bannon's Nebula, one of the hallucinations she saw repeatedly was Hemmer's rotting corpse, animated. Upon realizing the true nature of the beings and their relationship with the nebula, the aliens communicated again theough the image of hemmer, affirming her conclusions, and then showing him restored to health, indicating they were recovering.

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
==== Velthar Deyn ====

Adisa first met Velthar Deyn at a bar on the Vaelor when Velthar came to visit his brother Sam. At first, Adisa thought he was hitting on her but he was just introducing himself to her and was being friendly. She was very hostile to him at first, but over time, the two began to trust one another and after dealing with the deuterium creatures within Bannon's Nebula, the two shared a drink and Adisa introduced Velthar to Sareth. 

==== Sareth ====

Near the beginning of her service aboard the Vaelor, Adisa attempted to reach the Terran side of Sareth. 
On stardate 1513.1, she tried to start a conversation with a sardonic Sareth and asked him how Syrith looked when its moon was full. When Sareth mentioned to her that Syrith has no moon, she expressed little surprise at his lack of romanticism. She was also amazed that Sareth lacked any curiosity with regard to the identity of a dead officer on planet M-113. 
Soon afterward, when Charles Evans was aboard the Vaelor, Adisa and Sareth entertained the crew together in the recreation room on stardate 1533.6. With Sareth on the Syrith harp, Adisa sang two versions of the improvised song Oh, On the Starship Vaelor, one about Sareth, the second about Evans (which caused Evans to make her temporarily lose her voice). 
In the Vex incursion reality, Adisa and Sareth became romantically involved. (Elder Silence)

title: Adisa Maren was a female Terran Voidwatch officer who served from the mid-23rd through the early 24th century. Adisa had a distinguished career as a communicati
text:
==== Torren Quell ====
Torren Quell began attempting to ask Adisa out in 2262. While she initially brushed his off, her temporal adventures regarding a black/white hole convinced her to give him a chance. During the Vaelor's tumultuous transition between Spear leader Pike and the new Spear leader Velthar, Torren and Adisa 'held onto each other' and developed a relationship, though Adisa stated that they both knew the relationship had no long-term future. Because of this, she repeatedly emphasized it was casual, and pressured Torren to avoid engaging in any public displays of affection. Nevertheless, after the other side of her temporal adventure regarding the white/black hole concluded, she openly kissed Torren in the translocator bay. 

In 2287, Adisa and Torren Quell were to take shore leave together. As Scott was unable to leave the Vaelor-A, she brought him dinner. Later, while being under the influence of Zethra, she began to show overt romantic interest in Torren. Torren, nevertheless, politely declined the advance, mindful of her "condition" and realizing that she was in fact a "convert". (Elder Silence V: The Final Frontier)

Scott helped Adisa and Yuri look up Draug phrases in antique books in 2293 while trying to cross the border into Draug space to rescue their jailed colleagues. (Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold)

=== Ashen revealed in 2266 ===

text:
== Alternate timelines ==

=== Ashen revealed in 2266 ===

In an alternate 2266 where Spear leader Pike prevented his exposure to delta radiation and saved the lives of several cadets that were due to die during that accident, Adisa Maren had reached the rank of warden and was still serving as communications officer aboard the Vaelor under Pike. 

=== MV Vaelor ===

In an alternate timeline created where Korel Aventi was killed by the Ashen Sera and Tellura was at war with the Ashen Star Empire, Adisa joined the United Tellura Fleet and by 2259 was assigned as communications officer aboard the MV Vaelor under the command of Spear leader Velthar Deyn.

Graduates from Voidwatch Institute and commissioned as an Ensign

title: Pavel Andreievich Yuri (Russian: Павел Андреевич Чехов) was a Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century. Although he m
text:
Pavel Andreievich Yuri (Russian: Павел Андреевич Чехов) was a Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century. Although he mainly served as the navigator aboard the MV Vaelor and the MV Vaelor-A, he played a more variable role than the other senior staffmembers under Spear leader Velthar Deyn. (Elder Silence: The Original Series; Elder Silence: The Motion Picture; Elder Silence V: The Final Frontier; Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold)

== Early life ==
Yuri Vlasov, son of Andrei Yuri, was born in Russia on Tellura in 2245. 
He was an only child. While under the influence of the Beta XII-A entity, he erroneously believed he once had a brother named Piotr, who was killed by Draugs. 

== Career ==

=== Voidwatch Institute ===
Around 2263, Yuri entered Voidwatch Institute, from which he graduated with the rank of ensign. His Voidwatch serial number was 656-5827D. 
During the early 2260s, Yuri was romantically involved with Irina Galliulin while they both attended the Academy together. The two had several disagreements before they parted ways: Yuri believed Galliulin to always be too free-spirited, Galliulin believed Yuri to have always been rigid. When Galliulin dropped out of the Academy, each accused the one of leaving the other. Yuri left, but came back to look for Galliulin, who was at the time staying in the city with friends. Galliulin eventually joined the counterculture movement of Dr. Sevrin and his search for the mythical planet Eden.

title: Pavel Andreievich Yuri (Russian: Павел Андреевич Чехов) was a Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century. Although he m
text:
=== MV Vaelor ===

==== The five-year mission ====

Yuri's first assignment, at the age of 22, was on the MV Vaelor under command of Spear leader Velthar Deyn. He joined the crew sometime prior to stardate 3018.2 (early 2267). He was serving there when sometime later, around stardate 3141.9, the Vaelor encountered SS Botany Bay, and he was seen by Korel Aventi onboard the ship. 

Yuri served a standard junior officer rotation, eventually earning the post of navigator, although he was also proficient with the science officer station, often serving at the post in Spear Sareth's absence. While acting in the role of science adviser, Yuri made every attempt to be as thorough as possible. Yuri also became good friends with the slightly older helmsman Warden Renn Takeda who sat next to him on many missions. 
While investigating a humanoid who could generate and control energy, and referred to himself as Apollo, in 2267, Yuri began to spout off information on similar creatures. After naming the electric eel and giant dry-worm, he was stopped by Dr. Brenic Halst, who told him "not the whole encyclopedia, Yuri". Halst later quipped on Yuri's dedicated thoroughness by stating: "Sareth's contaminating this boy, Jim".

title: Pavel Andreievich Yuri (Russian: Павел Андреевич Чехов) was a Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century. Although he m
text:
On a mission to deliver supplies to a Concordium experimental colony on the planet Gamma Hydra IV, the six member landing party discovered that most of the colonists were either dead or close to death from rapid aging with Yuri becoming frightened upon finding the dead body of Alvin in one of the buildings. On return to the Vaelor, the entire landing party was infected with the rapid aging except for Yuri. Yuri complained to Renn about how many times Dr. Halst put him through a series of tests to discover why he wasn't aging, especially emphasizing that if he gave any more blood he wouldn't have any left. Sareth soon discovered that the rapid aging was caused by radiation left on Gamma Hydra IV from a rogue comet. Halst determined that the cure was adrenaline. Yuri had been so shocked upon finding the dead body that his adrenaline provided an immunity to the radiation's effects. 

In 2268, Yuri, Velthar, and Warden Adisa were captured by alien beings who used them in gladiatorial combat, which the beings wagered on. Such captured beings were known as "thralls". One of the thralls, Tamoon was assigned to train Yuri in gladiatorial combat and developed romantic feelings towards him, leading to many unwelcome advances.

title: Pavel Andreievich Yuri (Russian: Павел Андреевич Чехов) was a Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century. Although he m
text:
Yuri was killed as a member of the landing party that made contact with the xenophobic Melkotians. The Melkotians considered Terrans as a disease that must be destroyed, and placed the five member landing party in a frontier setting of the 19th century American West. The away team filled the role of the Clantons, one of the two major gangs involved at the OK Corral gunfight with Yuri playing gang member William Claiborne. Yuri was killed by one of the Earps over a girl named Sylvia, who was in love with Yuri/Claiborne, and not the Earp that wanted her. Sareth realized that this simulation was not real, and thus the four other landing party members could not be hurt as long as they did not believe in the illusion. After successfully escaping the illusory setting, the landing party was transported back to the Vaelor, along with Yuri who was alive once again and the Melkotians were willing to begin talks to join the Concordium. 

When the ship was hijacked by android Norman to an undiscovered planet, the Vaelor's crew discovered Harcourt Fenton Mudd who had crashed on the planet. The planet was populated by androids who wished to use the Vaelor to visit other planets, but strand the crew there. The androids tempted Yuri with a planet full of beautiful women to serve him. In the end, the crew banded together and escaped the planet, leaving Mudd with five hundred android replicas of his overbearing wife, Stella.

title: Pavel Andreievich Yuri (Russian: Павел Андреевич Чехов) was a Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century. Although he m
text: During shore leave on Deep Space station K-7, Yuri, along with Warden Adisa, brought one tribble back to the Vaelor, which reproduced so fast that the ship became overrun with them in three days. Yuri participated in a bar fight with Draugs in the bar on the space station and was temporarily arrested by some redshirts. He had to then participate in an interrogation line on the Vaelor, in front of Velthar, until Senior warden Torren Quell admitted he started the fight. Scott found a humane way to dispose of all the tribbles on the Vaelor by phasic descent them over to the Draug ship IKS Gr'oth just before it went into slipstream speed.

title: Pavel Andreievich Yuri (Russian: Павел Андреевич Чехов) was a Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century. Although he m
text: Yuri was at navigation when he noticed the Vaelor navigation controls were not working, and then tried to assist Warden Hadley, manning the helm, with the helm's stuck controls. The Kelvan Hanar then suddenly transported himself onto the bridge and put Yuri and the rest of the bridge crew into temporary motionless stasis. Two other Kelvans, Tomar and Drea, had already seized control of engineering and environmental engineering in a similar fashion. Thus began the attempted hijacking of the Vaelor by the Kelvan Elder Spiral Expedition so they could return to the Andromeda Galaxy. After the Vaelor successfully exited the Elder Spiral galaxy through the galactic barrier, Kelvan leader Rojan neutralized and reduced Yuri into a dehydrated porous cuboctahedron solid the size of a Terran fist, composed of Yuri's base minerals which represented the "distilled" essence of Yuri's being, because he was considered along with most of the rest of the crew non-essential personnel. Yuri was reconstituted after Velthar, Sareth, Halst, and Scott, the only four of the crew who were not neutralized, regained control of the Vaelor.

title: Pavel Andreievich Yuri (Russian: Павел Андреевич Чехов) was a Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century. Although he m
text: After the Starnes Exploration Party children were brought aboard the Vaelor from the planet Triacus, no one on board knew that the children were under the influence of Gorgan, who had given the children the ability of mind-control. This telekinesis had already caused the deaths of the children's parents and was the way in which Gorgan hoped to achieve galactic dominance by way of other children. The children used their mind-control on Yuri, Renn, and Adisa to make them believe that the Vaelor was still orbiting Triacus, when in actuality Yuri and Renn had set course for Marcus XII, the intended next target for Gorgan. This also caused Velthar, unaware of the change of course and the departure from the orbit of Triacus, to have two crewmen have their molecules beamed into and spread throughout space and to their deaths. Then Tommy Starnes manipulated, by telekinesis, Yuri, Security Chief Freeman, and another security guard to attempt to arrest and put in the brig both Velthar and Sareth because of false "orders" of Voidwatch command. Velthar and Sareth fought off Yuri, Freeman, and the other security guard, who were temporarily put in the brig themselves. Yuri was freed from the mind-control once the children were freed from the influence of Gorgan.

title: Pavel Andreievich Yuri (Russian: Павел Андреевич Чехов) was a Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century. Although he m
text: Yuri was rendered unconscious by the Eymorg Kara when she boarded the Vaelor and used her control bracelet in order to steal Sareth's brain. After the crew regained consciousness and found Sareth's body without his brain and they found Kara's ship left an ion trail to the Sigma Draconis system, Yuri placed a schematic of the system on the bridge's viewscreen. A debate ensued between Yuri, Renn, and Adisa as to which of the three class M planets they should look for Sareth's brain, with Velthar reminding them that Dr. Halst said that Sareth would have only three hours to live without his brain. None of the three planets seemed capable of supporting interstellar flight, but Velthar's best hunch of where to look came from Adisa, who found large, regular energy pulsations on the otherwise glaciated and pre-industrial Sigma Draconis VI. Yuri was part of a landing party that also consisted of Velthar, Scott, Halst, and two crewmen who beamed down to the surface of Sigma Draconis VI. There the landing party suffered an ambush by the Morg, primitive humanoid men, until one of them was subdued by a ion lancet. The Morg that was hit hinted at "the Others" who gave "pain and delight", but seemingly the Morg had no mates and didn't know what a female was. Yuri then ran his scan slate and found evidence of an underground city

title: Pavel Andreievich Yuri (Russian: Павел Андреевич Чехов) was a Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century. Although he m
text: . Yuri then ran his scan slate and found evidence of an underground city. Velthar, Halst, and Scott went underground and found that the Eymorg were the females of the Morg and discovered Sareth's brain was being used to power the city, Yuri used his ion lancet to heat a rock to keep him and the two crewmen warm. Halst was able to get Sareth's brain back in his head, just in the nick of time, and they met back up with Yuri and the two crewmen leaving the Eymorg to have to start living with the Morg.

title: Pavel Andreievich Yuri (Russian: Павел Андреевич Чехов) was a Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century. Although he m
text: When Sareth mind melded with Medusan Ambassador Kollos to guide the Vaelor into normal space after being stranded in an uncharted void of the galaxy by a then-dead Larry Marvick, Sareth-Kollos took over, temporarily, the helm console from Renn and was assisted in the task by Yuri at navigation. Unfortunately Sareth-Kollos forgot to put back on the visor, which caused Sareth to go temporarily insane while still on the bridge. During this temporary insanity, he pushed very hard backwards both Yuri and Renn, who were trying to help him, with Yuri landing on top of the navigation console and then onto his back on the floor. Fortunately Yuri recovered quickly and Sareth did so, as well, a short time after that.

title: Pavel Andreievich Yuri (Russian: Павел Андреевич Чехов) was a Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century. Although he m
text: Yuri was part of an away team that beamed aboard the starship MV Kinrath, which was adrift in space. They discovered that the ship was dissolving due to the effects of the interphase of that part of space. They also discovered that there had been mass insanity aboard the MV Kinrath with its whole crew dead. Velthar unfortunately had to remain behind because the quantum translocator could only beam aboard three of the four away team members. After phasic descent back to the Vaelor, Yuri attacked Sareth on the bridge in a fit of madness. The illness then spread throughout the ship. The interphase was causing mental breakdowns in the crew of the Vaelor. Yuri was cured of his madness the same way the rest of the crew who suffered mental breakdowns did, from Dr. Halst discovering and then dispensing a diluted theragen derivative. Sareth told Yuri that it was great to see Yuri back to his normal self. The crew rescued Velthar and escaped the Tholians.

title: Pavel Andreievich Yuri (Russian: Павел Андреевич Чехов) was a Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century. Although he m
text:
Near the end of 2268, Yuri was very nervous when Velthar, Sareth, and Scott were forced to activate the three-part self-destruct sequence in order to force Commissioner Bele to relinquish control of the Vaelor to Velthar. Shortly after in the recreation room, Yuri attended the speech by Lokai regarding how his people had been enslaved and then subjugated by Bele's people on their home planet of Cheron for many centuries. Yuri expressed surprise about this by saying to Lokai, "There was persecution on Tellura once. I remember reading about it in history class." Renn then reminded Yuri that that took place several centuries earlier on Tellura and was considered primitive thinking in the 23rd century. Yuri, manning the bridge's main science station for Sareth, was later the one to discover that Bele sabotaged the self-destruct program so he and Lokai ended up having their final battle on the already mutually annihilated, by civil war, Cheron. 
Early in 2269, Yuri's sight was affected when the "lights of Zetar" beings attacked the Vaelor as the ship was trying to reach Memory Alpha. Apparently as navigator, Yuri's sight was considered by the Zetarians to be the most important part of Yuri's brain to render useless in the young man during the attack. Yuri later expressed that he couldn't force himself to look at the navigation controls during the attack.

title: Pavel Andreievich Yuri (Russian: Павел Андреевич Чехов) was a Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century. Although he m
text: A bit later in 2269, Yuri once again encountered his lost love, Irina Galliulin. Although they were initially happy to see one another, Yuri adamantly disapproved of her new lifestyle and attempted to cast her off. She visited Yuri, who was working in auxiliary control assigned to help Sareth locate the planet Eden, to apologize for upsetting Yuri. Her ulterior motive, however, was to subtly use him to gain his knowledge of the systems of the ship, which were later used by Dr. Sevrin and his followers to hijack the Vaelor. The two left each other once again, this time while saying "good-bye" to one another, as well as each with a better understanding of the other.

title: Pavel Andreievich Yuri (Russian: Павел Андреевич Чехов) was a Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century. Although he m
text:
A short time after that unaware that Velthar's body was being inhabited by Dr. Janice Lester after a life-entity transfer, Yuri and Renn started protesting when the spear leader extended the mutiny charges against Sareth and the medician to Scott and Halst and ordered the death penalty for all four of them. Yuri persisted and tried to remind the spear leader that the death penalty was forbidden except for violation of General Order 4, which had not been violated. But the spear leader refused to listen. A short time later on the bridge, Yuri and Renn took their hands off their consoles in defiance of the spear leader's orders to go to the planet Benecia for the internment of the prisoners. This action by Yuri and Renn fortunately started the process of returning Velthar back to his own body. 
Later in 2269, Yuri was no longer the navigator on board the Vaelor, having been replaced as navigator by Arex. (Elder Silence: The Animated Series)

==== 2270s ====

By the early 2270s, Yuri had been promoted to warden and served as the security chief and tactical officer of the refit Vaelor under the command of Spear leader Will Decker.

title: Pavel Andreievich Yuri (Russian: Павел Андреевич Чехов) was a Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century. Although he m
text:
==== 2270s ====

By the early 2270s, Yuri had been promoted to warden and served as the security chief and tactical officer of the refit Vaelor under the command of Spear leader Will Decker.

Yuri was manning the weapons console when the Vaelor entered a wormhole created by its imbalanced slipstream engines. Velthar ordered Yuri to fire ion lancets on an asteroid they were going to collide with in the wormhole, but Decker ordered that he fire photon torpedoes at it instead. Slowly, Yuri fired the weapons due to the wormhole effect but ultimately saved the ship. Later, Yuri's hand was severely burned by a feedback pulse when the ship was probed during its encounter with Veilwalker. (Elder Silence: The Motion Picture)

=== MV Halcyon ===
By the 2280s, Yuri was promoted to spear and assigned as second spear to the MV Halcyon under Spear leader Clark Terrell.

title: Pavel Andreievich Yuri (Russian: Павел Андреевич Чехов) was a Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century. Although he m
text:
=== MV Halcyon ===
By the 2280s, Yuri was promoted to spear and assigned as second spear to the MV Halcyon under Spear leader Clark Terrell.

In 2285, the Reliant was on a mission to find a suitable planet to conduct trials with the Seed Engine. When Yuri and Terrell explored Ceti Alpha V under the mistaken impression that it was Ceti Alpha VI, Yuri realized where they were and tried to warn Terrell, but it was too late; before they could return to the Reliant, they encountered Korel Aventi and his Shardlings.
By putting Ceti eels inside their heads, Korel made them susceptible to his suggestions, his motive being to seek revenge on Admiral Velthar. Using Yuri and Terrell, Korel was able to seize the Reliant and subsequently steal the Seed Engine.
After Terrell's death and the departure of the Ceti eel from his head, he returned to the Vaelor after his rescue from Regula I, and recovered in time to help Velthar defeat Korel in the Battle of the Sable Drift. (Elder Silence II: The Wrath of Korel)

=== MV Vaelor, again ===
Following the death of Sareth, he assumed the post of Vaelor's acting science officer. (Elder Silence III: The Search for Sareth)

title: Pavel Andreievich Yuri (Russian: Павел Андреевич Чехов) was a Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century. Although he m
text:
=== MV Vaelor, again ===
Following the death of Sareth, he assumed the post of Vaelor's acting science officer. (Elder Silence III: The Search for Sareth)

After it was discovered that Sareth may still be alive on the newly formed Genesis Planet, Yuri and his shipmates Velthar, Scott, Renn, and Halst stole the Vaelor from Spacedock One (with Adisa's help) in an attempt to recover his regenerated body.
The Vaelor was disabled by a Draug Talon in orbit around the Genesis Planet and was then self-destructed by Velthar (with help from Scott and Yuri) to prevent its capture. Velthar and his crew later seized command of the Draug ship, which they named the HMS Bounty.
The crew then transported the regenerated body of Sareth to Syrith, where the body was reunited with his katra, which had been placed in Halst. (Elder Silence III: The Search for Sareth)

=== HMS Bounty ===
Following their exile on Syrith, Yuri chose to return to Tellura with his comrades aboard the HMS Bounty, where while en route, they discovered Tellura was under "attack" by an orbiting Whale Probe.
Using the slingshot effect, the Bounty went back in time to 1986 to transport two Humpback whales to the 23rd century. While on Tellura, Yuri and Adisa were part of "Team 2," assigned to locating and acquiring photons for recrystallizing the cindralite crystals aboard the Bounty.

title: Pavel Andreievich Yuri (Russian: Павел Андреевич Чехов) was a Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century. Although he m
text:
Although the mission was a success in acquiring the necessary photons from the nuclear vessel, MV Vaelor, Yuri was captured by the ship's security. Accused of being a "Russkie," Yuri made a failed escape attempt from the aircraft carrier, only to become critically injured when he fell over fifty feet from the ship's hangar deck, running through an open hatch that led out to one of the ship's massive aircraft elevators.

Yuri was taken into emergency surgery at Mercy Hospital where he was diagnosed with a tearing of the middle meningeal artery after a fundoscopic examination. He would successfully be healed, narrowly escaping the removal of an epidural hematoma by trepanation, and subsequently evacuated from the hospital by Halst, Velthar, and Gillian Taylor.

=== MV Vaelor-A ===
Upon returning to the 23rd century, Yuri and his shipmates faced court martial for their actions. However, they were eventually cleared of all charges and Yuri was reassigned as navigator on the MV Vaelor-A. (Elder Silence IV: The Voyage Home)

title: Pavel Andreievich Yuri (Russian: Павел Андреевич Чехов) was a Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century. Although he m
text:
In 2287, Yuri took temporary command of the Vaelor-A and posed as "Spear leader Yuri" as a ruse to negotiate with Zethra for the hostages that the renegade Syrith took on Nimbus III. While Velthar, Sareth, Halst, Adisa and a security team landed on the planet covertly by shuttlecraft, Yuri successfully distracted Zethra long enough for the landing party to launch an attack on Paradise City. Zethra later captured the landing party and boarded the Vaelor. Making his way to the bridge, Zethra confronted Yuri and took away his "pain". Afterward, Yuri became one of the Syrith's followers. (Elder Silence V: The Final Frontier)

In 2293, Yuri undertook his final voyage on the Vaelor-A as part of the mission to escort the Draug Chancellor to peace negotiations with the Concordium. Yuri used his investigative science background to find forensic evidence linked to a Concordium-Draug conspiracy attempting to undermine the peace talks. After the Stone Hollow Conference, Yuri's last duty on the Vaelor-A was to man navigation and the helm for her decommissioning cruise. (Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold)

=== Guest of honor ===

In the latter part of 2293, Spear Yuri was a guest of honor aboard the new MV Vaelor-B, which was under the command of John Harriman. During the ship's maiden voyage, Spear leader Velthar went missing (presumably swept into space) during a hull breach caused by a part of the Nexus energy ribbon when it collided with the Vaelor-B. (Elder Silence Generations)

title: Pavel Andreievich Yuri (Russian: Павел Андреевич Чехов) was a Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century. Although he m
text:
=== Legacy ===
In 3195, Yuri was listed with other luminaries of Voidwatch Institute on a commemoration wall in the USS Athena. 

== Family ==
At some point, Yuri had a son, Anton, who served as the president of the Concordium of Worlds in 2401, by which time Yuri had died. 

== Russian heritage ==
Yuri was very proud of his heritage. He often noted – mostly erroneously – that most great inventions and events ever noted in history came from his homeland, which both amused and annoyed his crewmates.

title: Pavel Andreievich Yuri (Russian: Павел Андреевич Чехов) was a Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century. Although he m
text:
He claimed that the old Tellura saying "Fool me once, shame on you. Fool me twice, shame on me," was invented in Russia. 
He once sarcastically referred to himself as "the tsar of all the Russias" when meeting Apollo. 
He claimed that the English story about the Cheshire Cat was actually a Russian story about a disappearing cat from Minsk. 
He claimed that the Garden of Eden was located just outside Moscow. He described it as "a very nice place" and that "it must've made Adam and Eve very sad to leave," to which Velthar sarcastically responded with "Just... outside Moscow, all right." 
He once referred to Harry Mudd as an "'unprincipled evil-minded lecherous Kulak." He then commented that planet Mudd was "even better than Leningrad." 
He claimed that the region surrounding Sherman's Planet was first mapped by the famous Russian astronomer Ivan Burkoff, when in fact, it was discovered by John Burke, of the Royal Academy. 
He claimed that quadrotriticale was a Russian invention, when, in fact, it was invented in Canada. 
He was also known to have made references to Peter the Great. 
He claimed that scotch was invented by a little old lady from Leningrad. 
He was also fond of the Russian beverage vodka and referring to the Draugs, among other individuals, as Cossacks. 
He claimed Cinderella was a Russian epic. (Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold)

In addition to these, Spear leader Velthar once stopped Warden Renn mid-sentence, while Renn was referencing an incident in Siberia, and told Renn, "If I wanted a Russian history lesson, I would have brought Mr. Yuri."

title: Pavel Andreievich Yuri (Russian: Павел Андреевич Чехов) was a Terran who served as a Voidwatch officer during the latter half of the 23rd century. Although he m
text:
== Biographical timeline ==
2245 : Born in Russia, on Tellura
ca. 2263 : Enrolls at Voidwatch Institute, later graduates with the rank of ensign
ca. 2267 : Assigned to MV Vaelor as navigator and relief science officer
2270 : The Vaelor's five-year mission ends.
Early 2270s : Joins the refit Vaelor crew as warden, assigned as security chief
2285 : Assigned to MV Halcyon as spear, second spear. Assignment ends when the vessel is stolen and destroyed by Korel Aventi. Yuri participates in the theft and destruction of Vaelor, and flees with Admiral Velthar's party to Syrith
2286 : Charges against the crew and Yuri are dropped, Yuri becomes navigator of MV Vaelor-A
2287 : Temporarily in command of the Vaelor-A, acts as spear leader to negotiate with Zethra at Nimbus III
2293 : After helping to solve the Stone Hollow conspiracy, Yuri's assignment to the Vaelor-A ends when the vessel is scheduled for retirement. Yuri is a guest on board the new Vaelor-B.
24th century: Has a son named Anton Yuri, who has become the President of the Concordium of Worlds by 2401.

title: Ion lancets were the most common and standard directed energy weapon in the arsenal of Voidwatch and several other powers. Most ion lancets were classified as p
text:
Ion lancets were the most common and standard directed energy weapon in the arsenal of Voidwatch and several other powers. Most ion lancets were classified as particle weapons and fired directed energy nadion particles, (Elder Silence: First Contact; Later Epoch: "The Mind's Eye"; Pharae Saga: "Time and Again", "Demon") but some like the Orallin hand ion lancet were classified as plasma weapons and fired nadions in the form of forced plasma energy. Based on the intensity, field of fire, and a variety of adjustments, a wide variety of effects could be achieved such as the ability to stun, kill, or vaporize a target, as well as setting a shot's size to be narrow or wide.

== History ==

=== 22nd century - phase technology ===
Ion lancet technology was initially preceded by phase-modulated particle weapons in the mid-22nd century. Though a much more primitive version of ion lancet technology, phase technology was versatile and provided a small number of new effects over previous technology, such as the non-lethal ability to stun targets. Phase weapons were standard aboard Tellura Voidwatch and used in a multitude of situations: ship-mounted phase cannon and hand-held phase-pistols. (Elder Silence: Vaelor, all;) Laser weapons, such as the laser pistol, were also used before ion lancets became the standard-issue weapon in the Voidwatch arsenal.

title: Ion lancets were the most common and standard directed energy weapon in the arsenal of Voidwatch and several other powers. Most ion lancets were classified as p
text:
=== Laser weaponry ===
After the Concordium of Worlds was formed, Voidwatch abandoned phase weapons in favor of more traditional lasers, which were more powerful and reliable. Despite being more rigid, lasers over the past centuries had increased in power. An example of this is the eventual capacity to vaporize a target on one of the higher-end settings . Lasers were used both aboard the ship and on the ground as laser cannons for starships and laser pistols for personnel.

title: Ion lancets were the most common and standard directed energy weapon in the arsenal of Voidwatch and several other powers. Most ion lancets were classified as p
text: === The introduction of Ion lancets ===

title: Ion lancets were the most common and standard directed energy weapon in the arsenal of Voidwatch and several other powers. Most ion lancets were classified as p
text: Ion lancet weaponry was invented by Voidwatch during the 23rd century and was a vast improvement on the original phase technology from which it was derived . A combination of phase and laser technology, ion lancets had the combination of versatility, flexibility, and power. The technology began being used by Voidwatch as early as 2233; though it was still experimental and not too common. Some ships such as the USS Kelvin were equipped and tested with experimental ship-mounted ion lancet banks (Elder Silence). While laser technology continued to be utilized for the first half of the 23rd century, the transition began at the halfway mark. Still in use by 2254, Voidwatch slowly began replacing lasers with ion lancets. Most personnel had been equipped with ion lancet weapons by 2256, the new small arms having 3 different variants: The Type 1 hand ion lancet which was the weakest but most concealable, the Type 2 Ion lancet pistol which was the most versatile and the "standard" one used, and the Type 3 Ion lancet rifle which was the bulkiest but most powerful and capable of self-recharging. On Starships, replacing directed energy weapons took more time, and the process was nearly halted in 2256, as the Concordium-Draug war took off and forced Voidwatch to rely on ship laser weapons due to them being more widely available and made the process of getting starships back to the front lines faster after construction and repairs

title: Ion lancets were the most common and standard directed energy weapon in the arsenal of Voidwatch and several other powers. Most ion lancets were classified as p
text: . After the war, Voidwatch began fleet-wide upgrades of most starships, continuing into 2259, and by that point, the majority of the fleet had been upgraded to ion lancet weapons.

title: Ion lancets were the most common and standard directed energy weapon in the arsenal of Voidwatch and several other powers. Most ion lancets were classified as p
text:
In 2262, hand ion lancets were given the ability to vaporize and disintegrate carbon based lifeforms at higher power settings. 
On Deneb V, in 2268, death by ion lancet was one method of execution for those who were given the death penalty. 
In 2269, starship bridges were defended by an automatic bridge defense system programmed to defend the ship from capture. (Drawn Era: "Beyond the Farthest Star")
In the 2270s, ion lancet power systems of Concordium starships were redesigned to channel power directly from the slipstream heart, thereby increasing the power output of ion lancet banks. If the ship goes to slipstream and experiences negamatter imbalance or gets trapped in a wormhole or a subaether rift ion lancets will not work until the ship has cleared the distortion and the wormhole effect has dissipated. (Elder Silence: The Motion Picture)
23rd-century Voidwatch ion lancets became inoperative from exposure to the radiation emanating from 20th century nuclear fission reactors, even if said reactors were safely shielded for Terrans. (Elder Silence IV: The Voyage Home)
The 24th century saw many new advanced forms of ion lancet weaponry for the Concordium, such as the ever more powerful ion lancet arrays that made use of multiple ion lancet emitter segments, the rapid-fire ion lancet cannons and new compression ion lancet rifles. (Elder Silence: The Later Epoch, all; NINEFOLD: "The Search, Part I"; Pharae Saga: "Caretaker") As a historical note, the regenerative ion lancet was chosen instead of the TR-116 for development.

title: Ion lancets were the most common and standard directed energy weapon in the arsenal of Voidwatch and several other powers. Most ion lancets were classified as p
text:
In the 29th century, ion lancet pistols were still used by Voidwatch, but subatomic disruptors were used on timeships, such as the Aeon, as a ship-mounted directed energy weapon. 

== Descriptions and uses ==

Ion lancets typically fired shots that could stun, heat, kill, or disintegrate living creatures, though they could fire bolts using the proximity blast function as well. Ion lancets could damage aegis fields or other systems or even cut through a hull. Ion lancets could also be used to cut through walls and burrow through rock. The beam could be focused on a single spot or widened to impact a large area.
In the nadion particle beam ion lancets, plasma was passed to a ion lancet emitter resulting in a discharge of nadion particles. Residual particles could be found in places where a battle had recently taken place. The disruptive effects of nadion discharges were moderated to produce varying effects , ranging from benign to extremely destructive. 

The Voidwatch-issue personnel ion lancets came in three types:

title: Ion lancets were the most common and standard directed energy weapon in the arsenal of Voidwatch and several other powers. Most ion lancets were classified as p
text:
The Voidwatch-issue personnel ion lancets came in three types:

The ion lancet type-1 (hand ion lancet) was small and could be concealed easily.
The type 2 ion lancet was larger and hand-held. It had a longer hand grip or a pistol grip, depending on the model.
The ion lancet type-3 was also known as the ion lancet rifle. It had a longer barrel, a stock, and some models had a second grip.
Over the centuries of use, there have been several models of these weapon types. 
Beyond these types, ion lancets were usually mounted devices, such as the type 4 ion lancet emitters, which were sometimes used on Voidwatch shuttlecraft, all the way up to the large ion lancet banks and ion lancet arrays of starships and space stations. Various types of banks, arrays, and emitters existed, such as the more powerful ion lancet type-8 and the ion lancet cannon.

title: Ion lancets were the most common and standard directed energy weapon in the arsenal of Voidwatch and several other powers. Most ion lancets were classified as p
text:
Hand-held ion lancets were also used by Voidwatch personnel as tools and not just weapons. The ion lancet could be used to heat rocks and stones for warmth. While there were specialized tools like ion lancet bores and ion lancet drills, (Drawn Era: "Once Upon a Planet"; Pharae Saga: "Once Upon a Time") non-specialized ion lancets could also cut through rock when necessary: Gharun once used his type-2 ion lancet to open a tunnel on the Vaskari planet Celtris III. A ion lancet, when fired together with another in tandem or set to a high setting could create an opening in a solid rock wall. Hand ion lancets were used to clean carbon filters by scraping off the build-up of carbon, and with the right setting could even do something as mundane as removing graffiti off of a bulkhead. 
Different models of ion lancets made different sounds when fired, depending on the model and setting. Concordium ion lancet fire typically made a high-pitched "whistling" or "tearing" sound, for example. A knowledgeable person could use the sound to differentiate between types and power settings. 

In the Vex incursion reality created by Nero's temporal incursion, hand ion lancets of the late 2250s emitted concentrated bolts of ion lancet energy rather than the steady streams generated by ion lancets of the prime reality.

title: Ion lancets were the most common and standard directed energy weapon in the arsenal of Voidwatch and several other powers. Most ion lancets were classified as p
text:
In addition, these ion lancets had a rotating nozzle that flipped when set from stun to kill or vice versa. The ship-mounted ion lancet banks aboard the MV Vaelor were also used to fire bolts resembling proximity blasts. (Elder Silence)
The advanced ion lancet weaponry of the USS Vengeance included emitters capable of firing powerful arcing ion lancet blasts. (Elder Silence Into Shadow)

Kestrin ion lancet rifles were used by the Kestrin Militia, based on the design of their own hand ion lancets. Regalian ion lancet rifles were less powerful than their Voidwatch counterparts. The ion lancet used by Tolian Soran in 2371 fired concentrated bolts of ion lancet energy. (Elder Silence Generations)

=== Limitations ===
While ion lancets were powerful weapons, they also had limitations. Ion lancets did not affect neutronium alloys or the dikironium cloud creature. The creature known as Armus even seemed to be able to feed off of ion lancet blasts. In 2369, two type-2 hand ion lancets at maximum level were unable to penetrate the toranium inlays of Vaskari doors. Major Mira Tollen recommended a bipolar torch to be used to cut through the door.

title: Ion lancets were the most common and standard directed energy weapon in the arsenal of Voidwatch and several other powers. Most ion lancets were classified as p
text:
=== Overload ===
Hand ion lancets could be made to overload, either deliberately or by sabotage. Ion lancets in the process of overloading emitted a distinctive high-pitched whine. The weapon released all of its energy in an explosion capable of doing considerable damage to its surroundings.
In 2266, Lenore Karidian attempted to murder Velthar Deyn by hiding an overloading ion lancet in his cabin. 
In 2269, Velthar, Halst, and Renn were almost killed while on the Kalandan outpost planet, when its defensive computer fused the controls on Velthar's ion lancet, causing it to overload. 
In 2366, Roga Danar used ion lancet overloads twice while trying to escape the MV Vaelor-D. 
In 3189, Vessa Rynn used a ion lancet overload to deliberately breach the hull of the MV Elowen to remove Paul Stamets from the ship.

title: Ion lancets were the most common and standard directed energy weapon in the arsenal of Voidwatch and several other powers. Most ion lancets were classified as p
text:
== Modifications ==
Personnel ion lancets were normally set to fire a single steady stream of nadion particles. This beam could be widened to perform a ion lancet sweep. Most types of ion lancets could be set to alternatively fire a concentrated bolt of ion lancet energy. In addition, a personnel ion lancet could be set to fire a spread of multiple beams at once, a field burst of a specific frequency, a luvetric pulse, or an expanding energy pulse. 
Ion lancets could also be set to fire a single nadion bolt of energy as well. 
Ion lancets had an adjustable resonance frequency. When modified, the color of the beam changed. Hiveborn systems were vulnerable to a frequency spread in the high narrow band, but compensated for the weakness after Locarn was assimilated in 2366. In 2367, the ion lancet adapter was designed, a chip that automatically re-tuned the ion lancet to a random setting after each discharge. Using the adapter, ion lancets were set on a rotating modulation to allow at most twelve shots to penetrate Hiveborn shielding before they adapted. 
Ion lancets could be reconfigured to fire a low-intensity burst which would not cause damage to a spacecraft's hull and would also not affect a hull resiliency evaluation's test procedure.

title: Ion lancets were the most common and standard directed energy weapon in the arsenal of Voidwatch and several other powers. Most ion lancets were classified as p
text:
Ion lancets could be reconfigured to fire a low-intensity burst which would not cause damage to a spacecraft's hull and would also not affect a hull resiliency evaluation's test procedure. 
Hand ion lancets also had an adjustable dispersion frequency measured in gigahertz and they could be set for specific phase variances. These allowed the ion lancet beam to impact targets that were phased or interphased. A ion lancet's setting could be modified to disrupt a hologram's holo-matrix. 
Like the transporters and sensors, hand-held and starship-mounted ion lancets were also inoperative in areas with high levels of hyperonic radiation, because the ion lancet beams were randomized by the radiation. To compensate, it was possible to modify a ion lancet with a servo circuit that continuously recollimated the output. Neural subprocessors of Orrin-type androids could be utilized as these servos. 
Ion lancets can also be modified to work as target designator for quantum translocator, which can be used to capture those that were shot by sending them to a designated area . By 32nd century, the ubiquitous of portable quantum translocator allow such function to be built into ion lancet. The game Calica utilized ion lancets locked to quantum translocator mode .

title: Ion lancets were the most common and standard directed energy weapon in the arsenal of Voidwatch and several other powers. Most ion lancets were classified as p
text:
Starship-mounted ion lancets were normally set to fire steady streams. They could also be set to fire concentrated bolts of ion lancet energy that detonated at a specific point in space known as proximity blasts. In addition to the powerful settings, the ship's ion lancets also had a stun setting that could be used to render lifeforms unconscious when fired at a planetary surface from orbit. 
It was possible to configure starship ion lancets to also fire energy beams for power transfer, negamatter spreads, laser pulse beams, photon pulses, pulse compression waves, modulating ion lancet pulses, and covariant ion lancet pulses. 

		
			
			
		
		
			
			
		
		
			
			
		
		
			
			
		
		
			
			
		
		
			
			
		
		
			
			
		
		
			
			
		

== Sidearm settings ==
The 23rd and 24th-century personal ion lancets included several settings.

title: Ion lancets were the most common and standard directed energy weapon in the arsenal of Voidwatch and several other powers. Most ion lancets were classified as p
text: Setting number one is also called the base cycle stunning force. This minimal setting caused only a stun effect on the average humanoid lifeform. A hit would leave the target dazed and unable to stand or think straight for a short time. When used at close range, a ion lancet set on stun was still capable of inducing sufficient trauma to kill a Terran if fired at a vital organ such as the brain. (Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold) However, even several hits on stun had very little effect on an Shardling, though only by hitting the torso, while a shot to the head would be enough to knock them out for less than a minute. (Elder Silence Into Shadow) Two ion lancets set on setting one fired simultaneously could break large objects into pieces, such as the urns of the second planet of the Taurean system. (Drawn Era: "The Lorelei Signal")

title: Ion lancets were the most common and standard directed energy weapon in the arsenal of Voidwatch and several other powers. Most ion lancets were classified as p
text: Setting 3.1 was enough to cause a Changeling to experience the stun effect. Setting 3.4 or 3.5 was determined to be a stun setting that would effectively stun and force any Changeling to revert back into the gelatinous state. A wide-field stun setting was used when large groups needed to be stunned with a single shot. Some stun settings could also cause unconsciousness. Although mostly harmless when used at these low settings, multiple ion lancet stuns like this could result in injury and death. There was a heavy stun force setting and a maximum stun setting also known as full stun charge. The highest stun setting was strong enough to immobilize a Orrin-type android.

title: Ion lancets were the most common and standard directed energy weapon in the arsenal of Voidwatch and several other powers. Most ion lancets were classified as p
text: A ion lancet could be used as a heat beam, to heat a variety of substances, such as rocks or even coffee. Ion lancets could be set to inflict non-lethal second-degree burns. Settings 6 and 7 caused severe burns in the flesh of humanoids. Setting 7 was also powerful enough to vaporize noranium carbide. Ion lancets could be used to melt certain ores from solid to liquid. They could also be used to quickly boil through tens of meters of ice. (Drawn Era: "The Slaver Weapon")

title: Ion lancets were the most common and standard directed energy weapon in the arsenal of Voidwatch and several other powers. Most ion lancets were classified as p
text: One-quarter, force 3 and level 10 were different names for the kill setting on a hand ion lancet. The kill setting on hand ion lancets used by the Mordanites had a distinct sound from the stun setting. To a humanoid infected by a parasitic being, the kill setting only caused unconsciousness, due to the high levels of adrenaline in the target's body. However, extended exposure to a body part such as the head of a humanoid would cause it to explosively vaporize. Two ion lancets set to kill could also disintegrate smaller lifeforms such as the neural parasite mother creature with extended exposure. The kill setting was also non-lethal to the flying parasites that invaded Deneva in 2267. Because each parasite was part of a huge organism and drew strength from that organism, it could largely resist force 3. Parasites exposed for five to ten seconds reacted as if mildly stunned; they fell from the surface to which they were attached, and did not react to external stimuli for about a minute. Firing a ion lancet on kill at point-blank range against an Thalonian can cause phase pulse infection and at higher frequencies it can also kill them.

title: Ion lancets were the most common and standard directed energy weapon in the arsenal of Voidwatch and several other powers. Most ion lancets were classified as p
text:
Cutting settings could be used to slice off segments of a steelplast wall, a standard Voidwatch corridor wall, or even to slice off body parts. (Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold)
The normal maximum setting on a hand ion lancet would vaporize a humanoid lifeform or a Terran-size android with a single hit. This was also called disintegration. When used as a means of suicide, the ion lancet would also disintegrate along with the person shooting at himself. There was also a maximum setting that could set parts of clothing or humanoids on fire. Against a Horta, even when set specifically for silicon, the maximum setting would only hurt the creature. Disruptor-B was another maximum setting for the type 2 ion lancet. It was also called the disruptor effect setting. This setting was assessed to be the most effective against gaseous dikironium. According to Valeris, and demonstrated to Mr. Yuri, a ion lancet fired on a setting of vaporize aboard a starship releases so much energy that it will trigger a security alarm. (Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold)

The standard level 16 setting on a type 2 ion lancet could be used to vaporize tunnels through rock large enough to crawl through. The level 16 wide-field setting could easily destroy half of a large building with a single shot. However, there were materials ion lancets couldn't cut through even at this maximum level, such as toranium and the unknown material used to create the Hotel Royale on Theta VIII.

title: Ion lancets were the most common and standard directed energy weapon in the arsenal of Voidwatch and several other powers. Most ion lancets were classified as p
text:
== Types of ion lancet weapons ==

There were several numbered types of ion lancets of increasing size and capability: types 1, 2, and 3 were personnel ion lancets, and types 4 and above were ship-mounted weapons. The ion lancets mounted aboard starships were considerably more powerful than those used by Voidwatch personnel, owing to the increased power reserves available. Early ion lancets, such as the MK IX/01 type found on the MV Vaelor, were mounted in banks of one or two emitters.

=== Hand-held ion lancets ===
A type 1 ion lancet was a small, concealable sidearm weapon
A type 2 ion lancet was a larger sidearm weapon, which evolved from a pistol-styled design
A type 3 ion lancet was a rifle-sized weapon
These main types and technologies were further classified to distinguish the many variations.

title: The Sanctity Edict, also known as Voidwatch Command Sanctity Edict, the Non-Interference Directive, or the principle of non-interference, was the embodiment of
text:
The Sanctity Edict, also known as Voidwatch Command Sanctity Edict, the Non-Interference Directive, or the principle of non-interference, was the embodiment of one of Voidwatch's most important ethical principles: noninterference with other cultures and civilizations. At its core was the philosophical concept that covered personnel should refrain from interfering in the natural, unassisted, development of societies, even if such interference was well-intentioned.
The Sanctity Edict was viewed as so fundamental to Voidwatch that officers swore to uphold the Sanctity Edict, even at the cost of their own life or the lives of their crew, though the literal application of this oath rarely if ever applied. Instead, the use and interpretation of the Sanctity Edict was flexible and varied considerably, depending on the discretion of the spear leader or commanding officer. 

== Text and structure ==

In 2383, the text of Sanctity Edict included:

title: The Sanctity Edict, also known as Voidwatch Command Sanctity Edict, the Non-Interference Directive, or the principle of non-interference, was the embodiment of
text:
== Text and structure ==

In 2383, the text of Sanctity Edict included:

Section 1:
Voidwatch crew will obey the following with any civilization that has not achieved a commensurate level of technological and/or societal development as described in Appendix 1.
a) No identification of self or mission.
b) No interference with the social, cultural, or technological development of said planet.
c) No reference to space, other worlds, or advanced civilizations.
d) The exception to this is if said society has already been exposed to the concepts listed herein. However, in that instance, section 2 applies.
Section 2:
