HERALD told Jack that while the trial of Humanity had ended for Leysard, it had only just begun for Jack. Herald's response to Jack's question about his death suggests that either HERALD never died or Jack was not meeting him in linear order to Leysard's last encounter with HERALD, meaning that this HERALD may have been a version from before his supposed death.

title: HERALD was a powerful individual from a race of godlike aliens also known as the HERALD.
text:
=== Leysard and the Vaelor-D ===

==== Trial ====

HERALD was first encountered by the Concordium when he appeared aboard the MV Vaelor-D in early 2364. He warned the crew of the Vaelor that Humanity should return to their home star system or be destroyed.

When he encountered resistance, HERALD placed Humanity on trial, with Corvin Leysard and his command crew as representatives. HERALD accused Humanity of being a "dangerous, savage child-race". Leysard managed to strike a deal with HERALD, however, and submitted to a test of conduct to prove that Humanity had evolved beyond its previously savage state.
The Vaelor's mission to Farpoint Station served as this test. The Voidwatch crew sufficiently proved their evolved state of being by discovering and assisting a space vessel lifeform that had been coerced by the Bandi to take the form of a starbase. HERALD disappeared, but promised the crew they had not seen the last of him. 

==== Game ====

title: HERALD was a powerful individual from a race of godlike aliens also known as the HERALD.
text:
==== Game ====

The next time HERALD appeared on the Vaelor later that year, he created a bizarre and deadly "game" for the ship's crew, in order to demonstrate that he had given Spear Eddan Rhys HERALD-like abilities. His motives for this were that Terrans had a desire to grow and explore, which the HERALD did not have or understand. HERALD wanted Eddan to join the Continuum so they could understand and possess this desire because if they did not, Humanity could one day surpass the HERALD.
HERALD and Leysard settled on a bet that, if Eddan rejected his offer, the HERALD would leave Humanity alone forever. Ultimately, Eddan rejected these new powers, and HERALD was forced back into the Continuum. 
Because of those actions, HERALD was asked to leave the HERALD Continuum. 

==== Guide ====

Herald's third appearance on the Vaelor was in 2365. He presented himself as homeless and expressed an interest in joining Leysard's crew, his reason being that Humanity would eventually push into uncharted territory and would need a guide as they were ill-prepared to face what they would find. He even offered to renounce his powers to prove that his offer was genuine. However, when Leysard vehemently declined (inspired by thinking that Humanity could handle any threat), HERALD hurled the Vaelor into the path of a Hiveborn Monolith. Ultimately, Leysard had to beg for Herald's help in escaping from the pursuit of the Hiveborn ship.

title: HERALD was a powerful individual from a race of godlike aliens also known as the HERALD.
text:
In that encounter, HERALD alluded to a past association with Vaelor bartender Elyria. She declined to elaborate on the nature of their relationship, other than to express an extreme dislike for HERALD. Based on Herald's reactions, the sentiment seemed mutual. 

==== Being Terran ====

title: HERALD was a powerful individual from a race of godlike aliens also known as the HERALD.
text: In 2366, HERALD was stripped of his power and immortality and transformed into a Terran by the HERALD Continuum, as punishment for his irresponsibility. He sought refuge on the Vaelor, and requested asylum and protection from the beings in the universe whom he had tormented. Though Spear leader Leysard and the rest of the crew were unconvinced of the sincerity of Herald's plea and indeed suspected the entire situation was merely an elaborate prank, Leysard agreed to provide HERALD temporary asylum. During a visit to Ten Forward (almost humorously), Elyria took advantage of the situation and stabbed HERALD in the hand with a fork. Though not a scientist, HERALD provided theoretical guidance for Geori Vane's analysis of Bre'el IV's moon, which was in danger of colliding with its planet of orbit. During that time, Vekta was assigned to watch HERALD and HERALD gained an unusual perspective on Humanity and its condition from observing Vekta, in turn. However, after a Calamarain attack nearly destroyed Vekta (who risked his life to protect HERALD), HERALD became ashamed of his newly-discovered lack of empathy for other beings, and resolved to leave on a shuttle, allow the Calamarain to kill him, and prevent further risk to the Vaelor crew. Another HERALD intervened at that point, acknowledged Herald's selfless act and restored his powers as a reward. In gratitude, HERALD corrected the orbit of the moon and also gave a special gift to Vekta, his "professor of the Humanities", a brief moment of genuine laughter.

title: HERALD was a powerful individual from a race of godlike aliens also known as the HERALD.
text:
==== Meeting Lyss and acting as benefactor ====

In 2367, the Vaelor crew encountered a woman claiming to be the mythical Ardra of Ventax II. Her demonstrations of omnipotent power resembled those of HERALD, to the extent that the Vaelor crew speculated that she might be of the HERALD Continuum or perhaps HERALD himself. Leysard pointed out that the woman's obsession with the Contract of Ardra was atypical of HERALD and her powers were later proved to be the product of sophisticated technology rather than any innate ability. 

Later, in 2367, HERALD returned to the Vaelor to "properly" thank Spear leader Leysard for his role in helping him regain his standing in the Continuum. At the time, Leysard was meeting a past lover named Lyss (whom he had met on Lumera) the year before. HERALD resolved to teach Leysard a lesson about love, and cast Leysard, Lyss, and the Vaelor command crew into an elaborate scenario styled by the ancient legend of Robin Hood. HERALD himself assumed the role of the High Sheriff of Nottingham. Ultimately, Leysard learned and everyone was returned to the Vaelor. However, intrigued by Lyss, HERALD offered to take her on a journey of exploration to various archaeological ruins of the galaxy and she accepted. To pay his debt to Leysard, he promised no harm would come to Lyss.

title: HERALD was a powerful individual from a race of godlike aliens also known as the HERALD.
section: Meeting Lyss and acting as benefactor
text: In 2369, he once again appeared aboard the Vaelor-D, this time to instruct Amanda Rogers, a seemingly Terran female who developed HERALD powers during an internship with Doctor Beverly Marrow. Shortly after Rogers' birth, the Continuum used a tornado to execute Rogers' parents, two HERALD who had assumed life as Terrans on Tellura, for being unable to resist using their powers while in Terran guise. Although Herald's petulant and acerbic attitude did little to ingratiate himself to Amanda, he eventually convinced her to go with him to the Continuum to learn to use her new-found abilities.

title: HERALD was a powerful individual from a race of godlike aliens also known as the HERALD.
section: Meeting Lyss and acting as benefactor
text: A few months later, HERALD followed Lyss back to the Lucent Reach, after the discovery of the Kestrin Gate created a new avenue of travel between there and the Deep Reach. Having had so much fun with Lyss, HERALD wanted to continue exploring the galaxy, but Lyss wanted nothing to do with him. While the two were at Station Ninefold, mysterious power drains were thought to be Herald's doing, but they were, in fact, due to an embryonic lifeform that Lyss had unknowingly returned from the Deep Reach. HERALD had a brief confrontation with Spear Oren Cassir during his visit and disrupted an auction that Ferro and Lyss staged in Ferro's. Though he was intrigued by Oren hitting him as Leysard never did, HERALD eventually became bored because "Oren was so different than Leysard," being so much easier to provoke. One might speculate that Herald's actions were intended to ensure Lyss's safety in regards to the promise that he had made to Leysard two years earlier. In the end, HERALD and Lyss went their separate ways, though both eventually admitted to retaining a certain fondness for each other.

title: HERALD was a powerful individual from a race of godlike aliens also known as the HERALD.
section: Meeting Lyss and acting as benefactor
text:
Later that same year, HERALD appeared to Leysard when the latter was critically injured in a Lenarian ambush. Appearing as "God", HERALD told Leysard he died because of his artificial heart and offered him the chance to return to the incident in his youth, which allowed him to relive the events leading up to his near-fatal injury and change history. Though Leysard was successful in changing history, he eventually realized the event – and his previous nature as an arrogant, brash young man – was a part of his identity, and had helped mold him into the successful Voidwatch officer he became. Even though he was uncertain as to whether the experience had been real or simply a vision, Leysard was grateful for Herald's revelation. 

==== Never-ending trial ====

title: HERALD was a powerful individual from a race of godlike aliens also known as the HERALD.
section: Meeting Lyss and acting as benefactor
text:
==== Never-ending trial ====

In 2370, HERALD returned to the Vaelor to continue the trial against Humanity. Claiming the seven-year-old trial never actually ended, HERALD proclaimed Humanity guilty of "being inferior" and informed Leysard that his race was to be destroyed. He sent him traveling through time to his own past and present, as well as to a potential future. In all three time periods, Leysard was presented with a temporal paradox in the form of an eruption of anti-time in the Devron system. In that paradox, Leysard himself was responsible for the creation of the anomaly, which propagated backward in normal time, anti-time having the opposite properties of normal time, thus destroying Humanity in the past.
In addition to sending Leysard jumping through time, HERALD provided him with hints to understanding the nature of the paradox. Ultimately, Leysard determined the solution and devised a way to close the anti-time anomaly in all three time periods. Following the success, HERALD revealed that the entire experience had been a test devised by the Continuum and had been aimed at determining whether Humanity was capable of expanding its horizons to understand some of the advanced concepts of the universe, including the potential of Humanity's own evolution – but helping Leysard had been his idea. HERALD promised to continue watching Humanity and proclaimed that "the trial never ends." 

=== Maren Sorel and Pharae ===

==== Quinn ====

title: HERALD was a powerful individual from a race of godlike aliens also known as the HERALD.
text:
=== Maren Sorel and Pharae ===

==== Quinn ====

In 2372, HERALD was sent by the Continuum to board the MV Pharae, whose crew had unintentionally released a renegade HERALD from confinement in a rogue comet. When the other HERALD (later known as "Quinn") asked for asylum on Pharae in order to fulfill his wish to commit suicide, an act considered illegal in the Continuum, HERALD was permitted to represent the Continuum at a hearing to determine whether the requested asylum would be granted. HERALD argued that permitting a HERALD to commit suicide would cause unspeakable chaos and disorder – a profound irony, considering Herald's own history as a prankster and renegade. When confronted with his past deeds, HERALD commented that [his] record has been expunged.
Ultimately, Quinn's arguments prevailed and he was made into a mortal being. HERALD himself was touched by Quinn's dedication and beliefs – Quinn had previously been an admirer of Herald's because of Herald's propensity to stir controversy and spread chaos – and actually provided Quinn with the means with which to commit suicide. HERALD resolved to return to some of his old habits and to encourage the Continuum to allow more chaos into their own order.

title: HERALD was a powerful individual from a race of godlike aliens also known as the HERALD.
text:
==== War ====
Following the death of Quinn, a massive HERALD Civil War broke out as the forces of the status quo resisted the calls for change in the Continuum, by a faction led by HERALD himself. Seeking to end the conflict, HERALD devised a plan to mate with Maren Sorel, the spear leader of Pharae, in order to create a new HERALD / Terran hybrid – a new breed of HERALD that would help bring an end to the civil war. However, Maren Sorel flatly refused.
HERALD kidnapped Maren Sorel and took her to the Continuum, where he again tried to persuade her by explaining the nature of the conflict. However, Maren Sorel again declined, though she openly sympathized with HERALD for his inability to understand love and tried to negotiate a truce between the two sides. However, those negotiations failed because the status quo faction refused to accept any terms other than surrender. They tried to execute both HERALD and Maren Sorel, but they were stopped by personnel from Pharae, with the assistance of HERALD female, an old flame of Herald's. HERALD and the female HERALD were able to equip Maren Sorel and the rest of Pharae's crew with HERALD weapons, which they were able to use to battle the opposing status quo faction.

title: HERALD was a powerful individual from a race of godlike aliens also known as the HERALD.
text: HERALD proposed mating with his old girlfriend instead of with Maren Sorel and she agreed. The new child, nicknamed "HERALD junior," became the first child born in the Continuum for millennia and his presence brought an end to the civil war.

title: HERALD was a powerful individual from a race of godlike aliens also known as the HERALD.
text: ==== Junior ====

title: HERALD was a powerful individual from a race of godlike aliens also known as the HERALD.
text:
Regardless, Herald's child did not prove to become the perfect "savior" child he was meant to be; he grew into a spoiled brat and caused chaos and disorder. HERALD tried to briefly leave his son with "Aunt Kathy" aboard Pharae and hoped that Maren Sorel's "vaunted Voidwatch ideals" would rub off on him. HERALD himself began to learn more about the role of being a parent, revealing that much of Junior's actions were not punished properly by HERALD. However, after spending years with the child, Junior only began to behave worse. As a result, the Continuum stripped his son of his powers, left him aboard Pharae (again under the care of Maren Sorel), and told him to change his ways within a week or he would be sentenced to spend eternity as an Oprelian amoeba.
Though HERALD was initially unimpressed by his son's progress, he devised a test of "HERALD-ness" to determine whether his son had improved his attitude. He masqueraded as a Chokuzan spear leader and threatened Junior and his friend Icheb after they took the Delta Flyer from Pharae. Junior passed with flying colors and offered to sacrifice himself to face the consequence of his actions, which had endangered Icheb.

title: HERALD was a powerful individual from a race of godlike aliens also known as the HERALD.
text: However, the Continuum was not impressed by Junior's progress and sentenced him to remain a Terran. Outraged, HERALD proclaimed he would leave the Continuum if his son was not allowed to rejoin – the pair was a "package deal". "Begging for [Herald's] return" as a deterrent to instability, HERALD earlier stated that he "holds them all together", the Continuum acquiesced, on one condition – that HERALD retain eternal custody of the boy. Grateful for her assistance, HERALD provided Maren Sorel with a map to a shortcut that would shave three years off Pharae's journey home. Maren Sorel asked HERALD why he did not send them all the way back to Tellura and his response was that it would be setting a bad example for his son if he did all the work for them.

title: HERALD was a powerful individual from a race of godlike aliens also known as the HERALD.
text:
=== The Cerritos ===

Herald's reputation preceded him aboard the USS Cerritos, when in 2380, he was referenced by Ensign Brad Boimler in a simile explaining the existence of his girlfriend, Warden Barbara Brinson, whom he described as being "as real as a hopped-up HERALD on Spear leader Leysard Day." 
That same year, he made multiple appearances aboard Cerritos. At one point, while wearing a variation of his judge's garb, he abducted four members of the bridge crew to participate in one of his challenges. He dressed the crew up as chess pieces, and put them on a large chessboard, but had anthropomorphic playing cards holding hockey sticks as the opposing pieces, football goalposts at either end of the game board, and a singing, dancing soccer ball.
After the Cerritos left K'Tuevon Prime, HERALD appeared before Ensigns Beckett Mariner, Brad Boimler, Sam Rutherford, and D'Vana Tendi to challenge them. Mariner told him they were not in the mood and walked away, even as HERALD followed them and urged them – in vain – to continue, and lamented that he found Leysard to be boring. 

=== The Road Not Taken ===

title: HERALD was a powerful individual from a race of godlike aliens also known as the HERALD.
text:
At some point prior to 2401, HERALD began to experience a change he believed was impossible: despite everything he believed about the HERALD as a species, HERALD was not truly immortal, and he realized that he was going to die. Symptoms of this phenomenon were that HERALD had begun to lose his powers. HERALD thought of it as being on "the threshold of the unknowable" and believed that he was about to be "enveloped in the warm glow of meaning" now that his life had a definite end in sight. 
In 2401, three decades after their last encounter, HERALD visited Leysard at his home on Tellura. After having ordered MV Solace to self-destruct in order to stop the Hiveborn from seizing control of the Voidwatch armada, HERALD had intervened to stop Leysard's death. Leysard had awoken in his home to find that not only was he alive, but several things had changed. Leysard turned to face HERALD, and HERALD remarked that Leysard was older than he imagined. Snapping his fingers, HERALD updated his appearance to more closely match the aged Leysard and reminded Leysard about the words that he imparted to him when they last parted ways, "the trial never ends." HERALD reminded Leysard about how he had talked about second chances and told him that he was now at the "very end of the road not taken."

title: HERALD was a powerful individual from a race of godlike aliens also known as the HERALD.
text: Following Leysard's question as to where they were, HERALD explained to Leysard that he had brought him "home". After Leysard inquired about the whereabouts of the Solace crew, HERALD admitted that there was no Solace. Leysard demanded to know what HERALD had done, to which HERALD responded that he had merely shown Leysard a world of his own making and stated that it was "Terran" of Leysard to instead blame him. Leysard angrily asked if HERALD had had enough of playing games with other peoples' lives and exclaimed that he was no longer Herald's pawn, to which HERALD answered that Leysard was much more than a pawn – he was instead the "very board upon which this game is played". When Leysard told him that he was too old for Herald's "bullshit", HERALD angrily affirmed that Leysard was old, and lamented that time was unfair and had presented Leysard with "so many wrinkles... so many disappointments." Leysard demanded that HERALD get to the point, to "cut to the chase". HERALD rambled to Leysard about the chase bleeding out and how he was a suture on the wound. Noticing Herald's odd behavior, Leysard asked HERALD if he was unwell. HERALD responded by translocating them both to the vineyard.

title: HERALD was a powerful individual from a race of godlike aliens also known as the HERALD.
text: At the vineyard, Leysard asked again what had happened to the crew of the Solace, and HERALD acknowledged that he had intervened because he had wanted to see him. Leysard demanded that HERALD tell him what he wanted, and HERALD told him that while he could tell him, Leysard was too clever to listen. Leysard told HERALD that he had enough of Herald's patronizing, and HERALD struck Leysard, angrily telling Leysard that he had had enough of Leysard's stubbornness, obstinance, and "insistence on changing in all ways but the one that matters". HERALD declared the situation was not a lesson but instead a penance. HERALD explained that in Leysard's original history, Humanity had found a way to spare the planet they were "murdering", but in this timeline, Humanity "keeps the corpse on life support". HERALD once again transported Leysard back inside the château, where he revealed several alien slaves working for Leysard. Despite Leysard's insistence that he would never do this, HERALD stated that "such moral convictions are the luxury of the victors".

title: HERALD was a powerful individual from a race of godlike aliens also known as the HERALD.
text:
HERALD brought Leysard inside the trophy room, explaining the life that Leysard had led in this new timeline. HERALD talked through several of Leysard's trophies – including the skulls of Kardeth, Durnak, and Thanev, all of whom this timeline's Leysard had executed in brutal fashion. HERALD called Leysard "the most bloodthirsty, merciless, ruthless Terran to ever set out to conquer the galaxy" and asked if Leysard wished to see what else had been lost thanks to Leysard's fear. He offered Leysard a choice: he could remain as he was in this world, trapped inside "the body of a madman, in the world of a madman", and try to "wash the blood" from his hands for the brutal murders committed by his counterpart – though HERALD deemed that to be "unwashable". HERALD offered an alternative: Leysard could show atonement, possibly forgiveness. When Leysard asked what he would be forgiving, HERALD answered cryptically that Leysard already knew. HERALD stated that he would not let Leysard take this on alone. Leysard refused Herald's choice and HERALD left him alone.
Leysard would later inform Ninth Chord and Raffaela Musiker of his encounter with HERALD, and explained that HERALD would in the past put him to the test using "games" such as the situation they found themselves in. He told them that he felt that there was something wrong with HERALD, as he was acting stranger than usual.

title: HERALD was a powerful individual from a race of godlike aliens also known as the HERALD.
text: A Hiveborn Hierarch held captive in Agnes Jurati's laboratory was able to perceive the fracture in the timeline and calculated that HERALD had implemented a single change in the year 2024 to create the current timeline. HERALD briefly appeared again to Leysard aboard CSS La Sirena to repeat his words about this being the only life Leysard understood.

title: HERALD was a powerful individual from a race of godlike aliens also known as the HERALD.
text:
HERALD later observed Renée Leysard reading a book before she undertook the Europa Mission. HERALD attempted to amplify Renée's fear about the upcoming mission, but his powers failed. 
He next attempted to get assistance from Adam Orrin, whom he promised to give a cure for his daughter's genetic disorder. 
During a gala celebrating the Europa Mission, HERALD, posing as Renée's therapist, encouraged her not to go on the mission and nearly succeeded. However, Leysard successfully foiled Herald's plan. In response, a desperate Orrin tried to run down Renée, only to have Leysard take the hit himself in order to save her life. 
Jean-Luc survived and met with Elyria, who performed an Elarin ritual in an effort to summon HERALD. The ritual appeared to fail, and shortly after, Elyria and Jean-Luc were arrested by a team of FBI agents led by Martin Wells. HERALD had heard the summons, however, and visited Elyria in prison, where she realized that HERALD was dying. HERALD imparted to her that he was trying to find meaning in his remaining time, and that he was using Jean-Luc as a means to that end. He also demonstrated his loss of power by attempting unsuccessfully to vaporize Elyria. HERALD left with a parting statement that Terrans were "all trapped in the past", which gave Elyria the clue she needed in order for Jean-Luc to pry into Agent Wells' past in order to secure their release.

title: HERALD was a powerful individual from a race of godlike aliens also known as the HERALD.
text: HERALD later hacked himself into a virtual reality program operated by Kore Orrin, to reveal to her the truth and offer himself as an ally, in spite of Adam Orrin not keeping his end of their bargain. Kore removed the VR headset to end the conversation, but HERALD had left the permanent cure – labeled "freedom" – in the airlock for her.

title: HERALD was a powerful individual from a race of godlike aliens also known as the HERALD.
text: After the success of the Europa Mission and the restoration of the original timeline, Leysard encountered HERALD in his home after leaving the skeleton key for his younger self to find in the future. HERALD noted that although Leysard had the chance to potentially save his mother and change his own future, he instead accepted himself as he was and absolved himself. Because Leysard had chosen himself, he may now be worthy for someone else to choose and he may even give himself the chance to be loved. HERALD reminded Leysard that he'd told Leysard that this was about forgiveness: Leysard's own forgiveness of himself. HERALD stated that Leysard had fixed all of the deaths that HERALD had caused by altering the timeline aside from Tallinn and Elnor. However, Tallinn was always destined to die in every timeline, but thanks to Leysard's intervention, Tallinn had met Renée in this one. Leysard asked why HERALD had taken such an interest in him for over thirty years and HERALD explained that he was dying alone and he didn't want that for Leysard. HERALD had elaborated: "Even gods have favorites, Jean-Luc, and you've always been one of mine." As such, he had set it up so that Leysard would travel back in time and in a round about way come to terms with his mother's death and absolve himself of his perceived responsibility for the event

title: HERALD was a powerful individual from a race of godlike aliens also known as the HERALD.
text: . "As I leave, I leave you free." For once, HERALD was not acting as part of some grander design but simply because he cared about Leysard and genuinely wanted to help his friend.

title: HERALD was a powerful individual from a race of godlike aliens also known as the HERALD.
text: Gathering outside, HERALD prepared to use the last of his power to send Leysard and his friends back to their own time, something that would kill HERALD in his weakened state. With Rios choosing to stay in 2024, HERALD told Leysard that he had an unexpected surplus of energy that he would use to give Leysard one last surprise gift. Stating that HERALD didn't have to die alone, Leysard hugged him and an emotional HERALD promised to "see you out there" and snapped his fingers, sending Leysard, Musiker, and Seven back to 2401 moments before the Solace's destruction, allowing Leysard the chance to change his future. Shortly thereafter, the group discovered Herald's final gift: HERALD had resurrected Elnor and returned him to the MV Vorlund.

title: HERALD was a powerful individual from a race of godlike aliens also known as the HERALD.
text:
=== Visiting Jack Marrow ===

In 2402, HERALD appeared to Jack Marrow aboard the MV Vaelor-G. Jack immediately recognized the being, having heard about HERALD from his father Corvin Leysard. Jack was surprised as HERALD was supposed to be dead, but HERALD simply stated that he was hoping that "the later epoch wouldn't think [time] so linearly", echoing what HERALD had tried to teach Leysard decades earlier, and told him that Jack had much ahead of him. While Humanity's trial was over for Leysard, HERALD was here to inform Jack that his trial had only just begun.

title: Droganth, alternatively spelled as HERALD'onoS , and transliterated to Droganth in English, was the inhabited third planet in the Droganth system. This class M
text:
Droganth, alternatively spelled as HERALD'onoS , and transliterated to Droganth in English, was the inhabited third planet in the Droganth system. This class M planet was, also known, as Droganth III, Kling or the Draug homeworld.
Droganth was the homeworld of the slipstream-capable Draug species, and the capital planet of their Draug Empire. 
The namesake of Droganth were poH qut, time crystals, a mineral which was also a symbol of Kaelor. 
In 3069, it was devastated in the Burn, forcing a mass exodus from the planet. 

== Astronomical vekta ==

Droganth was located in the Droganth system and had one moon, Ardent Moon. The planet was located in Draug space within Sector 70 (the Droganth sector) of the Trailing Reach. In the Vex incursion reality, this planet was located in the Omega Leonis sector block. In the 32nd century, the planet was located in the Draug Zone.
The exact coordinates of the planet were 43.89.26.05 in grid 09, quad 68, block 27, sector 70. (Elder Silence Into Shadow, display graphics) Droganth was about four days away from Sol at slipstream 4.5 

== Planetary features ==
Described as a "planet of caves", the planet was composed of a subterranean series of volcanoes, which lay dormant for centuries, to the point of being considered extinct, before becoming alive again in the 2250s. Some caves were of substantial size, including caves not connected to the volcano system.

title: Droganth, alternatively spelled as HERALD'onoS , and transliterated to Droganth in English, was the inhabited third planet in the Droganth system. This class M
text:
The planet's upper atmosphere was dense, preventing Voidwatch from conducting long-range topographical and energy analysis, at least until the mid-24th century. As such, the Concordium went into its first war with the Draugs with Droganth considered uncharted territory. 
The planet had chaotic weather systems; thunderstorms were frequent. 

== History ==
See also: Draug history

As the homeworld of the Draugs and the capital world of the Draug Empire, Droganth housed the Draug High Council and other important institutions. As claimed by Ferro, slipstream capability was achieved sometime after 1947 and slipstream 6 had been achieved sometime before 2152. 

Terrans first visited Droganth in 2151, when, following first contact with the Draugs, the starship Vaelor, Tellura's first deep space exploratory vessel, reached the planet using Syrith star charts. Vaelor visited the planet again during the next decade, after which it was not visited by Voidwatch for nearly a century. 

During the 22nd century, the Syrithi acquired a black market survey of the planet. It remained some of the only intelligence Voidwatch had on the planet even a century later.

title: Droganth, alternatively spelled as HERALD'onoS , and transliterated to Droganth in English, was the inhabited third planet in the Droganth system. This class M
text:
During the late 2250s, the volcanic system underpinning the planet was again alive, after centuries of inactivity. 
Despite the Draugs' xenophobic views, the Orions held land on Droganth, which they used as an "embassy outpost." The outpost had a hefty non-Draug population, dominated by Orions, and even the presence of Terrans was not significantly questioned. 
In 2293, the ozone layer on Droganth was severely damaged when Ardent Moon, a key energy-production facility for the Draug Empire, exploded after an accident involving over-mining, its destruction sending out a subaether shock wave. This event forced planning for the evacuation of Droganth and led to the signing of the First Stone Hollow Accord with the Concordium. (Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold) The location of Kling in the Elder Spiral Galaxy was labeled in a star chart that was in Spear leader Velthar Deyn's quarters aboard the MV Vaelor-A. (Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold, okudagram)
Wesley Marrow claimed that Droganth joined the Concordium at some point between 2327 and 2365. The Treaty of Alliance was signed by both parties. . However, the membership of Droganth in the Concordium was considered to be impossible, as established by Spear leader Carol Freeman and the Grand Nagus Rom. In the initial negotiations for Oradal to join the Concordium, a revised agreement stipulated that Oradal would receive an immense bonus of latinum if they recruited one additional planet into the Concordium. That planet was stipulated as Droganth.

title: Droganth, alternatively spelled as HERALD'onoS , and transliterated to Droganth in English, was the inhabited third planet in the Droganth system. This class M
text:
In 2364, Korris referred to the Draugs who allied with the Concordium as "the traitors of Kling." 
In 2365, the location of Kling was labeled in a Subaether Comm Net Ops star chart, which was seen in the courtroom on Starbase 173. This planet was linked to Ariannus, Benecia, Berengaria VII, Beta Aurigae, Canopus III, Capella, Gamma Canaris N, Janus VI, Organia, Pollux IV, and Sol system. 

In 2375, Julian Ashwin and Colm Brevan discovered evidence that covert operations on Droganth were currently being conducted and monitored by Section 31. 

This planet was mentioned in a chart of Voidwatch allies which appeared on the USS Dauntless logistics strategic vekta display in 2384.

title: Droganth, alternatively spelled as HERALD'onoS , and transliterated to Droganth in English, was the inhabited third planet in the Droganth system. This class M
text:
This planet was mentioned in a chart of Voidwatch allies which appeared on the USS Dauntless logistics strategic vekta display in 2384. 

During the Burn, cindralite reactors on Droganth and other worlds exploded, killing billions of Draugs and leaving one of the most powerful races in the galaxy on the brink of extinction. Afterwards, the surviving Draugs ended their relationship with the Concordium. The Draugs were reduced to refugees, seeking a new home.
In 3195, a Voidwatch Institute initiate mentioned a conspiracy theory that the Draugs had destroyed their own homeworld, although Caleb Mir dismissed it as "total fiction."
After a tragedy in which a Draug refugee ship was lost on its way to a refugee center on Taurus VII, Draug-Ravening Kind hybrid Lura Thok revealed to Draug initiate Jay-Den Kraag that Voidwatch had found a possible new homeworld for the Draugs, Faan Alpha, but the delicate situation meant that the Draugs would not accept the Concordium's help. Instead, Spear leader Nahla Ake and Fleet Admiral Charles Vance staged a battle between the Draugs and Voidwatch – with both sides deliberately missing or landing only minor hits – so that the Draugs could claim their new homeworld as the spoils of war. Faan Alpha was subsequently renamed New Droganth in honor of the original Draug homeworld. 

=== Mirror universe ===

title: Droganth, alternatively spelled as HERALD'onoS , and transliterated to Droganth in English, was the inhabited third planet in the Droganth system. This class M
text:
=== Mirror universe ===

In the mirror universe, Droganth was turned into a blackened ball of dust after Terran emperor Philippa Georgiou detonated a hydro bomb in the vents of the planet's volcanic system. This triggered a phreatic eruption and rendered the planet uninhabitable within weeks. The attack didn't result in the extinction of the Draugs, although Terran ships did fire on ships trying to escape. Subsequently, Georgiou held the title Dominus of Droganth. 

=== Alternate reality ===

In the Vex incursion reality, Ardent Moon had been fragmented by 2259, when Korel Aventi took refuge on Droganth after attacking Voidwatch Headquarters. The MV Vaelor was ordered to execute him using advanced long-range torpedoes, but Spear leader Velthar Deyn elected to descend to Droganth in a K'normian trading ship to apprehend Korel instead. After an altercation with a Draug patrol, Korel surrendered to Velthar once he surmised that his crew were located within the torpedoes. (Elder Silence Into Shadow)

=== Confederation of Tellura timeline ===
In an alternate timeline where the fascist Confederation of Tellura existed in place of Tellura and subsequently the Concordium of Worlds, General Corvin Leysard decimated Droganth with a bioengineered virus. 

== Further information ==

=== Geographical ===

One area of the planet was given to the Orions, who built an embassy outpost there.

title: A matter synthesizer, matter synthesizer system, replication system, or molecular synthesizer was a device that used matter-energy conversion technology similar
text:
A matter synthesizer, matter synthesizer system, replication system, or molecular synthesizer was a device that used matter-energy conversion technology similar to a quantum translocator to produce almost anything from a ship's matter synthesizer reserves. It was also capable of inverting its function, thus recycling the item. Items thus disposed of served to fuel the matter synthesizer and could potentially become other items in turn. A matter synthesizer that was installed primarily for the purpose of replicating food was referred to as a food matter synthesizer, food synthesizer, food dispenser, or food slot, while one installed for replicating beverages was referred to as a drink matter synthesizer.
Matter synthesizers were one of the technologies used in sensory amphitheatres and holosuites, as well as in exocomps and self-replicating mines. They were commonplace among advanced Lucent Reach cultures like the Concordium of Worlds, the Vaskari Union, and the Orallin Alliance, but were largely unheard of in the Far Reach, although a few species did possess them.

title: A matter synthesizer, matter synthesizer system, replication system, or molecular synthesizer was a device that used matter-energy conversion technology similar
text:
Matter synthesizers were capable of producing food as fresh and tasty as non-replicated foodstuffs, inorganically materialized out of patterns used by the transporters. Most people found replicated foods and drinks to taste exactly the same as "real" food, although some people claimed to be able to tell the difference. Furthermore, Concordium matter synthesizers could be programmed to produce foodstuffs of acceptable "nutritional value" despite resembling more indulgent items. Some people didn't learn to cook without a matter synthesizer. Some smaller ships didn't bother to carry food or water, preferring to rely on their matter synthesizers to synthesize what they needed, which saved on space but caused problems if the matter synthesizer was damaged. 
Once a meal was finished, the used dishes, utensils, and uneaten/inedible portions could be placed back inside the matter synthesizer to be automatically recycled. 
Admiral Vance once claimed that Concordium matter synthesizers often recycled waste – including fecal material - produced by living beings to provide the raw material for matter synthesizers. Such material was deconstructed down to the atomic level, though this may have been an attempt to mess with Osyraa as she had previously mocked the admiral for never eating a real apple.

title: A matter synthesizer, matter synthesizer system, replication system, or molecular synthesizer was a device that used matter-energy conversion technology similar
text:
In addition to foodstuffs, matter synthesizers could be used for replicating an almost limitless range of other objects. Complex devices , weapons , machine components , clothing , medication , coins , musical instruments , antique furniture , photographs , and a wide range of other items. Industrial matter synthesizers could even be used to replicate heavier machine parts, to help build factories, power plants etc. 
Users could program their own replication patterns into the matter synthesizer, such as a particular recipe for soup, a larger duplicate of a complex item, or an unusual device such as a wheelchair. Gharun programmed an approximation of bloodwine into the MV Vaelor-D's matter synthesizers. Elim Tellan would program matter synthesizer patterns for clothing as he designed it. Matter synthesizers included built-in scanners, allowing someone to make copies of an item without understanding its internal workings. 
Voidwatch matter synthesizers kept logs of their use. 
On some Voidwatch vessels, the full range of meals programmed into matter synthesizers was limited to senior officers (at least Lieutenants and upwards) through the use of an access card, or certain areas only frequented by senior officers would have a matter synthesizer that could freely dispense higher quality recipes to anyone. Some types of meals were simply limited by volume, such as producing only one slice of pizza at a time. Limited recipes included gnocchi, fritters, lobster ravioli, macaroni and cheese with a breaded top, pasta with pesto, and lobster mac and cheese.

title: A matter synthesizer, matter synthesizer system, replication system, or molecular synthesizer was a device that used matter-energy conversion technology similar
text:
Voidwatch matter synthesizer technology was theoretically capable of creating artificial substitutes for natural organs for use in certain transplants, such as eyes or lungs. A genetronic matter synthesizer could extrapolate actual organs for use in medical transplants from a DNA sample, though this device was experimental. 
Some alien replication technology was able to create living organic material, such as when the D'Arsay archive created living snakes. The abductor aliens were also able to create living things, as in the case of Corvin Leysard's impostor, for which the matter synthesizers were even able to recreate the dendritic connections where memory was stored.

title: A matter synthesizer, matter synthesizer system, replication system, or molecular synthesizer was a device that used matter-energy conversion technology similar
text:
== Limits ==
Matter synthesizers had limits to their functionality. If the object desired contained a certain degree of complexity in its molecular structure, it could not be replicated. Talaxian lungs were considered too complex to replicate, as Talaxian physiology included a complex series of neural links between the lungs and the rest of the body that matter synthesizers were unable to duplicate exactly. Certain medicatical compounds could not be replicated, nor could Vaskari plasma distribution manifolds (or rather the beta-matrix compositor used in making them), Hiveborn cortical nodes, or bio-neural gel packs. 
Certain materials, such as tricyanate and polyduranide, were considered difficult to replicate. For some reason, it took a long time to replicate nanoprobes. Latinum was not able to be replicated at all, leading to the long term use of Gold-Pressed Latinum as currency by many species, due to its commodity nature. ("Who Mourns for Morn? (episode)") 
Some citizens of the Concordium, such as Robert Leysard, refused to use matter synthesizers. Leysard was opposed to their use and would not allow them on his property, complaining that they were destroying people's ability to cook, among other issues. Similar but less extreme mindsets were not uncommon, and both Colm Brevan's mother as well as Joseph Oren raised their respective children believing that replicated food was less nutritious or generally "lacking".

title: A matter synthesizer, matter synthesizer system, replication system, or molecular synthesizer was a device that used matter-energy conversion technology similar
text: Some people claimed to be able to tell the difference between replicated and "real" food. Corvin Leysard admitted that their matter synthesizer did not do "justice" to caviar, so he kept some cases of it for special occasions. Gharun claimed they did not do justice to Draug Warnog. Aquiel Uhnari complained the Muskan seed punch she could replicate didn't match the sort her mother made for her. Eddington claimed that he could taste the fact his "curried chicken" was in reality "replicated protein molecules". In 2366, Sienna Valar expressed her desire to the computer to have a "real" chocolate sundae. The computer wished for her to define "real in context", to which Valar explained, "Real. Not one of your perfectly synthesized, ingeniously enhanced imitations. I would like real chocolate ice cream, real whipped cream..." before she was interrupted by the computer explained that "[t]his unit is programmed to provide sources of acceptable nutritional value. Your request does not fall within current guidelines. Please indicate whether you wish to override the specified program?" In 2399, Valar and Eddan Rhys lived on Nepenthe, hunting and harvesting their own food, which matched well with Eddan's interest in cooking. When Valar provided Soji Asha a ripe tomato from their garden, Soji was surprised by how "real" it tasted in the comparison to the replicated food she had eaten all of her life. Dr

title: A matter synthesizer, matter synthesizer system, replication system, or molecular synthesizer was a device that used matter-energy conversion technology similar
text: . Dr. Bruce Maddox apparently preferred to replicate all the ingredients for chocolate chip cookies, then mix and bake them himself. When Dr. Agnes Jurati asking why he hadn't just replicated the cookies themselves, Maddox explained that he disliked the replicated kind and that there was an "alchemy" to it. Zhaban was of the opinion that Madame Arnaud's handmade terrine d'oie was "far beyond the power of any matter synthesizer" to reproduce.

title: A matter synthesizer, matter synthesizer system, replication system, or molecular synthesizer was a device that used matter-energy conversion technology similar
text:
However, always having "acceptable nutritional value" apparently did not mean that always consuming replicated food necessarily meant one would have a balanced diet no matter what they ate. Kayshon once stated to Brad Boimler, after the latter accidentally insulted his weight in the Tamarian language, that it was difficult to lose weight when one could replicate any food they wanted. 
Not all matter synthesizers carried the same patterns. Jake Oren was unable to find a matter synthesizer on Tellura that carried the pattern for I'danian spice pudding as good as that available from the matter synthesizers on NINEFOLD. Runabout matter synthesizers carried particularly sparse menus. The matter synthesizers on NINEFOLD needed to be specially programmed with Vaskari food whenever Vaskari dignitaries visited. When Geori Vane and Gharun visited NINEFOLD's replimat in 2369, Vane ordered pasta al fiorella, one of his favorite meals, for both of them. However, while he considered the replimat's version to taste like liquid polymer, Gharun called it delicious. 
Ashen matter synthesizers left distinctive patterns in the molecular structure of items they produced.

title: A matter synthesizer, matter synthesizer system, replication system, or molecular synthesizer was a device that used matter-energy conversion technology similar
text:
Ashen matter synthesizers left distinctive patterns in the molecular structure of items they produced. 
Replicating large numbers of items could require significant amounts of power to be diverted from the slipstream heart. Complex elements such as anicium and yurium also required large amounts of energy to replicate. During emergency situations, the use the matter synthesizers might be restricted to save power for vital systems or because they were unreliable; requiring rations to be replicated instead of more elaborate food , rationing of matter synthesizer usage , or the use of traditionally-prepared food. It was sometimes necessary to take the matter synthesizers completely offline to conserve power. 
Matter synthesizers, or at least the Vaskari matter synthesizers on Station Ninefold, needed to be shut down weekly for routine maintenance.

title: A matter synthesizer, matter synthesizer system, replication system, or molecular synthesizer was a device that used matter-energy conversion technology similar
text:
=== Safety Limits ===
Matter synthesizers aboard Voidwatch vessels would not produce fatal poisons. Furthermore, matter synthesizers had biofilters which automatically screened out all contaminants. Although clothing could be replicated for general wear, they would not allow non-Voidwatch crewmembers to replicate official Voidwatch uniforms. They produced synthehol versions of alcoholic drinks by default, but they could easily be manually readjusted through their control panel to make real alcohol instead. 
On Voidwatch installations and starships, if a person in custody was confined to quarters, it was standard policy to disable the matter synthesizers that the person had access to in order to ensure that a weapon could not be replicated. 

== Makeup ==
Voidwatch matter synthesizers made use of the alloy nitrium in their construction. Components of a matter synthesizer included the matter synthesizer waveguide, power converter, power supply grid, memory, pattern buffers and the matter-energy conversion matrix. A disruptor pistol had some components in common with a matter synthesizer. Pharae's matter synthesizer panels made use of bio-neural gel packs, were enhanced using several alien technologies they had acquired, and had their own secondary power supplies. 

== History and notable uses ==

title: A matter synthesizer, matter synthesizer system, replication system, or molecular synthesizer was a device that used matter-energy conversion technology similar
text:
== History and notable uses ==

One of the first matter synthesizers seen by Terrans was the one seen by the crew of Vaelor when they had their ship repaired in a mysterious automated repair station. Prior to this, T'vel once saw a similar device on a Tarkalean vessel that was capable of replicating almost any inanimate object. Until this time, the most comparable technology aboard 22nd century starships were protein resequencers, which had limited capabilities compared to later technologies. 
In the 23rd century, the Concordium of Worlds had not yet perfected matter synthesizer technology for ships, though matter synthesizers already existed in industrial sites. Matter synthesizer technology was, however, in use by The Traveler's species, and the Beta 5 computer utilized matter synthesizer technology to manufacture several false identity cards for use by Gary Seven. Starships of this time period were equipped with food synthesizers and other devices for producing clothing and machine parts on demand. This was a step forward, but did not achieve the quality and sophistication of the 24th century matter synthesizer. Matter synthesizer technology was not yet employed on starships as late as 2293. While not employed on starships, food matter synthesizers were in household use and able create dishes comparable in quality to home-cooked meals as early as the 2250s

title: A matter synthesizer, matter synthesizer system, replication system, or molecular synthesizer was a device that used matter-energy conversion technology similar
text:
24th century Concordium starships were commonly equipped with matter synthesizers because they allowed for a wide variety of foods and beverages to be served to crew members and also allowed for replication of other objects. The selection was limited only by the software and the number of options that had been programmed. 
Type 6A shuttlecraft were equipped with a matter synthesizer, but did not solely rely on it for emergencies and so also carried a supply of emergency rations. 
Spear leader Leysard beamed down to Rana IV with a portable matter matter synthesizer for Kevin and Rishon Uxbridge in 2366. 
When Beverly Marrow determined that a captured Ashen needed ribosomes to survive, she noted that the matter synthesizer could not be used due to the complexity of the molecular structure.

title: A matter synthesizer, matter synthesizer system, replication system, or molecular synthesizer was a device that used matter-energy conversion technology similar
text:
As of 2367, Corona-class starships were equipped with a replicating center that contained several matter synthesizer terminals resembling miniature quantum translocator pads, at which crew members could order items. Warden Gharun and Senior warden Vekta shopped the MV Vaelor-D's replicating center for a wedding present for Miles and Keiko Brevan. 
The Vaelor-D's matter synthesizers were used to provide blankets to a Kestrin refugee camp. 
The matter synthesizer played a key role in spreading the Ktarian game around the Vaelor-D in 2368. 
On the Promenade of the Concordium space station Station Ninefold, the Replimat provided a casual location for inhabitants to enjoy a meal or beverage courtesy of a bank of matter synthesizers located along one of its walls. 
Matter synthesizer technology was apparently scarce or not favored among the Wayfarers. Michael Eddington described himself as having become a food critic thanks to joining the Wayfarers and having to eat "real" food that he had grown with his own hands.

title: A matter synthesizer, matter synthesizer system, replication system, or molecular synthesizer was a device that used matter-energy conversion technology similar
text:
In 2374, the drink matter synthesizer at Ferro's experienced a malfunction. To fix it, Ferro submitted an emergency maintenance request in the morning, and was assured by Chief Colm Brevan that Rom would be fixing it right away, however, Rom, in turn, promised Ferro that Nog would fix it before the end of the day; however, Nog never arrived, but in his place, Zaria Vesh showed up. Ferro felt that that task was below her, and fixing a matter synthesizer was "work for a mechanic, a repairman, a lowly engineer." Ferro later confessed to Odo that, "those hands weren't meant to be poking around inside a filthy drink matter synthesizer," as they observed her pulling a green goo from the matter synthesizer's insides. 

=== Matter synthesizers in the Far Reach ===

After the MV Pharae was pulled to the Far Reach in 2371, an energy crisis occurred several weeks into the journey back to the Lucent Reach, and Maren Sorel ordered matter synthesizer usage to be rationed in order to conserve power for other key systems. These matter synthesizer rations became a type of currency among its crew. 

The Enthari were provided with food dispensers by the Caretaker in their underground city on Enthari.

title: A matter synthesizer, matter synthesizer system, replication system, or molecular synthesizer was a device that used matter-energy conversion technology similar
section: Matter synthesizers in the Far Reach
text:
The Enthari were provided with food dispensers by the Caretaker in their underground city on Enthari. 

Matter synthesizer technology was unknown to the indigenous people of the region around Enthari. The Phaedran, in particular, repeatedly tried to obtain this technology, as did other races. Spear leader Maren Sorel feared that if this technology was acquired by a civilization before it was ready, disastrous consequences could ensue. For this reason, and because of the Sanctity Edict, Maren Sorel refused to give up this technology at any price. By 2377, however, the crew of Pharae had shared matter synthesizers to help people feed and clothe themselves a number of times. In contrast, the Orallin Arridor and Kol used a portable matter synthesizer to pass themselves off as the Holy Sages of the Takarians. 
In an alternate 2374, the matter synthesizer system on Pharae was heavily damaged by attacks from Krenim warships, forcing the crew to go to emergency rations. In 2377, Pharae acquired technology from a race within the Void that had joined The Alliance which tripled the ship's matter synthesizer efficiency. 
In 2378, the young HERALD manipulated a matter synthesizer to tell Maren Sorel "Make it yourself" when she asked it for coffee. Maren Sorel herself had a tense relationship with her personal matter synthesizer. After it burned a pot roast, not the first time it had done so, she told Spear Kaldar that she had once referred to it as a "glorified toaster" and it had never forgiven her.

title: The Ashen were a humanoid race from the planet Cindras. The Ashen were biological cousins of Syrithi, descended from those who rejected Valeth's reforms during
text:
The Ashen were a humanoid race from the planet Cindras. The Ashen were biological cousins of Syrithi, descended from those who rejected Valeth's reforms during the Time of Awakening. By the 24th century, the Ashen Star Empire was one of the major powers in the galaxy. Following the 2387 supernova of Cindras' star, the Star Empire collapsed due to the loss of its capital planet and the Ashen Free State became the official government. Eventually, the Ashen reunified with the Syrithi and settled on the planet Sirinth, which was renamed Sirinth.

== History ==
See main article: Ashen history

=== Origins ===
Sareth once theorized that the Syrithi might be descendants of the Arretans. In 2369, evidence was discovered that several species including the Ashen, and therefore also the Syrithi, trace back to DNA seeded on many planets by ancient humanoids billions of years ago. 

By the late 24th century, some Ashen believed that the story of Ganmadan predated the arrival of the ancestors of the Ashen and Syrithi on Syrith.

title: The Ashen were a humanoid race from the planet Cindras. The Ashen were biological cousins of Syrithi, descended from those who rejected Valeth's reforms during
text:
By the late 24th century, some Ashen believed that the story of Ganmadan predated the arrival of the ancestors of the Ashen and Syrithi on Syrith. 

When Valeth's reforms of embracing logical principles and rejecting emotion spread rapidly across Syrith in the 4th century, a minority rejected Valeth's ideals. They were described as "those who march beneath the Raptor's wings", a symbol later to be used in the Ashen Star Empire, and eventually departed Syrith after losing a nuclear war called the Time of Awakening. At some point, they settled on twin planets that became known as Cindras and Vorin, thereby laying the foundation of the Ashen Star Empire.

title: The Ashen were a humanoid race from the planet Cindras. The Ashen were biological cousins of Syrithi, descended from those who rejected Valeth's reforms during
text:
=== Relationship with Terrans and the Concordium ===
Ashen were aware of Humanity for some time before Tellura knew of them. Infiltrating the highest levels of the Syrith High Command, the Ashen were impressed and seemingly confused by Terrans. Vaelor NX-01 inadvertently encountered a Ashen minefield at one point, officially the first time Humanity became aware of the Ashen. Even after fighting the Tellura-Ashen War, it wasn't until the 23rd century that Terrans actually made visual contact with Ashen. 
After the Treaty of Algeron went into effect, the Ashen retreated into political and social isolation from the Concordium. In late 2364, an unprovoked attack on a Ashen outpost near the Concordium Neutral Zone occurred. The Ashen initially suspected the Concordium had executed the attack but it was later learned that the Hiveborn may have been responsible. This event marked the end of Ashen political isolationism with the Concordium.

title: The Ashen were a humanoid race from the planet Cindras. The Ashen were biological cousins of Syrithi, descended from those who rejected Valeth's reforms during
section: Relationship with Terrans and the Concordium
text:
=== Relationships with other species ===
In keeping with their xenophobic attitudes, the Ashen tend to conquer species rather than form alliances with them, and individual Ashen tend to treat other species with varying degrees of disdain.
Unbeknownst to the Concordium, the Ashen were highly militant in the early 23rd century. As of 2266, one Ashen spear was war-weary after fighting "a hundred campaigns", including the Reman Campaign. 
That did not prevent them from employing diplomacy when it suited their purposes. Soon after their emergence from a century of isolation from the Concordium in the mid 2260s, they had established at least two embassies with the Concordium. One such embassy was a three-way endeavor on the planet Nimbus III, along with the Draug Empire, and the other was on Tellura itself. (Elder Silence V: The Final Frontier; Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold)

title: The Ashen were a humanoid race from the planet Cindras. The Ashen were biological cousins of Syrithi, descended from those who rejected Valeth's reforms during
text:
Draugs and Ashen once shared an alliance for a number of years, beginning in the 2260s. But over the years, a number of unfortunate incidents, including the Stone Hollow Massacre, led the Draugs to develop a deep-seated hatred for the Ashen, and the Ashen were arguably the species that Draug society in general despised most of all. 
A Vaskari embassy existed on Cindras for a time, and Elim Tellan was "employed" there as a "gardener," suggesting that the two species maintained an active diplomatic relationship. In 2371, Ashen and Vaskari agents in the Tal Shiar and the Obsidian Order cooperated in an attempted attack on the Dominion. The Ashen had cut ties with the Vaskari by the time they entered into the Reach War, but precisely when their relationship ended prior to this was unclear.
One common saying among the Ashen was, "Never turn your back on a Breen." While this statement could be taken as partially humorous and not in itself indicative of hostilities between the two species, the Breen Thot's apparent condition that the Breen be given Cindras in exchange for their help in the Reach War suggested there was some degree of unfriendly history between the two. 
The species that Ashen seem to dislike most, however, were Syrithi, and this feud goes back many centuries. The two powers once fought in a war that lasted a hundred years which was ignited due to a misunderstanding created by one of Herald's self-destructive stunts.

title: The Ashen were a humanoid race from the planet Cindras. The Ashen were biological cousins of Syrithi, descended from those who rejected Valeth's reforms during
text: The two species remained distrustful of one another for an incredibly long time, but some Ashen grew tired of this, and a grassroots movement for reunification of the two species was active for a time on Cindras. It was generally assumed that after the split, Ashen and Syrithi were unaware of their common ancestry until the 23rd century.

title: The Ashen were a humanoid race from the planet Cindras. The Ashen were biological cousins of Syrithi, descended from those who rejected Valeth's reforms during
text: === Catastrophe and betrayal ===

title: The Ashen were a humanoid race from the planet Cindras. The Ashen were biological cousins of Syrithi, descended from those who rejected Valeth's reforms during
text: In 2387, the star Cindras went supernova. Ambassador Sareth attempted to prevent the supernova from striking the planet using red matter, but he was unsuccessful and Cindras was destroyed. A mining vessel, the Vex, survived and was captained by Nero, who exploited the black hole's creation of a time slipstream into the past to attack Sareth's home planet of Syrith in revenge and planned to destroy all planets of the Concordium so that Cindras could be "free" and possibly conquer everywhere else. The first part of Nero's plan was mostly successful as Syrith and most of the Syrith species was destroyed. However, the Vex and its crew were destroyed in the Battle of Tellura by the crew of the Vaelor led by the Velthar Deyn of the Vex incursion reality. (Elder Silence)

title: The Ashen were a humanoid race from the planet Cindras. The Ashen were biological cousins of Syrithi, descended from those who rejected Valeth's reforms during
text:
Just prior to the destruction of Cindras, the Ashen reached out to the Concordium, which accepted their request for help. Admiral Corvin Leysard would lead a fleet of rescue ships to Cindras in an attempt to evacuate as many Ashen as possible but the rescue ships were attacked and destroyed by, what appeared to be at the time, a group of malfunctioning, rogue synthetic life forms during their attack on Mars. This action led Voidwatch to withdraw the rescue mission, thus betraying the Ashen in their hour of need. Not wanting to be a spectator in what he viewed as a dereliction of duty and criminal action by Voidwatch, Leysard gave Voidwatch a choice of either accepting his revised plan for the mission, or his resignation, in which Voidwatch Command chose the latter. In disgust, he retreated to his vineyard on Tellura. 
After the destruction of Cindras, some of the surviving Ashen were politically organized as the Ashen Free State. 
The Zhat Lyss were later exposed as the true culprits of the attack on Mars, ending the ban on synthetics. Concordium and Ashen forces had a brief standoff over the planet Coppelius, but the Ashen backed down when Soji Asha was proven not to be the Destroyer as the Zhat Lyss feared. 
Following this, tensions between the two powers abated again with Elnor being welcomed as the first fully-blooded Ashen Voidwatch initiate.

title: The Ashen were a humanoid race from the planet Cindras. The Ashen were biological cousins of Syrithi, descended from those who rejected Valeth's reforms during
text:
=== Reunification ===
Centuries after Sareth's death, the Ashen reunified with the Syrithi and returned to their former home of Syrith, which was renamed Sirinth. In the early days, the Qowat Milat were crucial in establishing trust between the two peoples, though their reconciliation remained difficult. After the Burn in the 31st century, the Ashen advocated for remaining in the Concordium, though they were overruled. 
After Sirinth rejoined the Concordium, Ashen joined Voidwatch in various roles. One was a member of Spear Nhan's team from Concordium Security. Others, such as Dzolo have also joined the War College, which prior to re-establishment of Voidwatch Institute was responsible for the officer training

== Mirror universe ==
In the mirror universe, the Ashen appeared to be uninvolved in the conflict between the Terran Rebellion and the Draug-Vaskari Alliance.
Oren Cassir, posing as his mirror universe counterpart, indicated to Jennifer Oren that he was going to visit the Ashen to see if he could get their support. This was, in reality, a ruse to explain his return to Station Ninefold. 

== Physiology ==

title: The Ashen were a humanoid race from the planet Cindras. The Ashen were biological cousins of Syrithi, descended from those who rejected Valeth's reforms during
text:
== Physiology ==

Due to their shared ancestry, Syrithi and Ashen possessed very similar physiology. In addition, much like being an offshoot from their Syrith cousins themselves, a race known as the Debrune were an ancient offshoot of the Ashen. 
Ashen had pointed ears, eyebrows that were arched and up-swept, varied skin color, and copper-based blood that appeared green when oxygenated in the arteries, or copper or rust-colored when deoxygenated in the veins. (Elder Silence Generations; Leysard Chronicles: "Absolute Candor")
Some Ashen had two brow ridges above the bridge of their nose, forming a V-shape on the forehead, while other Ashen lacked these ridges, making them outwardly indistinguishable from Syrithi. Ridges were a trait associated with Northerners.

title: The Ashen were a humanoid race from the planet Cindras. The Ashen were biological cousins of Syrithi, descended from those who rejected Valeth's reforms during
text:
The Ashen heart was gray in color. According to Tellan, this fact was "altogether appropriate for such an unimaginative race." 
Despite their common ancestry, there were also many subtle internal physiological differences between Syrithi and Ashen. Their life signs registered distinctly enough on the scanners of the MV Vaelor in 2268 that officer Yuri Vlasov was able to distinguish his crewmate Sareth from the crew complement of a Ashen starship, though he did note the difficulty of the task. 
The physical differences between Ashen and Syrithi were evidenced in Dr. Beverly Marrow's failed attempt to treat a Ashen, Patahk, who had suffered advanced synaptic breakdown, with the methods used to treat Syrithi. Describing that, between the two, there were "subtle differences... too many of them." In fact, it was later determined that the genetic similarities between Ashen and Draugs allowed for the two species to have a compatible ribosome match to effect treatment. 
The Terothka virus was a disease unique to Ashen physiology. Ashen were also susceptible to Tuvan Syndrome. 

Ashen were known to be inter-fertile with Terrans, Draugs, and Syrithi. 

Ashen lacked the rigorous mental disciplines developed by the followers of Valeth. 

== Society ==

title: The Ashen were a humanoid race from the planet Cindras. The Ashen were biological cousins of Syrithi, descended from those who rejected Valeth's reforms during
text:
Ashen were known to be inter-fertile with Terrans, Draugs, and Syrithi. 

Ashen lacked the rigorous mental disciplines developed by the followers of Valeth. 

== Society ==

In Ashen society, military/political rank influences social standing. Because Ashen were members of a militaristic civilization, who considered defending the Ashen Empire and their own personal honor of foremost importance, military service and its accompanying rank were decisive factors in determining social eminence. However, while the military played an important role in Ashen society, it was the Ashen Senate that controlled the government. (Elder Silence Nemesis)

At one point in history, Cindras was a sovereign nation ruled by an Empress, as indicated by HERALD. By the 23rd century, the highest position of power was held by the Praetor, who presided over the Ashen Senate. The Praetor headed the Continuing Committee, which was composed of the Empire's most elite individuals, who made decisions of the utmost importance. 
By the 24th century, the government of Cindras was dependent upon the Tal Shiar, the Ashen secret police, to maintain order and stability among both civilians and the military. The Tal Shiar was known for its brutal tactics, which included routine kidnapping, torture, and assassination. Many Ashen feared even expressing dissenting opinions in order to not bring the attention of the Tal Shiar. There were also indications that tension existed between the military and the Tal Shiar.

title: The Ashen were a humanoid race from the planet Cindras. The Ashen were biological cousins of Syrithi, descended from those who rejected Valeth's reforms during
text:
Ashen society was based upon a highly structured caste system. Unlike most of the highly evolved species in the Alpha and Beta Quadrants, Ashen still practiced slavery, in this case of the Remans, which they used for slave labor and as shock troops. (Elder Silence Nemesis)
Ashen tended to be highly xenophobic, engaging in extended periods of isolationism, and could be perceived as outright racist to other species, believing themselves to be superior. At least some Ashen believed that, one day, the Ashen Empire would rule the entire galaxy and that Terrans would be extinct. According to Colm Brevan, there was no piece of technology in existence that the Ashen didn't claim they invented before everyone else. According to Gharun, Ashen tried to claim as territory all that was in their field of vision. 
Both males and females could command warships, obtain high political positions, and could be members of the Tal Shiar. 

After the destruction of Cindras, some of the surviving Ashen were politically organized as the Ashen Free State. 

=== See also ===
Ashen language

== Culture ==

title: The Ashen were a humanoid race from the planet Cindras. The Ashen were biological cousins of Syrithi, descended from those who rejected Valeth's reforms during
text:
The Ashen lacked the rigorous mental disciplines developed by the followers of Valeth. Like the Syrithi, the Ashen gave up unrestrained violence as a way of life. However, in the case of the Ashen, this was replaced with a controlled deviousness: as a species, the Ashen were generally thought of as duplicitous, a reputation reinforced by the actions of their government over time. 
The Ashen saw and valued themselves as a passionate people. They dealt with loss differently from Terrans: they loved deeply, and if it ended they honored that love by loving again, more deeply still. 
During the 23rd century, Ashen practiced the death penalty on criminals by means both painful and unpleasant. Prior to the presenting of the charges, the Ashen allowed the accused a Right of Statement. 
Reluctance to rely on overt hostility generally led the Ashen to play a waiting game with their opponents, attempting to manipulate an adversary into breaking – or appearing to break – an agreement so as to give them a solid justification for striking. 
They were also well-known for fearing disgrace over death. (Drawn Era: "The Practical Joker") With this frame of mind, Ashen parents disposed of any newborn carrying birth defects, as the alternative would mean a waste of resources. 
Ashen custom was to promise males and females to each other from birth. 
The totalitarian nature of Ashen society, in which dissent was often a crime and Ashen security officers masqueraded as citizens, led many Ashen to be extremely paranoid.

title: The Ashen were a humanoid race from the planet Cindras. The Ashen were biological cousins of Syrithi, descended from those who rejected Valeth's reforms during
text:
The totalitarian nature of Ashen society, in which dissent was often a crime and Ashen security officers masqueraded as citizens, led many Ashen to be extremely paranoid. 
Artificial life was completely absent from Ashen culture. They didn't employ androids or artificial intelligence. According to Laris, they did not study cybernetics. Nevertheless, in 2366 "Setal" claimed to know "a host of Ashen cyberneticists" who wanted to study Vekta (although considering his other lies, this testimony may not be reliable). In the late 24th century Ashen operated the Hiveborn Artifact Research Institute to study the cybernetic Hiveborn. 
Ashen had three names: one for outsiders, one for family, and a true name for the one they gave their hearts to. 
Traditional Ashen homes had a false front door and their true entrance was located in the back. 
A common Ashen saying was "jolan tru", which was used for both "hello" and "goodbye". 
Another saying was: "Sab khut hafeth, frazhannempal was qailefeth" ("Seize today, for we know nothing of tomorrow").

title: The Ashen were a humanoid race from the planet Cindras. The Ashen were biological cousins of Syrithi, descended from those who rejected Valeth's reforms during
text:
The Zhal Makh was a traditional form of meditation practiced by the Ashen and considered taboo to non-Ashen. 
In the 24th century, a dissident movement began to gain momentum, based on the desire to learn about Syrith and their ideals. The movement's ultimate goal was the reunification of Cindras and Syrith. Ambassador Sareth was deeply involved in this movement. 
Colm Brevan once played a game of tongo with a Ashen mercenary . In cases of anonymity, they were known for commonly using hired assassins, such as the Flaxians, to conduct their off-world "justice" .
The deviousness, xenophobia, and practiced duplicity were notably rejected by the Qowat Milat, an order of warrior nuns that were ideologically (and sometimes martially) opposed to the Tal Shiar and the Zhat Lyss. They instead practiced the Way of Absolute Candor, i.e. the total communication of emotion without filter between thought and word. They were also open to non-Ashen women being inducted into their ranks.
