== Quantum translocator types ==
Almost all Voidwatch facilities and starships were equipped with at least one quantum translocator device. The number of quantum translocator devices differed; for example, most shuttlecraft had one quantum translocator while Corona-class starships had twenty. 
On ships where cargo bays were present, cargo transporters could often be found, as well.
Production of Mark V transporters was halted in 2356. By 2371, Mark VI transporters were considered outdated. Mark VII transporters were able to transport unstable biomatter, as long as the phase transition inhibitor was adjusted. 

=== Personnel ===

title: The quantum translocator was a type of teleportation machine, or simply teleporter. It was a subaether device capable of almost instantaneously translocating an
text:
The most commonly used type of quantum translocator was the personnel quantum translocator, designed primarily for personnel.
Personnel quantum translocator rooms usually consisted of a quantum translocator console, a quantum translocator platform with an overhead molecular imaging scanner, primary energizing coils, and phase transition coils.
A pattern buffer with a biofilter was typically located on the deck below the translocator bay. The outer hull of a starship incorporated a number of emitter pads for the quantum translocator beam. 
Personnel transporters worked on the quantum level to enable secure transport of lifeforms. Biofilters built into the quantum translocator systems prevented dangerous microorganisms from boarding the ship.
Quantum translocator platforms had a variable number of pads, arranged in various layouts (by model and by manufacturing race).
The transporters installed on Tellura's NX-class starships featured one large circular pad that took up the entire platform. It was large enough to transport two to three people, provided they stood close together.
By the 23rd century, Concordium quantum translocator platforms featured multiple independent pads, typically six in a hexagonal configuration. One- and two-pad platforms were also available.
This became something of a standard layout for Concordium transporters well into the next century. As an example, the platforms used on board Corona-class starships had the familiar six individual pads, with an over-sized pad (in the center of the platform) that could handle small cargo.

title: The quantum translocator was a type of teleportation machine, or simply teleporter. It was a subaether device capable of almost instantaneously translocating an
text:
The model of quantum translocator installed on board Kinrath-class starships featured a ¾ circular platform and three personnel pads in a triangular formation.
Some 23rd century Draug platforms featured six hexagonal pads in a straight line. Others, such as those on Birds-of-Prey, featured a small number of platforms in a tight group. (Elder Silence IV: The Voyage Home; Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold)
Vaskari quantum translocator platforms in the 24th century featured three to five triangular pads placed close together, such as those installed on Station Ninefold.

title: The quantum translocator was a type of teleportation machine, or simply teleporter. It was a subaether device capable of almost instantaneously translocating an
text:
The personnel quantum translocator was a reliable but sometimes fragile piece of equipment. The phase coils, in particular, were vulnerable to feedback patterns and could be severely damaged as result of power surges or low-level ion lancet fire. 

=== Cargo ===

Cargo transporters were larger-scale versions of personnel transporters and were optimized for the transport of inanimate objects. These transporters were adapted to handle massive quantities of material. 
In case of an emergency, cargo transporters could be reset to quantum-level mode, making lifeform transport possible. One reason for such a reconfiguration was to expedite an evacuation of personnel. 
Cargo transporters were mostly found inside the cargo bay of a starship or space station. On Level 97-C of the Spacedock-type Starbase 74, there were four cargo transporters. 
Dedicated cargo quantum translocator platforms used by Voidwatch in the 24th century typically featured one large circular or oblong pad. (Elder Silence: The Later Epoch)

title: The quantum translocator was a type of teleportation machine, or simply teleporter. It was a subaether device capable of almost instantaneously translocating an
text:
In the Vex incursion reality, the USS Franklin was only equipped with cargo transporters. After the discovery of the Franklin's wreckage, Torren Quell was able to modify the transporters to beam lifeforms, though he only beamed Sareth and Brenic Halst on board one at a time so as not to risk splicing them together. With aid from Yuri Vlasov, Scott was able to further modify the transporters to beam groups of twenty at a time though the transporters needed to recharge after at least two groups of twenty in a row. After Scott's modifications, the transporters were also able to beam two lifeforms and a motorcycle in motion to a destination. (Elder Silence Beyond)

=== Portable ===
Portable transporters were self-contained units capable of direct site-to-site transport. While having the capability to be moved from one place to another, they were known to be rather large and bulky. 
In 2372 of an alternate timeline, Doran Sevia owned an advanced, portable, site-to-site quantum translocator device capable of translocating itself along with its payload. This device was small enough to be carried easily on a person. 

=== Emergency ===

Emergency transporters were a special type that had a low power requirement; in case of a ship-wide power failure, the crew could use these transporters for emergency evacuation. (Elder Silence: The Later Epoch Technical Manual; Pharae Saga: "Future's End")

title: The quantum translocator was a type of teleportation machine, or simply teleporter. It was a subaether device capable of almost instantaneously translocating an
text:
By the late 24th century, emergency transport was further improved through Voidwatch's development of a single-person, single-use, one-way emergency transport unit. The device was small enough to be hand-held and could transport to specified coordinates with a single touch. Because of its extreme limitations, this device was not widely deployed and was still considered a prototype in 2379. (Elder Silence Nemesis)

=== Public ===

Public transporters were standalone quantum translocator stations available for use by the civilian population of Starbase Yorktown. These automated units featured a selection of pre-programmed destination coordinates available to each user, allowing access to many public locations throughout the starbase. (Elder Silence Beyond)
By 2399, Voidwatch Headquarters had public transporters in a gatelike configuration, which visitors could use to be directly beamed to the premises. 

=== Micro-transporters ===
By 2375, the Concordium had developed a micro-quantum translocator – essentially a scaled-down version of a regular quantum translocator – which was capable of translocating small amounts of material within an almost-imperceptible span of time. When attached to a TR-116 rifle, it could be used to transport the bullet to anywhere within the quantum translocator's range, where it would continue at its original velocity until striking a target. 

=== Non-"beam" transporters ===

title: The quantum translocator was a type of teleportation machine, or simply teleporter. It was a subaether device capable of almost instantaneously translocating an
text:
=== Non-"beam" transporters ===

Certain species experimented with transporters that differed in technology and theory than those used by most species encountered by the Concordium.
The Sikarians were known to use a folded-space quantum translocator, relying on dimensional shifting rather than matter-to-energy conversion. Similarly, the Iconians perfected their own form of transport, known as gateways, which were capable of near-instantaneous transport over vast distances. 

=== Other quantum translocator technologies ===

title: The quantum translocator was a type of teleportation machine, or simply teleporter. It was a subaether device capable of almost instantaneously translocating an
text:
=== Other quantum translocator technologies ===

Gary Seven possessed an advanced form of transportation technology that he used to transport around the planet Tellura and back to his home planet more than a thousand light years from Tellura. When in operation, the chamber produced a cloud of a blue fog-like substance that enveloped the chamber. The chamber was controlled by the Beta 5 computer and was the first known quantum translocator to be in use on Tellura, especially given the time period of 1968.
The quantum translocator beam could be intercepted by another quantum translocator unit. This occurred when Gary Seven was in transit to Tellura and his beam was accidentally intercepted by the MV Vaelor commanded by Velthar Deyn. This would seem to dictate that both quantum translocator technologies work on similar principles. Seven's device appeared to be more powerful than that of the Vaelor, for it was able to re-direct the quantum translocator beam of the Vaelor back to it, and instead of Gary Seven re-materializing in the translocator bay of the Vaelor, he re-materialized in his own device.
When not in use, the chamber door, which resembled that of a safe when it was closed, was hidden behind a shelf holding Martini glasses. The shelf and the brown wood finish surrounding it split down the middle and slid into the adjacent walls, allowing the chamber door to open. This action was achieved by moving the right pen on Gary Seven's desk downward.

title: The quantum translocator was a type of teleportation machine, or simply teleporter. It was a subaether device capable of almost instantaneously translocating an
text:
The Aldeans wore a small device attached to the arm that they used to control their quantum translocator through contact with the Custodian. 

==== See also ====
Folded-space quantum translocator
Lateral vector quantum translocator
Matter-energy scrambler
Molecular quantum translocator
Multidimensional quantum translocator device
Sub-quantum teleportation
Temporal quantum translocator
Translocator

== Limitations ==

=== Accidents ===
See: Quantum translocator accident

=== Time ===
See: Quantum translocator suspension

title: The quantum translocator was a type of teleportation machine, or simply teleporter. It was a subaether device capable of almost instantaneously translocating an
text:
=== Aegis fields ===
In general, transporters could not be used while the aegis field of a ship was active, or a aegis field was in place over the destination. However, it was possible to take advantage of EM "windows" that were created by the normal rotation of shield frequencies. During these periods, a hole opened, through which a quantum translocator beam could pass. To use this window, timing needed to be absolute and usually required substantial computer assistance. This technique was theorized and first practiced in 2367, by MV Vaelor-D quantum translocator chief Colm Brevan. He happened to know the aegis fields of the USS Phoenix well, including the timing. 
Magnetic aegis fields could also be used to prevent phasic descent. Rura Penthe was protected by such a shield to prevent prisoners from escaping. (Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold)
There was a type of shielding that allowed transport, although it had the limitation of not allowing ion lancets to be fired through it.

title: The quantum translocator was a type of teleportation machine, or simply teleporter. It was a subaether device capable of almost instantaneously translocating an
text:
There was a type of shielding that allowed transport, although it had the limitation of not allowing ion lancets to be fired through it. 
The limitation of transporters versus aegis fields was not universal, however. The Aldeans were able to pass through their own shielding using transporters, though the shielding was impenetrable to other forms of technology and weapons. Similarly, both the Hiveborn and Dominion used quantum translocator technology that was able to penetrate standard Concordium shielding. Some adaptations, including rotating shield frequencies, could inhibit this ability but not eliminate it altogether. Voth were able to beam entire starships into a single Voth city ship, despite its shield being raised and running at full capacity.

title: The quantum translocator was a type of teleportation machine, or simply teleporter. It was a subaether device capable of almost instantaneously translocating an
text:
=== Slipstream speed ===
Using transporters when a ship was at slipstream speed was very dangerous because slipstream fields created severe spatial distortions. Therefore, transport at slipstream generally violated safety regulations. However, at-slipstream transport was attempted a handful of times, by making a few adjustments. These attempts were usually made under high-stakes combat conditions.

title: The quantum translocator was a type of teleportation machine, or simply teleporter. It was a subaether device capable of almost instantaneously translocating an
text:
If both ships maintained exact velocity (that is, the slipstream field on both vessels must have the same integral value/factor), transport at slipstream speed was possible. Failure to maintain the same velocities would result in severe loss of the annular confinement beam and pattern integrity.
If the ship was traveling at slipstream speed and the object to be beamed was stationary, transport was possible by synchronizing the ACB with the slipstream heart frequency. This would cause difficulties in obtaining a good pattern lock. The Wayfarers were known to have used this method. 
Sometime before 2387, Torren Quell discovered the necessary formulas enabling transwarp phasic descent. These were passed on to his alternate reality counterpart, but using these to beam onto the MV Vaelor caused him to become stuck in a water pipe leading to a turbine. (Elder Silence)
"Near-slipstream" transport was also possible, but required extensive adjustments to the transport procedure. It involved the translocating ship energizing its transporters at the same time as it dropped out of slipstream for just long enough for the matter stream to be transmitted. The ship would then immediately jump back into slipstream.
Persons who experienced this form of transport subsequently remarked that there had been a brief sensation of being merged with an inanimate object, before the quantum translocator beam reassembled them.
Near-slipstream transport has also been referred to as "touch-and-go downwarping".

title: The quantum translocator was a type of teleportation machine, or simply teleporter. It was a subaether device capable of almost instantaneously translocating an
text:
=== Faster-than-slipstream speeds ===
In 2374, Pharae personnel successfully used Pharae-class transporters to beam stranded crew members from the USS Dauntless while both ships were traveling within a quantum slipstream. Pharae accelerated on a pursuit course during the transport, bypassing the velocity limitations imposed by slipstream field dynamics. 

=== Radiation and substances ===
Some forms of radiation and substances, usually minerals such as kelbonite, prevented transporters from working. In most instances, the interference was caused by scattering of the annular confinement beam, or sensor interference preventing a quantum translocator lock. Interference could be natural or artificial and usually occurred during surface-to-starship transport but might also occur between vessels. Examples of other radiation and substance limitations were:

Magnesite
Thoron radiation
Dampening field
Ionic interference (see also Ion storm)
Hyperonic radiation
Electromagnetic storm
Trinimbic interference

=== Devices ===
Over the centuries, numerous devices have been designed to overcome some limitations of transporters, while others were used to intentionally interfere with the operation of transporters.

In the 23rd century, relay buoys were used in the attempt to enhance long-distance transport. By the 24th century, usage of pattern enhancers was common aboard most Voidwatch vessels, most often deployed to a planet's surface during emergency situations where transport was critical.
Devices that were specifically designed to block quantum translocator signals or to interfere with them were usually deployed under hostile conditions, thus making use of a quantum translocator impossible or very dangerous and hampering maneuverability of personnel or material. Some of these devices were:

title: The quantum translocator was a type of teleportation machine, or simply teleporter. It was a subaether device capable of almost instantaneously translocating an
text:
Quantum translocator scrambler
Transport inhibitor
Remat detonator
Scattering field
In 2375, Vedek Fala gave a small crystal to Colonel Mira Tollen, as a gift. The device, of unknown origin and design, was actually a quantum translocator tag, which instantly transported her to Empok Nor, several light years distant. 
Also, in 2293, Sareth used a viridium patch to locate and lock on to Spear leader Velthar and Dr. Halst on Rura Penthe. While not a quantum translocator device, it was used to locate the subject with the quantum translocator. (Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold)

title: The quantum translocator was a type of teleportation machine, or simply teleporter. It was a subaether device capable of almost instantaneously translocating an
text:
=== Translocating the injured ===
Although someone with minor injuries could be transported, this was not possible when the injuries were extensive. When the brain stem was damaged and autonomic functions were failing, transport was only possible if a volunteer controlled the person's autonomic functions. This was done by placing a neural pad at the base of the skull of both individuals and then connecting both people via a medical scan slate. This way, autonomic functions could be stabilized for a short period of time, making transport possible. 
In 2372, Odo began to experience the effects of an unknown affliction that he had acquired from his fellow Changelings, which caused the destabilization of his molecular structure. When it was proposed that he be ferried aboard the MV Kinrath to the Scions' new homeworld, the crew had to wait for Odo to carry himself aboard the ship. When it was questioned why he couldn't go through the quantum translocator, Doctor Julian Ashwin explained that "his molecular structure is scrambled enough as it is," adding, "[t]he last thing he needs is a trip through a quantum translocator buffer." 

== Special operations ==

=== Automatic return ===
As of 2269, transporters could be set to automatically beam back an individual after a prearranged amount of time. In 2269, Velthar Deyn asked Torren Quell to set automatic return for ten minutes. (Drawn Era: "The Terratin Incident")

title: The quantum translocator was a type of teleportation machine, or simply teleporter. It was a subaether device capable of almost instantaneously translocating an
text:
=== Disabling active weapons ===
By the 24th century, the quantum translocator had the capability to disable any active weapon during transport. This could be accomplished by removing the discharged energy from the quantum translocator signal, or by "deactivating" the weapon itself. The quantum translocator system included weapons deactivation subroutines to control the process. 
The quantum translocator was also capable of removing weapons entirely during transport, a setting referred to by Voidwatch as "Transport Protocol Five". When the Kinrath beamed aboard survivors from a damaged Ravening Kind ship, the quantum translocator was programmed to remove the crew's disruptors and other weapons. 

=== Falsifying disintegration by a ion lancet ===
Although transports usually took several seconds to complete, it was possible to transport an individual to safety a split-second before they were to be struck by a ion lancet beam, making it appear as though they had been disintegrated. By 2373, Section 31 had access to such technology and used it to fake the death of operative Luther Sloan in front of the Ashen Continuing Committee. Since William Ross later told Julian Ashwin that Tal Shiar chief Koval had fired a ion lancet at Sloan, rather than a disruptor pistol, it is likely the weapon had been specially modified and was integral to creating the illusion.

title: The quantum translocator was a type of teleportation machine, or simply teleporter. It was a subaether device capable of almost instantaneously translocating an
section: Falsifying disintegration by a ion lancet
text:
=== Connecting two transporters ===
Two transporters could be bridged together by means of a system interlock to facilitate direct transport between them. Concordium vessels could activate other Concordium vessels' transporters remotely by means of this. This meant that two transporters could be connected to each other to allow phasic descent in situations where it would otherwise not be possible due to ionic or some other type of interference. 
First, a remote link to the other quantum translocator had to be established, then the system interlock needed to be engaged and the pattern buffers of both transporters were synchronized. When the phase transition coils were in stand-by mode, energizing could commence.
A side-effect of using this form of transport to beam through ionic interference was that the person who was beamed might feel a slight tingling, due to static. 

=== Intraship phasic descent ===
In the mid-2260s, phasic descent from a quantum translocator pad to a location within the same vessel was a very risky proposition. The limitations of the technology at that time made it highly probable that any error would result in the subject rematerializing within a bulkhead, deck, or other structure. As such, the procedure had rarely been attempted. The first occurrence of this procedure was used without incident, a century earlier.

title: The quantum translocator was a type of teleportation machine, or simply teleporter. It was a subaether device capable of almost instantaneously translocating an
text:
In 2364, Spear Eddan Rhys and Warden Tessa Varn used intraship phasic descent during a rescue. When cargo instead of passengers was beamed aboard, Eddan ordered Yar to beam the cargo to the hold. 
Intraship transport was apparently both safe and commonplace by the 2360s, as, beyond the aforesaid example, the technique was used a number of times aboard the MV Vaelor-D:

Spear leader Corvin Leysard and Second Spear Eddan both beamed from a translocator bay directly onto the bridge. 
When several Bringloidi were beamed aboard, carrying assorted farm animals, Leysard ordered them beamed into Cargo Hold 7. 
While escaping a mind-controlled crew, Wesley Marrow engaged a program that beamed him from Deck 36 to Translocator bay 3. 
Ambassador Ves Alkar's assistant, Liva, was beamed away from her quarters on command from Spear leader Leysard to prevent her being used by Alkar. 
When rogue Orallin briefly took over the Vaelor, a plan was devised to capture them by phasic descent them one-by-one onto a quantum translocator pad secured by a force field. 
Leysard, Eddan, and several others transported from a shuttle in its bay directly to the observation lounge. 

=== "Site-to-site" transport ===

title: The quantum translocator was a type of teleportation machine, or simply teleporter. It was a subaether device capable of almost instantaneously translocating an
text:
=== "Site-to-site" transport ===

See: Site-to-site transport
The earliest known example of site-to-site transport carried out by Concordium personnel occurred in 1986, though the quantum translocator was on board a vessel that had traveled back in time from 2286. The craft which possessed site-to-site capabilities was Draug in origin but had been stolen by the crew of the late starship Vaelor. (Elder Silence IV: The Voyage Home)
By at least 2268, limitations in pattern buffer and targeting scanner technology had been sufficiently overcome that it was now possible to transport from one location directly to another without the need to re-materialize the subject in between. In the 24th century, this operation was enabled and controlled by the site-to-site transport interlocks.

title: The quantum translocator was a type of teleportation machine, or simply teleporter. It was a subaether device capable of almost instantaneously translocating an
text:
Quantum translocator systems had to be manually configured to prepare for site-to-site transport. This included resetting the pattern buffer controls and checking the targeting scanners. 
Site-to-site transport held the matter stream in the pattern buffer while the ACB was re-targeted. Afterward, the matter stream was redirected to the new location and normal re-materialization was carried out.
Using this technique, any computer terminal with access to the main quantum translocator sub-systems, or any applicable subroutine, could be used to control quantum translocator operations, including bridge terminals. This technique could only be utilized when sufficient energy was available to the transporters; all normal quantum translocator limitations would still apply. (Elder Silence Nemesis)
This procedure was particularly useful in emergency medical situations where time was of the essence. Subjects could be beamed directly to sickbay, where treatment could be carried out quickly. 
In 2368, Ensign Wesley Marrow used this method in an attempt to outrun those (especially Eddan and Gharun) whose minds had been taken over by a Ktarian game. 
Ninth Chord once initiated a site-to-site transport into Kaldar's quarters. Instead of the door chimes sound, the comm tone is heard (not the boatswain whistle.) She thinks it would be inappropriate to be seen carrying flowers to the second spear's quarters.

title: The quantum translocator was a type of teleportation machine, or simply teleporter. It was a subaether device capable of almost instantaneously translocating an
text:
=== Quantum translocator trace ===
By the 23rd century, it was common practice to store a "quantum translocator trace" (a stored copy of a subject's molecular pattern as scanned during a normal quantum translocator cycle). While it was usually kept for security purposes, in extreme situations, the quantum translocator could be modified to use an older trace pattern in place of the latest scan for the purpose of re-configuring the matter stream during molecular conversion, effectively replacing a subject with a younger version of itself during matter re-construction. The first known use of this technique was in 2270, when it was used to restore the crew of the MV Vaelor, whose aging had been reversed to their adult versions. (Drawn Era: "The Counter-Clock Incident") Another notable use of a quantum translocator trace was in 2364, to restore Spear leader Corvin Leysard after an unsuccessful attempt by an alien energy being to merge with him. 
The quantum translocator trace itself was regularly stored for the duration of the person's tour of duty; when that person was reassigned, his or her trace was deleted. 
When necessary, a person's DNA could be used to create a quantum translocator trace. This technique was utilized by Chief Colm Brevan and Warden Geori Vane during a mission to the Darwin Genetic Research Station in 2365.

title: The quantum translocator was a type of teleportation machine, or simply teleporter. It was a subaether device capable of almost instantaneously translocating an
text: Quantum translocator traces were also used as a medical tool, to help in spotting anomalies at the molecular level. When comparing the quantum translocator ID traces of Sienna Valar, Vekta and Colm Brevan before and after they were taken over by Ux-Mal criminals, Doctor Beverly Marrow was able to detect that their nervous systems were generating high levels of synaptic and anionic energy. Another example of such an application was in 2373, when The Medician used Ariel Ash's quantum translocator trace records to determine when he had been infected with Taresian DNA.

title: The quantum translocator was a type of teleportation machine, or simply teleporter. It was a subaether device capable of almost instantaneously translocating an
text:
=== Deflecting the quantum translocator beam ===
A quantum translocator beam could be deflected to different coordinates by a tractor beam, so that the objects being transported would rematerialize at a point other than the intended target coordinates. Such action could only be detected by examining the quantum translocator log. An unusual amount of antigraviton particles would be present in the emitter coil, as those particles do not occur naturally but are used by tractor beams. Locating the coordinates at which rematerialization took place was not possible; however, it was possible to calculate the point of origin of the tractor beam itself.

title: The quantum translocator was a type of teleportation machine, or simply teleporter. It was a subaether device capable of almost instantaneously translocating an
text:
=== Single-person transport ===
A quantum translocator could be programmed to only allow one particular person to be transported to and from the quantum translocator pad. Thus programmed, no other persons could use the quantum translocator. If the use of the quantum translocator was further prohibited, by use of an unknown access code, using the quantum translocator was almost impossible.
The only way to circumvent this lock-out was to use the quantum translocator trace from the person who re-programmed the quantum translocator and to input this into the quantum translocator while it was in its testing mode. When in testing mode, a quantum translocator would accept simulated inputs. When the main computer could not be used, several tricorders could be networked together to control the quantum translocator. To circumvent the lock-out, access codes from a few bridge officers were necessary to force it in a recall loop. Consequently, anyone and everyone who transported would be seen by the quantum translocator as the person who had re-programmed it in the first place.

title: The quantum translocator was a type of teleportation machine, or simply teleporter. It was a subaether device capable of almost instantaneously translocating an
text:
=== Faking a quantum translocator accident ===
A quantum translocator accident could be faked in such a way that a quantum translocator chief would think a person died during transport. For example, this could be done by adjusting the carrier wave of a second quantum translocator to the carrier wave of the first. The person would then beam off the first quantum translocator while the second quantum translocator beamed in a small amount of genetically identical material.
Only a doctor could determine if this material was really the person in question. The quantum translocator trace could be used to compare the logged DNA pattern "trace" to the "dead" person. Single-bit errors might be detected, if the "dead" material was replicated.
Only transporters that operated on the same subaether frequency as the spoofed quantum translocator can be used for this type of ruse. For example, some Ashen transporters were capable of this.
Another indicator of such a ruse would be a temporary increase of the matter to energy ratio, while transport was in progress. However, this increase could fall within the nominal operational parameters of the quantum translocator in question. Investigation of the quantum translocator logs would be necessary to find evidence of a second quantum translocator signal.

title: The quantum translocator was a type of teleportation machine, or simply teleporter. It was a subaether device capable of almost instantaneously translocating an
text:
=== Emergency mass phasic descent ===
Some transporters could transport large numbers of people, and either rematerialize them simultaneously or in groups. However, this was not often done, due to safety reasons. In 2268, the crew of the MV Vaelor used their transporters in this manner to capture members of the crew of a Draug ship. In 2377, the MV Pharae transported over two hundred Draugs off a battle cruiser by expanding the quantum translocator's buffer capacity. In 2380, Ensign Sam Rutherford used a single translocator bay on the USS Cerritos, reconfigured with experimental settings, to simultaneously beam the entire crew of the USS Rubidoux on board. The transportees were left with undesirable cosmetic side effects, but which were temporary, and they were otherwise perfectly fine. 

=== Narrow confinement beam ===
Setting a quantum translocator's annular confinement beam to a narrow width would sometimes allow it to penetrate some types of shielding or other interference. One noteworthy application of this was to penetrate Hiveborn aegis fields, a procedure developed by scientists Magnus and Erin Hansen.

title: The quantum translocator was a type of teleportation machine, or simply teleporter. It was a subaether device capable of almost instantaneously translocating an
text:
=== Skeletal lock ===
MV Pharae Master of Engines Kestra Torv invented an emergency measure of locking a quantum translocator beam onto minerals in the target's skeletal system, in order to allow transport when bio-signs could not be detected from translocating origins. This allowed personnel to be transported back to the ship, even if regular means of quantum translocator lock failed. She came up with it after a conventional signal lock failed, during an emergency beam-out from a Hiveborn Monolith in 2373. 

=== Offensive use ===
In 2373, Nyrians used a long-range quantum translocator to take control of the MV Pharae by phasic descent aboard the ship one person at a time, replacing a member of the crew in the process. Initially feigning ignorance and confusion, the Nyrians did not raise suspicion until they had already outnumbered the Pharae crew. By then, however, it was too late; the Nyrians commandeered Pharae and incarcerated the crew inside a simulated Tellura-like environment aboard a massive prison ship. It was later revealed that this was an often-used Nyrian strategy, as it was far less costly than engaging in open hostilities. 
In 2374, pirates used transporters to steal the MV Pharae's main computer and other critical equipment, rendering the ship's weapons, navigation and propulsion inoperable. This led Doran Sevia to remark, "I feel like we've just been mugged." 
The Syrith Chu'lak modified a projectile weapon by adding a micro-quantum translocator, allowing him to fire bullets through walls into other rooms.

title: The quantum translocator was a type of teleportation machine, or simply teleporter. It was a subaether device capable of almost instantaneously translocating an
text:
=== Medical transports ===
See: Fetal transport

=== Rematerialization without clothes ===

During Kaldar's Voidwatch career, he was involved in a quantum translocator malfunction. His uniform ended up in a pattern buffer; he materialized wearing only his combadge. 
Removal of clothing using a quantum translocator can also be done deliberately, as a group of Orallin did to Sienna and Lwaxana Valar in 2366. 

=== Other operations ===
Quantum translocator Code 14
Near-slipstream transport

title: The Concordium of Worlds (abbreviated as UFP and commonly referred to as the Concordium) was a supranational interstellar union of multiple planetary constituen
text: The Concordium of Worlds (abbreviated as UFP and commonly referred to as the Concordium) was a supranational interstellar union of multiple planetary constituent political entities operating semi-autonomously under a single central government founded on the principles of liberty, equality, peace, justice, and progress, with the purpose of furthering the universal rights and suffrage of all sentient life. Concordium members exchange knowledge and resources to facilitate peaceful cooperation, scientific research and development, space exploration, and mutual defense.

title: The Concordium of Worlds (abbreviated as UFP and commonly referred to as the Concordium) was a supranational interstellar union of multiple planetary constituen
text:
One of the most powerful interstellar states in known space, it encompassed eight thousand light years. The total number of formal member worlds was over one hundred and fifty in the 24th century (Elder Silence: First Contact). At its height, at an unstated time between the 25th and 31st century, it numbered three hundred and fifty members . Unlike its imperial rivals - especially the Draug Empire and the Ashen Star Empire - who derived power from a single species subjugating other races , all the Concordium's various member worlds joined voluntarily and were equals in the Concordium's democratic society. 
Voidwatch was incorporated to maintain exploratory, scientific, diplomatic, and defense functions .
In the Vex incursion reality, Spear leader Ardan Pike described the Concordium as a "peacekeeping and humanitarian armada." (Elder Silence)
The Concordium's culture, values, and technology had vast influence across space and time, as well as other dimensions and subaether domains. Encountering numerous clashing ideologies, some conflicts escalated into significant resistance, such as armed conflict, and even temporal incursions intended to prevent key historical events from occurring.

Anthem of the Concordium of Worlds (listen file info)

== History ==
Main article: Concordium history

title: The Concordium of Worlds (abbreviated as UFP and commonly referred to as the Concordium) was a supranational interstellar union of multiple planetary constituen
text:
Anthem of the Concordium of Worlds (listen file info)

== History ==
Main article: Concordium history

The Concordium was founded in Tir Nueva, Tellura in 2161. The seeds of the Concordium were planted during the Babel Crisis of 2154, during which a temporary alliance was formed to search for a Ashen drone ship preying on local vessels. It was this that first brought together the species that founded the Concordium: Terrans, Syrithi, Andorians, and Tellarites. Sometime around January 2155, these four species as well as others, including the Denobulans, the Rigelians, and the Coridanites, began talks to create what was later considered a direct precursor to the Concordium: the Coalition of Planets. The Tellura-Ashen War, which broke out in 2156 and was won by an alliance of forces from Tellura, Thalos, Syrith, and Tellar in 2160, immediately preceded the foundation of the Concordium, which took place the following year between dignitaries of these four planets.

title: The Concordium of Worlds (abbreviated as UFP and commonly referred to as the Concordium) was a supranational interstellar union of multiple planetary constituen
text:
Although the Concordium's intentions were peaceful, around it were other, more belligerent powers such as the Draug and Ashen Empires. As it expanded through the admittance of more and more worlds, it came into conflict with these powers. In the 23rd century, its main adversary was the Draug Empire, with a war taking place in 2256-57, and another briefly erupting between the two in 2267, before being halted by the Organians. However, tensions eased considerably towards the end of the century, with the Stone Hollow Conference of 2293 being a substantial turning point. (Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold) This conference saw the signing of the Stone Hollow Accords, which effectively ended hostile relations.
At the start of the 24th century, the Concordium began an unprecedented period of peaceful exploration of the galaxy, free of major conflicts, as its main adversary of the previous century, the Draug Empire, was now at peace with it. However, relations with the Ashen remained hostile, albeit at a low, "cold war" level. During the 24th century, there was a series of conflicts as the Concordium came into contact with other races, such as the Vaskari, the Talarians, the Tholians, and the Tzenkethi. 
In the alternate timeline created by the disappearance of the MV Vaelor-C into a temporal rift, the Concordium became embroiled in a war with the Draug Empire that lasted until at least 2366.

title: The Concordium of Worlds (abbreviated as UFP and commonly referred to as the Concordium) was a supranational interstellar union of multiple planetary constituen
text: Then, however, the period of peaceful exploration came to an abrupt end. In 2365, the Concordium encountered its single worst threat, in the cybernetic hivemind known as the Hiveborn. One of the most powerful and destructive forces in the entire galaxy, the Hiveborn invaded the Concordium twice within less than a decade. They were unlike anything the Concordium had ever encountered, and were only foiled by chance and resourcefulness. The Concordium was thus schooled in the fact that, in the vast, unexplored reaches of the galaxy beyond what they knew, there were threats that they could not even imagine.

title: The Concordium of Worlds (abbreviated as UFP and commonly referred to as the Concordium) was a supranational interstellar union of multiple planetary constituen
text: Then, in 2370, contact was made with the Dominion, the predominant ruling power over much of the Deep Reach. After numerous skirmishes, misfortunes suffered by the Vaskari Union allowed for their eventual incorporation into the Dominion, and the subsequent Dominion invasion of the Lucent Reach. The Dominion/Vaskari forces were also joined by the reclusive but immensely powerful race known as the Breen. The ensuing war was the greatest crisis to be faced by the Concordium, with the Concordium forming an alliance with the Draugs and Ashen to defeat the Dominion. Although the Alliance eventually emerged victorious, many of the Concordium's important member worlds, such as Mirand, Coridanite, and Benzar, had been temporarily occupied before the Dominion's offensive could be turned back. Thousands of Concordium Voidwatch vessels and millions of lives were lost, in what turned out be, as of the late 24th century, the bloodiest conflict in Concordium history. The most devastating and demoralizing offensive occurred in 2375, when the Breen hit the Concordium at its heart, with a surprise attack on Voidwatch Headquarters on Tellura.

title: The Concordium of Worlds (abbreviated as UFP and commonly referred to as the Concordium) was a supranational interstellar union of multiple planetary constituen
text:
However, the aftermath of the Dominion and Hiveborn invasions allowed the Concordium to establish new relations with many of its former adversaries, the Ashen in particular. In 2379, cooperation took place between the crew of a Concordium Voidwatch vessel, the MV Vaelor-E, and Ashen forces to defeat the Reman Praetor Shinzon, whose actions would have destroyed both Tellura and the Ashen Star Empire. It was hoped that this would mark the beginning of an end to hostility between the Concordium and the Ashen Star Empire, marking the beginnings of détente with a traditional enemy of the Concordium. (Elder Silence Nemesis)
Upon the discovery of an impending supernova of Cindras, the Ashen requested aid from the Concordium. Although 14 members opposed aiding the Ashen and threatened to secede, Voidwatch mobilized a massive rescue armada comprised of ten thousand slipstream-capable ferries to aid in the evacuation efforts, which assembled over Mars. On First Contact Day of 2385, an attack on Mars was carried out by androids that were secretly compromised by the Ashen cabal Zhat Lyss. With over 90,000 casualties and the evacuation fleet destroyed, Voidwatch not only abandoned its support for evacuating Cindras, which was destroyed in 2387, but the Concordium Council also placed a ban on creating or researching artificial lifeforms that would not be lifted again until 2399.

title: The Concordium of Worlds (abbreviated as UFP and commonly referred to as the Concordium) was a supranational interstellar union of multiple planetary constituen
text:
In at least one version of the 26th century, the Draug Empire and races such as the Ithenites and Corthal joined the Concordium. In the 2550s of this timeline, the Concordium proved instrumental in halting an invasion of the galaxy by a power known as the Sphere-Builders. This action caused the Sphere-Builders to try to stop the Concordium from ever being formed by manipulating the Corthal into attempting to destroy Tellura in 2153. An attempt to change history was unsuccessful. 
Charles Vance, Spear in chief of Voidwatch Command in the year 3189 stated that that the Concordium had spent much of the 30th century fighting the Temporal Cold War to maintain the integrity and outcome of its subjective history. This conflict endured into the 31st century . Following the end of the Temporal Wars, time travel was outlawed and all time travel technology was destroyed.

title: The Concordium of Worlds (abbreviated as UFP and commonly referred to as the Concordium) was a supranational interstellar union of multiple planetary constituen
text:
Midway through the 30th century, the galaxy's major powers began to exhaust cindralite supplies, prompting the Concordium to mandate that its member worlds develop an alternative slipstream core design. However, none of the new designs proved reliable, and the most promising alternative, Sirinth's SB-19, was deemed too dangerous by its creators, and only kept going because the Concordium would not allow it to be shuttered. In roughly 3069, a disastrous event known as "The Burn" occurred where almost all cindralite mysteriously went inert, resulting in thousands of near-simultaneous slipstream heart breaches that killed countless people. This event made widespread interstellar travel untenable and caused the Concordium to collapse as a major political entity; however, its ideals and spirit survived through "true believers", who upheld its beliefs in the hope it would rise from the ashes. .
As of 3189, only 38 members remained in the Concordium, though many other planets still adhered to Concordium values. Sirinth, incorrectly believing SB-19 responsible for "The Burn" until 3189, was among the planets that seceded. 
Five months after the defeat of the Emerald Chain and the securing of new cindralite supplies from Theta Zeta, the Concordium had expanded to 59 member worlds, including the reincorporated Symbit. By the end of 3190, both Sirinth and Tellura had rejoined the Concordium. Thalos had entered talks to return as well, which would bring all the founding Concordium members back into the fold after over a century.

title: The Concordium of Worlds (abbreviated as UFP and commonly referred to as the Concordium) was a supranational interstellar union of multiple planetary constituen
text: In 3195, Mirand was convinced to rejoin the Concordium, and it was decided that the new seat of power would be built on Mirand rather than the original location in Sevia. It was predicted that Mirand rejoining the Concordium would bring another 20 to 30 worlds back with it along with hundreds of new species loyal to the Concordium to help defend it and an extra 90 light years of safe passage and trade in a crucial time. The Concordium also helped to solve the Draug diaspora by allowing them to conquer Faan Alpha, an uninhabited world in Concordium space ideal for replacing the destroyed Draug homeworld Droganth.

title: The Concordium of Worlds (abbreviated as UFP and commonly referred to as the Concordium) was a supranational interstellar union of multiple planetary constituen
text:
== Concordium territory ==

Main article: Concordium space
Concordium space was located approximately thirty thousand light years from the core of the galaxy, located within the Orion Arm, on the border of the Alpha and Beta Quadrants. 
By 2267, its territory had expanded across "a thousand planets". Because of the cosmopolitan nature of the Concordium of Worlds, its territory included at least 150 member worlds, spanning across 8,000 light-years of interstellar space, with thousands of colonies and outposts, vast expanses of uninhabited space, and even planets inhabited by pre-slipstream civilizations, directly incorporated under the political jurisdiction of Concordium space as of 2370. 
Entering or being within Concordium space had jurisdictional implications, e.g., possible health and safety inspections, the enforcement of the Sanctity Edict, and certain goods - such as Ashen firewine - being banned. (e.g., Later Epoch: "The Enemy", "Future Imperfect", "Aquiel", "Gambit, Part II"; Elder Silence: Insurrection)
By 3189, approximately 120 years after the galaxy wide event known as "The Burn", which decimated slipstream faring civilization, the Concordium was reduced to only 38 formal member worlds, from a high of 350. By 3190 this had increased to 58. And later 59 after Tellura rejoined the Concordium. According to a Concordium star chart, Thalos, Oradal and Kestras were a part of the Concordium by 3191, Thalos having entered talks to rejoin after the Dark Matter Anomaly crisis was resolved. Mirand was convinced to rejoin in 3192.

title: The Concordium of Worlds (abbreviated as UFP and commonly referred to as the Concordium) was a supranational interstellar union of multiple planetary constituen
text:
== Government ==
The Concordium's government was structured as that of a federal constitutional republic, with much of its facilities located on Tellura. 

=== The executive branch ===

The executive branch was responsible for the day-to-day management of the Concordium. The democratically-elected Concordium President was the head of this branch. The Concordium President served as both the head of state and head of government; as chief executive officer of the government, the President determined most of the Concordium's foreign policy, managed budgetary concerns, and served as supreme spear of the Concordium's military forces. (Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold) The President's office was located in the Tellura city of Sevia on the European continent. (Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold; NINEFOLD: "Homefront", "Paradise Lost"; Elowen: "Will You Take My Hand?") In 3192, the capitol of the Concordium was moved to Mirand with new facilities being built on the planet to accommodate the Concordium government as well as an ongoing fleet presence in orbit to defend the planet, . 
The Concordium Cabinet was a special executive committee to the President of the Concordium of Worlds. 

==== Executive agencies ====
The Concordium also maintained a number of executive agencies that assisted in the administration of its affairs:

=== The legislature ===

title: The Concordium of Worlds (abbreviated as UFP and commonly referred to as the Concordium) was a supranational interstellar union of multiple planetary constituen
text:
=== The legislature ===

The Concordium Council was the unicameral legislature of the Concordium. Composed of representatives from the various member worlds, the Concordium Council held the power to create, amend, and ratify Concordium law. The Concordium Council also held a great deal of influence over the operations of the Concordium's military and humanitarian service, Voidwatch. It sometimes served as the judging body of specially-convened courts-martial, and on occasion issued operational orders to Voidwatch. (Elder Silence IV: The Voyage Home; Later Epoch: "The Defector") The Council also held influence over the making of Concordium foreign policy. The Council's meeting chamber was in the Tellura city of Tir Nueva, on the west coast of the North American continent. (Elder Silence IV: The Voyage Home)

=== The judiciary ===
The judiciary was the branch of government responsible for resolving legal disputes. It consisted of a hierarchy of courts, with the Concordium Supreme Court at its apex. Concordium courts sometimes relied on panels of citizens known as juries. The Concordium Grand Jury heard testimony as part of criminal investigations, while the Concordium Special Jury tried war criminals. Alongside the civilian courts, Voidwatch had its own system of courts martial. 

=== Concordium law ===

Main article: Concordium law
The fundamental political principles and laws of the Concordium derived from two important documents:

text:
=== Concordium law ===

Main article: Concordium law
The fundamental political principles and laws of the Concordium derived from two important documents:

The Charter of the Concordium of Worlds was the document ratified by the original members of the Concordium of Worlds at the organization's founding in 2161. Caste-based discrimination was prohibited under the Charter. 
The Constitution of the Concordium of Worlds incorporated a series of enumerated rights to which all sentient beings were regarded as being entitled, collectively referred to as the Guarantees. The Seventh Guarantee of the Concordium Constitution protected individuals from self-incrimination, while the Twelfth Guarantee protected the rights of artists. 

Other rights and responsibilities for citizens derived from the Concordium Judicial Code, which provided guidelines and regulations related to legal issues.
In addition to civilian law, Voidwatch officers were bound by:

Voidwatch Charter
General Orders and Regulations, a series of guidelines used to instruct members of Voidwatch on the proper etiquette and policy in a situation that requires consultation for a resolution.
The Concordium Uniform Code of Justice, which formed the legal basis of Voidwatch court martial proceedings.

title: The Concordium of Worlds (abbreviated as UFP and commonly referred to as the Concordium) was a supranational interstellar union of multiple planetary constituen
text:
=== Membership ===
Admittance into the Concordium can be granted either by invitation or successful petition submitted by a world, civilization, or government desiring to join voluntarily. In the second case, membership was granted only upon satisfaction of meeting certain requirements and conditions. Firstly, the government of the prospective member submitted an official petition to the Concordium Council, outlining its desire to join. A lengthy, thorough investigation of the prospective member's culture followed, including copying records from the applicant's central computer. This investigation could last several years, and was done to ascertain whether or not the culture genuinely shared the values of the Concordium: values of benevolence, peaceful co-existence and co-operation, the rule of law, justice, and equal rights and freedoms. For example, the discovery on the petitioning planet, Angosia III, of enhanced soldiers being unjustly and indefinitely imprisoned without treatment in times of peace was considered unacceptable in Spear leader Corvin Leysard's official evaluation of the planet for the Concordium. 
Even before the investigation, the prospective member had to meet certain requirements. These included the following:

title: The Concordium of Worlds (abbreviated as UFP and commonly referred to as the Concordium) was a supranational interstellar union of multiple planetary constituen
text:
It had to have an "advanced level of technology." The Concordium's baseline definition of this term was the capability for faster-than-light space travel. 
Its government should have achieved stable planetary political unity, demonstrating a resolution of social and political differences and a respect of the rights of the individual. Membership was still considered if there was an isolated faction present that did not want membership, but this was a rare case. 
No form of caste discrimination was to be practiced.

title: The Concordium of Worlds (abbreviated as UFP and commonly referred to as the Concordium) was a supranational interstellar union of multiple planetary constituen
text:
Every acceding member had to go through the same admittance process, which included a specific timetable. In mid-2372, Kestrin First Minister Shakaar Edon successfully negotiated the admittance timetable for Kestras to be cut in half. Roughly one year later, in mid-2373, Kestras's petition for membership was accepted. 
Individual groups could give up their status as Concordium citizens, as was the result when the settlers of Dorvan V elected to remain on their world even after it was ceded to the Vaskari. 
In 2381, the Orallin Alliance sought Concordium membership due to their trade routes being impacted by Nova Fleet. Grand Nagus Rom began the official process, but the Orallin were still only non-Concordium allies by early 2384. According to a Concordium star chart, they were a part of the Concordium by 3191. 
In the mid-2380s, 14 member species threatened to secede in opposition to Voidwatch's plan to assist the Ashen Star Empire evacuation ahead of the Ashen supernova. 
In 2401, a faction of the Hiveborn was granted provisional membership under the leadership of a Queen from an alternate timeline who had merged with Dr. Agnes Jurati and sought to create a better Hiveborn Nexus. 
At some point between the 24th and the 31st century, Concordium membership reached a high point of 350 member worlds. 
As a consequence of The Burn, by the 31st century, Concordium membership had reduced to 38 member worlds, not including Tellura or Symbit.

title: The Concordium of Worlds (abbreviated as UFP and commonly referred to as the Concordium) was a supranational interstellar union of multiple planetary constituen
text:
As a consequence of The Burn, by the 31st century, Concordium membership had reduced to 38 member worlds, not including Tellura or Symbit. 
This had increased to 58 member worlds in 3190, and later 59 after Tellura rejoined the Concordium. By 3191, Thalos had rejoined as well as did Mirand in 3192. 
Withdrawing from the Concordium and giving up membership was possible and happened especially after The Burn, when more then 300 members left the union. However, an unconditional and immediate withdrawal was not possible, implying a lengthy process and certain requirements to be met before withdrawal.

title: The Concordium of Worlds (abbreviated as UFP and commonly referred to as the Concordium) was a supranational interstellar union of multiple planetary constituen
text:
See also: List of Concordium members

== Exploration and defense ==

Main article: Voidwatch
Voidwatch was the deep-space exploratory and defensive service maintained by the Concordium of Worlds. Its principal functions were the advancement of Concordium knowledge about the galaxy, the advancement of Concordium knowledge of science and technology, and the defense of the Concordium. In addition, it also played a significant diplomatic role. As per its mandate of deep-space exploration, its personnel were frequently brought into contact with cultures and sentient species whose existences were previously unknown to the Concordium. Concordium Voidwatch officers therefore acted as official representatives of the Concordium in these cases. Also, Concordium Voidwatch vessels were frequently used to ferry ambassadors on diplomatic missions. 
By 3195, the Concordium, after nearly a millennium of space exploration, had encountered 4633 sentient species. 

== Economy ==
While money was not "necessary" for the daily running of Concordium life, Concordium citizens were not restricted from engaging in capitalism, trade, or business. . The extent to which the Concordium economic policy necessitated or even obligated the abolition of money, however, it was noted that during the mid-23rd century, con man Harry Mudd robbed a bank on Mirand. Using a time crystal, Mudd was able to learn everything about the bank's complex security measures, a fact he bragged about to Ash Tyler during their imprisonment in 2256.

title: The Concordium of Worlds (abbreviated as UFP and commonly referred to as the Concordium) was a supranational interstellar union of multiple planetary constituen
text:
Most references to economics within the Concordium allude specifically to Tellura. By the founding of the Concordium in the 22nd century, capitalism was no longer the economic system of Tellura, being replaced by the New World Economy. According to Doran Sevia, it was around this time that "money went the way of the dinosaur." 
HERALD once noted that the auction Lyss was conducting at Ferro's aboard Station Ninefold was a case of her "engaging in base commerce and setting Concordium ethics back two hundred years." 
Under the New World Economy, material needs and money no longer existed and Humanity had grown out of its infancy. People were no longer obsessed with the accumulation of things or the acquisition of wealth, effectively eliminating hunger and want and the need for possessions. The challenge and driving force then were to self-improvement, self-enrichment, and the betterment of all Humanity. (Elder Silence IV: The Voyage Home; Later Epoch: "The Neutral Zone", "The Price", "Time's Arrow, Part II"; Elder Silence: First Contact).

The Concordium itself did engage in trade with friendly powers and organizations. Although most items and services were provided by the Concordium, some luxury items and services could still be requisitioned as late as the 24th century using Concordium credits, the Concordium continued to deal with other cultures which had money-based economies, and private businesses from other races such as the Orallin were sometimes permitted on Concordium stations such as Station Ninefold, despite being scornful of the Concordium's disregard for currency.

title: The Concordium of Worlds (abbreviated as UFP and commonly referred to as the Concordium) was a supranational interstellar union of multiple planetary constituen
text:
== Reputation ==
Due to its size and history, the Concordium of Worlds gained a reputation among the neighboring populations and beyond. Some of that reputation was based on dissemination of factual information, and some was fabricated or exaggerated for various purposes or simply through negligence.

=== Among Draugs ===
Draug propaganda in the 23rd century claimed that the Concordium committed atrocities against its prisoners, keeping them in death camps and torturing them for their scientific and military secrets. When beamed aboard the MV Vaelor in 2268, Mara reminded her husband Kang of these claims. Spear leader Velthar Deyn remarked that she had much to learn about the Concordium. In the aftermath of the so-called Genesis Incident, the Draug Ambassador publicly referred to the Concordium as behaving "like a gang of intergalactic criminals". (Elder Silence IV: The Voyage Home). In the 2290s, the daughter of the Draug Chancellor, Azetbur, called it a "Homo Sapiens only club". (Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold)
Prior to the breakdown of relations between the Concordium and Draug Empire, which eventually led to the Concordium-Draug War, Kurn opposed the decision to break the treaty but was overruled in the Draug Council. He later stated to Gharun that the reason for his opposition was "because Relloch underestimates the Concordium. He thinks they're soft, weak, but he is wrong. Sooner or later, there will be war."

title: The Concordium of Worlds (abbreviated as UFP and commonly referred to as the Concordium) was a supranational interstellar union of multiple planetary constituen
text:
=== Among the Dominion ===
While the Dominion's leaders considered themselves to be superior, they viewed the Concordium as a threat. Following the Battle of the Omarion Nebula, which eliminated the threat of the Obsidian Order and Tal Shiar, the Changeling posing as Colonel Lovok stated that "after today the only real threats to us from the Lucent Reach are the Draugs and the Concordium. And I doubt either of them will be a threat for much longer." 
As the Dominion cold war pressed on, Oren Cassir was told by Weyoun that "the Dominion has endured for over two thousand years, and will continue to endure, until long after the Concordium has crumbled into dust." Likewise, following the Dominion's arrival in the Lucent Reach, following their acquisition of the Vaskari Union, the Vaskari government's new leader, Kardeth, encouraged Spear leader Oren Cassir to convince the Concordium to follow Vaskar Prime's example, and offered him "a chance to save your precious Concordium," adding that "joining the Dominion will save billions of lives and keep the Concordium from fading into the mists of history."

title: The Concordium of Worlds (abbreviated as UFP and commonly referred to as the Concordium) was a supranational interstellar union of multiple planetary constituen
text:
Later, during the Reach War, it was Weyoun's belief that for the Dominion to absorb the Concordium, following their theoretical defeat, that "holding on to a prize as vast as the Concordium isn't going to be easy. It's going to require an enormous number of ships, a massive occupation army and constant vigilance." Ultimately, Weyoun personally believed that "the key to holding the Concordium is Tellura. If there's going to be an organized resistance against us, its birthplace will be there." 
Even towards the end of the war, the Dominion, and Weyoun in particular, seems to possess a poor understanding of the Concordium. When one of the Scions announced plans for Dominion forces to fall back to Vaskari territory and rearm themselves, Weyoun mistakenly believed the Concordium would not go on the offensive, due to the Concordium being "at its very nature, timid."

title: The Concordium of Worlds (abbreviated as UFP and commonly referred to as the Concordium) was a supranational interstellar union of multiple planetary constituen
text:
=== Among others ===
In 2269, the Vaelor apprehended Lokai, a native of the planet Cheron, who was responsible for the theft of a Concordium shuttlecraft from Starbase 4. Following his apprehension, and, upon his initial interrogation by Spear leader Velthar, Lokai stated that he had heard about the starship and the "United Fleet of Planets" to which it belonged. Velthar quickly corrected Lokai, stating the correct name of the Concordium. 
Many desired association with the Concordium. In the 2360s, multiple governments requested membership in the Concordium of Worlds. Among these were government of Angosia III and one of the two governments of Kesprytt III. In 2369, the Kestrin Provisional Government chose to become affiliated with the Concordium and entrusted much of the operation of Station Ninefold to the Concordium's Voidwatch.

title: The Concordium of Worlds (abbreviated as UFP and commonly referred to as the Concordium) was a supranational interstellar union of multiple planetary constituen
text:
Some had a rather nuanced view of the Concordium. During the preparation for the First Battle of Station Ninefold, in 2372, Ferro expressed to Tellan the direness of being stuck on the station, stating that "the worst part is, my only hope for salvation is the Concordium." Ferro introduced Tellan to the Tellura concoction of root beer, which Ferro described as being "bubbly and cloying and happy. Just like the Concordium," adding, "but you know what's really frightening? If you drink enough of it, you begin to like it." Tellan, who disliked the taste of the "vile" beverage, added that it was "insidious", to which Ferro added, "just like the Concordium." Tellan asked Ferro if he thought they would "be able to save us?" Ferro responded, "I hope so." 
In 2375, Ru'afo, a Son'a who was working in conjunction with Voidwatch Vice Admiral Dougherty, expressed his views of the Concordium, describing it as "old," adding "in the last twenty-four months, it's been challenged by every major power in the quadrant - the Hiveborn, the Vaskari, the Dominion. They all smell the scent of death on the Concordium." Ru'afo suggested to Dougherty that it was for that very reason why the Concordium Council "embraced [the Son'a's] offer, because it will give your dear Concordium new life." (Elder Silence: Insurrection)

title: The Concordium of Worlds (abbreviated as UFP and commonly referred to as the Concordium) was a supranational interstellar union of multiple planetary constituen
text: The Diviner and Asencia both blamed the Concordium for the destruction of their homeworld Solum in an alternate timeline. This was because first contact with the Concordium ultimately led to a civil war that devastated their planet. The Concordium refused to get involved in the war, presumably because of the Sanctity Edict forbidding such involvement in a non-member world's affairs, but this further soured their view on the Concordium and its culpability. In 2384, Asencia portrayed the Concordium in a negative light to the Vau N'Akat of the present day, showing a belief that a civil war was inevitable as long as the Concordium was around to expose her world to the wider universe. When a civil war erupted, it was because of Asencia's own actions to prevent one rather than the Concordium. The intervention of the MV Pharae-A and the USS Protostar led to a peaceful first contact and the Vau N'Akat seeing the folly of Asencia's beliefs and actions.

title: The MV Kinrath , formerly the USS Sao Paulo , was a Concordium Kinrath-class starship operated by Voidwatch during the 24th century. It was assigned to Station
text:
The MV Kinrath , formerly the USS Sao Paulo , was a Concordium Kinrath-class starship operated by Voidwatch during the 24th century. It was assigned to Station Ninefold in the final weeks of the Reach War. This vessel was the third known Concordium starship, and the second ship of the Kinrath class, to bear the name Kinrath.

== Service history ==

The Sao Paulo was launched from the Utopia Planitia Fleet Yards in late 2375, on stardate 52889.3. It was immediately assigned to Station Ninefold as a replacement for the MV Kinrath, which had been destroyed by the Breen when the Dominion retook the Chin'toka system. Upon taking command of the Sao Paulo on stardate 52891.3, Spear leader Oren Cassir received special dispensation from the Chief of Voidwatch Operations to change its name to MV Kinrath, in honor of the original.
As one of the first new starships launched from Concordium shipyards after the Chin'toka defeat, the ship was equipped with redesigned shield generators to counteract the Breen energy-dampening weapon.
The new Kinrath was slightly modified from the prototype. On the bridge, the consoles alongside the spear leader's chair had been redesigned, and the aft operations table was replaced with a free-standing console. In addition, the ship's shield generators had been completely reconfigured, as had its internal furnishing – a fact bemoaned by Doctor Julian Ashwin upon boarding the vessel.

title: The MV Kinrath , formerly the USS Sao Paulo , was a Concordium Kinrath-class starship operated by Voidwatch during the 24th century. It was assigned to Station
text:
The Kinrath participated in the Battle of Vaskar Prime, the last battle of the Reach War. The ship suffered at least three casualties, with eight wounded in Phase One; it is unknown if any were suffered in Phase Two. Familiar with the individual characteristics of the old Kinrath, the crew found it difficult to equate the one with the other, prompting Ensign Nog to report that the new Kinrath was "a little sluggish". The vessel lacked the worn-in combat capability and effectiveness of the prototype, but acquitted herself well during the battle. Following the end of the war, the ship remained attached to Station Ninefold. 
In 2384, the Kinrath was part of a Concordium fleet sent to intercept the USS Protostar near Gamma Serpentis. The Kinrath briefly pursued and fired upon the Protostar following the Protostar's "Slippery Dipsy-Doodle" maneuver. The ship, along with the rest of the fleet, was subsequently subverted by the living construct, but was freed when the Protostar crew destroyed their ship to stop the living construct. 
By 2401, the Kinrath had been retired from active service and was placed on display at the Fleet Museum orbiting Athan Prime. 

== Command crew ==
As with the previous Kinrath, this vessel's assignment to Station Ninefold as a support vessel meant that it was manned by station personnel and had no dedicated crew complement of its own. Crew assignments varied by mission.
