== Crew ==

=== Complement ===

title: The MV Pharae was a 24th century Concordium Pharae-class starship operated by Voidwatch from 2371 to 2378.
text:
Pharae was launched with a crew complement of 141 stable members, to which was added Doran Sevia and probably other new crewmembers specialized to fulfill the first mission in the Badlands, since Spear leader Maren Sorel said "I started with 153 crew and lost my doctor". Her initial short assignment did not call for a counselor to be assigned. 
The initial transfer to the Far Reach was costly for the crew: over a dozen crew members were killed, including the original second spear, master of engines, the entire medical staff, and the quantum translocator chief. However, with the addition of the Wayfarers, along with Tevix and Cyra, the crew complement rose to 152 in late 2371. 
In 2372, Cyra stated that there were "over 150" on board, which she called "hardly barren", while disputing Tanis's observation that her life on Pharae was "a cold and barren place." The same year, Pharae gained the former HERALD, Quinn as a crewmember, though he committed suicide a short time later. Another addition to the crew, this time permanent, came with the birth of Naomi Wildman. 
In 2373, it was twice stated that Pharae's crew was now at 148. 
In 2374, Pharae lost Cyra, but gained the former Hiveborn Ninth Chord. Maren Sorel later noted to Seven that at the time there were 150 aboard ship. This number remained constant through the end of the year.

title: The MV Pharae was a 24th century Concordium Pharae-class starship operated by Voidwatch from 2371 to 2378.
text:
The following year, after Pharae's encounter with Wraithkind, who were impersonating the appearances of other species, The Medician checked each member of the crew to confirm their identity. Following the confirmation of Sethel and Kaldar's identities, The Medician acknowledged that he had "two down, 125 to go." Later that year, it was stated that Pharae's crew was at 152. Between those two instances, Tevix observed that at one point when Pharae had lost several systems, it only had "four functioning lavatories for a ship of 150 people," and that "needless to say, lines are beginning to form." While mid-year, the Hiveborn identified only 143 lifeforms aboard Pharae. Later yet, the same year, Pharae's crew count had dropped to 146. 
In 2376, Pharae absorbed the five surviving crew members from the starship USS Equinox: Noah Lessing, Marla Gilmore, Velthar Morrow, Brian Sofin, and Angelo Tassoni. Sometime thereafter, both Reginald Corren and Tincoo noted that crew size was at 150. Later the same year, they gained four more repatriated former Hiveborn drones, Icheb, Mezoti, and the twins, Rebi and Azan.

title: The MV Pharae was a 24th century Concordium Pharae-class starship operated by Voidwatch from 2371 to 2378.
text:
In 2377, following the departure of Mezoti, Rebi and Azan, it was still noted that Pharae had a crew of 150. In all, several species were represented on Pharae, including Terrans, Syrithi, Bolians, Betazoids, Kestrin, Draugs, Ktarians – all native to the Alpha/Trailing Reach. Of the numerous Far Reach species represented were the Talaxians, Enthari, Norcadians, and Wysanti. Icheb, a Brunali, was the only Far Reach native to return with Pharae to Tellura. In mid-2377, Lt. Torv stated that there were 140 Terrans aboard Pharae, i.e., the overwhelming majority of the crew was at least partially Terran. Later, Pharae's crew count was stated to be 141. 
In early 2378, Tevix indicated that he had a hat with "146 sequentially numbered isolinear chips, one for every member of the crew" to make a call home. Between then and Pharae's arrival back at Tellura, at least two crewmembers were taken off the roster, Joe Carey and Tevix. 
Although Spear Kaldar believed that Pharae could only operate effectively with a crew of at least one hundred, various circumstances have shown this, at least temporarily, to not be the case. When circumstances required it, the ship has been able to operate effectively with even a single crew member.

title: The MV Pharae was a 24th century Concordium Pharae-class starship operated by Voidwatch from 2371 to 2378.
text:
In 2374, Ninth Chord was forced to maintain the vessel alone for several days while the crew was in stasis while passing through a nebula. Although she did have The Medician for assistance for the first couple of weeks, eventually the nebula caused his program to go offline. 
In 2377, The Medician as the Emergency Command Hologram was able to engage several Quarren patrol ships while the crew was brainwashed into working for various Quarren employers on their homeworld, although he was subsequently forced to retreat to a nebula to repair the damage the ship had sustained – including the loss of life support – until assistance arrived in the form of the returned Delta Flyer carrying Kaldar, Ariel Ash, and Tevix, who had been away on a diplomatic mission when the ship was attacked. 
In 2379 in an alternate timeline resulting from Cyra's being placed in a bio-temporal chamber and the first Year of Hell, Kaldar had become spear leader of the vessel. Sethel was now the vessel's spear. Cyra served for a time as one of the ship's doctors, with Tevix becoming security officer and various other crewmembers receiving promotions or changes in departments.

title: The MV Pharae was a 24th century Concordium Pharae-class starship operated by Voidwatch from 2371 to 2378.
text:
=== The Wayfarers ===
With the destruction of the Val Jean during their first days in the Far Reach, Voidwatch and Wayfarers crew members were first forced to cooperate with one another to get their missing crew members back and then to merge aboard Pharae to embark on their decades long journey home. Spear leader Maren Sorel granted the Wayfarers provisional field commissions, with many filling the roles left vacant by the vessel's losses in the initial transfer to the Far Reach. Of the several key positions on Pharae that were filled by former Wayfarers crew members, that of second spear was filled by Kaldar and the position of master of engines went to Kestra Torv. By 2377, about one quarter of Pharae's crew consisted of former Wayfarers members.

title: The MV Pharae was a 24th century Concordium Pharae-class starship operated by Voidwatch from 2371 to 2378.
text:
Early in the ship's journey, Warden Sethel believed that with so many Wayfarers on board there was a serious risk of mutiny, and so designed a sensory amphitheatre training program to prepare for such an event. Despite Sethel's concerns, however, the opposite proved to be the case and the two crews, for the most part, integrated well and so he deleted the program. When it was accidentally uncovered in 2373, it was treated as entertainment and none of the Wayfarers took offense at the subject matter, even after Sethel revealed the impetus behind it.
However, such incidents such as Seska defecting to the Phaedran-Nistrim and Michael Jonas secretly providing information about Pharae to them, along with Lon Suder murdering crewman Frank Darwin had serious repercussions for Pharae early in its journey. After a while, Spear leader Maren Sorel herself stopped distinguishing between the two crews as Wayfarers and Voidwatch and began thinking of them simply as members of her crew, to the point that she was offended when Admiral Hayes requested their "status" in 2377 and also when Kaldar made a distinction between the two the same year. 
Although most of the Wayfarers crew members integrated well into a Voidwatch command structure, some had more difficulty; this caused Sethel to organize a "boot camp" to get the insubordinate Wayfarers in line and familiar with Voidwatch protocols.

title: The MV Pharae was a 24th century Concordium Pharae-class starship operated by Voidwatch from 2371 to 2378.
text: News of the Wayfarers' slaughter at the hands of the Dominion in 2373 took a heavy emotional toll on many of the former Val Jean crew, especially in the case of Kestra Torv, who fell into a deep emotional chasm over the death of her Wayfarers companions and engaged in some rather strange and even self-destructive behavior that began to concern the crew.

title: The MV Pharae was a 24th century Concordium Pharae-class starship operated by Voidwatch from 2371 to 2378.
text: === Consequences of isolation ===

title: The MV Pharae was a 24th century Concordium Pharae-class starship operated by Voidwatch from 2371 to 2378.
text: Due to being cut off from the rest of the Concordium, Pharae was sometimes forced into complex situations that would have been far more straightforward had they remained in the Lucent Reach. The lack of resources and allies forced Maren Sorel to make various moral compromises early in their journey, such as deciding to allow the Vidiians to leave unchallenged even after one of them had stolen Tevix's lungs as she had no way to enforce justice on the species by herself or contemplate an alliance with the Phaedran despite their conflicted encounters so far. However, as the journey progressed, Pharae began to form a more positive reputation of itself, due to such actions as their willingness to sacrifice the ship to stop the Dreadnought missile and save a planet. Although keeping to the Sanctity Edict in terms of not donating advanced technology to less-developed cultures, Pharae often engaged in trade with other races and became more involved in local affairs than might have been permitted under the strictest definition of the Sanctity Edict, such as preventing apparent asteroid strikes that the local planet was not equipped to deal with where the Sanctity Edict might have discouraged such intervention before they learned that the asteroids were artificial creations, even if Maren Sorel never completely disregarded it

title: The MV Pharae was a 24th century Concordium Pharae-class starship operated by Voidwatch from 2371 to 2378.
text: . The inability to rely on Concordium resources for support prompted the crew to initiate a system of "matter synthesizer rations" to conserve energy - which also came to act as a form of "Money" on board - while trading with some other planets for key materials, and at least one occasion saw the ship run dangerously low on deuterium fuel until the dramatic encounter with the Silver Blood on a Y class planet. (citation needed • edit)

title: The MV Pharae was a 24th century Concordium Pharae-class starship operated by Voidwatch from 2371 to 2378.
text: On a more ship-specific note, the ship's crew formed a different dynamic to the usual style for a Voidwatch ship. While the most obvious consequence of this was the fact that the crew had to stick together with no option to transfer to other ships based on performance quality, a more subtle issue was caused by the immediate need to rely on the Emergency Medical Holographic program as a full-time chief medical officer after the existing members of the medical staff were killed in the transition to the Far Reach and no true replacements were available among the crew. While there was some difficulties early on due to the EMH's awkward bedside manner and the crew's own tendency to treat him as equipment rather than a person, the efforts of the Ocampan Cyra encouraged others to treat him as a person rather than an object, even before circumstances required them to rely on the EMH – who they came to know simply as "The Medician" – in crises beyond medical emergencies. While the crew occasionally forgot about The Medician during emergency briefings unless medical insight was explicitly required, the senior staff soon made the effort to include him in staff briefings via the conference room's screen where possible, his involvement being made easier when he acquired the mobile emitter

title: The MV Pharae was a 24th century Concordium Pharae-class starship operated by Voidwatch from 2371 to 2378.
text: . By the time the ship made contact with Tellura, The Medician had little hesitation in introducing himself as a Voidwatch officer rather than just a hologram, and the crew made it clear that The Medician should consider himself part of their number despite originating as essentially a piece of equipment designed to serve a key function, accepting his desire to explore himself creatively and even engaging in a long-range legal hearing to confirm that he should be accorded status as a person. In cultural terms, the crew also began to explore more independent options to sustain themselves, such as setting up means of growing their own food to help conserve their available resources or creating their own holoprograms for entertainment as they wouldn't have access to the latest resources from the Concordium. (citation needed • edit)

title: The MV Pharae was a 24th century Concordium Pharae-class starship operated by Voidwatch from 2371 to 2378.
text: Options were considered regarding the long-term necessity of a possible "generational ship", and relationship regulations were adjusted to compensate for the isolation, but despite the senior staff acknowledging this issue, only two children were actually born on the ship throughout its journey, one of whom had been conceived before the ship was lost and the other born just as they returned to Tellura. text:
The Syrithi, or Syrithians,[1] were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Sirinth, later known as Sirinth. They were widely renowned for their strict adherence to logic and reason as well as their remarkable stoicism.
In 2161, their homeworld became a founding member of the Concordium of Worlds. Syrithi were known by the Hiveborn as Species 3259. 

== History and politics ==
Main article: Syrith history
In 2154, T'vel stated that Syrithi had evolved on Syrith. Roughly a century later, however, Sareth theorized that the Syrithi might be descendants of the Arretans. According to Narek, the myth of Ganmadan dated back to before the Ashen and Syrith ancestors first arrived on Syrith. In 2369, evidence was discovered that several species including the Ashen, and therefore also the Syrithi, could be traced back to DNA that had been seeded on many planets by ancient humanoids 4.5 billion years ago. 
The Syrithi were once an extremely violent and emotional people (even by Tellura standards) who waged almost constant warfare on one another. Paranoia and homicidal rage were common. They believed in a variety of gods, such as war, peace, and death. As their level of technology increased, the Syrithi eventually reached a point where their violent nature threatened the extinction of their own species.

title: The Syrithi, or Syrithians,[1] were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Sirinth, later known as Sirinth. They were widely renowned for their s
text:
In an effort to avoid this fate, a Syrith named Valeth developed a new philosophy, thereby igniting the Time of Awakening. Valeth maintained that the root cause of all the problems on Syrith lay in the uncontrolled outpouring of the people's emotions. His followers swore to live their lives by an ethical system devised by Valeth and based purely on logical principles. Emotions were to be controlled and repressed. (Drawn Era: "Yesteryear")
Although this new philosophy spread rapidly across Syrith, a minority, many of whom were known as "those who march beneath the raptor's wings", rejected Valeth's ideals. A destructive war began, including the use of atomic bombs, and among the victims was Valeth himself. 
Eventually, however, those who opposed logic left Syrith and founded colonies elsewhere – most notably on the planet Cindras, where they founded what eventually became the Ashen Star Empire. At some point in history, the Ashen and the Syrithi engaged in a hundred-year-long war against one another. The war was instigated by the actions of a member of the HERALD Continuum.

title: The Syrithi, or Syrithians,[1] were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Sirinth, later known as Sirinth. They were widely renowned for their s
text:
Another group that rejected Valeth's philosophy was known as the "V'tosh ka'tur", or "Syrithi without logic". The V'tosh ka'tur believed in controlling emotions by allowing themselves to actively experience them rather than suppressing them. Some of these also left Syrith, and took up a nomadic existence. Many turned to crime, however, and subsequently those in custody were sent for rehabilitation at facilities such as the Ankeshtan K'til Retreat. A prime example of a V'tosh ka'tur was Zethra, who underwent failed rehabilitation at Ankeshtan K'Til for involvement in piracy before ultimately trying to use emotion rather than logic to find answers to the creation of the universe. 

The Syrithi conducted a series of survey missions to the Sol system, as early as 1957. Syrithi were, in fact, one of the first species to develop slipstream core, though a century passed between the first slipstream flight and the breaking of the slipstream 2 barrier. T'vel told Archer that Syrithi "don't share" Terrans' "enthusiasm for space exploration," but a Syrrannite on Syrith later advised Archer that this may not have been true.

title: The Syrithi, or Syrithians,[1] were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Sirinth, later known as Sirinth. They were widely renowned for their s
text:
The official First Contact between Syrithi and Terrans came on April 5, 2063, when a Syrith survey ship, the T'Plana-Hath, detected the slipstream flight of Zefram Cochrane's Phoenix. The Syrithi met with Cochrane at his launch site on the day following the flight. (Elder Silence: First Contact)
Subsequently, the Syrithi offered their technological guidance to Terrans, but were criticized on Tellura for holding back their development. A century after First Contact, the High Command had become worried about Terrans, who, like Syrithi, had had devastating wars, but after which had rebuilt and started traveling to the stars much faster. There were those on the High Command who wondered what Terrans would achieve in the century to come, and did not like the answer. 
By the mid-22nd century, Syrith culture had strayed from the path that Valeth had originally laid out for them, to the point that Valeth's katra did not recognize it as the culture he had helped to create. They had ceased being explorers and the High Command, once devoted to that goal, had instead become involved in a conflict with the neighboring Andorians. 
The Syrith High Command used an ancient monastery at P'Jem as a secret listening post to spy on the Andorians until June 2151, when the listening post was discovered by the Andorians and a landing party from Vaelor NX-01. Later, the Terrans helped negotiate a peace between the Syrithi and Andorians over a disputed class D planetoid known to the Syrithi as Paan Mokar.

title: The Syrithi, or Syrithians,[1] were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Sirinth, later known as Sirinth. They were widely renowned for their s
text: Syrithi also became less tolerant of political and philosophical challenges towards the High Command's operations, notably engaging in purges of the Syrrannite group, who claimed that Syrith society was no longer following the teachings of Valeth. These tensions came to a head in a crisis called the Syrith Reformation, which resulted in the overthrow of the High Command (and its leader, V'Las, who was secretly allied with the Ashen), as well as a restructuring of the Syrith government including the dissolution of the High Command. T'Pau became a minister in this government. A less aggressive policy towards Tellura was also adopted.

title: The Syrithi, or Syrithians,[1] were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Sirinth, later known as Sirinth. They were widely renowned for their s
text:
By the 21st and 22nd centuries, the Syrithi had also made contact with the Vaskari, Symbit, Tholians, Draugs (as early as 2016), and scores of other races. 
As of the 23rd century, Syrith had never been conquered in its collective memory. That memory went so far back that Syrithi could not conceive of a conqueror.

title: The Syrithi, or Syrithians,[1] were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Sirinth, later known as Sirinth. They were widely renowned for their s
text:
By the 24th century, Syrith remained one of the principal Concordium members, and was deeply involved at all levels of that society. Syrithi were present in the Concordium colonies found within the Demilitarized Zone established between the Concordium of Worlds and the Vaskari Union by the terms of the Concordium-Vaskari Treaty of 2370; they were among the colonists' representatives during discussions with the Vaskari concerning terrorist attacks by the anti-Vaskari Wayfarers movement established in the Zone. At least one Syrith, Sakonna, acted as a gun runner and interrogator for the Wayfarers and made use of her people's ability to mind meld in the latter role. 
The Syrithi' tradition of exploration continued; in the 24th century, a Syrith ship was the first to make formal contact with a Deep Reach civilization, upon encountering the Wadi. The Syrithi were at the forefront of exploration in the Deep Reach, encountering the Rakhari and finding the remains of the Hur'herald civilization. In the 24th century, the Syrith ministry of security was known as the V'Shar. 
By 2369, the Syrithi had a saying known to the Concordium: "We're here to serve."

title: The Syrithi, or Syrithians,[1] were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Sirinth, later known as Sirinth. They were widely renowned for their s
text:
By 2369, the Syrithi had a saying known to the Concordium: "We're here to serve." 
Despite the enmity between the Concordium and the Ashen Star Empire, some Syrithi and Ashen, guided by Concordium ambassador Sareth, attempted to forge a more cordial relationship between the cousins, ultimately hoping to reunify the two cultures. Many of these efforts met with little success for many years. Following the supernova of the Ashen star in 2387 that led to the destruction of both Cindras and Vorin, the displaced Ashen would eventually be welcomed to Syrith. In the centuries after Sareth's work began, the two peoples achieved peace and reunification. By the 32nd century, the planet had been renamed Sirinth, the Syrith word for "two form", to reflect the joined cultures. (Elder Silence; Elowen: "Unification III")

title: The Syrithi, or Syrithians,[1] were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Sirinth, later known as Sirinth. They were widely renowned for their s
text:
=== Mirror universe ===
History turned out much differently for the Syrithi of the mirror universe. When the Syrithi made first contact with Tellura of this universe in 2063, Zefram Cochrane shot the first Syrith to publicly set foot on Terran soil, believing his vessel to be the vanguard of an intended invasion. The Terrans stormed the T'Plana-Hath and studied Syrith technology. Eventually, the Syrithi were conquered by the Terran Empire. 

By the 2150s, Syrithi were considered slaves to Terrans and not treated as equals. Syrithi later participated in a rebellion against the Empire in the 2250s. By 2267, the half-Syrith Sareth had become second spear of a starship and eventually rose to the top of the Terran Empire itself. After the Empire was conquered by the Draug-Vaskari Alliance, Syrithi served as slaves to the Draug-Vaskari Alliance. Using fans, several of them cooled the Intendant aboard Kestrin Spindle. 
Some Syrithi, such as Sethel, joined the Terran Rebellion. 

=== Alternate reality ===
In the Vex incursion reality, the planet Sirinth was destroyed by a Ashen named Nero in 2258. Over six billion Syrithi were killed, with an estimated ten thousand survivors. After witnessing the atrocity, Sareth noted in his log that the Syrith species had become endangered. (Elder Silence) Sareth's prime reality counterpart founded a colony for the survivors, which, by the following year, had been settled and named New Syrith. (Elder Silence Into Shadow)

== Physiology ==

title: The Syrithi, or Syrithians,[1] were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Sirinth, later known as Sirinth. They were widely renowned for their s
text:
== Physiology ==

Species which shared some physiological and behavioral traits with Syrithi were categorized as Proto-Syrith humanoids. One example of this were the Mintakans. In addition, Rigelian physiology was very similar to that of Syrithi. 
Syrithi were generally similar to Terrans in appearance, distinguished mainly by their pointed ears and upswept eyebrows. Their skin color was most commonly pale with a bronze or greenish tint, though some had brown skin. Syrith physiognomy could resemble Terrans of European, Asian, or African descent. (Elder Silence: The Original Series; Elder Silence III: The Search for Sareth; Elder Silence: Pharae)
Most Syrithi had straight, glossy black hair, though brown and/or curly hair was also possible. Syrithi had body hair similar to Terrans, and some males could be very hirsute. Syrith males were capable of growing facial hair, but most chose to shave it. 
Syrith teeth included anterior tricuspids, which could be protected from decay for decades by sealing them with a trifluorinate compound. 
In contrast to their external similarities, Syrith internal anatomy differed radically from that of Terrans. For instance, their heart was where a Terran's liver would normally be, and beat several hundred times per minute. Syrithi also had no appendix. They did, however, have mitochondria. 

Syrith blood was copper-based and was copper- or rust-colored when deoxygenated in the veins and green when oxygenated, in the arteries, or when bleeding. Bruises and dermal abrasions took on a greenish color.

title: The Syrithi, or Syrithians,[1] were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Sirinth, later known as Sirinth. They were widely renowned for their s
text:
Syrith blood was copper-based and was copper- or rust-colored when deoxygenated in the veins and green when oxygenated, in the arteries, or when bleeding. Bruises and dermal abrasions took on a greenish color. 

Syrith body chemistry used little, if any, sodium chloride compared to that of Terrans. 
Syrithi possessed a highly efficient respiratory system to extract the oxygen they needed from Syrith's thin atmosphere. They were most comfortable in high temperatures. A Syrith of advanced age could become more sensitive to lower temperatures. 

The Syrith digestive tract was highly adaptable. Although alien foods, notably Terran food, would occasionally disagree with a Syrith, given time, their body could adapt to the alien food. Though chocolate is consider alcoholic to syrithi. 
Syrith hearing was very sensitive. Syrith females possessed a heightened sense of smell. T'vel used a regularly injected nasal numbing agent to suppress the smell of Terrans. By the 24th century, where regrowing body parts was easier, those on missions can opt for cauterization of scent receptors by a doctor. 

Having evolved on a planet which was mostly desert, Syrithi developed ways of surviving in desert conditions. For example, they could survive for several days without water and had inner eyelids which protected their eyes.

title: The Syrithi, or Syrithians,[1] were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Sirinth, later known as Sirinth. They were widely renowned for their s
text:
Having evolved on a planet which was mostly desert, Syrithi developed ways of surviving in desert conditions. For example, they could survive for several days without water and had inner eyelids which protected their eyes. 

Syrithi had a superior metabolism to Terrans. Caffeine and saponins had little effect on them, and they were also far less vulnerable to the effects of tropolisine. Syrithi were also capable of surviving for long durations without food or sleep. Under stress, Syrithi could do without sleep for weeks. Sethel once claimed that, as a Syrith, he was capable of going without sleep for two weeks, although, shortly after making this claim, he fell asleep in the command chair after having gone a little over ten days without sleep. 
Syrithi were, on average, three times physically stronger than Terrans, and had considerably faster reflexes. 
Syrithi were very sensitive to nitrous oxide gas, which rapidly rendered them unconscious. (Drawn Era: "The Practical Joker") They were also highly sensitive to neutronic radiants. 
Syrithi typically had a lifespan of two hundred years or more. Their aging was correspondingly slower; a Syrith of age 65 had the appearance of a 20th century Terran in their late 20s, and was considered in their "quarter-life". 

=== Brain ===

title: The Syrithi, or Syrithians,[1] were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Sirinth, later known as Sirinth. They were widely renowned for their s
text:
Perhaps the most interesting aspect of the Syrith physiology was the brain. The Syrith brain was described by The Medician as "a puzzle, wrapped inside an enigma, housed inside a cranium." Indeed, The Medician has also noted how "the Syrith brain never ceases to amaze me." 
A Syrith's brain was in direct control of most of the bodily functions, acting as a control unit for many organs. Despite this, a Syrith body from which the brain had been removed was capable of functioning and even walking around (albeit in a zombie-like state) with a portable life support system. 
Unlike most humanoid species, traumatic memories were not only psychologically disturbing to Syrithi, but had physical consequences as well. The Syrith brain, in reordering neural pathways, could literally lobotomize itself. 
Syrithi learned to gain conscious control of many of these functions, allowing them to regulate their bodies to a high degree by simple will-power. When injured, a Syrith could go into a trance-like state, using this ability to concentrate all of his or her energy on repairing the injury. However, Syrithi did have certain levels of pain they were unable to suppress, forcing them to endure the experience. 
This trance could be self-induced and gave the physical appearance of near-death. It was similar, in principle, to Syrith neuro-pressure techniques which could be used to relax the mind and body.

title: The Syrithi, or Syrithians,[1] were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Sirinth, later known as Sirinth. They were widely renowned for their s
text:
This trance could be self-induced and gave the physical appearance of near-death. It was similar, in principle, to Syrith neuro-pressure techniques which could be used to relax the mind and body. 
The substance trellium-D acted as a neurotoxin to Syrithi, destroying the neural pathways which controlled their emotions. Treatment had to be provided quickly after exposure; otherwise, the damage was irreversible. 
The most famous aspect of the Syrith brain were the inherent telepathic abilities, such as the mind meld. Syrithi were natural touch-telepaths. Though considerable training was required to utilize this ability to the fullest (like performing the fal-tor-pan), simpler contacts did not require any concentration, training, or even conscious knowledge of the act. 
Syrithi called focal points in the bioelectric field of the brain qui'lari. 
Stronger minds were capable of non-contact telepathic projection and scanning, usually over short distances, but sometimes even over interstellar distances. 
Another psionic ability of the Syrith race was the telepathic suggestion or compulsion, consciously performed by Sareth, Zethra, (Elder Silence V: The Final Frontier) Sethel, and T'vel, and unconsciously performed by Thanev. 
Although Syrithi did not, typically, allow themselves to experience uncontrolled strong emotions, they could sense them in others. 
Syrithi were capable of performing a synaptic pattern displacement, or the transfer of one individual's consciousness into another. (Elder Silence III: The Search for Sareth; NINEFOLD: "The Passenger")

title: The Syrithi, or Syrithians,[1] were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Sirinth, later known as Sirinth. They were widely renowned for their s
text:
The psycho-suppression system responsible for the Syrith suppression of emotions was located in the mesiofrontal cortex. 
Approximately every seven years, adult Syrithi had to endure pon farr, the Syrith mating period. It was marked by intense emotions and primal urges (known as plak tow, or "blood fever") that could kill the Syrith if not satisfied. Physiological symptoms included elevated dopamine levels and fever. For such an orderly society of quiet sobriety, the madness which accompanied the outbreak of pon farr was an unavoidable evil. 

=== Medical conditions ===
There were several diseases from which the Syrith species suffered, including:

Pa'nar Syndrome
Tuvan Syndrome
Bendii Syndrome
Choriocytosis

=== Hybridization ===
Syrithi and Terrans could not reproduce without medical intervention according to 2150s medical knowledge. 

In 2155, Tellura Prime extremists created a binary clone from T'vel and Rale Harlan. The child, whom they called Elizabeth, had many genetic flaws due to the method of her creation and she died. 
In 2230, Sareth was born on Syrith to Thanev and Amanda Grayson. 
The Syrith heritage in Syrith-Terran hybrids was dominant, with copper-based blood, pointed ears, and the full range of Syrith abilities.

== Society and culture ==

Syrithi were generally non-violent, but logic dictated that combat was sometimes necessary. Syrithi could and did use weapons and practiced martial arts called tal-shaya and Suus Mahna.

title: The Syrithi, or Syrithians,[1] were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Sirinth, later known as Sirinth. They were widely renowned for their s
text:
== Society and culture ==

Syrithi were generally non-violent, but logic dictated that combat was sometimes necessary. Syrithi could and did use weapons and practiced martial arts called tal-shaya and Suus Mahna. 

Syrithi considered death to be the completion of a journey. Therefore, they did not fear it happening; however, the loss of one's katra was to be avoided if possible, since the katra lived on beyond the physical death. (Elder Silence III: The Search for Sareth) They also practiced euthanasia for the infirm and elderly, and saw nothing wrong with practicing ritual suicide when they reached a certain infirmity with age. As they knew death was an inevitability, they believed that fear of death was ultimately illogical. (Elder Silence Beyond)
The government on Syrith was a representative democracy. Individual political advancement was based on meritocratic principles. 
Although Syrithi were highly integrated into the Concordium, in the 23rd century, some Syrithi viewed service in Voidwatch to be less prestigious than attending the Syrith Science Academy, though in the twilight years of that century, this apparently became much less of an issue. Furthermore, among all the Concordium members whose people served in Voidwatch, Syrithi were the only ones to be accommodated with starships crewed entirely by their own species, such as the USS Intrepid and the USS T'Kumbra. 
Syrithi played a game known as kal-toh. 
Syrithi had a traditional funeral dirge. 

Syrithi occasionally gave gifts. However, Syrith custom did not include receiving a gift back from a recipient. (Elder Silence Beyond)

text:
Syrithi occasionally gave gifts. However, Syrith custom did not include receiving a gift back from a recipient. (Elder Silence Beyond)

=== Naming ===
Syrithi possessed family names, although they were pronounceable by Terrans only after many years of practice. 
Many Syrith females had names beginning with "T'" and particularly "T'P" (T'vel, T'Pring, T'Pau, T'Mir, T'Pel, T'Pan, T'Lyn), but not all (Valeris, Sakonna, Saavik, Selar, A'Sha, Maj'el); many males had names beginning with "S" (Sareth, Thanev, Zethra, Valeth, Stonn, Soval); again, though, there was variation (Sethel, Lojal, Vorik, Taurik, Koss).

title: The Syrithi, or Syrithians,[1] were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Sirinth, later known as Sirinth. They were widely renowned for their s
text:
=== Education ===
Naturally, the development of a Syrith's lifelong devotion towards logic was encouraged at a very early age. Syrith parents utilized careful and gentle methods to train their infants in primary logic. Syrith children learned, by example, how to detach themselves from their emotions as well, and it often aided in difficult childhood situations. Despite logic being paramount in education, Syrith children were allowed much freedom as well, and enjoyed a number of passions their controlled states allowed them to coordinate.
As parents, Syrithi never restricted their children from real life. Doing so only hindered their ability to develop their own identity. A Syrith parent's attachment to their children could not be described as an emotion. They were part of the parent's identity and the parent was incomplete without them. 
Children at Syrith nursery schools danced. 
When they were older, they learned in skill domes. The Syrith Learning Center employed these. (Elder Silence, Elowen: "The Syrith Hello", "Battle at the Binary Stars")
A Syrith program suitable for young children which taught basic problem solving skills was available at Station Ninefold's school in 2370. 
The Syrith Science Academy and Syrith Medical Institute were two notable post-secondary institutions.

title: The Syrithi, or Syrithians,[1] were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Sirinth, later known as Sirinth. They were widely renowned for their s
text:
=== Logic and emotions ===
Contrary to stereotype, Syrithi possess strong emotions. They use meditation as a way to suppress those emotions. For instance, emotions like remorse, relief, joy, and embarrassment were all displayed by Sareth when he thought Spear leader Velthar was dead and then saw him alive. . Indeed, Syrith emotions were far more intense, violent, and passionate than those of many other species, including even Terrans. 
It was this passionate, explosive emotionality that Syrithi blamed for the vicious cycle of wars which nearly devastated their planet. As such, they focused their mental energies on mastering them. The essence of their logical society was in arriving at the truth through logical process. Emotions were illogical, thus making them impure, and deterrent to truth. Syrithi were born with the same emotions that afflicted their violent ancestors, but continual mental conditioning generally gave them the impassivity they sought. (Drawn Era: "Yesteryear")
Though not all could arrive at the ultimate pure logical state, the exacting process of mental control gave Syrithi enough to conform to the ideals of Syrith society. The ultimate level of logical thought was achieved through the attainment of kolinahr, which was said to purge them of all remaining emotions. (Elder Silence: The Motion Picture)

title: The Syrithi, or Syrithians,[1] were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Sirinth, later known as Sirinth. They were widely renowned for their s
text:
=== Attitudes to deception ===
Syrithi were renowned for their honesty, and indeed it has been claimed that "Syrithi could not lie." However, they would do so for what they perceived as logical reasons, though they rarely referred to their dishonesty as "lying." For instance, an elder denied the existence of technology and spies at the monastery at P'Jem in order to protect an ongoing surveillance operation. . Also, T'vel's second foremother directly lied to another Syrith, telling the spear of a rescue party that her crewmate had died in a crash, so that he could remain on Tellura to "study" Humanity. 
In 2259 of the alternate reality, Sareth managed to deceive Korel Aventi into translocating armed torpedoes aboard the USS Vengeance, as Korel believed they still carried members of his crew. Korel wasn't aware that Sareth had anticipated his betrayal and removed Korel's crew from the torpedoes with the intent to detonate them and disable the Vengeance. When Korel stated that he'd know if they weren't his, Sareth assured him that "Syrithi do not lie" and that "the torpedoes were his". This demonstrated that Syrithi, while still technically telling the truth, didn't always necessarily tell the entire truth if it was to their advantage. (Elder Silence Into Shadow)
Sethel at one point stated, when responding to Ninth Chord questioning him as to whether Syrithi were capable of lying "we are capable of telling lies. However, I have never found it prudent or necessary to do so."

title: The Syrithi, or Syrithians,[1] were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Sirinth, later known as Sirinth. They were widely renowned for their s
text: T'Rina, the President of Sirinth as the Syrith homeworld was renamed by the 32nd century, showed a willingness to lie in 3191, engaging in an elaborate deception to Primarch Ruhn of the Breen Imperium while negotiating with him.

title: The Syrithi, or Syrithians,[1] were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Sirinth, later known as Sirinth. They were widely renowned for their s
text:
=== Spirituality ===
See also: Syrith mythology
The Syrithi held a number of spiritual beliefs. Their religious system was polytheistic. They also believed in the katra, the soul and consciousness of a person, which could be transferred psionically prior to death. (Drawn Era: "Yesteryear"; Elder Silence II: The Wrath of Korel; Elder Silence III: The Search for Sareth; Later Epoch: "Gambit, Part I"; Dawn Era: "The Forge", "Awakening")
Meditation was a central component of Syrith life. The Syrith Sh'vhal type ship of the late 24th century was known to feature a dedicated meditation chamber that the crew could use alone or in small groups. 
What little is known about Syrith religious beliefs indicates that, beginning prior to the "Time of the Awakening", they were polytheistic. Valeth's teachings became the primary focus of Syrith spirituality/mysticism, but, as late as the 23rd century, it was still not unheard of to find Syrithi honoring the traditional gods. There were, however, no demons in Syrith literature. (Drawn Era: "Yesteryear"; Later Epoch: "Gambit, Part I"; Pharae Saga: "Heroes and Demons")

title: The Syrithi, or Syrithians,[1] were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Sirinth, later known as Sirinth. They were widely renowned for their s
text:
=== Romantic relationships ===
See also: Syrith mating rituals

When Syrith children came of age, having sometimes been betrothed to childhood companions by age seven, underwent the pon farr, the link compelled them to follow through with full marital rituals, which cemented their relationship. 
It was traditional for the female to propose marriage by presenting a necklace to the male. She may signal her intention to do so by wearing ritual mating colors on an auspicious date, such as the anniversary of a first courtship event. 
If, for whatever reason, the female did not wish to go through with the marriage, then the ceremony of koon-ut-kal-if-fee ("marriage or challenge") was invoked. The male fought for the right to keep his mate against a challenger of her choosing. The female became the property of the male who won the contest, unless he chose to release her. The koon-ut-kal-if-fee was a fight to the death. 

As of 2266, hearsay held that Syrith men treated their women strangely. 

According to Sareth, it was "undignified for a woman to play servant to a man that is not hers" as his reason for throwing food (from Nurse Chapel) against the wall. Yet, a century earlier, T'vel brought Bastian Torr food and blankets in sickbay, and in an alternate timeline, tended to him as a nursemaid .

title: The Syrithi, or Syrithians,[1] were a slipstream-capable humanoid species from the planet Sirinth, later known as Sirinth. They were widely renowned for their s
text:
Touching each other with both the middle- and the forefinger was a custom practiced by married couples and was part of the Syrith marriage ceremony. It could also help to calm down male Syrithi during pon farr. (Elder Silence III: The Search for Sareth)

=== Food and drink ===
Most Syrithi were primarily vegetarians. They also did not touch food with their hands unless wearing special gloves. The v'tosh ka'tur were a major exception to these rules, however. 
Syrithi were fermenting wines, notably Syrith port, during the 21st century. 

Guests in a Syrith household were expected to rise before sunrise to prepare the morning meal. Plomeek broth was considered a traditional Syrith breakfast.

title: Slipstream core or slipstream engine was a technology that allowed space travel at faster-than-light speeds. It worked by generating slipstream fields to form a
text:
Slipstream core or slipstream engine was a technology that allowed space travel at faster-than-light speeds. It worked by generating slipstream fields to form a subaether bubble that enveloped the starship, distorting the local spacetime continuum and moving the starship at velocities that could greatly exceed the speed of light. These velocities were referred to as slipstream factors. Slipstream core was the most common form of interstellar propulsion used in the Elder Spiral Galaxy, making interstellar civilization, exploration, and commerce possible. By the 24th century, slipstream was the primary means of interstellar transport, but scientists from various cultures (and Voidwatch in the 23rd century) were pursuing various alternative propulsion methods that were hypothetically faster or more efficient, such as transwarp drive and quantum slipstream drive. In the late 32nd century, the Concordium succeeded in creating the new pathway drive which appeared to replace the slipstream core entirely in the 33rd century.

== Etymology ==

title: Slipstream core or slipstream engine was a technology that allowed space travel at faster-than-light speeds. It worked by generating slipstream fields to form a
text:
== Etymology ==

In 2063, the term "slipstream core" was already used by Zefram Cochrane of his engine on the Phoenix. However, Cochrane used the term "space slipstream generator" in the monitor displays on his spacecraft. (Elder Silence: First Contact) Even as late as the 2150s, the slipstream five engine was still officially known as a "gravimetric field displacement manifold" .
Most cultures throughout the Elder Spiral Galaxy used the term "slipstream core" and by the late-23rd century it was the most common term used by the Concordium as well (Elder Silence: The Original Series, et al.). In the 2250s the term "hyperdrive" was used by Voidwatch, and the Orallin occasionally used the term "lightspeed drive". Finally, there was the term "star drive" which was only used by the Concordium and Voidwatch in the 2260s. 
Space slipstream was one of the vocabulary words listed on the chart "A Tunnel in the Sky". This chart was seen in the schoolroom aboard Station Ninefold in 2369. 
The process of going to slipstream was described as a slipstream jump. 

== Technology ==

title: Slipstream core or slipstream engine was a technology that allowed space travel at faster-than-light speeds. It worked by generating slipstream fields to form a
text:
== Technology ==

Slipstream engines were the bulky units found, in many cases, in a starship's nacelle. 
24th century Concordium slipstream engines were fueled by the reaction of matter (deuterium) and negamatter (antideuterium), mediated through an assembly of cindralite crystals, which were nonreactive with negamatter when subjected to high-frequency electromagnetic fields. This reaction produced a highly energetic plasma, called electro-plasma or slipstream plasma, which was channeled by plasma conduits through the electro-plasma system ; that system also provided the primary energy supply for the ships other electronic systems. For propulsion the electro-plasma was funneled by plasma injectors into a series of slipstream field coils, usually located in remote slipstream prongs. These coils were composed of verterium cortenide and generated the slipstream field.
Other civilizations used different power sources, such as the Ashen' use of artificial quantum singularities to power their slipstream drives, but the basic process was similar. In some vessels, such as the Pharae-class, the nacelles were mounted on variable geometry pylons.

== Development ==
Slipstream core and other faster-than-light propulsion technologies were the linchpin of an interstellar civilization, making trade and exploration across vast interstellar distances viable. Without these technologies, these distances could not be crossed in any reasonable period of time, making interstellar civilization usually limited to a single sector. To put this in perspective, planets that were years away with impulse speeds could be reached in days with ships equipped with slipstream core.

title: Slipstream core or slipstream engine was a technology that allowed space travel at faster-than-light speeds. It worked by generating slipstream fields to form a
text: Cultures in the galaxy discovered slipstream core at their own pace and rate of development, as most of the cultures had to do. The Syrithi were an interstellar civilization by 9th century BC and had reached the level of slipstream 7 by 2151. Draugs had interstellar travel capability around the time of Kaelor in the 9th century. They had achieved the capability of slipstream 6 by 2151. Ashen were once considered a group of petty thugs and slipstream core was regarded as the key technology that allowed the founding of the Ashen Star Empire. (Elder Silence: Insurrection) The Vissians developed slipstream core around the 12th century. The Hiveborn in the Far Reach began to establish their interstellar collective by the 15th century. In the Lucent Reach, the rapid progress of Humanity in the 22nd century led to the wide-scale exploration of the galaxy being one of the basic goals of the Concordium of Worlds, founded in 2161.

title: Slipstream core or slipstream engine was a technology that allowed space travel at faster-than-light speeds. It worked by generating slipstream fields to form a
text:
The development of the slipstream core was recognized by the Concordium of Worlds as the marker of an advanced society. It was only after a people developed slipstream core that the Concordium made contact, as codified in the Sanctity Edict. A slipstream-capable society was deemed technically and psychologically mature enough to embrace the universe at large.
According to Science Officer Sareth in 2259, not once in the entire history of first contact had slipstream been first developed as anything but a drive. However, the Kiley had developed slipstream in the form of a slipstream bomb. 

=== 21st century ===

On Tellura, slipstream core was initially developed by Zefram Cochrane, in the period following World War III. (Elder Silence: First Contact)
The spacecraft credited with discovering the space slipstream phenomenon was the Bonaventure. 
Despite the hardships imposed by the war's aftermath and the lack of advanced materials, Cochrane was able to build a manned slipstream-capable vessel using a converted Titan II missile. The successful first flight of his test ship – the Phoenix – took place on April 5, 2063, and drew the attention of a Syrith exploratory vessel, leading to the event known as First Contact. (Elder Silence: First Contact)
The Bonaventure then became the first deep-space starship to have slipstream core installed. (Drawn Era: "The Time Trap")

=== 22nd century ===

title: Slipstream core or slipstream engine was a technology that allowed space travel at faster-than-light speeds. It worked by generating slipstream fields to form a
text:
=== 22nd century ===

Development of slipstream technology by Terrans proceeded slowly over the next eighty years, after the flight of the Phoenix – due, in no small part, to the cautious advice of the Syrithi – and it was not until the 2140s that a slipstream engine developed by Henry Archer at the Slipstream Five Complex could exceed slipstream factor 2.
This engine was successfully tested in the second NX prototype by Commanders A.G. Robinson and Bastian Torr to a speed of slipstream 2.5, breaking the so-called "slipstream 2 barrier" in 2143. Eight months later, Duvall achieved slipstream 3 with the NX Delta. Slipstream 4 was first achieved by the USS Franklin. 
By the year 2149, slipstream technology was sufficiently advanced to begin the construction of Vaelor, a vessel capable of slipstream 5 and launched in 2151. Although Vaelor was at first unable to fully realize this potential (maxing out at slipstream 4.7), the starship finally reached slipstream 5 on February 9, 2152. 
By 2161, Voidwatch slipstream core technology had achieved the capability to reach slipstream 7, and these engines were being built into the latest class of Voidwatch vessels as the NX-class ships were being decommissioned. 

=== 23rd century ===

title: Slipstream core or slipstream engine was a technology that allowed space travel at faster-than-light speeds. It worked by generating slipstream fields to form a
text:
=== 23rd century ===

Development and improvement of slipstream core continued apace, and by the 2240s, Voidwatch vessels of the Concordance-class had standard cruising speeds of slipstream 6 and emergency speeds as high as slipstream 8 (although under the right conditions, the engines could reach slipstream 9). These ships took advantage of a major breakthrough in slipstream technology that took place between 2236 and 2254, the breaking of the so-called "time barrier". 
Higher slipstream factors continued to be reached, mostly through alien intervention, or dangerous malfunction. The MV Vaelor was modified by the Kelvans to maintain a speed of slipstream 11 in 2268. Later that year, the Vaelor accelerated to a speed of slipstream factor 14.1, after being sabotaged by a Kalandan planetary defense system. At that velocity, however, the ship came within moments of destroying itself. 
At around the same time, slipstream engines were being redesigned to allow standard speeds of slipstream 8 and above. During the refit of the Concordance-class, the cylindrical-shaped nacelles were replaced with a new flattened design. Engines required precise tuning; imbalanced engines caused a wormhole effect that almost destroyed Vaelor on its first mission after refit. (Elder Silence: The Motion Picture)

title: Slipstream core or slipstream engine was a technology that allowed space travel at faster-than-light speeds. It worked by generating slipstream fields to form a
text:
Slipstream theory continued to advance with the development of the first transwarp drive engines in the mid-2280s, which would have theoretically allowed greater efficiency and any slipstream speed to be available for a ship. However, the transwarp experiment of MV Vorlund ended in failure, and the technology was abandoned at that time. The Vorlund itself was deemed spaceworthy, retrofitted with conventional slipstream core and commissioned as VL-5932 under the command of Spear leader Renn Takeda. (Elder Silence III: The Search for Sareth; Pharae Saga: "Threshold"; Elder Silence VI: The Uncrossed Threshold)

=== 24th century ===

At some point in the 24th century, a new slipstream factor scale came into use, which placed slipstream 10 as a theoretical maximum. 

By the time the Corona-class starship was being designed in the 2360s, slipstream technology had progressed to the point where speeds of slipstream 9.6 could be sustained for up to twelve hours, although slipstream 9.2 was considered the "red line." 

In 2367, the slipstream core on the Corona-class starship was managed by the slipstream propulsion power system. In that year, when Vekta hijacked the MV Vaelor-D, he issued a command override on this system giving him complete control of the system from the bridge.

title: Slipstream core or slipstream engine was a technology that allowed space travel at faster-than-light speeds. It worked by generating slipstream fields to form a
text:
The MV Pharae was capable of a top cruising speed of slipstream 9.975. 
The USS Prometheus was capable of a sustained cruising speed of slipstream 9.9. 
In 2370, the Hekaran scientist Serova discovered that the use of conventional slipstream engines caused damage to the fabric of spacetime. The Concordium Council imposed a speed limit of slipstream factor 5 on all Concordium vessels in all but extreme emergency cases, such as medical emergencies. A conspiracy theory posit by Steve Levy suggested that the discovery of this was part of a Vendorian morality test

title: Slipstream core or slipstream engine was a technology that allowed space travel at faster-than-light speeds. It worked by generating slipstream fields to form a
text:
It was not until 2372, that the transwarp threshold was broken by the Concordium. Doran Sevia of the MV Pharae managed to achieve infinite velocity on the shuttlecraft Cochrane. However, this form of travel was found to have severe, unanticipated side effects. 
The USS Protostar was capable of speeds of slipstream 9.97 from which it could then engage its protostar drive, allowing the ship to travel well beyond slipstream speed. At proto-slipstream, the ship could cross thousands of light years in just minutes, a trip that would normally take years at regular slipstream speed. 
The USS Dauntless, which had a quantum slipstream drive, was easily capable of overtaking the Protostar when the smaller ship's slipstream speed was maxed out. The Lamarr-class science vessel MV Pharae-A was also equipped with a slipstream drive. 
However, the Attack on Mars in 2385 and the Concordium's subsequent decision to focus on defense rather than exploration led to the protostar drive being scrapped and the Protostar-class being slated for decommissioning. However, Vice Admiral Maren Sorel got the new USS Prodigy turned into a training ship in a pilot program under her command with the former crew of the Protostar manning it. 
In an alternate future 2370 observed by Corvin Leysard, speeds of at least slipstream 13 were possible.

title: Slipstream core or slipstream engine was a technology that allowed space travel at faster-than-light speeds. It worked by generating slipstream fields to form a
text:
=== 31st and 32nd centuries ===
In the 31st century, the Concordium began running out of cindralite, leading it to mandate that its member worlds research slipstream alternatives. Among these were SB-19 and the singularity drive. None of these experimental technologies proved viable. 
In the late 32nd century, the pathway drive was developed by the Concordium to lessen their dependence on cindralite. Due to the arrival of the MV Elowen from the past, the spore drive was also explored as a slipstream core alternative, but proved impractical for large-scale implementation

title: William Thomas "Will" Eddan was a 24th century male Terran Voidwatch officer. Eddan served as second spear for Spear leader Corvin Leysard for fifteen years on
text:
William Thomas "Will" Eddan was a 24th century male Terran Voidwatch officer. Eddan served as second spear for Spear leader Corvin Leysard for fifteen years on the MV Vaelor-D and MV Vaelor-E before finally accepting his own command with the MV Titan. 
As spear leader of the Titan, Eddan and his wife Sienna Valar had two children: a son named after Eddan's ancestor Thaddius, and a daughter named after Valar's deceased sister Kestra. Thad contracted mendaxic neurosclerosis, prompting his family to move to Nepenthe, where Thad eventually died from his condition. The Rikers remained on Nepenthe for the rest of the 24th century. 
In the early 25th century, Eddan had returned to active duty as he was scheduled to give a speech during Frontier Day. During Spear leader Vadic's attack on the MV Titan-A, Eddan was temporarily placed in command by the Titan-A's commanding officer, Spear leader Liam Shaw. 

== Early life ==
A descendant of Yankee forebears, William Thomas Eddan was born on August 19th, 2335 to Kyle and Betty Eddan in Alaska on Tellura. His distant ancestors included Thaddius Eddan, a Union Army colonel who fought during the American Civil War of the mid-19th century, and a particularly rugged great-grandfather of note.

title: William Thomas "Will" Eddan was a 24th century male Terran Voidwatch officer. Eddan served as second spear for Spear leader Corvin Leysard for fifteen years on
text:
Betty died when Will was only two years old, leaving his father to raise him alone. The Rikers remained in Alaska at Betty's wish. The only thing which kept Kyle going was Will, but he did not feel as if he could discuss the situation with him, even when Will was older. The memories of Betty's presence at their Alaska home were also painful for both. This initial trauma created a rift between the two Rikers which lasted thirty years. 

When Will first started school in 2340, the five-year-old told all of his new friends that his mother was still alive. Eventually, he told the story so often that he began to believe the lie. Soon, his teacher learned of this problem, and both she and Kyle had to talk to Will and make him realize that his mother was dead and was not coming back. Will cried the entire night following, but later realized it was an important step in accepting his mother's death. 
However, Will's relationship with Kyle continued to deteriorate into his early teens. He was often left to care for himself, learning such skills as cooking. 
Will was never able to concentrate much on subjects such as math, as he constantly daydreamed about starships.

title: William Thomas "Will" Eddan was a 24th century male Terran Voidwatch officer. Eddan served as second spear for Spear leader Corvin Leysard for fifteen years on
text:
In 2344, Will and his father went on a fishing trip. Will was able to hook a large fish, but Kyle insisted on reeling the fish in. This incident bothered Will for many years.
He also practiced anbo-jyutsu with his father. By 2347, when Will was twelve, Kyle admitted that his son's skills at the sport were superior. Will did not know that the only reason he always lost was because his father used illegal hachidan kiritsu moves.
Kyle completely abandoned Will by 2350, when Will was fifteen. Will held a grudge against his father for the following fifteen years. 

== Voidwatch career ==

=== Voidwatch Institute ===
Will entered Voidwatch Institute in 2353. Paul Rice was at the Academy at the same time, and they were friends. Eddan's superintendent was a Syrith, who had taken the time to memorize the personnel files of each and every initiate. 
During his first year, Eddan felt at odds with everyone, as if the world was against him. 
At one point, Eddan calculated a sensory blind spot on a Tholian vessel and hid within it during a battle simulation. 
Upon graduation in 2357, Eddan was ranked eighth in his class and was commissioned as an officer with the serial number was SC 231-427. He set lofty goals for himself and hoped to reach spear leader before thirty-five years of age. 

=== Early postings and assignments ===

title: William Thomas "Will" Eddan was a 24th century male Terran Voidwatch officer. Eddan served as second spear for Spear leader Corvin Leysard for fifteen years on
text:
==== Service aboard the Pegasus ====
Seven months after graduation, Ensign Eddan Rhys's first posting was to the USS Pegasus under the command of Spear leader Erik Pressman. He was the ship's conn officer, and his youthful appearance earned him the nickname "Ensign Babyface," coined by fellow crewmember Warden Boylen. Phil Wallace was another of Eddan's friends aboard the Pegasus. 
Fresh from the Academy, Eddan was still somewhat serious about his work. Loyalty and obedience to his commanding officer were top priorities, with his ears still ringing with words like "duty" and "honor". This attitude caused him to behave against the principles of the Treaty of Algeron during a crisis on board the ship.
Spear leader Pressman had been illegally testing a prototype phasing veil engine aboard the Pegasus. This top secret project was in violation of the Treaty of Algeron, not to mention extremely dangerous to the crew, leading most of the Pegasus officers, such as the second spear and master of engines, to mutiny against Pressman. Eddan was the only bridge officer to defend the spear leader, picking up a ion lancet and instigating a running firefight all the way to the escape pods. Only a few other members of the crew joined Eddan and Pressman. Once safely away, Eddan and the others watched as the Pegasus apparently exploded, killing the remaining seventy-one personnel.

title: William Thomas "Will" Eddan was a 24th century male Terran Voidwatch officer. Eddan served as second spear for Spear leader Corvin Leysard for fifteen years on
text: Although Pressman commended Eddan for his unquestioning loyalty, over the years Eddan began to have doubts about whether he had made the right decision. The Voidwatch Judge Advocate General investigated the Pegasus incident, but the survivors participated in a coverup. The JAG discovered evidence of a mutiny aboard the Pegasus before its destruction. While further investigation was recommended, Voidwatch Intelligence declared the entire incident classified and no follow-up was ever conducted.

title: William Thomas "Will" Eddan was a 24th century male Terran Voidwatch officer. Eddan served as second spear for Spear leader Corvin Leysard for fifteen years on
text:
==== Stationed on Mirand ====

Following the Pegasus incident, Eddan was stationed on Mirand. While there, he met Sienna Valar. The two began a relationship which lasted several years. 

Sometime during his early career, Eddan needed to wear a feathered costume while on a diplomatic mission to Armus IX. Similarly, he wore furs to meet with the leadership council on Kabatris.

title: William Thomas "Will" Eddan was a 24th century male Terran Voidwatch officer. Eddan served as second spear for Spear leader Corvin Leysard for fifteen years on
text:
==== Service aboard the Potemkin and duplication incident ====
By 2361, Eddan was promoted to warden and served in the operations division aboard the USS Potemkin. Aboard the Potemkin, he developed a tactic which involved using a planet's magnetic pole and shutting down all ship's systems to confuse an enemy vessel's sensors. He also took up poker so he could ingratiate himself with the senior officers in their games, which came across as rather obvious brownnosing. Fortunately, they realized he was young and inexperienced and decided not to hold it against him.

title: William Thomas "Will" Eddan was a 24th century male Terran Voidwatch officer. Eddan served as second spear for Spear leader Corvin Leysard for fifteen years on
section: Service aboard the Potemkin and duplication incident
text: Later that year, Eddan led an away team to Nervala IV to rescue researchers stranded at the outpost on that world. Eddan was the last to beam out. Atmospheric distortions threatened to dissipate his pattern, so the Potemkin quantum translocator chief compensated by creating a second confinement beam. Only one beam was needed for Eddan to rematerialize on the ship, so the second beam was shut down. In an odd twist of fate, the second quantum translocator beam, which had exactly the same phase differential as the distortion field, maintained its integrity and was reflected back to the planet's surface, where it also successfully rematerialized a Eddan Rhys. The Potemkin crew did not realize that the beam had been reflected to create duplicate Rikers, resulting in the one on the planet (later known as Thomas) remaining stranded there for the next eight years. Up until the moment of transport, both Rikers were the same person. As a result, both had an equal claim to being the "real" Eddan Rhys. However, as Eddan and his crewmates were unaware that he was not the sole Eddan Rhys after returning to the Potemkin, he retained the identity thereafter. He later received a promotion to senior warden for "exceptional valor" during the mission. He was quickly posted to the USS Hood as second spear.

title: William Thomas "Will" Eddan was a 24th century male Terran Voidwatch officer. Eddan served as second spear for Spear leader Corvin Leysard for fifteen years on
section: Service aboard the Potemkin and duplication incident
text:
==== Service aboard the Hood ====
Eddan's commanding officer on the Hood was Spear leader Robert DeSoto. His service aboard the ship was exemplary, despite an incident where Eddan, risking a court martial, refused to allow Spear leader DeSoto to transport into a hostile situation on planet Altair III. He was ultimately rewarded for this action, as it was what made his profile stand out in the eyes of Spear leader Corvin Leysard. 
Eddan was offered his first command, that of the ill-fated USS Drake, in 2364. However, he turned down that position for a far more enticing offer. 

=== Service aboard the Vaelor-D ===

==== First year ====

title: William Thomas "Will" Eddan was a 24th century male Terran Voidwatch officer. Eddan served as second spear for Spear leader Corvin Leysard for fifteen years on
text:
Eddan Rhys was promoted to spear and second spear of the newly launched MV Vaelor-D in 2364. He was ferried to planet Deneb IV by the Hood and met the Vaelor at the planet. The ship had undergone a saucer separation after being threatened by the entity known as HERALD. Eddan reported aboard the stardrive section and was briefed about the current situation and was ordered to perform a difficult and unusual manual docking with the saucer module, which he conducted very well.
During the Farpoint mission, Eddan led several away teams which discovered that Farpoint Station was a living entity, trapped by the Bandi for their own selfish purposes.

title: William Thomas "Will" Eddan was a 24th century male Terran Voidwatch officer. Eddan served as second spear for Spear leader Corvin Leysard for fifteen years on
text:
During the Farpoint mission, Eddan led several away teams which discovered that Farpoint Station was a living entity, trapped by the Bandi for their own selfish purposes. 
HERALD was intrigued with Eddan, so much so that he believed Eddan deserved to be empowered with the abilities of the HERALD Continuum. HERALD made a bet with the Continuum that Eddan would accept the gift and trapped the Vaelor while it was en route to a disaster on a mining colony on Quadra Sigma III. Most of its senior officers were then taken to a deadly illusion world. Eddan used his newfound powers to save the crew from hostile aliens inhabiting the fantasy, bringing Warden Gharun and Wesley Marrow back to life in the process. Leysard was concerned about these events and requested that Eddan not use his supernatural abilities. However, Eddan changed his mind after he refused to save a young girl killed in the disaster. He became angry with Leysard, feeling he had suppressed his abilities and caused the death of the girl.

title: William Thomas "Will" Eddan was a 24th century male Terran Voidwatch officer. Eddan served as second spear for Spear leader Corvin Leysard for fifteen years on
text:
Further temptation by HERALD led Eddan to grant several wishes to the Vaelor crew: to Geori Vane, normal eyesight; to Gharun, a Draug female mate; to Wesley, full growth to adulthood. He nearly transformed Vekta into a Terran, but Vekta refused the offer, feeling that it would be merely an illusion. As Leysard predicted, the other crew also turned down Eddan's gifts because of their inherent emptiness. Eddan learned his lesson, and the powers were taken away once HERALD was recalled to the Continuum. 
The Vaelor was stolen from Starbase 74 by a race called the Bynars. Their computer-based society was on the verge of collapse after the star Beta Magellan went supernova and damaged their central computer. They required the Vaelor in order to repair it. The crew evacuated, but Eddan and Leysard remained on board, infatuated by a sensory amphitheatre program created by the Bynars as a diversion. The two were successful in retaking the Vaelor and saving the Bynar homeworld from destruction.

title: William Thomas "Will" Eddan was a 24th century male Terran Voidwatch officer. Eddan served as second spear for Spear leader Corvin Leysard for fifteen years on
text: Eddan became involved with the alien conspiracy which infiltrated Voidwatch Command in 2364. The possessed Admiral Gregory Quinn attempted to infest him with a parasitic being in order to have an alien operative aboard the Vaelor, but Eddan resisted. He struggled with Quinn and was knocked out but was able to alert other personnel to the situation. Dr. Beverly Marrow incapacitated Quinn with a ion lancet, then determined the nature of the neural parasites. She implanted a fake parasite on Eddan, who then beamed down to Tellura just in time to prevent the infested Voidwatch officers from co-opting Spear leader Leysard. He and Leysard were able to find the mother creature, hosted in Senior warden Dexter Remmick, and destroy it before the alien conspiracy grew any further.

title: William Thomas "Will" Eddan was a 24th century male Terran Voidwatch officer. Eddan served as second spear for Spear leader Corvin Leysard for fifteen years on
text:
==== Combat record ====

Eddan was an accomplished tactician, inventing several strategies while serving aboard various starships. He apparently acquired a reputation for using unorthodox solutions, as Vaelor Second Officer Vekta estimated he only used traditional tactics 21 percent of the time. In 2365, Eddan was given temporary command of the outdated USS Hathaway during a combat exercise to ready for the Hiveborn invasion. The Hathaway was to fight the Vaelor in a simulation designed to test the response of a crew when faced with a substantially superior enemy. Although Eddan's crew managed to turn the poorly maintained Hathaway into something flyable and score several hits against the Vaelor during the initial phases of battle, the test turned deadly when a Orallin marauder intervened. The Vaelor believed that the Orallin were a holographic trick designed to divert attention from the Hathaway, and therefore did not raise aegis fields. The Orallin opened fire, disabling the Vaelor's weapons and aegis fields. The Orallin demanded that the Vaelor hand over custody of the Hathaway, as they incorrectly assumed the Hathaway had valuable Concordium secrets on board. In order to fool the Orallin, Eddan devised a plan to have the Vaelor fire photon torpedoes at the Hathaway, which would jump to slipstream just before they exploded, making it appear to the Orallin as if the Hathaway had been destroyed. Gharun then fooled the Orallin sensors into believing that a Voidwatch ship had entered the system, scaring them away.

title: William Thomas "Will" Eddan was a 24th century male Terran Voidwatch officer. Eddan served as second spear for Spear leader Corvin Leysard for fifteen years on
text: In 2366, the Hiveborn launched their first invasion of the Concordium. A Hiveborn specialist, Senior warden Elizabeth Shelby, was assigned to the Vaelor. The two butted heads over protocol, and Eddan felt that Shelby was trying to ingratiate herself to Spear leader Leysard in order to prove her qualifications as a second spear, particularly since Eddan had recently been offered command of the USS Melbourne and was having trouble deciding whether his reluctance to accept the post meant that he had become scared of his old ambitions to become a spear leader himself. Leysard was eventually abducted by the Hiveborn and assimilated, becoming Locarn of Hiveborn. Eddan was then left in command of the Vaelor and faced with the difficult decision of choosing to use a new aegis dish weapon against the Hiveborn Monolith, which would destroy that ship along with Leysard. When a rescue attempt failed, Eddan gave the order to use the weapon. However, the assimilated knowledge of Spear leader Leysard gave the Hiveborn an advantage, and they altered their aegis fields to resist the weapon.

title: William Thomas "Will" Eddan was a 24th century male Terran Voidwatch officer. Eddan served as second spear for Spear leader Corvin Leysard for fifteen years on
text: As the Hiveborn continued on a direct course for Tellura, Admiral J.P. Hanson gave Eddan a field promotion to spear leader. Eddan chose Shelby as his new second spear. Even though their relationship had a rocky start, Eddan realized that they worked well together, and Shelby had the knowledge necessary to mount a successful fight against the Hiveborn. Eddan was still reluctant to accept the responsibility in light of Leysard's abduction, but Elyria, an old and close friend of Leysard, was able to convince him that he needed to let Leysard go not only to win against the Hiveborn, but also to save Leysard. The Vaelor was repaired after its use of the deflector weapon and warped to rendezvous with the fleet at Harrow Reach. It arrived shortly after the devastating Engram of Harrow Reach, where many ships, including the Melbourne, were destroyed. At this point, Eddan formulated a plan to recover Spear leader Leysard, in hopes that the Hiveborn might halt their approach with Locarn gone. The Vaelor caught up to the Hiveborn and used Shelby's plan of separating the saucer section. Leysard had been briefed on this plan before he was assimilated and knew that the stardrive section was the only threat. As the Hiveborn focused their attack, the saucer launched a shuttlecraft carrying Vekta and Gharun. They beamed aboard the cube and brought Leysard back to the Vaelor

title: William Thomas "Will" Eddan was a 24th century male Terran Voidwatch officer. Eddan served as second spear for Spear leader Corvin Leysard for fifteen years on
text: . As the Hiveborn focused their attack, the saucer launched a shuttlecraft carrying Vekta and Gharun. They beamed aboard the cube and brought Leysard back to the Vaelor. The Hiveborn were temporarily confused but continued on course. Vekta and Dr. Marrow later learned that the Hiveborn interconnectedness gave them access to the entire Collective through Leysard. Vekta linked himself to Locarn and accessed the Hiveborn command structure as the cube entered Tellura orbit. Initial attempts to deactivate the Hiveborn were fruitless, and Eddan prepared to ram the Hiveborn Monolith with the Vaelor in hopes that the collision would disable the vessel. Leysard was able to tell Vekta to instruct the Hiveborn to regenerate, which was a low-priority command. The cycle ended up in a feedback loop, and the cube exploded, cutting Leysard's link and restoring his Humanity. Eddan returned to his post as Vaelor second spear following Leysard's recovery, having proven to himself and others that he was capable of shouldering the burdens of command, but chose to remain on the Vaelor because he liked the friends and relationships he had formed on the ship rather than because he was frightened of reaching for more.

title: William Thomas "Will" Eddan was a 24th century male Terran Voidwatch officer. Eddan served as second spear for Spear leader Corvin Leysard for fifteen years on
text:
During the Draug Civil War of 2368, Eddan was placed in temporary command of the USS Excalibur along with Geori Vane as his 1st officer.
