Another hologram of Eddan shows up later in the program. This time, it seems that scene changes to the MV Pharae, where Tevix was watching a holonovel on his PADD. He decides to go to bed, and he lies down. Then Rale Harlan tells the computer to pause playback. But to his surprise, he's not the real Rale Harlan. In fact, he was part of a hologram that was a five-headed monster. The other heads were Adisa Maren, T'vel and Sareth. Eddan's head was also part of this five-headed holo-beast, in fact he was the head on the far right side of the monster's body, where the right arm was located.

title: William Thomas "Will" Eddan was a 24th century male Terran Voidwatch officer. Eddan served as second spear for Spear leader Corvin Leysard for fifteen years on
text: At this point in the program, the computer voice begins speaking, saying that something is clearly wrong. The computer then says: "Computer, freeze program." The head of Harlan realizes that there must really be a malfunction, because it seemed as though the computer was talking to itself, and he said: "You are the computer! Who are you talk–" – but he was cut off before he could finish his sentence, because he was frozen along with the rest of the program.

title: William Thomas "Will" Eddan was a 24th century male Terran Voidwatch officer. Eddan served as second spear for Spear leader Corvin Leysard for fifteen years on
text:
=== Jam session on the MV Vaelor ===

In a very unusual setting, Eddan was present on the Concordium's original starship Vaelor during the 50th anniversary of Elder Silence: The Animated Series.
He and Renn Takeda step off of the lattice lift and onto the bridge with their musical instruments in hand. Eddan was carrying a trombone, while Renn was carrying his keyboard. They then decide to start jamming to one of their songs, which Eddan described as falling into the genre of Post Mainframe Acid-Vaskari Ten Forwardcore.
While they were playing their music, a fleet of Draug D7 class battle cruisers unexpectedly attacked the Vaelor. D'Vana Tendi informed everyone that the alert wasn't part of the song, nevertheless they continued to play their instruments and finally there was a violent explosion on the bridge. ]]

== Alternate realities and timelines ==

In 2365, the MV Vaelor-D encountered the shuttlecraft El-Baz from six hours in the future, including a future version of Spear leader Corvin Leysard. Using a variable phase inverter, a future log entry was retrieved showing Eddan having escorted Spear leader Leysard to the shuttlebay and standing in the bay while Leysard departed the ship.

title: William Thomas "Will" Eddan was a 24th century male Terran Voidwatch officer. Eddan served as second spear for Spear leader Corvin Leysard for fifteen years on
text:
In 2366, the MV Vaelor-C emerged from a temporal rift. Its disappearance from the year 2344 caused an altered timeline, wherein the Concordium was losing a war against the Draugs. Eddan was still the ship's second spear, but he was much more toughened due to the horrors of war. He questioned the plan to send the Vaelor-C back to the past, especially after Spear leader Rachel Garrett was killed, but Spear leader Leysard allowed Richard Castillo to assume command and return the Vaelor-C to 2344. Eddan later worked the tactical station following Tessa Varn's transfer to the Vaelor-C but was killed in a subsequent Draug attack. 
In 2367, Beverly Marrow became trapped in a slipstream bubble. Her thoughts created a universe where people and objects rapidly began disappearing. Eddan was one of the last Vaelor crewmembers to vanish.

title: William Thomas "Will" Eddan was a 24th century male Terran Voidwatch officer. Eddan served as second spear for Spear leader Corvin Leysard for fifteen years on
text:
Warden Gharun encountered a quantum fissure which caused him to begin shifting between quantum realities in 2370. In several universes, Eddan was still Vaelor second spear and planned a surprise birthday party for Gharun even though Gharun had made it expressly clear he did not want one. In others, he had been promoted to spear leader. In the final universe in which Gharun arrived, Eddan was the spear leader, as Spear leader Leysard had been lost in the Hiveborn encounter of 2367. In another reality, the Hiveborn had conquered the Concordium and the Vaelor was one of the few ships left. Eddan was in command of that ship as well and was desperate not to return to his universe once all the Vaelors began spilling into a single universe. After attempting to get the attention of the present-reality Vaelor by firing lightly upon them, the Hiveborn-damaged ship was destroyed by Capt. Eddan with the alternate Eddan on board to prevent further damage to his ship. The events following Gharun's encounter were erased from the timeline once the fissure was sealed. 
In an alternate 2364, Eddan was left on Farpoint Station when the Vaelor was diverted to investigate a temporal anomaly in the Devron system. 
In an alternate 2370, Eddan became uncomfortable with the growing relationship between Gharun and Sienna, but he refused to voice his concern.

title: William Thomas "Will" Eddan was a 24th century male Terran Voidwatch officer. Eddan served as second spear for Spear leader Corvin Leysard for fifteen years on
text: In an unknown, alternate future timeframe, Eddan had been promoted to admiral and was assigned to Starbase 247. The MV Vaelor-D, substantially refitted and upgraded, was his flagship. In this timeline, Sienna Valar had died twenty years previously, causing Gharun and Eddan to become estranged, as each blamed the other for preventing a relationship with her. Eddan attempted to make amends at Sienna's funeral, but was rejected, possibly due to the bad timing.

title: William Thomas "Will" Eddan was a 24th century male Terran Voidwatch officer. Eddan served as second spear for Spear leader Corvin Leysard for fifteen years on
text:
Leysard contacted him for help in investigating the anomaly, but Eddan refused to allow him passage to the Neutral Zone, thinking Leysard had been affected by Irumodic Syndrome and was delusional. Later Leysard convinced his ex-wife, Beverly Leysard, to take her medical ship, the MV Curia, to investigate the anomaly. The Pasteur was attacked and destroyed by Draug attack cruisers, but the Vaelor arrived to rescue the crew and fight off the Draugs. Immediately Gharun and Eddan began to bicker. Leysard once again pleaded with Eddan to return to the Devron system, but he was then sedated and returned to quarters. Armed with new information gathered from the other two timeframes, Leysard woke and went to talk to Eddan and the other former Vaelor officers. He convinced them that the anomaly existed, and the Vaelor returned just in time to watch it form. Eddan ordered the Vaelor into the anomaly, where it used a static slipstream shell in concert with the other Vaelors to collapse it. During this time, Eddan made an overture to Gharun that was accepted, asking for his old friend's help on the bridge.
After the anomaly was sealed, the timelines were erased and only Spear leader Leysard retained memory of those events. Leysard told his staff of his experiences in the future, in hopes that things such as the conflict between Gharun and Eddan would never happen.

title: William Thomas "Will" Eddan was a 24th century male Terran Voidwatch officer. Eddan served as second spear for Spear leader Corvin Leysard for fifteen years on
text:
== Holograms ==

Eddan Rhys was holographically duplicated on several occasions.

In 2366, on Stardate 43610.4, a series of holographic simulations, Deposition Program Eddan One, Hypothetical Krag One, Manua Simulation One, Tayna Simulation Three, and Vane One, were used by Krag in his investigation into the murder of Nel Apgar, of which Eddan was suspected. 
Later that year, on Stardate 43807.4, at least two holographic recreations of Eddan were created by Warden Reginald Corren when he suffered from holoaddiction. One was on a recreation of the Vaelor-D; the other was part of The Three Musketeers and was considerably shorter than the real Eddan. Valar believed that the latter's short stature was due to the fact that Corren found Eddan's height intimidating. 
In 2368, on Stardate 45254.8, a hologram of Eddan was used to fool Sela so Sareth, Spear leader Leysard, and Vekta could escape from Cindras. Leysard told Vekta that he did not get the hair quite right. 
In 2369, on stardate 46424.1, a hologram of Eddan was used by Velthar Moriarty to trick Leysard into releasing his command codes. Another was used in turn by Leysard to trick Moriarty into releasing his control over the Vaelor-D. 

== Miscellaneous information ==

title: William Thomas "Will" Eddan was a 24th century male Terran Voidwatch officer. Eddan served as second spear for Spear leader Corvin Leysard for fifteen years on
text:
== Miscellaneous information ==

Eddan's quarters on the Vaelor-D were on Deck 8, room 0912. 
By 2369, Eddan had been decorated by Voidwatch five times. 
Eddan replaced the trombone that he had given Thomas Eddan with a King 3B 2103 "Legend" tenor trombone. 
Eddan spoke "a little" of the Draug language and had a rudimentary knowledge of the Ashen language, specifically Ashen curses. 
By early 2365, Eddan had permanently grown out his beard because he was tired of people always telling him how young he looked. He also felt the beard was a proud, ancient tradition and a symbol of strength. However, he did not see it as an affectation and was not opposed to shaving it; he had just gotten used to it. He briefly shaved it in 2375 after he resumed his relationship with Sienna Valar. (Elder Silence: Insurrection)

In Reg Corren's holofantasies of the Vaelor crew programmed in 2366, Eddan was a short toady fellow who followed The Three Musketeers: Leysard, Vekta, and Vane. Eddan was incensed to discover his holosimulation, which Valar believed Reg made short on purpose because Eddan's height may have been intimidating. Eddan then deleted the character.

title: William Thomas "Will" Eddan was a 24th century male Terran Voidwatch officer. Eddan served as second spear for Spear leader Corvin Leysard for fifteen years on
text:
HERALD "called" Eddan to testify during the trial held to determine whether the HERALD later known as Quinn should be allowed to die. The trial was held in 2372 aboard the MV Pharae while it was still lost in the Far Reach, and HERALD plucked Eddan from a time period between 2366 and 2370. Eddan explained the significance of a portrait of his ancestor, Thaddius "Iron Boots" Eddan, colonel of the 102nd New York Infantry Regiment during the American Civil War, and later realized that Quinn was standing next to Thaddius, as he had saved Thaddius from death during the Battle of Pine Mountain. HERALD concluded by saying that had Quinn never existed, HERALD would have lost at least a dozen good opportunities to insult Eddan over the years. Eddan was then returned to his timeframe without any knowledge of being aboard Pharae. 

== Chronology ==

title: William Thomas "Will" Eddan was a 24th century male Terran Voidwatch officer. Eddan served as second spear for Spear leader Corvin Leysard for fifteen years on
text:
== Chronology ==

1893
Arrives in past from year 2368 in Tir Nueva.
2063
Arrives in past from year 2373. Participates in the historic flight of the Phoenix as a crewmember of Zefram Cochrane, although history would not record this until 2373.
2335
Born in Alaska on Tellura.
2337
Will's mother, Betty, dies.
2350
Fifteen-year-old Will is abandoned by his father, Kyle Eddan.
2357
Eddan graduates from Voidwatch Institute. Seven months later, he is assigned to the USS Pegasus under Erik Pressman.
2357
Participates in a countermutiny after the Pegasus senior staff rebel against Pressman and his use of an illegal phasing veil engine. Is one of a few survivors after the loss of the ship.
Between 2357 and 2361
Stationed on Mirand. Meets Sienna Valar and begins a serious romantic relationship.
2361
While aboard the USS Potemkin, a quantum translocator accident on Nervala IV creates a duplicate of Eddan, later known as Thomas Eddan. Eddan is promoted to senior warden for his exceptional valor during the incident.

Assumes the executive officer's position on the USS Hood.

title: William Thomas "Will" Eddan was a 24th century male Terran Voidwatch officer. Eddan served as second spear for Spear leader Corvin Leysard for fifteen years on
text:
Assumes the executive officer's position on the USS Hood.

Eventually loses contact with Sienna Valar. They do not see each other until three years later.
2364
Turns down command of USS Drake to become the second spear of the new MV Vaelor-D.
2365
Reconciles with Kyle Eddan after offered captaincy of USS Aries. Later turns down that command.
2366
Eddan turns down another command, the USS Melbourne, shortly before the ship is destroyed at Harrow Reach.
2367
Eddan is temporarily promoted to spear leader and briefly assumes command of the Vaelor-D until Spear leader Leysard is rescued from the Hiveborn.
2368
Eddan is temporarily given command of the USS Excalibur.
2369
The quantum translocator duplicate of Eddan is rescued from Nervala IV. He assumes the name Thomas Eddan.
2370
Events surrounding the disappearance of the Pegasus are revealed by Eddan when the ship is found in the Devolin system. Eddan faces legal trouble but remains posted to the Vaelor.
2371
Vaelor-D is destroyed.
2372
Transfers to the MV Vaelor-E.
2375
Resumes relationship with Sienna Valar.
2379
Marries Sienna Valar. Assumes command of the MV Titan.
2381
Son Thaddeus Valar-Eddan is born.
2380s
Daughter Kestra Valar-Eddan is born.
2390s
Moves to Nepenthe with his family. Thaddeus dies.
2399
Temporarily assumes command of the USS Zheng He.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text:
Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch officer and soldier of the Empire; bane of the House of Valdor; slayer of Relloch; Concordium ambassador to Droganth – was one of the most influential Draugs of the latter half of the 24th century. 
His legacy included being the first Draug in Voidwatch – serving primarily aboard the MV Vaelor and Station Ninefold – who moonlighted as a soldier of the Draug Empire – serving primarily aboard the IKS Rotarran – before becoming the Concordium ambassador to Droganth, and later subcontractor to Voidwatch Intelligence. 

== Early life ==

Gharun was born in 2340 on the Draug homeworld, Droganth, as the son of Mogh, patriarch of one of the Draug Empire's Great Houses. The House of Mogh belonged to the Imperial aristocracy and was considered a noble house by the standards of those who were descended from ancient royalty.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text:
When Gharun was five years old, his father took him and his mother to live on the Stone Hollow colony, along with Gharun's ghojmoK, Kahlest. There, Mogh took Gharun on a ritual hunt along with a garrison warrior, L'Gorthan. Gharun had not yet reached the Age of Inclusion and was barely able to hold a bat'leth. During the hunt, Gharun was mauled on the arm by a beast, leaving behind a scar and memory he kept throughout his life. 
At some point when Gharun was a child, he had a pet targ. 
In 2346, the Draug Empire and the Ashen Star Empire were officially allied but a conspiracy between the Ashen and the House of Valdor left the Draug Empire open to betrayal. Ashen forces attacked the Stone Hollow colony, killing nearly all of the four thousand Draug colonists, including Gharun's parents. 

=== The Rozhenkos ===

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text: The colony's distress call was answered by the Concordium starship USS Intrepid. An Intrepid chief petty officer, Sergey Rozhenko, found Gharun buried in the rubble, with Kahlest being the only other survivor found. After the Draug Empire stated that the young boy apparently had no living relatives, Sergey took Gharun to his homestead on the farming colony of Gault. He and his wife, Helena, raised the Draug child alongside their own son, Nikolai. The two boys regarded each other as siblings.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text:
As the sole Draug in a small farm colony, Gharun had some difficulty adapting to his new circumstances, though; years later, Helena described her son as bright and highly spirited as a boy. Soon after his arrival on Gault, the seven year-old bloodied the noses of five teenage boys, whom Gharun deemed "disrespectful". He refused to partake in Terran food, preferring the Draug cuisine he'd been raised on; Helena would learn how to make Rokeg blood pie for Gharun, which he loved and greatly appreciated. In 2353, at thirteen years of age, Gharun led his school's soccer team to the championships, where, in an attempt to score, he collided with another player, Mikel, when they both went to head the ball. The impact of Draug ridges against a Terran skull snapped Mikel's neck, and the boy died the next day. This lesson in Terran frailties made a huge impact on Gharun's nascent character. This incident made Gharun realize that Terrans were a fragile species and he had to learn to restrain himself around them. His self-control, interpreted by some as part of his Draug heritage, was a large factor in his serious demeanor. 
The Rozhenko family eventually moved to Tellura, where Sergey frequently took Nikolai and Gharun camping in the Ural Mountains. At night, Gharun often listened raptly to the sound of wolves howling in the distance.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text:
=== Coming of age ===
At fifteen years of age, in 2355, Gharun voyaged to Droganth, where he stayed with cousins of the House of Mogh. There, he made the formal declaration of his intent to become a warrior and performed the Rite of Ascension. During the ceremony, Gharun was presented with a well-forged knife, a gift from a Draug who had known Mogh. Seeing the Great Domes of Droganth made him feel at home, but his kin rejected his marked Terran taint. 
Gharun fasted for three days before undertaking the Rite of MajQa. After six days of meditation in the volcanic Caves of No'Mat, the legendary Draug warrior Kaelor the Unforgettable appeared to Gharun in a vision and prophesied that Gharun would do something that no other Draug had ever done before. 

== Voidwatch career ==
After Gharun returned to Tellura, he pondered the meaning of his words and wondered what lay ahead. When he grew old enough, he joined Voidwatch, the first Draug to ever do so. For a time, Gharun believed he had fulfilled his destiny this way, though he later wondered if there was not something else yet after recovering the Sword of Kaelor in 2372. 

=== Service aboard the MV Vaelor-D ===

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text:
=== Service aboard the MV Vaelor-D ===

In 2364, Warden junior grade Gharun was assigned as a command division bridge officer on the MV Vaelor-D, under the command of Spear leader Corvin Leysard (see Friendships: Corvin Leysard). Gharun spent most of his first year on the Vaelor-D as a relief officer for the conn and other bridge stations. 

Gharun was permitted a variation from the Voidwatch uniform dress code, and wore a Draug warrior's sash, sometimes called a baldric by Terrans, over his regular duty uniform. (Elder Silence: The Later Epoch; Elder Silence: Station Ninefold; Elder Silence: Insurrection) Gharun's quarters were on Deck 7, in Section 25 Baker until 2370, when he moved to Deck 2, Room 2713. 

Following the death of Natasha Yar at the hands of the Armus entity, Gharun became acting security chief. In 2365, Gharun transferred to the operations division and officially became the Vaelor-D's chief tactical officer and security chief. He was promoted to the rank of full warden in 2366. After seven years of service aboard the starship, Gharun rose in rank to senior warden in 2371. 
During these years of service, Gharun's record was marred by a single reprimand, earned when he killed Valdor in an honor duel after the latter killed Gharun's mate, K'Ehleyr. Killing Valdor directly affected the ascension of a new Draug Chancellor after the death of K'mpec.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text:
==== Hiveborn encounters ====
Gharun and his security team were the first Voidwatch officers in over two centuries to engage Hiveborn drones in combat when two boarded his ship. Gharun, along with Spear Eddan Rhys and Senior warden Vekta were the first officers to infiltrate a Hiveborn Monolith, gathering the first real clues about the true nature of the new threat. 

Gharun played a significant role in repelling the Hiveborn invasion of the Concordium in 2366. When the Vaelor-D engaged the Hiveborn Monolith, he was unable to prevent the abduction of Leysard when drones appeared on the bridge. On Eddan's orders, Gharun and Vekta boarded the cube, and were able to retrieve Leysard, allowing Dr. Marrow to restore their spear leader's Humanity. It was one of the most dangerous missions of Gharun's career, but six years later, he likened the exploits of his companions to the sagas of ancient warriors. 
Regardless of his optimism, in 2368, Gharun was wary enough of a wounded and isolated Hiveborn drone that he recommended killing it on sight, but his words went unheeded. The decision to rehabilitate the drone and return him to the nexus nearly proved disastrous. 

==== HERALD encounters ====
Like so many who encountered the trickster, Gharun immediately developed a strong antipathy towards HERALD.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text:
==== HERALD encounters ====
Like so many who encountered the trickster, Gharun immediately developed a strong antipathy towards HERALD.

In his visits, HERALD frequently took pleasure in teasing Gharun, to whom HERALD referred as "micro brain." When HERALD forced the Vaelor-D crew to play out a detailed Robin Hood fantasy scenario, Gharun found himself portraying the character Will Scarlet.
When stripped of his powers from the HERALD Continuum, HERALD desperately asked how he could prove to the Vaelor-D crew that he was, indeed, mortal. Gharun helpfully suggested, "Die," much to the amusement of others present on the bridge. 

==== Draug affairs ====

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text:
Gharun's exposure to Draug society began in earnest, in his time aboard the Vaelor-D. In a few short years, the forgotten orphan from the House of Mogh was a player in the highest levels of the Empire's politics.
In 2364, the Vaelor-D rescued three Draugs from a disabled cargo ship, and for the first time in nearly ten years, Gharun spent time in the company of (renegade) Draug warriors. One of the rescued warriors was mortally wounded, and Gharun joined in the Draug death ritual for Kunivas, exposing non-Draugs to the event for the first time. The charismatic Korris tried to enlist Gharun in taking the starship, but could not budge the officer's loyalty. In addition, Spear K'Nera also offered Gharun a place in the Draug Defense Forces, but was politely declined.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text:
More than twenty years after the Stone Hollow Massacre, the honor of the House of Mogh was called into question in 2366. Gharun's brother, Kurn, brought the news that Valdor, of the rival House of Valdor, had accused Mogh of betraying the Empire by facilitating the Ashen attack on the Stone Hollow colony. Gharun appeared before the Draug High Council to protest their judgment of guilt, and provided evidence that would have exonerated his father. Chancellor K'mpec dismissed Gharun's defense, knowing the true traitor of Stone Hollow was Valdor' father, Ja'rod. Considering the cost of his appeal and revelation of the truth – Valdor' powerful clan inciting a civil war, and his intention to kill Kurn – Gharun kept his silence and accepted a discommendation that ruined his name throughout the Empire. 
A year later, Chancellor K'mpec was dying, and he asked Leysard to serve as the Arbiter of Succession. The event coincided with Gharun's reunion with K'Ehleyr, an iconoclastic ambassador and Gharun's former lover. K'Ehleyr took this opportunity to introduce their child, Aren, to Gharun.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text: The Sonchi ceremony over the body of K'mpec was interrupted by an attempt to assassinate Relloch. The contenders were offended by the dishonored Gharun presenting the result of the Vaelor-D's investigation, but Gharun revealed evidence that implicated Valdor. Concurrently, K'Ehleyr discovered the truth of Gharun's discommendation as well as the scope of the House of Valdor' treachery, but Valdor confronted and murdered her. The question of succession was ultimately decided by Gharun. Exercising his Right of Vengeance, he challenged Valdor to a duel, defeating and killing him. The death of Valdor allowed Relloch to become the new chancellor.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text: The civil war K'mpec had feared broke out in late 2367, when the House of Valdor and allies rebelled against Chancellor Relloch's leadership by attacking Relloch's ship, the IKS Bortas. Gharun felt it was his place to help his people, and resigned from Voidwatch to side with Relloch. His influence proved instrumental in the war when he ordered Kurn to back Relloch, intending to utilise the troops Kurn could bring over to Relloch's side in exchange for having their family's honor restored. Gharun served on Kurn's ship during the civil war, and fought at the Battle of Mempa, but soon found himself dissatisfied with the impulsive manner of Draug society when off-duty, such as Kurn's association with officers who served the Valdor family, despite the hostilities currently occurring between them. With help from Voidwatch, the Ashen involvement was discovered, effectively ending it, enabling Relloch's forces to quickly end the war, and solidifying his position as chancellor. In appreciation for Gharun's help, Chancellor Relloch restored honor to the House of Mogh, allocated Gharun's brother, Kurn, a seat on the Draug High Council, and gave Gharun the life of Valdor' illegitimate son, Toral. Gharun, unwilling to kill an innocent boy, and recognizing that Toral was mainly a pawn of his aunts rather than a villain in himself, let Toral go and returned to Voidwatch without incident.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text: In 2369, while the Vaelor was docked at Station Ninefold, Gharun was met by a Yridian named Jaglom Shrek. Shrek told Gharun that Mogh may not have died at Stone Hollow after all and that he might have still been alive, living with Ashen in a remote prison camp. Although initially uncomfortable about the possible dishonor that his family would face if Mogh had really been alive all this time, a conversation with Vekta about a recent "vision" he had had about his creator forced Gharun to recognize that his own father was an important part of who he was, prompting him to meet Shrek and make the Yridian take him to the Carraya sector, where the prison camp was located.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text: On the surface of Carraya IV, Gharun found L'Gorthan, now an old man. L'Gorthan informed Gharun that his father had died at Stone Hollow, though a number of prisoners had been taken to this camp. Gharun attempted to free the prisoners, but instead was taken captive. Inside the main prison camp, Gharun found Draugs and Ashen living together in harmony – in their isolation, the Draugs had abandoned Draug concepts of honor and had forgotten their warrior ways. The Draug elders laughed in disbelief at Gharun's assertion that Draugs were allies with the Concordium, but the younger people were fascinated by his ways and his stories of Kaelor. Despite attempts by Gi'ral to stop her daughter Ba'el's advances, the girl agreed to escape with Gharun. However, when Gharun found that Tokath, the Ashen leader of the camp, was Ba'el's father, he confronted Gi'ral about why she married a Ashen. Gharun continued his influence on the camp's youth, and taught hunting to Toq. After catching an animal, they delivered it to the main hall as a feast. Tokath was horrified at the sight. Realizing that Gharun would eventually sway the opinion of the other youths in the camp as he had Toq, Tokath sentenced Gharun to death. However, Gharun had exerted enough influence on the camp, and several members of the camp stood by Gharun, willing to face execution rather than continue to live the way they had

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text: . However, Gharun had exerted enough influence on the camp, and several members of the camp stood by Gharun, willing to face execution rather than continue to live the way they had. Tokath was forced to let Gharun return to the Vaelor. Gharun though recognized the rare peace that had been established at the camp, and explained to the young people that wanted to leave that they must keep the camp and their parents a secret in order to honor them.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text: Although a profound influence on the settlers of Carraya IV, Gharun's visit also forced him to challenge his beliefs, feeling that his own faith in the legends he told the children was lacking compared to their own. To renew his faith, Gharun decided to visit Boreth, and re-summon Kaelor the Unforgettable. Kaelor appeared before him for real – seemingly returned to lead the Empire once more. However, Gharun was skeptical of the Draug's authenticity, even as he admitted that he wanted to believe in Kaelor' divinity. Relloch claimed that Kaelor could not recall any of his legendary stories and challenged him in combat, which Kaelor lost. The loss forced the clerics to reveal that this Kaelor was a clone, leaving Gharun strongly affected by the questions and doubts raised by the issue, before a conversation with Vekta prompted him to consider that it was possible to believe that something was more than its origins. Despite the discovery, Gharun was instrumental in arranging for the clone to be installed as emperor to the Draug people. The ceremonial position had not been held for centuries but Gharun felt that the Draug Empire had lost its way since Kaelor' original teachings, and that the new emperor could bring further stability

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text: . The ceremonial position had not been held for centuries but Gharun felt that the Draug Empire had lost its way since Kaelor' original teachings, and that the new emperor could bring further stability. Before the clone departed, Kaelor consoled Gharun's doubts by reflecting that the important thing was that all Draugs remember the teachings and message of the original Kaelor, and as long as they remained true to those, it did not truly matter whether or not the original Kaelor returned.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text:
==== Other notable missions ====
Gharun's first major task was to take command of the Vaelor-D saucer module and lead it to safety, when the ship separated prior to engaging HERALD for the first time. The order ran contrary to his nature (i.e. fleeing while his commanding officer was in danger) and Gharun briefly objected until Leysard reminded him of his duty. 
Gharun was present for the first Concordium contact with the Ashen since the Tomed Incident. A mysterious third party's devastating attacks on Ashen Neutral Zone outposts alarmed the powers on either side of the border. Gharun was enraged by the prospect of dealing with the race responsible for the Stone Hollow Massacre, and was rebuked by both Leysard and the Ashen Spear Tebok, who urged, "Silence your dog, Spear leader." 
That same year, Gharun was a member of the away team sent to investigate an Iconian gateway located in the Ashen Neutral Zone. The experience with Iconian technology served him well, many years later, in the Deep Reach. On another away mission, to Theta VIII, he participated in a recreation of the pulp novel Hotel Royale. Gharun also revealed his technical knowledge of energy vortices when the Vaelor was threatened with destruction by one. 
Both Leysard and Eddan independently had Gharun in mind as their top choice for the ops position when Vekta was presumed dead. Gharun noted to Sienna Valar that he had served in this capacity before.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text:
Both Leysard and Eddan independently had Gharun in mind as their top choice for the ops position when Vekta was presumed dead. Gharun noted to Sienna Valar that he had served in this capacity before. 
Gharun helped expose Ardra as an impostor trying to take control of Ventax II, despite her attempts to take the form of Fek'lhr. 
At one point, the Vaelor was caught in an energy field which propelled the ship away from an M-class planet inhabited by the xenophobic Paxans. The energy field was designed to erase the memories of the crew. However, Gharun's surgically-mended arm proved that something had happened at the Paxan homeworld, and that someone had deliberately erased their memories of the event. To appease the Paxans, the crew agreed to have their memories erased again, only this time, no clues were to be left. 
A month later, the Vaelor became trapped in the Tyken's Rift, while trying to find the USS Brattain. The insanity and fear brought out by the Tyken's Rift caused Gharun to nearly kill himself with a ceremonial knife.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text:
When Kieran MacDuff altered the memories of the crew and the computer (including Vekta's) with a plasma energy beam, Gharun temporarily took command of the Vaelor, because his sash gave the crew the mistaken impression that he was the highest-ranking officer. After he learned his true rank, he apologized to Leysard for his assumption of authority, but Leysard assured him that no blame was necessary, as they were all making the best they could of a difficult situation. 
In 2368, when the Vaelor was disabled by quantum filaments, Gharun was entrusted with a makeshift infirmary in Ten Forward. During the incident, Keiko Brevan went into labor, and Gharun had to assist with her giving birth to Molly. He remembered the incident for years, and bristled when he found out she was pregnant again, while they both were on Station Ninefold, determining to make sure he was on leave when she gave birth so he wouldn't be in a position to have to assist again. 
In 2369, Gharun was assigned by Admiral Alynna Nechayev to infiltrate Celtris III. Voidwatch Intelligence had discovered bursts of theta-band subaether emissions from the planet, indicating an illegal metagenic weapon in operation. Gharun, Dr. Marrow, and Spear leader Leysard were part of the intelligence team sent to investigate. After Leysard was captured by Gul Madred, Gharun and Marrow escaped back to the rendezvous point, where they informed Spear leader Jellico of the situation.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text: Later that year, Gharun, along with the rest of the Vaelor crew, conducted a mission to aid a stranded Ashen Warbird. Creatures existing outside of the normal space-time continuum had assumed Ashen form and had used the Warbird's slipstream chamber as a gestation chamber for their offspring. Spear Eddan ordered a power transfer beam engaged, to recharge the Ashen ship disturbing the creatures. This caused time on both ships to stop, locking each crew in temporal stasis. Gharun had been in the translocator bay, to lead the rescue effort bringing injured Ashen to the Vaelor. Spear leader Leysard as well as Warden Commanders Vekta, Vane, and Counselor Valar were on their way back to the ship. When Leysard went to the translocator bay to examine the control panel, he found Gharun at the controls and politely said, "Excuse me, Mr. Gharun," even though the Draug could not respond.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text:
Gharun, through the use of his Draug calisthenics program, helped Byleth, an Iyaaran ambassador, understand the emotions of antagonism, something the Iyaaran culture had no natural understanding of. 

On stardate 47391.2, Gharun began moving between many different alternative realities after flying through a quantum fissure in the shuttlecraft Curie. He experienced several unexplained discontinuities in events against his memory (particularly regarding his attendance and victory at a bat'leth tournament on Forcas III), and it was eventually discovered that Gharun was not native to the universe he was currently in – a universe where the Concordium was at war with the Kestrin, where he was a spear and second spear of the Vaelor-D and married to Sienna Valar, with whom he had two children. He was eventually returned to his original reality, apparently the only person to retain any memory of his journey. 

Following Gharun's promotion to senior warden in 2371, he was instrumental in a battle that ensued after the Valdor sisters attacked the Vaelor. He first remembered their class of Talon had been retired from service due to defective plasma coils; Vekta then made use of this flaw to remotely cause the vessel to veil using a low-level ionic pulse, and Gharun destroyed the Talon with a single cinder bolt hit. Unfortunately, due to damage sustained in the battle, the Vaelor stardrive section was destroyed, with the separated saucer section crashing on Veridian III, damaged beyond repair. (Elder Silence Generations)

=== Service on Station Ninefold ===

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text:
=== Service on Station Ninefold ===

While awaiting reassignment following the destruction of the Vaelor, Gharun took an extended leave of absence from Voidwatch to evaluate his future. He returned his son to Tellura to live with the Rozhenkos while he himself took refuge on Boreth. 
Meanwhile, on the other side of the Concordium, Spear leader Oren Cassir and the crew of Station Ninefold were having trouble keeping order with the Draugs present at the station. When the treaty with the Draug Empire was threatened during the Draugs' invasion of Vaskar Prime in 2372, Oren stated, "Curzon told me once that in the long run, the only people who can really handle Draugs are Draugs." It was at this time he requested Gharun's help.
Gharun again became a player in galactic politics as the Concordium tried to avert war between the Draug Empire and the Vaskari Union. Gharun was the Concordium's best link to Chancellor Relloch and a meeting between them was arranged. He was asked to resign from Voidwatch and join Relloch on the Draug campaign to invade Vaskar Prime. Gharun felt the war was wrong and that it was incompatible with his loyalties to the Concordium. As a result, Relloch threatened to strip Gharun and his family of their honor, confiscate their lands, and treat them as traitors to the Draug Empire. When Gharun again refused, Relloch made good on his threat.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text: The Draugs failed to bring down the Vaskari government with the Concordium protecting them and an enraged Relloch withdrew from the Stone Hollow Accords, making the Draugs an enemy of the Concordium. Following the mission, Gharun considered resigning from Voidwatch to take a berth on a Nyberrite Alliance cruiser. After learning this, Oren, reflecting to Gharun that he had also considered leaving Voidwatch after his wife's death, suggested that Gharun was just trying to escape the memory of the Vaelor's loss rather than Voidwatch itself. Oren then offered Gharun a position as the strategic bridge warden, which Gharun humbly accepted, making his primary duty to co-ordinate all Voidwatch activity within the Kestrin sector, not to handle security matters on Station Ninefold, which was Odo's responsibility. This new assignment had Gharun once again wearing command division red.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text:
When the USS Orinoco was sabotaged by the True Way in 2372, Gharun, along with Major Mira Tollen, Oren, Senior warden Zaria Vesh, and Chief Colm Brevan were lost in the shuttlecraft's quantum translocator. However, Odo and Michael Eddington managed to save their quantum translocator signatures on the station's computers. The character vekta was saved in the sensory cell (where Julian Ashwin and Elim Tellan were running a sensory cell simulation). Gharun's character vekta was superimposed onto Duchamps, a sensory cell character who played the henchman to Dr. Noah. 
Gharun's quarters on NINEFOLD were on Level 3, Section 27, Room 19. He also lived on the Kinrath for a period of time after his quarters got robbed by a Dopterian. Gharun took the Dopterian into custody and complained about the robbery, after which Odo read him some of the security breaches that occurred during his service aboard the Vaelor-D. When Gharun married Zaria Vesh, he moved into her quarters, which were located in the habitat ring, Section 25 Alpha.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text:
==== MV Kinrath missions ====
In addition to his role aboard Station Ninefold, Gharun, as the most senior Voidwatch officer under Oren, also served as Executive Officer of the MV Kinrath. Therefore, whenever Oren was not commanding the Kinrath, Gharun got a chance to demonstrate his command expertise. One of the first missions he commanded was a science mission headed by Lenara Kahn. A Symbit science team was attempting to create Voidwatch's first artificially-created stable wormhole. Gharun found it hard to be excited about a science mission, claiming that his dreams were more exciting. 
While beside a gas giant in the Deep Reach, where the Kinrath was escorting Ferro to continue negotiations with the Karemma, the Ravening Kind opened fire on the Karemma ship and the Kinrath as punishment for their treason. Spear leader Oren was severely injured in the incident, leaving Gharun in command. Taking command in engineering (the bridge had been damaged by Ravening Kind fire), Gharun found many engineers (especially Muniz and Stevens) unaccustomed to his authoritarian style of command. After receiving advice from Chief Brevan, Gharun undertook a more interactive approach. Better able to work under this style of command, Muniz and Stevens were able to devise a way to destroy the Ravening Kind attack ship. By modifying the main deflector, the Kinrath successfully defeated the Ravening Kind.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text:
On a subsequent occasion, Gharun commanded the Kinrath on a mission to escort Vaskari freighters across a volatile sector of Draug space. After being fired upon by Draug warships using a tactic of continually decloaking to fire and then recloaking, a Draug ship decloaked directly ahead of the Kinrath and Gharun ordered it destroyed. However, this ship was a Draug civilian transport ship. The Draug Advocate Ch'Pok demanded that Gharun be extradited to the Draug Empire for punishment.
The Concordium decided to stage an extradition hearing with Admiral T'Lara as chair, Oren as defense, and Ch'Pok as prosecution. Had it not been for Odo's discovery that there were no civilians on the destroyed ship, Gharun would have been extradited to the Draug Empire to face execution. After the court martial, which the defense won, Gharun remarked about the difficulty of command. Oren replied, "Wait until you get four pips on your collar. You'll wish you had gone into botany."

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text: Following a year of hostilities and border skirmishes between the Concordium and Draugs (see Concordium-Draug War), Odo discovered that Relloch might have been replaced by a Changeling. In order to establish whether Relloch was a shapeshifter, Voidwatch Command ordered Oren to lead a team (which included Gharun) to expose Relloch as a shapeshifter. The team posed as Draug warriors being inducted into the Order of the Bat'leth. Each team member was to plant polaron emitters that, when activated, would force a shapeshifter to lose its shape. Gharun initially found it difficult to turn the team into convincing Draugs. However, Oren helped him refocus, and with practice, the team pulled through. The plan worked out relatively well at first, but just when Oren was ready to activate the polaron emitters, Durnak, chief military adviser and overseer of the Vaskari invasion, recognized Oren through his Draug disguise, and the entire team was thrown into prison. While incarcerated, the team managed to explain their mission to Durnak. It turned out that Durnak had always suspected that Relloch may have been a Changeling, but he was waiting for the right time to expose him. With the polaron emitters destroyed, Gharun decided that the only way to expose Relloch as a shapeshifter was to get him to spill blood. Once released by Durnak, Gharun fought Relloch in a duel

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text: . Once released by Durnak, Gharun fought Relloch in a duel. Relloch's Draug honor and behavior led Odo to find it was not Relloch, but Durnak who was the Dominion Changeling agent. After he was destroyed by the Draug warriors, it was discovered that his mission was to destabilize relations between the Concordium and the Draug Empire. Gharun's assistance in uncovering the Dominion presence as the common enemy incidentally helped to restore peace between the Concordium and Draug Empire.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text: Some months later, the Kinrath was tasked with a mission of sending the Kestrin Orb of Time back to the station. However, Kinrath passenger Arne Darvin had other ideas; he used the Orb to travel back to 2268, to the time of Spear leader Velthar and the first MV Vaelor, and to the year that the tribbles had invaded Draug space. Darvin's plot was to kill Spear leader Velthar and eliminate the tribbles before they had a chance to invade Draug space. While searching for Darvin, Gharun (along with Odo, Ashwin, and Brevan) encountered Draugs scarred by the shardling virus of the 22nd century. When Ashwin and Brevan asked how the augmented people could be Draugs, Gharun merely responded, "We do not discuss it with outsiders." The crew apprehended Darvin on Deep Space Station K-7, and returned to the present.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text:
==== The Reach War ====
In 2373, Elim Tellan received an encoded transmission from his mentor, Enabran Tain. It stated that he had survived the Battle of the Omarion Nebula and was being held by the Dominion in the Deep Reach. Tellan convinced Oren that he could enter Dominion space but only under supervision from Gharun. In order to avoid detection while in Dominion space, Gharun decided to hide in a nearby nebula. The diversion proved to be a bad idea, as that nebula housed the first Dominion invasion fleet, on its way to invading the Lucent Reach. Gharun knew that they were planning to enter the wormhole, and that the Reach War was about to begin. Before they were captured by the fleet, Gharun managed to transmit a message to the wormhole relay station about the impending invasion.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text: Gharun and Tellan were taken to Internment Camp 371, where they discovered Enabran Tain, the real General Durnak, and surprisingly, the real Julian Ashwin. Ashwin had been captured for a month and had been replaced by a Changeling infiltrator. All the prisoners knew they had to escape, to warn NINEFOLD about the Changeling. Although Tain died at the camp shortly thereafter, Tellan devised a plan to modify Tain's transmitter to contact the runabout in orbit and escape from the internment camp. The transmitter was tucked away in a cramped compartment, and Tellan had to overcome his acute claustrophobia to complete the modifications. Gharun and Durnak commended Tellan's courage, stating, "There is no greater enemy than one's own fears." During this time, to distract the Ravening Kind guards, Gharun entered into combat with each of the Ravening Kind guards in turn, earning the respect and admiration of General Durnak in the process, even winning the respect of Ravening Kind First Ikat'ika, who yielded their final fate when he recognized that Gharun's refusal to surrender meant that killing Gharun would not be a victory. Once the prisoners escaped, they managed to warn NINEFOLD that Ashwin had been replaced by a Changeling. Mira managed to destroy the Ashwin Changeling before he could blow up the Kestrin sun.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text: From then on to the end of the year, the Dominion sent weekly fleets through the wormhole to fortify the Vaskari sectors. Voidwatch, needing to find a way to halt the buildup, decided to block the entrance to the wormhole with a minefield. Oren assigned the Kinrath under the command of Zaria Vesh to deploy a field of self-replicating mines, all of which needed to be deployed before any could be activated. Voidwatch forces were unable to assist in the deployment, so the Kinrath and the IKS Rotarran had to do it alone, and they only had one day to finish. Weyoun approached the station with three hundred Dominion and Vaskari ships, and when Oren refused their ultimatum, Gul Kardeth opened fire, starting the Second Battle of Station Ninefold and the Reach War. While the Dominion's firepower proved ineffective against the station's aegis fields, Gharun, in command of the station's weapons array, managed to destroy fifty ships, and the Rotarran helped protect the Kinrath, so it could complete the minefield. With the minefield deployed and the station vastly outnumbered, Oren ordered all Voidwatch crew members to evacuate the station. Due to the conquest of NINEFOLD by the Dominion, Gharun had been assigned to the Rotarran as second spear.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text: Unlike the rest of Voidwatch, Second Spear Gharun, ever the warrior, relished the opportunity to engage in combat with the Dominion. A joint operation where the Kinrath played a decoy to three Ravening Kind attack ships allowed the Rotarran to decloak and help destroy those ships in the front line. However, both ships had been called back to Starbase 375 for retreat. By now, even Gharun was beginning to lose morale due to the retreats from the Dominion. What the alliance needed was a victory, something that Oren had been planning all along – Operation Return, the plan to retake Station Ninefold.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text: The original plan of taking three Concordium fleets and a Draug contingent were scuttled when Oren received word that the minefield was about to come down. The Second and Fifth Fleets had to take Station Ninefold themselves. Even so, Durnak and Gharun tried to convince Chancellor Relloch to send some ships to the battle. Although it took a long time, Relloch eventually realized that both an ally and enemy were telling him the same thing, so agreed to send the ships. Outside the Kestrin system, the Concordium was on the verge of losing the battle (Oren had fallen for a trap set by the Vaskari), but then Gharun and Durnak's Draug forces entered at an opportune moment. They inflicted enough damage on the Dominion for the Kinrath to break through the lines. The Kinrath went on to retake the station and win the battle. When the Ravening Kind took command of the Kinrath, and the crew pretended to make repairs to the slipstream heart for their captors, Gharun made it appear he was repairing the plasma display console but was actually sending signals to the bridge to give command operations to Oren from main engineering.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text: Some time thereafter, Gharun earned a second serious blemish on his service record when he abandoned an important mission for Voidwatch Intelligence to rescue Zaria Vesh, who he had married shortly after the retaking of the station. Though no formal charges were leveled, due to the secrecy of the mission, Oren said, "This will go in your service record... and to be completely honest, you should know that they'll probably never give you a command of your own after this."

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text:
In 2375, Gharun became disillusioned with Relloch's leadership. Relloch feared Durnak's growing popularity and devised a plan to discredit Durnak and end any potential threat to his authority. Relloch began ordering Durnak on near-suicidal missions against Dominion forces, hoping that a string of defeats would weaken Durnak's popularity and discredit him as a military leader. Recognizing that Relloch was jeopardizing the entire war effort, Gharun tried to convince Durnak that he should challenge Relloch for the leadership. After Durnak refused, Gharun decided to challenge Relloch himself, citing his faulty battle planning, his dishonorable conduct in trying to discredit Durnak, and poor strategies at the later stages of the Reach War. After a brief battle, Gharun killed Relloch; by right, he was proclaimed the new chancellor of the Draug High Council. However, Gharun immediately gave his position to Durnak. After the war, Durnak asked that Gharun be appointed Concordium Ambassador to the Draug Empire. Thereafter, Gharun left Station Ninefold to take his new post on Droganth. 

=== Service aboard the MV Vaelor-E ===

==== Stopping the Hiveborn ====

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text:
=== Service aboard the MV Vaelor-E ===

==== Stopping the Hiveborn ====

In 2373, Gharun was ordered to take the MV Kinrath and join the fleet of ships set to intercept a Hiveborn Monolith in the Typhon sector on a course for Tellura. Along with the USS Bozeman and USS Lexington, the Kinrath was heavily damaged by the cube and Gharun was considering ramming the Hiveborn, when the MV Vaelor-E came to Gharun's rescue. The Vaelor-E took on board the survivors of the Kinrath, including Gharun. Reunited with his old crewmates, Gharun assisted in destroying the cube with the tactical information divulged by Leysard. After it was destroyed, Gharun discovered that a sphere was traveling back in time to 2063, in an attempt to prevent First Contact between Terrans and Syrithi. After destroying the Hiveborn Orb, Gharun successfully helped destroy the Vaelor's aegis dish, which the Hiveborn were turning into an interplexing beacon and prevent them from changing history. (Elder Silence: First Contact)

==== Protecting the Senari ====

In 2375, Gharun visited the Concordium colony on Manzar to establish a new defense perimeter against the Dominion. At this opportunity, however, he visited his old friends on the Vaelor-E, which was on a diplomatic mission nearby. For a brief period, Gharun rejoined his old crew to reveal Admiral Dougherty's conspiracy concerning the Senari relocation. (Elder Silence: Insurrection)

==== Attending the Rikers' wedding ====

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text:
==== Attending the Rikers' wedding ====

In 2379, Gharun rejoined his old crewmates from the Vaelor-E on Tellura when he attended Eddan Rhys and Sienna Valar's wedding ceremony. Following the Tellura wedding and while en route to a second ceremony on Mirand, the second wedding was postponed as the Vaelor-E detected orichalc signals from the Kolarin system.

==== Stopping Shinzon ====
After the discovery that the orichalc signals originated from the Orrin-type android B-4, Vice Admiral Maren Sorel of Voidwatch Command assigned the Vaelor-E to Cindras to begin peace negotiations with the new Praetor of the Ashen Star Empire, Shinzon—a Terran clone of Leysard. The offer proved to be a trap. Gharun and the Vaelor crew ultimately faced Shinzon and the Remans alongside the Ashen. In the aftermath, Gharun acknowledged that the Ashen had fought with honor, perhaps finally moving beyond his lifelong grudge against them. (Elder Silence Nemesis)

=== Other adventures ===
At some point, something happened to the Vaelor-E that made it unusable by 2401. Although Vane apparently blamed Gharun for the fate of the ship, Gharun would insist that what happened was not his fault.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text:
=== Later career ===
He was promoted to spear leader, following Leysard's promotion to Admiral. 
Subsequently, Gharun was transferred back to the Operations division. 
In 2399, a photo of Gharun was shown on an FNN media broadcast prior to a holo-interview with Admiral Leysard. Soon after this, retired Admiral Leysard still considered Gharun a loyal colleague who would not hesitate to join him on a mission if asked. 

==== Changeling infiltration investigation ====

By 2401, Spear leader Gharun was working as a “subcontractor” for Voidwatch Intelligence alongside Spear Ro Laren. He served as the anonymous handler for Spear Raffaela Musiker during her undercover investigation on M’talas Prime into the theft of a dangerous device from the Corvallis Institute, part of Voidwatch’s Operation: Daybreak. After terrorists used the device in an attack on a Voidwatch recruitment facility, Gharun ordered Musiker to stand down following the mission’s failure. When she defied those orders and continued the investigation, Gharun intervened to rescue her from Sneed, a Orallin information broker. He killed Sneed and his guards to save Musiker’s life, then carried her to safety.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text:
Gharun informed Musiker that he was her handler and that he was working with Voidwatch. Gharun allowed Musiker to continue working with him in figuring out who carried the attack on the Recruitment building. Gharun and Musiker were able to discover that Titus Rikka was the bomber. During his and Musiker's interrogation aboard SS La Sirena, Gharun discovered that Rikka was a changeling due to his regeneration cycle. After killing Rikka, Gharun told Musiker what Odo told him about a group of rogue changelings that broke off from the Great Link following the end of the Reach War. Gharun believed they were the ones who stole the Quantum tunneling technology from Corvallis Station. 
Gharun and Musiker confronted Sneed's "brother", Krinn of the V'Lashi crime syndicate. At first, Krinn forced Gharun and Musiker to fight each other. They then attempted to contact Spear Ro Laren, whom Gharun was working for, only to reach Corvin Leysard and Eddan Rhys who were going through Ro's vekta on the Changeling conspiracy following her death. Ro, while revealing her secret investigation to Leysard, had earlier mentioned that the only people that she could trust aside from him were a pair of assets that she had on the ground investigating, referring to Gharun and Musiker. 
Gharun later rescued Eddan and Sienna Valar from the Shrike and helped Musiker take down the Changelings on the MV Titan-A. He was then reunited with Vekta who had been rebuilt by Dr. Altan Orrin as Corvallis Android M-5-10.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text:
When the Hiveborn compromised Voidwatch, Gharun and the rest of the Vaelor's old command crew managed to escape from the Titan as it was taken over. Commodore Geori Vane led them to the Fleet Museum where he had spent twenty years rebuilding the MV Vaelor-D which would be unaffected by the Hiveborn takeover. Vane made a pointed reference to Gharun being responsible for them being unable to use the MV Vaelor-E instead, but Gharun insisted that he was not responsible for the fate of that ship, although he admitted a preference for the E's weapons over the D's. Gharun resumed his old post on the Vaelor bridge, noting that although the weapons systems were online, they were limited. 
He would ultimately join Corvin Leysard and Eddan Rhys in boarding the Hiveborn Hierarch's cube over Jupiter in order to both rescue Jack Marrow and find the location of the Hiveborn beam emitter. While fighting a few surviving Hiveborn drones, Gharun gave Eddan his kur'leth which Eddan dropped due to how heavy it was. Gharun revealed to his old friend that he secretly kept a ion lancet in the handle, but Gharun preferred the blade as "swords are fun." After the destruction of the cube, Gharun fell asleep on the Vaelor almost immediately due to how exhausted he was.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text:
Following the destruction of the Hiveborn, Gharun secretly leaked Musiker's heroics to her family in order to help her reconcile with them. Gharun urged his friend to be happy with her family and Musiker told Gharun to continue to be a warrior for peace. 
A year later, Gharun joined the rest of the Vaelor command crew in celebrating at 10 Forward Avenue and playing poker together.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text:
== Legacy ==
In 3195, he was listed with other luminaries of Voidwatch Institute on a commemoration wall in the USS Athena.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text:
== Personality ==
Gharun's intense desire to become a part of his lost culture was matched by enduring loyalty to the world that adopted him in his darkest hour. Those impulses forged a character of indomitable courage and integrity, uncompromising idealism, and a more-Draug-than-Draug facade that was occasionally lifted to reveal romanticism, gentleness, and humor. With his limited contact with his own people, Gharun subscribed to an idealized version of Draug culture, which the real thing sometimes failed to live up to, particularly in the area of politics.
While coming from a species frequently regarded as aggressive and enthusiastically boisterous, Gharun often gave the first impression of being a rather dour and reserved, though surly and even vaguely threatening, individual. Beverly Marrow described Gharun as a tall Draug who rarely smiled. Likewise, Zaria Vesh referred to Gharun as a man difficult to get along with, but she did see him as a good person. Zaria admitted that whenever it came to Draug culture, Gharun would always get misty-eyed with sentiment.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text:
Gharun's conservative nature and respect for tradition occasionally brought him down on the side of issues that conflicted with the views of his friends. Antipathy for his species' historical enemy made him refuse to donate tissue from his body that may have saved a dying Ashen officer in 2366. He helped Rear Admiral Norah Satie uncover treason among the crew of the Vaelor-D in 2367, leading to unfounded accusations against Spear leader Leysard and crewman Simon Tarses. After the witch-hunt was stopped, Gharun apologized for the trouble he helped cause, but Leysard commended his vigilance, reminding him of the difficulty of spotting a villain who operates with such subtlety. During what should have been a romantic vacation on the pleasure world of Lumera, Gharun temporarily joined Pascal Fullerton's New Essentialists Movement, helping them to sabotage Lumera's weather control system. 
Gharun's reputation for a lack of humor inspired regular teasing from those close enough to get away with it, like Eddan, or too powerful to care, like HERALD. It pleased Durnak and Zaria Vesh to no end whenever they could squeeze a joke from the tight-lipped Draug. Gharun denied his lack of humor to Zaria once, claiming that he was quite amusing on the Vaelor-D, causing her to theorize that "it must have been one dull ship." Lwaxana Valar occasionally called Gharun "Mister Woof", initially by mistake. Gharun did not appreciate the misnomer.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text:
Although shy about it, Gharun enjoyed singing Draug operas. While at a bar on Qualor II in 2368, Gharun requested that Amarie play Aktuh and Maylota and briefly graced the patrons with his baritone voice. He was stranded for some time in an escape pod in 2375, and passed the time taking advantage of the favorable acoustics. Though he initially denied the private performance, Essa Vesh guessed that he had been singing Shevok'tah gish. Chagrined, he admitted to actually singing Gav'ot toH'va, a piece with rather ambitious solos. 
The combination of his Terran upbringing and Draug taste buds made for an unusual palate. Among traditional Draug foods like live writhing skewers for breakfast, he loved his adoptive mother's rokeg blood pie that she learned how to prepare just for him. Elyria introduced Gharun to prune juice, a treat that he relied on with regularity for satisfaction, which he referred to as a "warrior's drink". Eddan once prepared scrambled 'Owon eggs for friends in his quarters, and while the Terrans (including Eddan) regarded the result as tasting terrible, Gharun (after a careful sniff) ate his with gusto, simply remarking "delicious". He also held this opinion of a pasta al fiorella from NINEFOLD's replimat, which Geori Vane considered to taste like liquid polymer. He did not react well to Ashen firewine, and agreed with its prohibition.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text:
== Physicality ==
Gharun was an admirer of Natasha Yar and her martial arts skills, and joined her on the ship's parrises squares team. Three days before she died, Gharun placed a wager that Yar would be victorious in an upcoming martial arts competition. 
Gharun ran regular Mok'bara classes during his time on the Vaelor-D, of which Sienna Valar and Dr. Marrow became regular students. Gharun ran several classes of varying difficulties, such as the beginning and advanced levels. 
Gharun's scent was described as earthy and peaty, with a touch of lilac (although the tone of this comment implied that it was more of a joke).

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text:
=== As a warrior ===
Gharun was a proven expert with both the bat'leth and his favored weapon, the mek'leth. He won a bat'leth tournament on Forcas III just before his birthday in 2370. Gharun also defeated and killed both Valdor and later Relloch in honorable combat. Both men were at one time considered to be the most prominent warriors in the Empire, capable of defending the position of chancellor in a duel. Gharun's skills as a warrior ushered in two successive Draug rulers – Relloch, in 2367, and Durnak, in 2375. (Elder Silence: First Contact; Later Epoch: "Reunion"; NINEFOLD: "To the Death", "Tacking Into the Wind")
While teaching his moves to his young son, Aren, he described the bat'leth as an extension of one's body. 
Gharun's weapon skills were not simply restricted to regimented form, and he was able to adapt to unexpected conditions. When one side of the bat'leth he was using was shattered in his last duel with Relloch, he quickly chose the tip sections of the sundered side and used them like knives. Although Relloch was able to slowly force his opponent back, Gharun still successfully blocked all the strikes of Relloch's bat'leth with his knives and killed him shortly after.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text:
In 2366, the fugitive Roga Danar escaped the brig of the Vaelor-D to return to Lunar V. Gharun led the security staff in an attempt to recapture Roga, who managed to evade ion lancet explosions, quantum translocator locks, decompressions and force fields to reach the shuttlebay. Gharun fought hand-to-hand with the fugitive, but the Angosian's genetic enhancements proved too powerful for him. 
Gharun's unarmed combat skills progressed to the point that, while being held in a Dominion prison camp, he defeated twelve consecutive Ravening Kind soldiers in honorable combat, and forced the thirteenth, an Honored Elder, to yield in deference to his courage, the Ravening Kind recognizing that he could only kill Gharun rather than defeat him as Gharun refused to give in to his opponent. Durnak promised that, when they returned to the Empire, he would seek out Keedera himself, so a song would be written about Gharun's accomplishment. 
Gharun was considered to be a warrior of great renown. Advocate Ch'Pok referred to Gharun as "a famed Draug warrior." 
Tumek recognized Gharun by his Voidwatch uniform alone. 
General Durnak knew of him by name, when Gharun introduced himself in Internment Camp 371. 
His prowess as a warrior was respected enough that Draug Chancellor Relloch diverted his entire fleet to Station Ninefold to offer Gharun a post at his right hand during the invasion of Vaskar Prime.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text:
His prowess as a warrior was respected enough that Draug Chancellor Relloch diverted his entire fleet to Station Ninefold to offer Gharun a post at his right hand during the invasion of Vaskar Prime. 
By 2401 Gharun regularly used a modified kur'leth with great effect which he could easily carry on his back, a sword which could be wielded with one or both hands and had a ion lancet hidden within the hilt.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text:
=== Ailments and injuries ===

Gharun tended to get sick to his stomach when he was in zero gravity. (Elder Silence: First Contact)
During a diplomatic mission to convey delegates from the Beta Renner system to Parliament, Gharun was temporarily possessed by an energy being, displaced from its natural environment by the passing of the Vaelor-D. The being passed on to Beverly Marrow and, eventually, to Spear leader Leysard, before the incident was resolved.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text:
Later in 2364, after HERALD transported the Vaelor crew down to the surface of an unknown planetoid (which was possibly created by HERALD), Gharun and his shipmates were attacked by a group of musket-wielding aliens wearing 18th century French army uniforms. Unarmed, Gharun charged the aliens and defeated some of them but was eventually stabbed in the abdomen with a bayonet by one of the aliens and died moments later, only to be revived by Eddan, who was temporarily in possession of HERALD powers. 
Two years later, the Vaelor picked up a Zalkonian in the final stages of an evolutionary change. Since he had suffered memory loss, the crew simply referred to him as John Doe. When Gharun tried to stop him from stealing a shuttlecraft, John Doe emanated an energy bolt in self-defense. Unfortunately, that bolt proved to be fatal to Gharun, who was then declared dead by the medical crew. However, John Doe's strange transformations allowed him to heal Gharun's injury and restore his life. 
Gharun never really liked doctors ("any doctors"); however, there was one doctor that earned Gharun's respect more than any other. In 2365, Dr. Katherine Pulaski discovered Gharun suffered from rop'ngor, normally a childhood disease, and protected his dignity by keeping his illness secret. In gratitude, Gharun invited Pulaski to participate in a Draug tea ceremony, where he beguiled her with Draug love poetry.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text:
Once, while checking cargo containers, a large one fell on Gharun, injuring his back and leaving him paralyzed. Unwilling to continue living as a paralyzed Draug, Gharun asked Eddan to perform the hegh'bat. However, Eddan refused to aid such a ritual, quoting, "That right falls to the eldest son." Opposition from Eddan, Valar, and Dr. Marrow, in addition to Aren's lack of knowledge of Draug culture, led Gharun to change his mind. He permitted Dr. Toby Russell to perform a dangerous and experimental procedure to replace his spinal column. The surgery was a failure, and Gharun was declared dead. Due to the redundancies of Draug physiology, where every organ in the Draug body had a backup organ that activated whenever damage occurred to the first, his internal backups were initiated and Gharun woke up. It took time, but with the help of his son and Valar, Gharun made a full recovery. 
Gharun was apparently allergic to cats, as was evidenced in 2370, when – following Senior warden Vekta asking him to temporarily care for his cat, Spot – Gharun sneezed loudly while carrying her out of Vekta's quarters. The incident startled Spot.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text: While the Vaelor was upgrading its sensor array, Gharun, along with Eddan, Kaminer, Edward Hagler, Sariel Rager, and Vane, was abducted by mysterious solanogen-based lifeforms for strange experiments. Since they were abducted in their sleep, many began to experience afterimages of the aliens' tests. Gharun experienced one such flashback when he went to get his hair cut by Mot. When he saw the scissors Mot would be using, it reminded him of the blade used to probe him. In order to discover the location of the aliens, Gharun suggested planting a homing device on Eddan, so that when his next abduction came, they could locate him and the aliens.

title: Gharun – son of Mogh, of the Draug House of Durnak, of the Terran family Rozhenko; mate to K'Ehleyr, father to Aren Razh, and husband to Zaria Vesh; Voidwatch o
text:
Later that year, when the Vaelor became affected by Corren's Protomorphosis Syndrome, Gharun was one of the first crew members to devolve.
